# Regression Guards

Index of `@leb-regression-guard` markers in the source tree.

A regression guard is a comment block placed directly above a fix that
- has a non-obvious correctness contract,
- has been broken-and-fixed at least once, and
- has a busted spec that locks in the invariant.

**Before editing code below an `@leb-regression-guard`, run the linked spec.**
If the spec passes after your edit, the invariant still holds and you're fine.
If it fails, your edit silently regressed a previous fix — read the linked
establishing commit and the spec rationale before forcing the change through.

To find every guard:

```sh
grep -rn '@leb-regression-guard' src/ spec/
```

## Active guards

### `item-tooltip-source-colour`

Item mod lines are coloured by SOURCE, mirroring the game's own per-line priority. The order is
load-bearing: item rarity is tested BEFORE affix tier (a Legendary item's affixes are crimson
even at T7, while the same T7 affix on a Set item is exalted purple), and the idol-enchant pool
is tested BEFORE tier (idol enchantments tier to T7 and would otherwise be painted purple).
White is the correct default, not a fallback: the game leaves implicit, unique-inherent and
T1-T5 affix text uncoloured. "LEB cannot use this line" moved from red text to the
`(NOT SUPPORTED IN LEB YET)` suffix -- red would destroy the source signal and collides with
LEGENDARY crimson. Depends on `idol-special-affix-type-is-integer`: every `sat ==` test here is
dead on idols without it.

**Sites:**

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `src/Modules/ItemTools.lua` | `sourceColorCode` (priority) + `formatModLine` (suffix) |
| `src/Data/Global.lua` | `SEALED` / `SEALEDCORRUPTED` / `PRIMORDIAL` / `CORRUPTEDAFFIX` |
| `src/Classes/Item.lua` | `Craft` carries `tier` / `specialAffixType` / `kind` onto the modLine |
| `src/Classes/ItemsTab.lua` | passes `item` in (rarity is not on the modLine) |

**Files:** `src/Modules/ItemTools.lua`, `src/Data/Global.lua`, `src/Classes/Item.lua`,
`src/Classes/ItemsTab.lua`.
**Invariant:** TWO INDEPENDENT AXES, never conflate them -- `modLine.kind` is the sealed axis
(nil / `"sealed"` / `"primordial"` / `"corrupted"`), `modLine.specialAffixType` is the affix
pool (0 Standard, 3 Set, 4 IdolEnchantment, 5 IdolWeaver, 6 Corrupted). `kind == "corrupted"`
(sealed BY corruption) and `specialAffixType == 6` (drawn from the corruption-only pool) are
different facts with different colours; an affix can be either, both, or neither. Exalted is
`tier >= 5` on the 0-indexed tier (display T6/T7; T5 is max craftable). Legendary is gated on
`modLine.affixType` so a unique's own mods stay white. `sat == 4/5` MUST precede the tier test.
Reads `specialAffixType`, NOT `modLine.enchant` -- that flag comes only from a `{enchant}`
raw-text tag, which appears zero times in `ModItem_*.json` / `ModIdol_*.json` and can never be
set by an affix roll (`Craft`'s `enchantMods` is a bucket name only). Set bonuses and the
corrupted-item marker are out of scope (separate render path / sprite art).
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestItemTooltipSourceColour_spec.lua`,
`spec/System/TestUniqueInherentNotCrafted_spec.lua`,
`spec/System/TestDisplayOnlyTooltipText_spec.lua`
**Snapshot coverage:** none -- display-only, corpus-inert.
**Establishing commit:** `<see git log>`

### `idol-special-affix-type-is-integer`

`specialAffixType` is the raw LE `AffixList.SpecialAffixType` enum integer. `ModItem_<ver>.json`
carries it; `ModIdol_<ver>.json` carries no such key, so `Data.lua` derives it from the section
an entry sits in -- and it used to derive STRINGS. Lua does not coerce, so `"Corrupted" == 6` is
false and `mod.specialAffixType == 6` was ALWAYS FALSE for a tier-0 idol affix, silently
disabling corrupted-affix bucket routing, the item-naming skip, and the corruption-gated Line-2
extension on idols. It was also tier-dependent (ModIdol stores only `_0`; `flat` chains to
ModItem via `__index`, see `idol-affix-tier-fallback`), so the same affix family was a string at
tier 0 and an integer at tier 1+. `CalcSetup`'s old `satEnumToStr` coercion patched the symptom
and is gone.

**Sites:**

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `src/Modules/Data.lua` | `sectionToSpecial` -- section to integer tag |
| `src/Modules/CalcSetup.lua` | `specialAffixType()` + altar `stdBoost` / `weaverBoost` gates |

**Files:** `src/Modules/Data.lua`, `src/Modules/CalcSetup.lua`.
**Invariant:** every idol affix's `specialAffixType` is a NUMBER (0/4/5/6), never a string, and
tier 0 and tier N of one family never differ in type. The section-to-integer mapping must stay
lossless: all 469 `ModIdol_1_4.json` entries agree exactly with `ModItem`'s integer for their
section, and no ModIdol entry carries a `specialAffixType` of its own. The spec re-derives that
comparison rather than trusting it, so a data regen that files an affix under the wrong section
trips instead of silently mis-tagging it. CalcSetup keeps the `_0`-preferred lookup (the idol
pool is authoritative for idol-specific corrections); it is no longer load-bearing for type.
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestIdolSpecialAffixTypeInteger_spec.lua`,
`spec/System/TestIdolRefractedWeaverEnchantBoost_spec.lua`,
`spec/System/TestIdolRefractedStandardBoostAllSubtypes_spec.lua`
**Snapshot coverage:** altar / refracted-idol builds. CalcSetup behaviour is unchanged (the
`_0` preference already returned the string tag for tier-N lookups), so expected corpus-inert.
**Establishing commit:** `<see git log>`

### `unique-inherent-not-crafted`

`uniqueInherent` marks a mod that comes from the unique/set definition itself, as opposed to a
rolled affix or a user-crafted mod. The unique importers used to tag those lines `{crafted}`
(two `TODO: avoid using crafted` comments marked the debt), which painted them CRAFTED pale blue
while the game renders them white. `crafted` had accreted three non-colour readers, so it could
not simply be dropped. Legacy builds carry `{crafted}` on unique mods, so `processModLine`
reclassifies `crafted and not enchant and not implicit` on a UNIQUE/SET/LEGENDARY item -- safe
because `{crafted}` only ever had two producers (the unique importers, and enchant lines, which
are forced implicit and thus excluded); nothing in the UI sets `crafted`.

**Sites:**

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `src/Classes/Item.lua` | `lineFlags`; both implicit/explicit splits; `Craft` `savedMods`; `BuildRaw` tag emit; `isLegendaryAffix`; legacy migration in `processModLine` |
| `src/Classes/ImportTab.lua` | LETools + offline-save unique importers emit `{uniqueInherent}` |
| `src/Modules/Build.lua` | unique import emits `{uniqueInherent}` |

**Files:** `src/Classes/Item.lua`, `src/Classes/ImportTab.lua`, `src/Modules/Build.lua`.
**Invariant:** every reader that used `not modLine.crafted` to mean "not unique-inherent" MUST
test both flags. The dangerous one is `isLegendaryAffix`, which gates Permanence's "increased
Effect of Skill Level modifiers on Legendary Affixes": dropping `not modLine.uniqueInherent`
there lets Permanence scale a unique's own mods and MOVES DPS. The others are the
implicit-vs-explicit split (a unique's mods must not be promoted into unfilled implicit slots)
and `Craft`'s `savedMods` set (they are destroyed on re-craft without it). The legacy migration
is calc-inert BY CONSTRUCTION for the same reason, and the spec asserts it directly by comparing
DPS between a `{crafted}` and a `{uniqueInherent}` build.
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestUniqueInherentNotCrafted_spec.lua`
**Snapshot coverage:** none expected -- migration is calc-inert (asserted by spec).
**Establishing commit:** `<see git log>`

### `display-only-tooltip-text`

Some unique tooltip lines carry no modifier at all: in the datamined game source they live in
the unique's `tooltipDescriptions` block, not its `mods` array (the dispatcher is
`tooltipEntries[].modDisplay` -- below 128 renders a real mod, 128+ renders raw text).
Throne of Ambition is the pure case: its only real mod is a hidden flag, and all six visible
lines are text. LEB transcribes them so the tooltip matches in-game, so the parser must consume
them to nothing. The mechanics they describe are modelled elsewhere and must stay there -- see
`throne-of-ambition-stacks`.

**Sites:**

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` | `displayOnlyModList` + the `parseMod` hook |
| `src/Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json` | Throne of Ambition (6 lines, verbatim) |

**Files:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua`, `src/Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json`.
**Invariant:** a display-only line yields zero mods AND `extra == nil`. `extra` must be `nil`,
NOT `""` -- an empty string is truthy in Lua and paints the line red UNSUPPORTED just the same.
A truthy `extra` is a lie here (the line is not an unmodelled mod, it is not a mod); a non-empty
modList injects a ghost mod into modDB. The stack cap stays modelled by the parser (`limit = 20`
on `per stack of ambition`), never by the transcribed text. LEB previously carried only 4 of the
6 lines and paraphrased the stack-gain line with a `100% Chance` prefix present in neither the
game data nor the in-game tooltip, dropping the `(1 second cooldown)` qualifier; the text is now
pinned verbatim by `TestUniqueDataIntegrity_spec.lua` (TOOLTIP_TEXT + EXPECTED_COUNT=6).
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestDisplayOnlyTooltipText_spec.lua`,
`spec/System/TestUniqueDataIntegrity_spec.lua`
**Snapshot coverage:** none -- both wordings parse to zero mods.
**Establishing commit:** `<see git log>`

### `wrongwarp-inline-rebuild-310`

> **Type: JSON-comment-incompatible.** The protected site is unique `310` in
> `src/Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json`, which cannot carry inline
> `@leb-regression-guard:` markers (JSON has no comments). The 3-layer
> contract is preserved by the spec + this index entry; any mass-edit of the
> uniques JSON MUST reference this guard id in its commit message.
> See "JSON-comment-incompatible guards" at the bottom of this file.

Wrongwarp is rebuilt to its in-game item: 6 rows in `tooltipEntries` order
(`[128,129,130,0,1,131]`), confirmed 6/6 against an in-game screenshot. Three rows LEB
carried exist nowhere in the game data -- two cooldown-recovery rows (real mechanics:
`CooldownRecovery` INC scoped to Teleport / Transplant) and a mana-cost row (inert). The
game's Wrongwarp has no cooldown-recovery and no mana-cost mod; its only cooldown text is a
minimum-cooldown FLOOR, the opposite of recovery. A fourth row, `+1 Wrongwarp with Teleport
or Transplant`, was the fallback-formatter artifact for the game's hidden mod (see
`unique-hideintooltip-letools-artifact`) and parsed to `{{},""}` -- empty modList AND empty
text. Only the LIVE file (`_1_4`) is rebuilt: `_1_2`/`_1_3` carry the same rows but are not
grounded in-game.

**Sites:**

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| data | `src/Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json` unique `310` | The 6 verbatim rows + `rollIds` |
| parser | `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` `displayOnlyModList` | Rows 1, 3, 6 consume to nothing |
| canonical | game data unique `310` `tooltipEntries` / `tooltipDescriptions` | Source of order + text; not in repo |

**Files:** `src/Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json`, `src/Modules/ModParser.lua`.
**Invariant:** exactly 6 rows, verbatim, in `tooltipEntries` order. No cooldown-recovery
row, no mana-cost row, no `+1 Wrongwarp` artifact. Exactly one row carries a range (the
Haste row) and it is the only row with a `rollId`, which is the game's `rollID` 0.
`rollIds` is a roll-GROUP id, NOT a line index (`unique-shared-rollids-not-independent`);
the stray `rollId` 1 dropped out as a consequence of deleting the two rows that used it --
it was never "fixed" from the export, whose `mods[].rollID` is unreliable. Do NOT assert on
`#rollIds`: JSON `null` decodes to Lua `nil`, so `rollIds` is SPARSE and `#` is undefined
for it. Both consumers index `rollIds[i]` under a nil check (`Build.lua`, `ImportTab.lua`)
and never take a length.
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestWrongwarpChronowarp_spec.lua`
**Snapshot coverage:** none. `data.uniques[]` is read only at save-import; saved builds
store unique rows as TEXT, so this edit cannot move an existing snapshot.
**Establishing commit:** `<see git log>`

### `unique-tooltip-entries-display-order`

A unique's tooltip is rendered from the game's `tooltipEntries` (entry `<128` -> `mods[entry]`,
`>=128` -> `tooltipDescriptions[entry-128]`), never from LEB's `mods[]` order. Mods flagged
`hideInTooltip` are absent from `tooltipEntries` and fold into a description; one description
can cover SEVERAL mods, so the row count is not the line count (Exsanguinous: 6 rows -> 4
lines). Ordering is decided by `tooltipEntries` alone: Exsanguinous puts descriptions LAST
(`[3,4,128,129]`), Shattered Worlds puts them FIRST -- both screenshot-verified. The display
layer is ADDITIVE: only `tooltipEntries` / `tooltipDescriptions` were added to the live data,
`mods[]` and `rollIds[]` are byte-identical (471/471 entries verified), so modDB is unchanged
by construction. Rollout is staged: only items whose LEB-row <-> game-mod correspondence
RESOLVED carry `tooltipEntries` (430 of 471); the other 41 have none and fall back to `mods[]`
order. "Resolved" = matched structurally against the game data, NOT confirmed in-game: only
uid 11 and 413 were read off screenshots, so the other 428 are structurally-matched only and
must never be described as in-game-verified (`reference_corpus_selfconsistency_not_ingame`).
The NOT SUPPORTED suffix stays per-modLine on directly drawn lines; folded lines get an
item-level count instead, because desc->mod attribution is not derivable (413 of 560
descriptions carry no rollID placeholder; 284 of 533 folded mods map to no description) and a
folded line can be only PARTIALLY supported.

**Sites:**

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| logic | `src/Modules/ItemTools.lua` `buildUniqueTooltipPlan` | Resolves `tooltipEntries` -> draw list; bails to nil on drift |
| render | `src/Classes/ItemsTab.lua` (`AddItemTooltip` mod loop) | Draws the planned block + item-level folded note |
| data | `src/Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json` (375), `src/Data/Set/set_1_4.json` (55) | Carry `tooltipEntries` / `tooltipDescriptions` |
| audit | `spec/tools/gen_unique_tooltip_order.py` | Regenerates the plan; reports unverified items + coverage gaps |
| canonical | game data `tooltipEntries` / `tooltipDescriptions` | Source of order + text; not in repo |

**Files:** `src/Modules/ItemTools.lua`, `src/Classes/ItemsTab.lua`,
`src/Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json`, `src/Data/Set/set_1_4.json`.
**Invariant:** `mods[]` and `rollIds[]` are never reordered or rewritten for display -- 464 of
the 699 rows LEB marks NOT SUPPORTED still emit modDB mods, so replacing a mod string with
in-game prose deletes mechanics. Every baked `tooltipEntries` index resolves inside its own
item. An item without `tooltipEntries` falls back to `mods[]` order and must not be presented
as verified. `explicitModLines` is NOT permuted in place: `ItemsTabCraft` seeds
`craftUniqueRanges[i]` from `explicitModLines[i]` and reads it back, so an in-place reorder
desyncs the craft roll sliders.
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestUniqueTooltipEntriesOrder_spec.lua`
**Snapshot coverage:** none. `data.uniques[]` is read only at save-import and saved builds
store unique rows as TEXT; this change adds display-only fields, so no snapshot moves.
**Establishing commit:** `<see git log>`

### `chronowarp-buff-conditional`

Chronowarp is Wrongwarp's buff (10s, granted on a Teleport / Transplant cast). Its stats are
stated only by the item's own data line, so the line parses to them directly rather than the
buff being defined in ConfigOptions -- the inverse of the Frenzy / Haste entries, which bake
their stats because no item text describes them.

**Sites:**

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| parser | `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` | Whole-line handler -> `Speed`(Cast) + `MovementSpeed` INC, tagged `Condition:Chronowarp` |
| config | `src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` | `conditionChronowarp` check; sets the FLAG only |
| data | `src/Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json` unique `310` row 2 | The verbatim line the number is read from |

**Files:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua`, `src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua`.
**Invariant:** the value is CAPTURED from the line, never hardcoded -- a rebalance changes
the data, not the code. Both mods carry `{Condition:Chronowarp}` and are NOT `nsList`: they
are real DPS-integrated mods (cast speed feeds hit rate), so a NotSupported label would be a
lie, and a flat always-on mod would fake 35% cast speed for every Wrongwarp build regardless
of whether the build casts Teleport at all. Cast speed is `Speed` + `ModFlag.Cast` and must
not leak onto attacks. `conditionChronowarp` sets ONLY the FLAG -- re-emitting the stats
there would double-count against the parser. It is gated by `ifCond = "Chronowarp"`
(reads `mainEnv.conditionsUsed`), so it stays hidden until a mod tagged with the condition
exists, i.e. until Wrongwarp is equipped; and it defaults OFF, because uptime depends on how
often the build actually casts Teleport / Transplant.
**Not modelled (recorded, not faked):** the desc0 random teleport + 1s damage immunity, the
desc2 time lock, and the desc3 minimum-cooldown floor. LEB has no time-lock/CC concept and
no minimum-cooldown floor; those rows are display-only (`display-only-tooltip-text`).
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestWrongwarpChronowarp_spec.lua`
**Snapshot coverage:** none -- the config defaults OFF, so no existing build changes.
**Establishing commit:** `<see git log>`

### `dev-merge-guard-gate-matching`

`scripts/dev-merge.sh` Gate 2 is fail-closed: it blocks a merge when a newly registered
guard has no Layer 1 (inline marker on the protected code) or no Layer 2 (a `*_spec.lua`).
That only works if its lookup can see a correctly written guard. As first landed it could
not — it matched one of the three inline marker spellings in the tree, searched Layer 1
under `src/` only, and accepted anything under `spec/` as Layer 2.

<!-- validation detail omitted: line 288 -->
<!-- validation detail omitted: line 289 -->
<!-- validation detail omitted: line 291 -->
<!-- validation detail omitted: line 292 -->

**Files:** `scripts/dev-merge.sh`
**Invariant:** the marker lookup accepts all three spellings in the tree (measured on dev
`<see git log>`: 1282 `<marker>:<id>`, 404 `<marker>: <id>`, 55 `<marker> <id>`) and anchors the
id so `foo` is not satisfied by `foo-bar`. Layer 1 = any tracked NON-test file under `src/`,
`spec/` or `scripts/` (guards legitimately live on `spec/` driver code — see
`regen-filter-env-fail-fast`); Layer 2 = a `*_spec.lua` specifically, never all of `spec/`,
or a Layer 1 comment sitting in `spec/` satisfies it and a 2-layer guard registers as 3.
A false positive here is worse than no gate: it blocks correct work and trains
`LEB_SKIP_CONVENTION_GATES=1` as a reflex.
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestDevMergeGuardGateMatching_spec.lua`
**Snapshot coverage:** none — merge tooling, not calc.
### `optional-artifact-pending-not-silent`

`spec/TestBuilds/` and `spec/tools/` are gitignored with ZERO tracked files, so they exist
only in the main repo working tree. Nine specs read them and failed on
`assert.is_not_nil(f, ...)` in every worktree and every CI checkout — 16 red results that
mean nothing, permanently. `spec/OptionalArtifact.lua` turns that into a visible `pending`,
but ONLY when the whole directory is absent.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| presence | `spec/OptionalArtifact.lua` `isPresent` / `resolveDir` | `os.rename(p,p)` existence probe, with the `../` retry for cwd=src |
| whole-block skip | same, `describe(name, dir, body)` | registers one `pending` when `dir` is absent |
| per-test skip | same, `requireDir(dir)` | `pending()` inside an `it`, for blocks that mix artifact and src-only tests |
| tolerant read | same, `readOptional(path)` | nil when the DIR is absent; **raises** when the dir exists and the file does not |

**Files:** `spec/OptionalArtifact.lua`
**Invariant:** skip on a missing DIRECTORY only. A missing FILE inside a directory that IS
present is a real deletion and must still fail loudly — that is what `readOptional` asserts
and what `requireDir` deliberately does not cover. Never collapse this into a blanket
"if the file won't open, skip": that reads green in the main repo while asserting nothing,
which is strictly worse than the noise it replaces (same failure shape as
[`regen-filter-env-fail-fast`] — a fallback quieter than the real path, so invisible).
Skips must surface as busted `pending`, never as a silent pass or an undeclared test.
Gate per-test with `requireDir` when a block mixes artifact-dependent and src-only tests;
a whole-block skip there would trade 16 noisy reds for ~10 silently lost src assertions.
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestOptionalArtifactPending_spec.lua`
**Snapshot coverage:** none — spec infrastructure, not calc.
**Establishing commit:** `<see git log>`

### `regen-filter-env-fail-fast`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestRegenFilterEnvFailFast_spec.lua`
**Sites:** `spec/RegenFilterEnv.lua` (the parsers), consumed by the snapshot-regen
drivers `spec/GenerateBuilds14.lua`, `spec/GenerateFromList.lua`,
`spec/GenerateOneBuild.lua`, `spec/GenerateSnapshotsFromList.lua`,
`spec/RegenOneBuild.lua` — those drivers are **gitignored dev tooling** (see
`.gitignore` "Internal snapshot-generator variants"), which is why the parsing they
share lives in this tracked module: it is the only layer of the regen filter chain
a busted spec can reach. A driver must `dofile("../spec/RegenFilterEnv.lua")`
(cwd=src) and must not re-implement the parsing inline.

- Every var the module parses (`LEB_ONLY_LIST`, `LEB_ONLY_FILE`, `LEB_SHARD`,
  `LEB_ROOT`) **narrows** which builds get regenerated. So a parse failure that
  falls back to "no filter" **widens** the run from the handful the caller asked
  for to the whole 639-build corpus (hours) — and does it **silently**, because
  intent and fallback differ in runtime, not in exit status. The contract: a
  filter var that is SET but unusable must `error()`, never continue with a wider
  selection than requested. Unset (`""`) stays the normal path = no filter.
- The mirror-image failure errors too: a filter that parses but matches **nothing**
  (empty list file, comment-only list, `LEB_SHARD="4/4"`, an `LEB_ROOT` holding no
  `.xml`) exits 0 having regenerated nothing, which reads as success.

**Why:** the `LEB_ONLY_LIST` branch used to `print("[LEB_ONLY_LIST] WARN could not
open …")` and continue with `onlyList = nil`. Combined with `LEB_FORCE=1` that
turns a scoped regen into a full-corpus regen. It fired twice: once on a `/tmp`
path native LuaJIT could not open, and again on 2026-07-16 when a build **name**
was passed where a **file path** was expected (the run was killed at 6m40s). Both
times the operator's only signal was one WARN line scrolling past. `LEB_SHARD` had
the same shape latently — `shardI = tonumber(shardI) or 0` / `shardN = … or 1`
means any malformed value (`"1 of 4"`, `"1/"`) degrades to `0/1` = everything.
Documenting the trap in notes did not prevent recurrence; failing the process does.

**Regression to prevent:** re-introducing a `print`-and-continue (or any `or ""` /
`or 0` / `or 1` default) on a SET-but-unparseable filter var; a driver bypassing
the module and parsing the env inline again; or dropping the CR-LF strip, which
leaves a trailing `\r` in a substring so it matches no build (silent-nothing).

**Corpus impact:** none. Tooling-only — no `src/` calc path is touched, so
snapshots are byte-identical (corpus-neutral).

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `javelin-spear-melee-to-throwing-conversion`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestJavelinSpearConversion_spec.lua`
- Javelin's datamined mechanic: with a **spear** equipped, the spear's own added
  **melee** damage applies to Javelin as added **throwing** damage at **50%**, which
  then rides Javelin's normal **250% damageEffectiveness** (alt-text worked example:
  a spear with +100 Melee Damage → Javelin deals +125 additional = 100 × 0.5 × 2.5).
  Added melee from non-spear sources has no effect. LEB previously modelled none of
  it (added flat 0), reading ~6.35× under a low-crit in-game capture.
- **Fix site:** `Modules/CalcActiveSkill.lua` `buildActiveSkillModList` — gated on
  `activeGrantedEffect.id == "Javelin"` + `skillTypes[Throwing]` + an equipped
  `flag=="Spear"` weapon; reads ONLY the equipped spear's weapon-sourced,
  `KeywordFlag.Melee` BASE damage per type, and injects a **skill-scoped**
  `<Type>Damage BASE = spearMelee × 0.5` (source `"Javelin Spear Melee Conversion"`).
  The injected flat carries NO Melee keyword (so it is not re-read/double-converted)
  and flows through the ordinary added pool → `addedPart × damageEffectiveness`; the
  skill's own 50 base stays in `skillPart × 1` (base is NOT effectiveness-scaled).
- **Invariant:** conversion is Javelin-only + spear-only; coefficient is exactly 0.5;
  converted flat gets the same per-unit effectiveness as ordinary added; non-spear
  melee contributes 0.
- **Snapshot coverage:** the corpus builds that socket Javelin AND equip a
  Two-Handed Spear (Phalanx/Pike) — regenerate those. Non-spear or non-Javelin
  builds are byte-identical (early-exit before injection).

### `idol-slot-dropdown-width`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestIdolSlotDropdownWidth_spec.lua`
- Clicking an idol grid cell opens a `DropDownControl` list of equippable idols.
  The list must widen to fit the item names, not stay clamped to the tiny cell.
- **Bug (pre-fix):** idol grid cells build their `ItemSlotControl` at the cell
  width (`self.cw` ≈ 68px) with `enableDroppedWidth` off, so the open list's
  `droppedWidth` collapsed to the box width — roughly the width of the "None"
  entry — clipping every idol name.
- **Fix (3 parts, all under this guard):**
  1. `Classes/IdolGridControl.lua` — each idol slot sets `enableDroppedWidth`,
     `maxDroppedWidth = 320`, and `dropExtraWidth = 3*18` (reserve for the
     leading type/primordial/corrupted row-icon strip).
  2. `Classes/ItemSlotControl.lua` — `Populate()` fills `self.list` directly
     (never through `SetList`), so it must call `CheckDroppedWidth(true)` at the
     end for slots that opted in, or the width never recomputes off the real list.
  3. `Classes/DropDownControl.lua` — `CheckDroppedWidth` measures label widths at
     the FIXED dropdown row font (16, matching `Draw`'s `itemFontSize`), not
     `self.height - 4`. A tall idol cell (height 46) otherwise over-estimates the
     width by ~(height-4)/16 ≈ 2.6x. The measurement also adds `dropExtraWidth`.
- **Do NOT** revert the measuring font to `self.height - 4`: it happens to equal
  16 only for standard 20px-tall dropdowns, and silently breaks any tall box.

### `dropdown-scrollselintoview-nil-selindex`

**Files:** `src/Classes/DropDownControl.lua`
**Invariant:** `DropDownControl:ScrollSelIntoView` never feeds a nil
`ListIndexToDropIndex` result into arithmetic. `ListIndexToDropIndex` returns
nil (not its `default` arg) when `selIndex` is nil, `<= 0`, or `> #list`;
`ScrollSelIntoView` clamps that to the first row (`or 1`) before the
`(dropIndex - 2) * itemLineH` expression.
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestDropdownScrollSelIntoView_spec.lua`
**Snapshot coverage:** none (UI-only, DPS/calc-inert)
**Establishing commit:** `<see git log>`
- **Bug (pre-fix):** opening a dropdown (`OnKeyDown` -> `ScrollSelIntoView`)
  whose `selIndex` was nil or out of range crashed OnFrame with
  `attempt to perform arithmetic on a nil value` at DropDownControl.lua:181.

### `config-label-fit`

**Files:** `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua`, `src/Classes/LabelControl.lua`, `src/Classes/CheckBoxControl.lua`
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConfigLabelFit_spec.lua` (wrapping invariants), `spec/System/TestConfigTabDrawSmoke_spec.lua` (Config tab `:Draw` renders without erroring)
**Establishing commit:** config-label-fit branch (`<see git log>`)
- Config-tab option labels sit to the LEFT of their control and grow leftward
  toward the section box's inner border (~228px away). Long labels overflow that
  border and must be brought inside — with a UNIFORM font, by WRAPPING onto
  multiple lines (an earlier font-shrinking approach was rejected: it made some
  labels too small to read).
- **Bug (pre-fix):** two rendering paths overflow the left border for the
  longest LEB-specific labels (e.g. `# of Skeleton Warriors Absorbed by
  Abomination:`, `Apply Tyrant's Skull per-attribute Tyrannosaur block?`):
  1. count / list / edit rows use a right-anchored `LabelControl`.
  2. check rows use `CheckBoxControl`'s own right-aligned label.
- **Fix (all under this guard):**
  1. `Classes/ConfigTab.lua` — `wrapLabel(label)` greedily breaks a label into
     lines each ≤228px at font 14, returning the newline-joined text and line
     count. Non-check labels set `labelControl.rightAlignLines = true`; both
     paths store `control.labelLineCount`, and the two row-height computations
     (section `height` + the layout loop) grow the row by
     `labelLineCount * (14+2)` so wrapped lines don't overlap the next control.
  2. `Classes/LabelControl.lua` — `width` returns the WIDEST line for a
     multi-line label (not the meaningless whole-string measurement, which for a
     right-anchored label mis-positions it); `Draw` honours an opt-in
     `rightAlignLines` flag (default keeps the historic left-aligned multi-line
     behaviour other callers rely on).
  3. `Classes/CheckBoxControl.lua` — `GetLabelWidth()` and `Draw` handle
     multi-line labels (widest-line hit width; one right-aligned `DrawString`
     per line). `labelSize` stays `size - 4` (uniform — never shrunk).
- **Do NOT** reintroduce font-shrinking to fit labels, and do NOT change
  `LabelControl:Draw`'s default multi-line branch to right-align (other tabs'
  multi-line labels depend on the left-aligned default — use `rightAlignLines`).

### `damage-type-ingame-order`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestDamageTypeOrder_spec.lua`
- `DamageTypes`, `DamageTypesColored` and `DamageTypeColors` (src/Data/Global.lua)
  must stay aligned index-for-index in the in-game resistance order:
  Fire, Lightning, Cold, Physical, Poison, Necrotic, Void.
- **Bug (pre-fix):** `DamageTypes` / `DamageTypesColored` used
  Fire, Cold, Lightning, Physical, Necrotic, Poison, Void (Cold/Lightning and
  Poison/Necrotic swapped vs the game). The Resists panel (`CalcSections.lua`)
  drives its row order from `DamageTypes`, so it read out of order; and
  `DamageTypeColors` was already in in-game order, so display sites that zip
  `DamageTypes[i]` with `DamageTypeColors[i]` (`Build.lua` max-hit rows +
  resist-over-cap rows, `Data.lua` power stats) tinted e.g. the Cold value with
  the Lightning color.
- **Fix:** reordered `DamageTypes` and `DamageTypesColored` to match
  `DamageTypeColors` (in-game order). Values are keyed by type name, not index,
  so calc output/snapshots are unaffected — display order + color only.
- **Do NOT** reorder one of the three arrays without the others; all iteration
  is by name (`ipairs`) with `[i]` used only to cross-index these parallel
  arrays, so they must move together.
- **Files:** `src/Data/Global.lua`
- **Establishing commit:** this branch

### `idol-altar-no-reforged-set`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestIdolAltarNoReforgedSet_spec.lua`
- Reforged Set affixes are a GEAR-only mechanic; Idols and Idol Altars can NEVER
  be Reforged Set pieces.
- **Bug (pre-fix):** the import reforged-set scan resolves every decoded affix
  against the generic `data.itemMods.Item` pool. An offline-save decode OVERREAD
  (trailing bytes misread as a valid affix id) injected a bogus gear affix onto
  an Ocular Altar — id `949` "Abandoned Chitin of the Weaver Reforged"
  (`specialAffixType 3`) — and the scan promoted the altar to the Weaver Set
  (rarity SET, `setInfo` Weaver Set, name "Abandoned Chitin of the Weaver
  Reforged"). The overread affix is dropped later by `Craft` (not in the altar
  pool), but the SET flag persisted via `REFORGED-RESTORE`.
- **Fix:** skip the reforged-set scan for Idol / Idol Altar bases at BOTH
  `Classes/ImportTab.lua` scan sites (the inline affix-loop scan gated on
  `not isIdolOrAltar`, and the offline-save `scanForReforged` block gated on the
  base name not matching `Idol`/`Altar`).
- **Do NOT** rely on the affix `specialAffixType`/pool alone — the overread id is
  a *valid* gear affix in `data.itemMods.Item`; the reliable signal is the item's
  base type (idols/altars are never sets). Twin naming guard:
  `idol-corrupted-affix-name-skip`.

### `idol-corrupted-affix-name-skip`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestIdolCorruptedAffixNameSkip_spec.lua`
- Idol / Idol Altar / Refracted display names are built from the base plus
  NORMAL prefix/suffix name words only. Corruption-exclusive affixes
  (`specialAffixType == 6`) and Class-Specific Idol enchants
  (`specialAffixType == 4`) carry a stat LABEL in their `affix` field, not a
  proper name word, and never rename the item in-game.
- **Bug (pre-fix):** the generated item name was built from the generic
  `data.itemMods.Item` pool, where these affixes carry the stat label (e.g.
  `1106`/`1104` = "Maximum Idols Equipped", `1071` = "Bees per 10 Seconds",
  `1067` = "Increased Mana Regeneration and Reduced Health Regeneration",
  `1063` = "Slow chance converted to Armor Shred chance"). The label got
  prepended and baked into the stored name line (`self.title`), e.g.
  "Maximum Idols Equipped Spire Altar of Eos" instead of "Spire Altar of Eos".
- **Fix — three coordinated sites (same guard slug):**
  - `Classes/ImportTab.lua` (import side): skip `specialAffixType` 6/4 and
    `kind == "corrupted"` when generating the name at import.
  - `Classes/Item.lua` `ParseRaw` (load side): rebuild the name from base +
    normal affixes so already-saved builds heal without a re-import. Classify
    corruption/enchant via `data.itemMods.Item` (authoritative) — the idol pool
    (ModIdol) can carry a `sat==6` affix such as `1063` in a non-corrupted
    section with NO `specialAffixType` marker, so the item's own pool is not a
    reliable classifier.
  - `Classes/Item.lua` `Craft()` (fresh UI craft): gate `namePrefix`/
    `nameSuffix` on the same exclusion.
- **Do NOT** classify corruption/enchant from the item's own affix pool alone,
  and do NOT strip to the base name blindly — legit normal prefix name words
  ("Sunrise", "Inspired") and suffix words ("of Eos") must be preserved.

### `summon-minion-data-namespace`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestSummonMinionDataNamespace_spec.lua`
- `SummonIllusoryTree` (Summon Illusory Tree) and `SummonMercenary` (Recruit
  Mercenary) each summon a minion. Their `skills.json` `minionList` MUST
  reference the `minions.json` **key**, NOT the raw in-game display/prefab name:
  - `SummonIllusoryTree` → key `"IllusoryTree"` (NOT display `"Illusory Tree"`).
  - `SummonMercenary` → key `"Mercenary"` (NOT prefab `"Summoned Mercenary"`).
- Ground truth (`datamined game source`): `minion_stats.json` `"Illusory Tree"` =
  maxHealth 100 / skillList `[]`, matching `minions.json` `IllusoryTree`
  (life `"100"`, empty skillList) EXACTLY. `leb_minion_mapping_v4.json` declares
  `leb_key="Mercenary"` ↔ `matched_prefab="Summoned Mercenary"` (name-match,
  bundle=player, actorType=Heavy, confidence=high); `minion_stats.json`
  `"Summoned Mercenary"` = maxHealth 400, matching `minions.json` `Mercenary`
  (life `"400"`, skillList `["Crossbow Bolt"]`) EXACTLY.
- **Bug (pre-fix):** `minionList` held the display/prefab name, which is absent
  from `minions.json`, so `createMinionSkills` (`CalcActiveSkill.lua` ~1346
  `minion.minionData = env.data.minions[minionType]`) resolved `nil` and crashed
  at ~1476 (`attempt to index local 'minionData' (a nil value)`) for ANY build
  with either skill enabled as an active skill. `createMinionSkills` runs
  per-active-skill from `CalcPerform.lua:548`, so the crash is NOT limited to the
  isolated single-skill probe that surfaced it.
- **Fix:** point each `minionList` at the existing `minions.json` key. Do NOT
  "re-align" to the display/prefab name — the `minions.json` key is the
  resolution key. Same namespace-gap bug class as `pontifex-cremate-minion-data`
  (BurningSkeleton).

### `pontifex-cremate-minion-data`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestPontifexCremateMinionData_spec.lua`
- `PontifexCremate` (Cremate) summons Burning Skeletons. Its `skills.json`
  `minionList` MUST reference the `minions.json` **key** `"BurningSkeleton"`,
  NOT the raw in-game prefab name `"SummonedBurningSkeleton"`. They are the
  SAME minion.
- Ground truth (`datamined game source`): `leb_minion_mapping_v4.json` declares
  `leb_key="BurningSkeleton"` ↔ `matched_prefab="SummonedBurningSkeleton"`
  (name-match, bundle=player, actorType=Heavy). `minion_stats.json`
  `SummonedBurningSkeleton` = skillList `["Fireball"]`, maxHealth 200,
  actorName "Burning Skeleton" — matching the existing `minions.json`
  `BurningSkeleton` (skillList `["Fireball"]`, life "200") EXACTLY.
- **Bug (pre-fix):** `minionList` held the prefab `"SummonedBurningSkeleton"`,
  which is absent from `minions.json`, so `createMinionSkills`
  (`CalcActiveSkill.lua` ~1346 `minion.minionData = env.data.minions[minionType]`)
  resolved `nil` and crashed at ~1476 (`attempt to index local 'minionData'
  (a nil value)`) for ANY build with PontifexCremate enabled as an active skill.
  `createMinionSkills` runs per-active-skill from `CalcPerform.lua:548`, so the
  crash is NOT limited to the isolated single-skill probe that surfaced it.
- **Fix:** point `minionList` at the existing `minions.json` key
  `"BurningSkeleton"`. Do NOT "re-align" it to the prefab name to match the
  other `Summoned*` skeletons — the `minions.json` key is the resolution key.

### `void-knight-echo-more`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestVoidKnightEcho_spec.lua`
- Void Knight mastery 2nd bonus (tree_2.json `"Void Knight"` `isAscendancyStart`
  node, 2nd stat): "Your melee attacks, throwing attacks and void spells have a
  **10% chance to be repeated by an echo** 0.5s later (excludes movement abilities
  and Anomaly)."
- datamining: `CreateVoidKnightEchoAfterDelay` = full re-cast of the ability;
  `Property_Player_81` = echoes do NOT chain; `Property_Player_57` "increased Echo
  Damage" default 0 → the echo deals the ability's FULL damage. A P% chance to
  repeat the whole ability = **×(1 + P/100) average output = a +P% MORE Damage**.
- **The bug this guards:** the echo line is bare prose (no "N% more/increased/added"
  form), so ModParser produced NOTHING and `PassiveTree:ProcessStats` flagged it
  `node.extra` → the bonus was **entirely unmodelled** (a flat ~+10% DPS miss on
  every Void Knight melee/throwing/void skill).
- **Parser** (`ModParser.lua` `specialModList`): a whole-line `^…$` handler captures
  the chance into a `VoidKnightEchoChance` BASE player mod. Whole-line so parseMod
  leaves **no `extra` residue** (a trailing-period residue would re-drop it — the
  `<see git log>` trap). Capturing the number (not a bare flag) keeps the MORE% tracking
  the tooltip if LE re-tunes it.
- **Consumer** (`CalcActiveSkill.lua`, after `skillModList` is built): reads
  `actor.modDB:Sum("BASE", "VoidKnightEchoChance")` (player-only — minions carry no
  VK flag) and adds `Damage MORE = chance` to the eligible set: **melee attack OR
  throwing attack OR (void AND spell)**, MINUS **movement skills** (`SkillType.Movement`)
  and **Anomaly** (by name). The any-of-minus-exclusions gate can't live on one
  keyword-tagged mod, so it is resolved per-skill at setup.
- **Numeric proof** (TitoGaoS4, save slot 106, gear-on, before→after): Erasing Strike
  (melee) DamageMORE ×2.00→×2.20, DPS 440,294.8→484,324.2 = **×1.100 EXACT**; Void
  Cleave (melee) ×2.32→×2.552; Devouring Orb (void spell) ×1.00→×1.10; **Anomaly (a
  void spell) UNCHANGED ×1.00** (excluded); Symbols of Hope (non-void spell) unchanged.
- **⚠ Headline DPS moves** for Void Knight builds (unlike `boss-crit-damage-taken`),
  so this landed WITH a Void Knight corpus snapshot regen (same VK set the mastery
  void-more fix regen'd; Paladin unaffected).

### `erasing-strike-obliteration-2h-double`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestErasingStrikeObliteration2h_spec.lua`
- Erasing Strike Obliteration (`es6ai-16`, maxPoints 5) raw per-point stats:
  `"+10% Damage"` + `" Doubled with a 2h Weapon"`. The node is "+X% **MORE** Damage,
  DOUBLED while wielding a 2h weapon" (bare "+X% Damage" parses to Damage MORE). The
  " Doubled with a 2h Weapon" line is its own stat and was residue-**dropped**, so LEB
  applied the un-doubled +50% MORE (×1.50 at 5 pts) to **every** build — undercounting
  2h builds, which should get +100% MORE (×2.00).
- **Why not a second additive mod:** two MORE mods **multiply** (1.5×1.5 = 2.25), not add.
  A naive "+50% more when 2h" on top of the base would give ×2.25, not ×2.00.
- **Fix** (`LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE`, `Data/Global.lua`): split into two **mutually
  exclusive** weapon-gated MORE mods so exactly one applies —
  `"+20% Damage with 2h weapon"` (×5 → +100% MORE = ×2.00, doubled) and
  `"+10% Damage with 1h weapon"` (×5 → +50% MORE = ×1.50, unchanged). Conditions are
  `UsingTwoHandedWeapon` / `UsingOneHandedWeapon`, auto-detected from the equipped weapon.
- **Numeric proof** (TitoGaoS4, 2h World Splitter): only the 2h mod applies (no
  double-count), non-crit void per-hit **74,115.637 → 98,573.80 = ×1.330**, More(Damage)
  2.20 → 2.926.
- **⚠ NOT corpus-neutral** (unlike `erasing-strike-conditional-melee`): the weapon
  condition is gear-deterministic, not a default-OFF config, so **2h Erasing Strike builds
  gain the doubling and were snapshot-regen'd**; 1h ES builds are unchanged. Per-point
  values are hardcoded (a %-capture can't double a value); an LE re-tune of "+10%" stops
  the pattern matching and the spec surfaces it (manifest-armor exact-value precedent).

### `erasing-strike-merciful-damaged`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestErasingStrikeMerciful_spec.lua`
- Erasing Strike Merciful (`es6ai-9`, maxPoints 4) raw per-point stats:
  `"+15% Cooldown Recovery Speed"` + `"+5% Melee Damage vs Damaged Enemies"`. The CDR line
  parses fine; the melee line's "vs Damaged Enemies" condition clause leaves `parseMod`
  `extra` residue → `PassiveTree:ProcessStats` drops the whole mod → the melee bonus
  silently contributes **nothing** (same residue-drop class as `erasing-strike-conditional-melee`).
- **MORE, not INCREASED:** like the two conditional-melee siblings, the in-game node
  tooltip (screenshot, 2/4 pts = +10%) reads *"Erasing Strike has increased cooldown
  recovery speed and deals **more** melee damage to enemies that are already damaged
  (**multiplicative with other modifiers**)."* → this is a **MORE** (multiplicative) mod.
- **Fix** (`LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE`, `Data/Global.lua`): re-expresses the melee line to
  `"N% more melee damage against damaged enemies"`, which parses (ModParser `^([%+%-]?[%d%.]+)%% more`)
  to Damage **MORE** + Melee keywordFlag (512) + an `ActorCondition{actor=enemy, var=FullLife,
  neg=true}` tag registered by the new `"against damaged enemies"` phrase in `ModParser.lua`
  ("damaged" = **not** full life). Runs on the raw per-point string BEFORE rank scaling; the
  captured leading value (5) is multiplied by node alloc afterwards (2 pts → +10% MORE,
  4 pts → +20% MORE).
- **⚠ NOT corpus-neutral** (unlike `erasing-strike-conditional-melee`): `conditionEnemyFullLife`
  **defaults OFF** → the enemy is not full life by default → the negated-FullLife condition is
  **TRUE by default** → the MORE applies by default (intentional; LEB "most combat occurs below
  full life" realistic-sustained-DPS convention). Merciful has **no weapon gate** (unlike
  Obliteration), so **every build allocating `es6ai-9` changes**. Blast-isolation (toggle
  `LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE["es6ai-9"]` nil vs set, FullDPS twice) identified **7 affected of
  9 allocating builds**; snapshots regen'd (all UP, 0-mismatch verified via `loadfile` ground truth):
  - `1.4/VoidCleaver lv84 VK` ×1.199, `1.4/<private build> lv100 Void Knight` ×1.099,
    `1.4/BakEPgze lv100 Void Knight` ×1.098, `1.4/bin/YsFckAFKKick Sentinel Legacy` ×1.098,
    `1.4/bin/YsAberrothKiller lv100 Void Knight` ×1.085, `1.4/bin/YsBonkVK_S2 lv100 Void Knight` ×1.055,
    `1.4/bin/YsAberrothKiller.xml` (per-hit keys change, FullDPS unchanged).
  - **Unaffected (not regen'd):** `1.4/bin/HoneyImCheatingATM lv100 Void Knight`,
    `1.4/bin/VoidCleaver lv84 VK` (main skill not a damaged-enemy melee hit; verified 0-mismatch
    against their untouched snapshots under the fix).

### `erasing-strike-ruthless-fullhealth` — RETIRED (folded into `enemy-full-health-alt-order`)

Erasing Strike Ruthless (`es6ai-10`) had a `LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE` entry rewriting
`"+25% Melee Damage Vs Full Health Enemies"` → `"N% more melee damage against full health
enemies"` to escape a residue-drop. `<see git log>` added the `"vs full health enemies"`
word-order key to `ModParser.lua` (guard `enemy-full-health-alt-order`), so the RAW line now
parses residue-free to Damage **MORE** + Melee keywordFlag (512) + a NON-negated enemy
`ActorCondition{FullLife}` — **byte-identical** to the rewrite's output. The rewrite was
therefore a **semantic NO-OP** and was removed (`Data/Global.lua`), along with its spec
(`TestErasingStrikeRuthless_spec.lua`). The surviving invariant (raw line → MORE not
INCREASED, Melee kept, non-neg enemy FullLife) is now a case in
`spec/System/TestEnemyFullHealthAltOrder_spec.lua` under `enemy-full-health-alt-order`.
Corpus-neutral (no build allocates `es6ai-10`; `conditionEnemyFullLife` defaults OFF).

### `nova-no-self-trigger`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestSparkNovaSelfTrigger_spec.lua`
- a skill flagged `data.skills[id].noSelfTrigger` must not re-trigger ITSELF. Only
  `SmallLightningNova` (Spark Nova) carries the flag (mirrors the existing
  skills.json calc-behaviour flag `excludeFromTriggerNameList` on
  `SparkChargeExplosion`).
- the bug: Spark Nova is a TRIGGERED-only skill (no manual gem group). The "Spark
  Nova (from Lightning Blast)" group carries `source="SkillId:LightningBlast"` and
  inherits Lightning Blast's mods via the `cfg.groupSource` channel (ModStore) —
  including the LB skill-tree node `ChanceToTriggerOnHit_SmallLightningNova`
  (`tree_1.json` `lb23il-8` "Halo Effect") — and also sees the global class-tree
  node (`Mage-64` "Distant Spark"). Iterated as a trigger SOURCE, the Spark Nova
  group re-found the chance and emitted a SECOND, spurious "Spark Nova (from Spark
  Nova)" Full DPS entry.
- locks: the grant insertion is gated by `triggerChance > 0 and not (skillId ==
  sourceSkillId and data.skills[skillId] and data.skills[skillId].noSelfTrigger)`.
  DATA-GATED to SmallLightningNova only, so non-self triggers (Spark Nova →
  Electrify/Poison ailments), Lightning Blast → Spark Nova, manual self-cast affixes
  (Shurikens, Shadow Cascade), and every other build are byte-identical.

**Site:** `src/Modules/CalcSetup.lua`, the `grantedTriggeredSkills` trigger loop
(`for skillId, skill in pairsSortByKey(data.skills)` over each source socket group);
flag in `src/Data/skills.json` (`SmallLightningNova.noSelfTrigger = true`).

an interaction with `cycle-weight-exclude-triggered` — an unverifiable artifact, and
those builds lack the per-skill in-game capture Spark Nova has. So the fix is scoped
by the data flag to the one ground-truth-confirmed skill. Do NOT add the flag to
another skill without (1) an in-game capture proving its 1:1 trigger ratio and (2) a
regen check that no parent skill's cycle-weight folding shifts. Do NOT touch the
Spark Charge detonation grant (`spark-charge-detonation-grant`).

### `weapon-attack-minion-weapon-inheritance`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestWeaponAttackMinionInheritance_spec.lua`
- a bow-attack minion (Falconer **Ballista**, granted skill `BallistaBolt`:
  `skillTypeTags` Bow|Physical + `baseFlags.attack` + `fromMinion`) inherits the
  equipped bow's per-type ADDED damage (`+Bow Fire/Cold/Lightning` affixes and the
  generic `+Bow Damage`) plus any weapon-keyword damage INC/MORE, copied PER TYPE
  from the player modDB onto the **minion** modDB
- locks: Lightning (added 20) == 2× Fire (added 10) — type-preserved, no cross-type
  bleed; a type with no source affix (Cold) stays exactly 0 (no blanket fold);
  elemental affixes do NOT inflate the bolt's Physical (no spurious phys)
- scoping: a non-bow equipped weapon (Dagger) is NOT inherited (the `weaponData1.type
  == "Bow"` gate); a non-weapon-attack minion (bear) does NOT inherit (the
  `band(skillTypeTags, Bow)` skill-type gate)
- source contract: the copy targets `env.minion.modDB` ONLY (zero player ripple), is
  `band(mod.keywordFlags, weaponKeyword)`-gated (global kw=0 player INC excluded), and
  must NOT resurrect the abandoned untyped player-hit `isWeaponAttack` gate

**Site:** `src/Modules/CalcPerform.lua`, the `if env.minion then` minion-modDB
population block (after the SkillId-tree-mods transfer).

(absent from `weaponData1`) are NOT inherited here — separate, still-open contributors
to the residual; extending the weapon→keyword mapping beyond Bow needs its own capture.

### `minionlist-resolves`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestMinionListResolves_spec.lua`
- every `minionList` entry in `skills.json` must be a real key in `minions.json`
- corpus-wide ratchet: a `KNOWN_DANGLING` allow-list tolerates pre-existing,
  not-yet-datamine-verified entries; any NEW dangling entry fails the spec
- pins `SwarmOfBees.minionList == {"Bee"}` (datamine-verified) + `SummonBee == {"Bee"}`
  (regression check for the auto-summon framework merge)

**Site:** `src/Data/skills.json` (`minionList` arrays) ↔ `src/Data/minions.json` keys.

**Why:** the engine indexes minions by the exact `minionList` token
(`CalcActiveSkill.lua` `minion.minionData = env.data.minions[minionType]`), so a
dangling entry yields `nil` minionData — a SILENT failure (the summon contributes
no minion stats/damage with no error). Caught 2026-06-15: `SwarmOfBees` (Swarm of
Bees, granted by the unique **Keeper's Gloves** — "10% chance to summon a swarm of
bees on melee hit") had `minionList=["SummonedBee"]`, the raw in-game PREFAB name,
but `minions.json` keys the worker bee as `"Bee"`. Datamine ground truth: the
`SwarmOfBees` abilityPrefab `SummonBees` carries a `SummonEntityOnDeath` whose
`ActorReference` → `ActorData{m_Name="SummonedBee", actorName="Bee", actorType=3}`,
and `leb_minion_mapping_v4.json` mapping[47] maps prefab `SummonedBee` → LEB key
`Bee` (life 60). Fixed to `["Bee"]` (same raw-prefab trap as `SummonBee`, already
fixed on dev by the auto-summon merge). The `KNOWN_DANGLING` set documents the
remaining pre-existing dangling entries; it should SHRINK as each is
datamine-verified — do NOT guess a prefab→key mapping. Auto-summon Phase B
datamine-verified + fixed three of them (`Summon AncientOasis01 Primordial Minion`
→ `PrimalAnurok`, `Summon Giant T_Rex Minion` → `PrimalTyrannosaur`, `Summon Tolmat
Minion` → `TolmatMinionDivine`; via `leb_minion_mapping_v4.json`). The last three
namespace-gap entries were then fixed too — `PontifexCremate` `SummonedBurningSkeleton`
→ `BurningSkeleton` (`<see git log>`), `SummonIllusoryTree` `"Illusory Tree"` →
`IllusoryTree` and `SummonMercenary` `"Summoned Mercenary"` → `Mercenary`
(`<see git log>`) — so **`KNOWN_DANGLING` is now EMPTY**: the corpus-wide invariant
enforces all 40 `minionList` entries with no exceptions. A positive Phase B
resolution test pins the Anurok/T_Rex/Tolmat links + their encoded primary attack
skills, and a `namespace-gap` resolution test re-asserts the
`BurningSkeleton`/`IllusoryTree`/`Mercenary` links so a re-extraction that
re-introduces a raw prefab/display name trips the spec instead of being silently
re-admitted.

### `no-spectre-library`

Upstream PoB let a granted effect ship an EMPTY `minionList` to mean "the user picks which
spectres this skill raises", resolved against a build-level library (`build.spectreList`)
populated from `data.spectres`. LE has no such mechanic -- a skill's minions are fixed by its
data -- and LEB never ported the backing data, so the whole chain was unreachable and partly
guaranteed to throw. Removed rather than repaired (user decision, 2026-07-16, after three
options were put up). Found incidentally during an item-tooltip affix-colour audit.

Measured before removal: `data.spectres` never assigned (READ-only, so the popup died on
`pairs(nil)`); `build.spectreList` never initialised; `skillFlags.spectre` never set, so the
CalcsTab section was permanently hidden; all 39 `minionList`s in `skills.json` non-empty, so
the CalcActiveSkill fallback was unreachable by DATA, not by a code guard; and
`MinionListControl`'s tooltip read six `minion.*` fields that `minions.json` does not carry.

**Sites:**

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `src/Modules/CalcActiveSkill.lua` | the "Create minion" block (empty-`minionList` fallback) |
| `src/Modules/Build.lua` | `OpenSpectreLibrary`, "Manage Spectres..." button, `mainSkillMinionLibrary` |
| `src/Classes/CalcsTab.lua` | the `flag = "spectre"` section |
| `src/Classes/CalcBreakdownControl.lua` | the `sourceType == "Spectre"` branch |
| `src/Classes/MinionListControl.lua` | deleted outright |

**Files:** `src/Modules/CalcActiveSkill.lua`, `src/Modules/Build.lua`,
`src/Classes/CalcsTab.lua`, `src/Classes/CalcBreakdownControl.lua`
(`src/Classes/MinionListControl.lua` deleted).
**Invariant:** the library-specific symbols stay gone -- `spectreList`, `data.spectres`,
`OpenSpectreLibrary`, `MinionListControl`, `mainSkillMinionLibrary` -- and every
`minionList` in `skills.json` stays non-empty (the fallback's absence is a data property and
rots silently otherwise). Generalised class-level check: every `colorCodes.X` referenced in
`src/` must be defined in `Data/Global.lua` (`colorCodes.CHAOS` was not -- LE has no Chaos
damage type; its types are Physical/Fire/Cold/Lightning/Void/Necrotic/Poison).
**DO NOT widen the spec's greps to a bare "Spectre".** `Blood Spectre` (Necromancer tree,
14 `ModCache.lua` rows + tree data) and `ActiveSpectreLimit` (`SkillStatMap.lua`) are REAL LE
game data and are deliberately untouched. Only the five library symbols above are banned.
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestNoSpectreLibrary_spec.lua`
**Snapshot coverage:** none -- the removed code was unreachable, so corpus-inert.
**Establishing commit:** `<see git log>`

### `lightning-blast-chain-rehit`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestLightningBlastChainRehit_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (specialModList: `maximum additional chains`
/ `doublecast chance` / `quadruple cast chance` rules + the two Convergence flag
rules), `src/Data/ModCache.lua` (the six per-point/flag rows, previously
silent-failure NO-OPs), `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (the node-gated
`output.HitSpeed` multiplier).

**Why:** LEB models Lightning Blast as a SPELL (no projectile, so
`skillFlags.chaining` never fires and the generic `ChainCountMax` machinery is
bypassed) and parsed every LB chain/cast tree node as a ModCache NO-OP. In-game,
"Convergence" (lb23il-18, `LightningBlastMutator.chainsBackOnItself` +
`halfChains`) makes chains re-hit the SAME target, and Overcharge/Hypercharge
doublecast/quadcast multiply casts, so on a single target LB hits ~3x its cast
rate (URA_YA_RANGE in-game 13.16/s vs cast 4.40/s). That hit rate is the
prerequisite for the Spark Charge detonation grant (`spark-charge-detonation`,
deferred), so it had to be modeled honestly first.

**Mechanism (no fabrication; datamined game source,
`datamined game source` — NB the datamined game source RVAs are 1.4.2 and
mis-decode, use the live `script.json` addresses):**
`numberOfChains = chains(0x148) + min(maxChainsForRecent(0x11C)+2,
recentDirectCasts(0x120)) + (staticOrb>0 ? 2 : 0)`, then `if halfChains:
Ceil(*0.5)`. `mutateDelayedCastDuration = previousDelayedCasts * 0.25f` → re-hits
land 0.25s apart, and a new cast pre-empts pending re-hits, so the realized count
is `min(numChains, castInterval/0.25)` — genuinely cast-speed dependent (faster
casters realize FEWER chains, which is why a fixed "chains = N hits" overshoots).
Applied on `output.HitSpeed` (node-gated on the Convergence flag) so the cast
rate itself (MaxStacks/Duration) is untouched and non-Convergence / non-LB skills
are unaffected. PassiveTree scales the stat number by points before parsing
(`ProcessStats:407`), so >1-point nodes live-parse the scaled text via the
ModParser rule while 1-point / flag nodes use the patched ModCache rows.

### `lb-chain-rehit-skill-scoped`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestLBChainRehitNovaLeak_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (the `LightningBlastChainsBackOnItself`
chain-rehit block, gated to the Lightning Blast skill name).

**Why:** the Convergence flag (`LightningBlastChainsBackOnItself`, lb23il-18) is
set on Lightning Blast, but the "Spark Nova (from Lightning Blast)" triggered
entry (skillId=SmallLightningNova, socketGroup source `SkillId:LightningBlast`)
INHERITS Lightning Blast's full modlist via `cfg.groupSource` (ModStore), so it
also carries the flag. Ungated, the chain-rehit block (`lightning-blast-chain-rehit`)
fired for the Nova entry too and set `Nova.HitSpeed = Nova.Speed * ~1.99`. But
`Nova.Speed` is ALREADY the LB *hit* rate (the trigger rate = LB's post-chain
`HitSpeed`), so the chain factor was double-applied — once in the trigger rate,
once again on Nova's HitSpeed — counting Spark Nova at ~2 hits per trigger.

**Fix:** gate the block to the Lightning Blast skill itself
(`activeSkill.activeEffect.grantedEffect.name == "Lightning Blast"`, mirroring the
sibling Maelstrom skill-name gate in the same file). Triggered children (Spark
Nova, ailments) no longer receive the LB-only chain multiplier; Lightning Blast's
own chain-rehit (`lightning-blast-chain-rehit`) is unchanged.

### `granted-group-placement-no-holes`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestSubSkillGrantRegistry_spec.lua` (placement assertions in the
end-to-end test)
- guard marker in `CalcSetup.lua` (granted-group create path)
- legacy index kept only when free AND contiguous; else first-free placement
- the raw `socketGroupList[5 + grantedIndex] = group` write is gone
- behavioral: socketGroupList stays dense (`#` == pairs count) after grant passes

**Site:** `src/Modules/CalcSetup.lua` (granted-skill materialization, the
`if not group then ... end` create path).

**Why:** the legacy placement wrote each newly-created granted group to the FIXED
index `5 + grantedIndex`, assuming <= 5 manual groups and a dense grantedIndex.
Both assumptions break: the per-activeSkill timer scan re-adds the same
`Timer:<id>` grant once per active skill (FugginBEESSS: 8 duplicate
Timer:Maelstrom entries), and XML-persisted granted groups match early entries —
inflating grantedIndex so the fixed write lands beyond the end of the list and
leaves **holes**. Lua's `#` stops at the first nil, so every
`for i = 1, #socketGroupList` consumer (snapshot slot dump, Full DPS UI,
selectors) silently lost the groups beyond the hole, while `pairs`-based
consumers (activeSkillList) still computed them. Probe-confirmed on FugginBEESSS:
Spirit Thorns / Thorn Shield landed at [11]/[12] with [7]-[10] nil → `#list` = 6 →
the registry sub-skills never reached the snapshot (3 of 9 Spriggan corpus builds
affected: <private build> / <private build> / FugginBEESSS). Post-fix the same build places them
at [7]/[8], `#list` = 8. The legacy position is preserved whenever it is free and
contiguous, so existing snapshot slot numbering is unchanged for the builds that
already worked. **Regression to prevent:** restoring the raw fixed-index write
(re-introduces invisible granted groups), or a placement that renumbers the
already-correct contiguous case (would churn every granted-group snapshot key).

### `weapon-added-preserved-through-conversion`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConversionBaseOnlyScope_spec.lua` (WEAPON-sourced added PRESERVES);
`spec/System/TestFormWeaponAddedBaseOnly_spec.lua` (forms are base-only too — Reaper PRESERVES
its weapon-added; replaced the obsolete TestReaperFormConvertAllAdded_spec when the carve-out
was reverted 2026-06-14, see `weapon-added-base-only-universal`);
`spec/TestBuilds/_conv_multihop/TestConversionMultiHopConservation_spec.lua` (the weapon Fire
added stays Fire while the skill's own Fire base chains Fire->Lightning->Cold).

**Sites:** `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (base-damage loop: the weaponAdded collection is
gated on bare `noWeaponAdded` — it folds weapon flats ONLY for the ailment-finisher DROP;
every other skill, forms included, keeps weapon-sourced typed flats type-preserved in
addedPart. The convert-all carve-out was removed — see `weapon-added-base-only-universal`).

**Why:** A weapon's "+X [Type] Damage" — whether a base-type **property-0 IMPLICIT**
(e.g. Crescent Axe `+(14-28) Melee Lightning`, tags 514 = Melee|Lightning) or a rolled
**affix** — is a statList ADDED stat, applied AFTER `convertBaseDamage`, so it keeps its
type. There is no convertible "weapon base-damage range" in LE (all 194 LEB weapon bases
express damage as property-0 implicits). The earlier `conversion-base-only-scope`
implementation folded these weapon-sourced flats into the convertible base — a stale
compensation for the pre-`<see git log>` typeless-adaptive mis-typing. Once
`adaptive-added-post-conversion-typing` landed, that fold became the residual bug: it
converted ShutFackUp's axe +25 lightning implicit to cold and zeroed the in-game 8.4%
light lane (LightningHitAverage 0 -> ~208 with the fix). **Root-caused 2026-06-13**
(Decision Log "Mana Strike per-type 残差 root", 3-agent rigorous workflow + datamine:
Mana Strike `convertAllAddedDamage=False`, `convertBaseDamage` acts only on
`baseDamageStats.damage[]`).
**convertAllAddedDamage carve-out — REMOVED 2026-06-14 (see `weapon-added-base-only-universal`).**
The carve-out (forms + Avalanche / Chthonic folding weapon-added into the convertible pool) was
DISPROVEN in-game and reverted; base-only is now universal. The earlier convert-all rationale was
never in-game-validated for the weapon-added lane.
**Regression to prevent:** re-gating the weaponAdded collection on `skillHasConversion`
(re-converts base-scoped weapon-sourced added — re-introduces the original bug); treating a weapon
implicit or affix typed flat as part of the convertible BaseDamageStats. (Re-adding a convert-all
carve-out is guarded separately by `weapon-added-base-only-universal`.)

**Sites:** `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (the `convertAllAdded` skill-name table is removed;

### `nonconv-typeless-added-proportional`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestNonconvTypelessAddedProportional_spec.lua`
- multi-intrinsic-type (Avalanche phys+cold): typeless added counted ONCE, split proportionally (no double-count)
- single-intrinsic-type (Fireball): typeless rides the one type 100% — BYTE-IDENTICAL safety property
- source contract: non-conversion branch distributes by intrinsic-base ratio

**Sites:** `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (base-damage loop). `nonConvIntrinsicTotal` = sum of
non-zero `source[<T>Damage]` for non-conversion skills; `allAddedDmg = genericAdded * (sv /
nonConvIntrinsicTotal)` distributes the typeless pool by intrinsic-base ratio. Zero-total
(all-zero base) falls back to the legacy single-pool to avoid div-by-zero.

**Why:** the typeless/adaptive added pool (`genericAdded`, "+X Damage" with no element) must be
added to a hit ONCE, distributed proportionally over the non-zero base — the game's
`DamageStats.buildDamageStats` does this (`datamining:294-356`), and the conversion
path already mirrors it (`adaptive-added-post-conversion-typing`). The non-conversion branch
historically added the FULL `genericAdded` to EVERY intrinsic type (`source[damageTypeMod] and
genericAdded`), which DOUBLE/TRIPLE-counts the pool for multi-intrinsic-type skills (Avalanche
phys+cold ×2, Disintegrate fire+light ×2, Prism Shard fire+cold+light ×3). Single-intrinsic-type
skills are unaffected (the lone type's ratio is 1.0 → byte-identical). Empirically the
double-count was the dominant base contributor for Smelter's Wrath (fire+phys) Forge Guards
(<private build> TotalDPS 52124→30993, −40.5%). **✅ SHIPPED + IN-GAME VALIDATED (dev `<see git log>`):** on a
state-matched Smelter's Wrath capture (Aurora_blank `.epoch`, cm 3.98) the fix lands fire **+51%→
+3.2% MATCH** — the prior "HELD because it worsens an under" rationale was based on a STALE −61%; the
clean capture shows fire was OVER (the double-counted typeless ×eff 6.0 was the dominant inflation).
**Blast = 19 builds** (full #builds-suite-confirmed, NOT the 10 first estimated — exact-skillId grep
missed namespaced ids like `Warlock 02 Ghostflame`): 10 Smelter's Forge Guards + 6 Ghostflame
(fire+necro) Lich/Warlock/Necro + 3 Swarmblade (phys+poison) Druids; all regenerated, full suite
459335✓/0✗. **Do NOT broaden to full-base weight** — REFUTED on 4guanghuan Firebrand (would push the
typeless onto the typed-added phys lane → phys +127% over; single-type must stay intrinsic-only =
100% to its one type). The Smelter's phys-under and the Firebrand single-type fire-over are SEPARATE
shred-resistance issues, not this fix.

### `whole-attack-conversion`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestWholeAttackConversion_spec.lua`
- wholeAttackConversion skill (Hail of Arrows): its OWN skill-scoped phys->fire converts the typed ADDED physical (no phys residue)
- non-flag skill (Fireball): the same skill-scoped phys->fire leaves the typed added (base-only)
- source contract: the flag is read AND the base-derived gate excludes it (Fix #1 preserved)
- data contract: `HailOfArrows` carries `wholeAttackConversion:true` in skills.json

**Sites:** `src/Data/skills.json` (`HailOfArrows.wholeAttackConversion = true`);
`src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` — (1) `sumGlobalConv` includes the skill's OWN skill-scoped
conversion when `wholeAttack` (so `globalConversionTable` is populated and the gct consumer
converts typed added off-type); (2) the base-derived gate's `hasActiveGlobalConv` check is
skipped (`... and not activeSkill.activeEffect.grantedEffect.wholeAttackConversion`) so the
adaptive-added-base-derived-types-only gate STAYS ON for the skill.

**Why:** ability-INTRINSIC (mutator-hardcoded) conversions convert the WHOLE attack slot
(weapon base + typed added + intrinsic) via LE's `convertAllDamageOfType`, not just the
intrinsic base (`convertBaseDamage` = the STAT-granted path). Hail of Arrows' physical->fire
is set in `HailOfArrowsMutator.Mutate()` (`datamined game source`, datamining) but
LEB parses it as a SkillId-tagged skill-scoped conversion, which absent this flag converts
the intrinsic base only and leaves `addedBasePart[Physical]` type-preserved → phys over-read
(near-zero in-game pre-mit phys) + fire slightly under
(`project_amhoa_hailofarrows_fire_light_under`). The flag folds the skill's own conversion
into the whole-slot path. Verified on the AmHoA save: fire DmgBase 205.36 → 210.0, phys 4.64
→ 0, **lightning 58.5 UNCHANGED** (Fix #1 not regressed); 5/5 conversion sentinels
(Swarmblade / Volatile Zombie / Avalanche / Spellblade / Sorcerer) byte-identical; blast =
11 Hail-of-Arrows Marksman builds only. GATED on the per-ability flag: every other skill has
`wholeAttack=false` and both edited paths are byte-identical (STAT-granted conversions like
Swarmblade / Mana Strike stay base-only — no regression). NOT corpus-neutral (8 HoA builds
change) → affected snapshots regenerated.

### `conversion-opposing-cycle-conservation`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConversionOpposingCycleConservation_spec.lua`
- opposing 100% cycle on the skill's own base CONSERVES total (pre-fix: dropped to ~0)
- the cycle base lands at the LAST-applied destination (DamageTypes order)
- 3-type pure cycle also conserves
- ACYCLIC single-hop stays byte-identical (the trapped branch must NOT fire)
- LEAKY cycle (has an exit) is left to the fixpoint and still conserves
- source contract: the sequential re-resolution is gated on a trapped (ungrounded) type

**Sites:** `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (conversion fixpoint block: after the Gauss-Seidel
loop, `retainedIntrinsic[t]` defaults to `fix[t] * retention(t)`; a grounding pass marks
each type that can reach a `retention>0` sink; if base is trapped in an ungrounded type,
the intrinsic base is re-resolved by a single sequential pass of each conversion edge
`seq[to] += rate*seq[from]; seq[from] *= (1-rate)` in DamageTypes order. `convBase[t]` and
the adaptive `postBase[t]` weight both read `retainedIntrinsic[t]`).

**Why:** Two OPPOSING base conversions forming a pure (exit-less) 100% **cycle** — e.g.
Primalist Avalanche allocating BOTH `av75ch-9` "Rockfall" ( Cold Damage -> Physical Damage)
and `av75ch-20` "Frost" ( Physical Damage -> Cold Damage) (`src/TreeData/1_4/tree_0.json`,
both 100% per `ModCache.lua`) — gives every cycle member `retention(t)=conversionTable[t].mult=0`.
The fixpoint `effBase[t] = rawBase[t] + Σ_{s≠t} effBase[s]·conv[s][t]` then drives the
circulating base to divergence (iteration-capped) and the final `fix[t]*retention` multiplies
it by 0, **dropping the whole convertible base**. Confirmed by isolation on `SuXes2 lv92
Shaman.xml` (toggle `av75ch-9` only — the other av75ch nodes are inc/utility): Avalanche
body cold base **417.92 → 337.92** WITH the cycle (80 pre-eff cold lost), total NOT conserved.
The in-game node reminders make the correct answer unambiguous: *"If you have this and Frost,
Rockfall has no effect"* → the pair nets to Frost-only = all cold = 417.92. Game truth:
`DamageStatsHolder.BaseDamageStats.convertBaseDamage(from,to,proportion)` (datamining)
is `damage[to] += proportion*damage[from]; damage[from] *= (1-proportion)`, applied ONCE per
conversion stat in sequence — mass is moved, never destroyed, so the total is conserved at
every step and the base lands at the type whose inbound conversion is applied LAST (Cold
before Physical in DamageTypes → all cold). The fix replays exactly that, but ONLY when the
fixpoint trapped base. The acyclic chains (`conversion-multi-hop-conservation`) and LEAKY
cycles (an exit to a `retention>0` sink — all types grounded) never enter the branch and stay
byte-identical (the grounding gate, not an absolute `intrinsicIn-intrinsicOut` threshold,
avoids a false positive from the iteration cap's tiny un-converged residual on a leaky cycle).
**Regression to prevent:** going back to `convBase[t] = fix[t]*retention` directly (re-drops
the pure-cycle base); gating the sequential re-resolution on a loose absolute conservation
delta (false-fires on not-yet-converged leaky cycles and changes their distribution); applying
the sequential pass to ALL builds (breaks acyclic multi-hop that runs against DamageTypes order
— `conversion-multi-hop-conservation`).

### `throwing-attack-damage-inc`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestThrowingAttackDamageInc_spec.lua`
- "6% Throwing Attack Damage" live-parses residue-free as `Damage INC 6, KeywordFlag.Throwing`
- "+12%" plus-prefixed variant identical; the stale MORE bakes are gone from ModCache

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (specialModList handler) +
`src/Data/ModCache.lua` (two stale rows removed).

**Why:** the "X% Throwing Attack Damage" family (passive **Rogue-49 "Pursuit"**
per-rank stat "6% Throwing Attack Damage"; one more node carries "+12%") was
baked as `Damage MORE keywordFlags=Throwing` with parse residue `"  Attack  "`.
Two bugs in one: (1) the tree layer drops residue-carrying mods entirely (the
`conversion-extra-nil-not-empty` consumer in PassiveTree.lua), so the stat
NEVER applied; (2) even the baked semantic was wrong -- in-game it is an
additive INCREASE, not a MORE. **In-game proof (Prepfor1o1 lv44 Bladedancer,
Pursuit x5, Acid Flask first-hit on a fresh dummy):** phys 300.20 / fire 349.31
vs LEB-without 266.48 / 316.66 -- both types back-solve to Damage INC ~+30
simultaneously (phys 30.3 / fire 29.3); a MORE x1.30 reading is excluded (it
would give phys 346). This was the UNCONDITIONAL part of the Acid Flask "+25%"
residual; the remaining CONDITIONAL part (~+33 INC present only after the first
hit -- Frenzy / Dusk Shroud / vs-Poisoned composite, exact source still open)
is documented in Prepfor1o1.diff.md. **Regression to prevent:** re-baking the
family as MORE or with residue (silently un-applying Pursuit again).

### `minion-selection-determinism`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestMinionSelectionDeterminism_spec.lua`
- inline markers: both fixed sites in `Build.lua` carry the guard tag (asserted ≥2)
- real data: the ambiguous legendary in `1.2/minions.json`'s hands slot resolves to the **smallest** sibling `uniqueId`
- synthetic: winner follows the minimum `uniqueId` regardless of table insertion order
- synthetic: the single-candidate fallback and the direct-`uniqueId` path are unchanged

**Sites:** `src/Modules/Build.lua` — `buildMode:ReadLeToolsSave` / `processItemData`:
the legendary-fallback recovery loop (`if not uniqueId then for _, baseEntry in pairs(data.LETools_itemBases)`)
and the base-name scan (`for itemBaseName, itemBase in pairs(latestBases)`).

**Why:** A Legendary Potential planner item (unique fused with an exalted affix) exports an
encoded LETools id that maps to a `bases.json` entry with **no** `uniqueId`; the recovery
loop guesses the unique from other entries sharing the same `baseTypeId`+`subTypeId`. Several
uniques share one base pair (six glove uniques on base `4/5`; the `minions.json` hands slot is
one), so the guess is ambiguous. The loop used to take the **first** `pairs()` match, but
**LuaJIT seeds string hashing per-process**, so iteration order over the string-keyed
`LETools_itemBases` — and therefore the equipped unique — changed run-to-run. Measured from a
fixed worktree, 8 fresh processes: `1.2/minions.json` → 6 distinct output hashes (hands cycled
Li'raka's Claws / Falcon Fists / Maehlin's Hubris; player `Armour` 423/473/567/634, `Att` 0↔3,
`CastRate` ×1.10 as Falcon Fists' cast/attack-speed affix flickered in and out),
`1.3/throwing.json` → 3, `1.2/warpath_channel.json` → 2. The `AverageHit=0` seen on some runs
was a downstream symptom (a different equipped weapon changed which socket group won FullDPS),
NOT a minion sub-skill flap — the minion, its kit, and its `mainSkill` were identical every
run. **Fix:** track the **minimum** `uniqueId` across all matches (order-independent, and stable
even if `bases.json`'s encoded-id keys are regenerated) instead of the first `pairs()` hit; the
base-name scan likewise keeps the lexically-smallest name (that table has **no** duplicate
`baseTypeID`+`subTypeID` pairs today, so this leg is inert but locked against a future
collision). This is the same house remedy as `tree-tag-swap-determinism` and
`createMinionSkills`' sorted grant ids: replace pairs()-order dependence with a deterministic
key. **Regression to prevent:** reverting either loop to a first-`pairs()`-match / last-writer
pick, or picking `max`/lexically-largest (would re-introduce a stable-but-different flap winner
and silently change which unique ambiguous legendaries resolve to).

**Snapshot coverage:** exactly 3 local corpus builds equip an ambiguous legendary
(`1.2/minions.json`, `1.3/throwing.json`, `1.2/warpath_channel.json`). Their `spec/TestBuilds/`
snapshots are **untracked** (never `git add`-ed) and were **already stale** before this fix
(snapshot `Armour=678` is unreachable by any current pairs() order — never among the live flap
values), so the fix turns no passing build into a failing one; it makes an already-DIFF,
nondeterministic build **deterministically** DIFF. These 3 are **regen candidates for the local
corpus owner** — not mass-regenerated here. The tracked default busted suite is unaffected
(`TestBuilds`/`builds`-tagged corpus is excluded from `default`).
**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestBulwarkApocalypse_spec.lua`
- `70% increased Void Damage during Apocalypse` parses to `VoidDamage INC 70` gated on `Condition:DuringApocalypse` (no residue)
- `+70% Melee Critical Strike Multiplier during Apocalypse` parses to `CritMultiplier 70` gated on `Condition:DuringApocalypse`
- behavioral: `conditionDuringApocalypse` OFF (default) → 0 Void INC (inert); ON → +70 Void INC
- the two mods are present in `uniques_1_4.json` Bulwark; parser + config sites carry the marker

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (`["during apocalypse"]` condition → `Condition:DuringApocalypse`)
+ `src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` (`conditionDuringApocalypse` check sets the FLAG, default OFF)
+ `src/Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json` (Bulwark of the Last Abyss: the two transcribed mods + null rollIds).

**Why:** Bulwark of the Last Abyss (Ironglass Shield) self-applies the **Apocalypse** buff
(3s, every 3s while on high health, costs 25% current health). Per the item's altText
"The only effects of the Apocalypse buff are the ones listed on this item" — those effects
are **`70% increased Void Damage during Apocalypse`** and **`+70% Melee Critical Strike
Multiplier during Apocalypse`**, which live in the datamine `tooltipDescriptions`
(display-only, NOT the structured roll table — `uniques_v3.json` Bulwark `mods` carries only
Block Chance / Armour / the trigger; the damage pair is tooltipDescriptions[1..2]) and were
dropped on transcription — the **same omission class as Frozen Ire / Hammer of Lorent**. LEB
already had the base block/armour mods + the (hideInTooltip) trigger; this adds the two
missing damage mods + the `during apocalypse` condition + the config gate. **Regression to
prevent:** dropping either mod from the unique (re-opening the omission), removing the
`during apocalypse` parser entry (mods would fall to `extra` residue / apply unconditionally),
or defaulting the config ON (the buff is self-damaging/conditional — must stay OFF so corpus
builds are inert). Apocalypse is a real buff (`Ailment_Apocalypse` in skills.json) but its
only damage effects are these item mods.
