### `falcon-per-dex-added`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestFalconPerDexAdded_spec.lua`
- `modLib.parseMod("+1 Falcon Melee Damage per 4 Dexterity")` emits a `MinionModifier` LIST scoped to `minionTypes = {"RogueFalcon"}`, wrapping an inner `Damage BASE 1` mod with `keywordFlags` 512 (Melee) and a `PerStat{actor="parent", stat="Dex", div=4}` tag (reads the PLAYER's Dex, ×0.25)
- `modLib.parseMod("+1 Falcon Throwing Damage Per 4 Dex")` emits the same shape with `keywordFlags` 1024 (Throwing)
- both lines are fully consumed (extra `nil` so PassiveTree does not drop the mod)

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (2 grant rules: `^%+([%d%.]+) falcon melee damage per 4 dexterity$` / `^%+([%d%.]+) falcon throwing damage per 4 dex$`), `src/Data/ModCache.lua` (`"+1 Falcon Melee Damage per 4 Dexterity"`@1381 / `"+1 Falcon Throwing Damage Per 4 Dex"`@1382 baked to the MinionModifier form, replacing the player-side `{{...}, " Falcon "}` residue no-ops).

**Why:** The Falconry per-Dexterity nodes route added damage onto the Falcon (RogueFalcon), scaling off the PLAYER's Dexterity. datamining ground truth (`FalconryMutator`): `falconMeleeDamagePer4Dex` → `Stats.AddedStat(tag 0x200 = Melee, Dex × value × 0.25)`; `falconThrowingDamagePer4Dex` → `tag 0x400 = Throwing`. Two SEPARATE tag-specific stats (NOT a global add). Tree `src/TreeData/1_4/tree_4.json`: **L31 "+1 Falcon Melee Damage per 4 Dexterity"** (Falconer ascendancy-start node, innate to every Falconer) and **L2296 "+1 Falcon Throwing Damage Per 4 Dex"**. ModCache baked both as a player-side `Damage BASE 1 PerStat + " Falcon "` residue — the residue drops the mod at the tree gate AND the scope was the player, not the Falcon — so the Falcon got neither. Fix routes via `MinionModifier{minionTypes={"RogueFalcon"}}` with the inner PerStat reading `actor="parent"` Dex and `div=4`, keeping each add tag-specific (`KeywordFlag.Melee` 512 / `Throwing` 1024). Rem-MK3 runtime dump (Dex 263): 65.75 added on both t512 and t1024 (263 / 4). This is the dominant Falcon added-damage component; the residual (~+18 = Falconer's Mark consume buff) is DEFER — no curve-fit. **Regression to prevent:** a ModCache regen / upstream re-sync reverting either row to the player-side `" Falcon "` residue no-op (dropping the Falcon add), a global (`keywordFlags` 0) add that leaks across tags, or a `minionTypes` drop that leaks the add to every minion.

**Scope / not-yet:** added-damage routing only. (2026-07-11 update: the "+18 residual" this
guard deferred as "Falconer's-Mark consume" was later datamined to the **Tactician**
flat grant on the SAME AddedStat family — see `falcon-tactician-flat-added`, which
closes it. The Mark-consume mechanism is real but separate — "Avian Arsenal", a
Falconry skill-tree node, 0 on the blank.) Sibling landing `falcon-feather-knives-grant`
grants the throwing sub-attack the throwing add now feeds.

**Snapshot coverage:** corpus-AFFECTING — the melee per-Dex node is the Falconer ascendancy START, so every Falconer build that summons the Falcon gains Falcon added damage. Blast radius = Falconer builds (76 `*Falconer.lua` in `spec/TestBuilds/1.4/`); builds without the Falconer tree emit zero new mods (the new parse rules match only these two Falconer node strings) = byte-identical. Snapshot regen scoped to `LEB_ONLY="Falconer"` (worktree src + `LEB_ROOT`=MAIN corpus, 76 builds, all loadfile-valid). Change isolated from stale-snapshot dev drift by a pure-dev control regen (<private build>: `PhysicalDamageBase` 69 → 124.875 = +Dex/4 is the ONLY my-change delta; the poison-duration drift is identical under pure-dev).
**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `falcon-default-skill-aerial-assault`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestMinionDefaultSkillIndex_spec.lua`
- `LE_MINION_DEFAULT_SKILL_INDEX["RogueFalcon"] == 2`
- Selecting the Falcon summon (`"Falconer 00 Falconry"`) defaults the Falcon's scored sub-skill to `"RogueFalcon Diving Attack"` (index 2), not the `"RogueFalcon Melee"` placeholder (index 1)

**Sites:** `src/Data/Global.lua` (`LE_MINION_DEFAULT_SKILL_INDEX` table, 1 new entry `RogueFalcon = 2`).

**Why:** The summoned Falcon's `skillList` (`src/Data/minions.json`) = `["RogueFalcon Melee", "RogueFalcon Diving Attack"]`. Index 1 `"RogueFalcon Melee"` is a placeholder basic attack the Falcon never uses in-game; its real primary attack is **Aerial Assault** — the innate **Falcon Strikes** (datamine `extracted/ability_attribute_scaling.json` `"Falconer 01.2 Falcon Strikes Damage"`, `displayName "Aerial Assault"`, `tagsList ["Physical"]`, base 30 Physical, isHit, INNATE / no node gate). LEB models that as index 2 `"RogueFalcon Diving Attack"` (name "Surge", `skills.json`: `melee_base_physical_damage 30` / eff 1.5, the only non-placeholder Falcon attack). The unselected minion default was index 1 (`skillMinionSkill or defaultSkillIndex`, `CalcActiveSkill`), so LEB scored the placeholder Melee (~823) instead of Aerial Assault. **Ground truth**: Rem-MK3 in-game capture (`datamined game source`) logs the Falcon's damage under EXACTLY `"Aerial Assault"` (×2) + `"Feather Knives"` (×2) and **zero** `"Melee"`/`"Surge"` lines — the Falcon has no basic-melee attack in play. Same class as the `SummonedAbomination = 2` default (index 1 = Devour consume spell, index 2 = the real Melee hit). A user's explicit sub-skill selection still wins; this covers only the unselected default. **Regression to prevent:** removing the `RogueFalcon` entry (reverting the Falcon to the placeholder Melee), or a `minions.json` skillList reorder that changes which index is Diving Attack.

**Scope / not-yet:** points the Falcon at the correct primary attack (Aerial Assault) and its datamined base (30). Does NOT curve-fit the per-hit magnitude to the capture (~89.4k): the residual depends on non-datamined factors (the Aerial Assault effectiveness LEB carries on Diving Attack is not contradicted by any datamine, and the Aerial Prowess `aa989-19` stacking MORE is a runtime stack mechanic) — DEFER, no fabrication. Feeds off the melee per-Dex add (`falcon-per-dex-added`, tag 512).

**Snapshot coverage:** corpus-AFFECTING — every Falconer build that summons the Falcon and has not manually selected a Falcon sub-skill switches its scored Falcon skill from the Melee placeholder to Diving Attack. Blast radius = Falconer builds (76 `*Falconer.lua` in `spec/TestBuilds/1.4/`); non-Falcon-summoning builds are untouched (the table lookup is keyed on minion type `RogueFalcon`). Snapshot regen scoped to `LEB_ONLY="Falconer"` (76 builds, all loadfile-valid).

### `falcon-avian-hurl-conversion`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestFalconAvianHurl_spec.lua`
- `modLib.parseMod("50% Added Throwing Damage Conversion To Falcon")` emits a PLAYER-side `FalconAddedThrowingConversion BASE 50` (not a `MinionModifier` wrapper), whole line consumed (extra `nil`)
- routing (behavioral): with the conversion mod + `+40 Throwing Fire Damage`, the RogueFalcon modDB gains `FireDamage BASE 20` matching BOTH a Throwing and a Melee cfg (ANY-match `Melee|Throwing` re-tag)
- controls: no conversion mod → 0 transferred; conversion with an empty player added-throwing pool → inert; player `100% increased Throwing Damage` does NOT change the transferred flat (added-flat only)
- source contract: the CalcPerform block reads `FalconAddedThrowingConversion`, is scoped `env.minion.type == "RogueFalcon"`, keyword-gates the copied source on `KeywordFlag.Throwing`, and adds to `env.minion.modDB` only

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (1 rule `^([%d%.]+)%% added throwing damage conversion to falcon$`), `src/Modules/CalcPerform.lua` (routing block after the weapon-attack-minion inheritance), `src/Data/ModCache.lua` (`"50% Added Throwing Damage Conversion To Falcon"`@14801 rebaked from the wrong player-side `Damage MORE 50` + residue misparse to the clean `FalconAddedThrowingConversion BASE 50`).

**Why:** Avian Hurl (`Rogue-90`, RogueTree `nodeList[86]`, Falconer mastery, maxPoints 6; datamine `extracted/passives_raw.json:21546`, prefab `"Falconer Added Throwing Damage To Falcon"`) carries two stats: `+2 Throwing Damage` per point (a normal player add, already parsed) and the fixed (notScalingStats) `50% Added Throwing Damage Conversion To Falcon`. datamining ground truth: `AbilityStatsMutatorManager` bucket `0x2d7` field `falconAddedThrowingAndMeleeDamagePercentageFromPlayerThrowingDamage` — the Falcon gains added **Throwing AND Melee** damage equal to 50% of the **player's added throwing** flat. EHG's "Conversion" wording is a GRANT/transfer, NOT an LE damage-TYPE conversion (contrast `"50% Base Damage -> Lightning"`). The stat's Property is 54 = `None` (sentinel: mutator-driven, not property-driven). The old ModCache row was a generic-parser misparse (`Damage MORE 50` keywordFlags 1024 on the PLAYER + residue `"   Conversion To Falcon "`) — inert only because the tree gate drops residue lines; a naive residue cleanup would have activated a bogus player 50% MORE. Model: the tree stat parses to a player percent mod; CalcPerform copies each player flat-added throwing-keyword damage mod (`Damage` / `<Type>Damage` BASE) onto the RogueFalcon modDB at pct/100, re-tagged `Melee|Throwing` — the same PLAYER→MINION per-type copy as `weapon-attack-minion-weapon-inheritance`, because "50% of my added-throwing pool" is a per-type sum with no `PerStat` primitive. Source pool (player added throwing) is disjoint from the per-Dex nodes (player Dex) — no double count. **Regression to prevent:** a ModCache regen reverting row 14801 to the `Damage MORE 50` misparse (a residue-cleanup would then create a phantom player 50% MORE throwing), the routing block losing its RogueFalcon scope (leaking player throwing onto every minion), transferring INC/MORE (player scaling must stay behind), or dropping the Melee half of the re-tag (the datamining field grants BOTH).

**Scope / not-yet:** routing only; magnitude is NOT capture-validated (no Falcon capture exists with a non-zero player added-throwing pool — Rem-MK3 has 0, where this is exactly inert). The "added flat vs total throwing" read is INFERRED from the datamining field name (the consumer multiply-site is absent from the datamining subset); if a future capture with player added-throwing contradicts it, revisit the CalcPerform block. Cadence/eff residuals remain DEFER per the sibling Falcon guards.

**Snapshot coverage:** corpus-NEUTRAL, probe-verified — `ProbeAffectedByCap` over all 79 `*Falconer*` snapshots (worktree src + `LEB_ROOT`=MAIN, 4 shards): **0 affected / 79 checked / 0 load-errors**. No corpus build both allocates Rogue-90 and scores the Falcon with a non-zero player added-throwing pool in its top-level output; non-Falconer builds cannot match the new parse rule. No regen needed.
**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `falcon-avian-arsenal-buff`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestFalconAvianArsenal_spec.lua`
- `modLib.parseMod("10% Character Damage -> Falcon Damage")` emits a PLAYER-side `FalconAvianArsenalPercent BASE 10` (not a `MinionModifier` wrapper) carrying a `Multiplier:FalconAvianArsenalStacks` tag, whole line consumed (extra `nil`); the live rule also covers the tree-scaled `30%` string (cache miss)
- routing (behavioral): with the node % line + `+40 Bow Fire Damage` + config pool=Bow(2048) + stacks=5, the RogueFalcon modDB gains `FireDamage BASE 20` (= 40 × 10%×5 = 40×0.5) matching a Melee cfg and NOT a Throwing cfg (melee-only re-tag); stacks=3 → 12; a Throwing pool re-tags to Melee too; only the selected pool transfers; player INC of the pool stays behind
- controls (corpus-neutral): default config (pool Off, stacks 0) → 0 transferred even with the node % present; pool selected but 0 stacks → inert; stacks set but pool Off → inert
- source contract: the CalcPerform block reads `FalconAvianArsenalPercent` + `FalconAvianArsenalPoolKeyword`, is scoped `env.minion.type == "RogueFalcon"`, keyword-gates the copied source on `band(srcMod.keywordFlags, arsenalPoolKw)`, re-tags `KeywordFlag.Melee`, and adds to `env.minion.modDB` only
- config: both `falconAvianArsenalPool` (list, `defaultIndex = 1` = Off) and `falconAvianArsenalStacks` (count, `math.min(val,5)`) are `ifMult = "FalconAvianArsenalStacks"`-gated and default OFF
- ModCache: row `"10% Character Damage -> Falcon Damage"` is baked to the clean player percent mod (carries `FalconAvianArsenalPercent` + `FalconAvianArsenalStacks`), NOT the empty-list residue no-op

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (branch in `parseArrowConversion`: `srcText == "character damage" and dstText == "falcon damage"` → `FalconAvianArsenalPercent BASE N {Multiplier:FalconAvianArsenalStacks}`), `src/Modules/CalcPerform.lua` (routing block after `falcon-avian-hurl-conversion`), `src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` (two inputs after `aerial-prowess-per-stack`), `src/Data/ModCache.lua` (row @10491 rebaked from `{{},"…"}` residue-drop to the clean player mod).

**Why:** Avian Arsenal (Falconry SKILL tree `falc0-4`, `maxPoints 3`; datamine prefab `"Falconry Consume Mark For Added Damage Buff"`, `skill_trees_raw.json:32920`) carries `"10% Character Damage -> Falcon Damage"` (per-point, tree-scaled to ≤30%) + notScalingStat `"5 Max Buff stacks"`. datamining ground truth (`FalconryMutator`, `consumingFalconMarkDamageBuffPercentage`, property 5110 = 10%/pt, property 54 = 5 max stacks, 10s): on CONSUMING a Falconer's Mark (ailment `0x7d`), the consuming ability's tag selects ONE player added-damage pool — Bow(0x800) > Spell(0x100) > Throwing(0x400) > else Melee(0x200) — that pool is summed across all 7 damage types × the node %, and granted to the Falcon re-tagged MELEE (0x200), once per stack (up to 5). EHG's "Character Damage -> Falcon Damage" wording is a GRANT, NOT an LE damage-TYPE conversion; because it carries a `->`, `parseMod` routes it through `parseArrowConversion` (an arrow line never reaches `specialModList`), where neither side is a damage type so the type-conversion branch declines and the Avian Arsenal branch matches (mirrors the `apocrypha-incregen-to-armour` / `pierce-chance-to-crit-multiplier` non-type arrow pairs). The old ModCache row was the empty-list + full-line residue no-op (dropped at the tree gate); a naive residue cleanup that kept a player-side generic `Damage` mod would leak (the residue-drop trap), so the row is rebaked to the novel `FalconAvianArsenalPercent` (no generic consumer). LEB cannot know which ability the player uses to consume the mark, so the pool is a config selector; the stack count drives `Multiplier:FalconAvianArsenalStacks` (the tag the parsed % mod carries), so `Sum` yields %×stacks and the `ifMult` gate surfaces the config only for an allocating build. Model: player percent mod → CalcPerform per-type copy onto RogueFalcon at (%Sum/100), keyword-gated to the selected pool, re-tagged Melee (mirror of `falcon-avian-hurl-conversion`; a per-type pool sum has no `PerStat` primitive). Only FLAT ADDED transfers; player INC/MORE stays behind. **Regression to prevent:** a ModCache regen reverting row 10491 to the residue no-op OR to a bogus player-side generic `Damage`, the routing block losing its RogueFalcon scope (leaking player adds onto every minion), re-tagging Throwing (Avian Arsenal grants MELEE only, unlike Avian Hurl), the config inputs losing their default-OFF (breaking corpus-neutrality), or transferring INC/MORE.

**Scope / not-yet:** WIRED, awaiting a specced Mark-consume capture — magnitude is NOT capture-validated (no in-game Falcon capture has Avian Arsenal specced; every existing Falcon capture is blank/ascendancy-only). Do NOT claim MATCH. The "added flat vs total pool" read and the pool-priority ordering are datamining but the consumer multiply-site is inferred; if a specced capture contradicts, revisit the CalcPerform block. Cadence (consume timing) / buff-uptime folding remain DEFER per the sibling Falcon guards.

**Snapshot coverage:** corpus-NEUTRAL by construction — both config inputs default OFF (pool "Off" → no `FalconAvianArsenalPoolKeyword` mod; stacks 0 → `Multiplier:FalconAvianArsenalStacks` unset → `FalconAvianArsenalPercent` Sum = 10 × 0 = 0), so the CalcPerform block's gate `arsenalPct > 0 and arsenalPoolKw > 0` is false and the block is a strict no-op even for a build that allocates `falc0-4`. The only always-on data change is the ModCache row rebake to the novel `FalconAvianArsenalPercent`. Neutrality is grep-substantiated: `FalconAvianArsenalPercent` / `FalconAvianArsenalPoolKeyword` / `FalconAvianArsenalStacks` are read ONLY by that one config-gated CalcPerform block — no other consumer exists in `src/`, so the rebaked row is inert data for every build. No snapshot regen needed. (The automated `ProbeAffectedByCap` sweep is currently blocked by a missing `lfs` in the luajit probe harness; the by-construction + no-consumer proof stands independently, and the falcon spec battery is 60/0.)
**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `dragonflame-nova-proc-rate`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestDragonflameNovaProcRate_spec.lua`
- the proc line emits the grant PLUS `ChanceToTriggerOnMinionSkillUse_DragonfireNova BASE 60` and `TriggerRateCapPerSecond_DragonfireNova BASE 1`, whole line still consumed; the ModCache row carries all three mods
- config: `minionSkillUsesPerSecond` is a `float` input emitting `MinionSkillUsesPerSecond BASE <val>`; unset/0 → apply not called → the fold falls back to the summoning skill's own cast rate (`usedEnv.player.output.Speed`)
- fold (behavioral, blank build + SummonBoneGolem in Full DPS): a "Dragonflame Nova" Full DPS entry appears at rate `min(0.6 × Speed, 1)` (skillPart `proc <rate>/s`), `count = 1`, `trigger = <summon skill>`; Full DPS == Σ entries; a 10-uses/s override clamps to `proc 1/s` with dps scaling exactly rate-for-rate (per-hit unchanged); a 0.5-uses/s override yields `proc 0.3/s`; no affix → no entry; TWO Full-DPS summon groups → exactly ONE nova entry

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (the dragonflame rule now emits 3 mods), `src/Data/ModCache.lua` (row re-rebaked with chance + cap), `src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` (`minionSkillUsesPerSecond` float input), `src/Modules/Calcs.lua` (calcFullDPS: `dragonflameNovaProcFolded` once-flag + the fold block after the cadence fold).

**Why:** the standing "proc-nova rate blocker" (reference_leb_trigger_framework) is that firing RATE is state/behavioral and absent from static datamine — EXCEPT Dragonflame Edict, where BOTH factors are grounded (2026-07-10 Explore datamine): chance = affix property 98 (`PlayerProperty`) value 0.6 in `extracted/items/uniques_v3.json`; the "(1 second cooldown)" is the game's real text constant (descriptor `98,83,0,0`; sibling `98,83,0,0,0` "up to 3 times per second" = the pre-cap family). So `rate = min(0.6 × minion_skill_use_rate, 1/s)` is datamined, NOT curve-fit — the ONE nova-family proc rateable without a capture-derived constant. `minion_skill_use_rate` is the player-side unknown: default = the Full-DPS summoning skill's own cast rate (`output.Speed` — the rate the build could actually re-use its minion skill; steady-state re-summon spam; for cooldown-gated summons like Bone Golem this is the cooldown rate ~0.1/s), overridable via the config input for builds whose real press cadence differs (permanent companions). The fold lives WHERE THE PER-HIT LIVES — the minion's granted DragonfireNova sub-skill (`calcs.offence` on the minion env, same per-hit source as the cadence fold; NO player-side triggered group: neither new stat name is scanned by the CalcSetup trigger loops, so no second scoring path). Contribution = `rate × AverageDamage` as its OWN Full DPS entry: NOT multiplied by `minionCount`/`activeSkillCount` and folded at most ONCE per Full DPS pass ("the NEAREST minion casts" = one nova per use, regardless of minions out or summon groups included; folded at the FIRST Full-DPS minion carrying the grant, deterministic by socket-group order). **Regression to prevent:** a ModCache regen dropping the chance/cap mods (silently reverting to rate-0), the fold multiplying by minion count or folding once per summon group (over-count), losing the `m_min` 1/s cap, the config override losing precedence, or a rename of either stat breaking the modDB reads.

<!-- validation detail omitted: line 2153 -->

Recompute-vs-snapshot (`_detect_affected_root.lua`, worktree src vs MAIN corpus): 2/2 affected, first diff key `SkillDPS` (the new nova entry) in both. Values: `1.4/QqwprgdN lv100 Necromancer` FullDPS 32497.19 → 68637.19 (mage re-summon spam ≥1.667 uses/s → CAP-bound `proc 1/s`, nova per-hit 36,140; the Skeletal Mage entry itself byte-identical 32497.192252877); `1.4/bin/BurningMyWood lv83 Beastmaster` FullDPS 6046.57 → 7504.87 (Storm Crows summon Speed 0.275/s → uncapped `proc 0.165/s`, +1458.3; Storm Crows / Bee entries byte-identical). ### `minion-grant-replacement-in-place`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestDragonflameNovaGrant_spec.lua` (REPLACEMENT-IN-PLACE cases)
- Skeletal Mage + " Adds Pyromancers" + the nova affix → the scored main stays "Fireball" (`activeSkillList[1]`), the nova is appended after the kit
- control: the pyromancer replacement alone still yields Fireball as main (same result as before the fix)

**Sites:** `src/Modules/CalcActiveSkill.lua` (createMinionSkills: `replacementFor` map + `placedGrants`, replacing the old drop-then-append-sorted handling).

**Why:** A REPLACEMENT grant (`ExtraMinionSkill.replaces` / `socketGroup.minionSkillGrant.replaces`) must stand IN the replaced skill's base-kit position — that is the granted-summon-pipeline's stated invariant ("the granted skill becomes the minion's main / FullDPS skill"). The old code dropped the replaced base skill and appended ALL grants in one `table.sort`ed pool; correct only while the replacement was the sole grant. With an additive grant co-present (the Dragonflame Edict any-minion nova), an emptied base kit (Skeletal Mage's only base skill is replaced by the pyromancer conversion) let the alphabetically-first grant win index 1: `"DragonfireNova" < "Skeletal Mages Fire Projectile"` → the PROC became the mage's scored main and FullDPS **tripled** (QqwprgdN probe: 32497 → 99650). Now `replacementFor` maps replaced-id → grant-id, the replacement is placed in-kit (once), and only unplaced grants append (sorted; a grant whose `replaces` target is absent still appends, not lost). For every existing corpus shape (single-replacement minions: pyromancer mage, Spriggan healing totems; additive-only minions: Manifest Armor, bear, abomination) the resulting skill order is IDENTICAL to the old code — full-corpus probe confirms. **Regression to prevent:** reverting to drop-then-append-sorted (re-exposing the alphabetical main-skill hijack), or appending replacement grants instead of placing them in-kit.

**Scope / not-yet:** ordering only; no damage math touched.

**Snapshot coverage:** calc-value-NEUTRAL for all existing snapshots. Probe-isolated vs a pure-dev control over the FULL corpus: the only deterministic flags are `QqwprgdN` (the co-landed nova grant's `MinionSkillBreakdown` row) and `bin/BurningMyWood lv83 Beastmaster` — whose key-level diff is ALSO `MinionSkillBreakdown` ONLY (both lenses): the in-place placement reorders that display breakdown array for its replacement-granted minion; every calc value byte-identical. Both snapshots regen'd.
**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `hydra-arc-bow-repeat`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestHydraArcBowRepeat_spec.lua`
- "verbatim affix parses to RepeatCount BASE 1 with no residue" (whole-line
  anchored — a rename/retune of the unique fails loudly)
- "the RepeatCount is scoped to the Bow keyword" (`keywordFlags == KeywordFlag.Bow`)
- "the RepeatCount carries a Condition:UsingEvade tag"
- gating via `Sum` with a crafted cfg: 1 for Bow AND UsingEvade; 0 for Bow without
  UsingEvade (default → inert); 0 for a non-bow cfg even with UsingEvade
- "with UsingEvade OFF (default) a bow attack keeps output.Repeats = 1"
  (corpus byte-identical, blast 0, no regen)
- **HONESTY LOCK** "a RepeatCount does NOT raise TotalDPS on a cooldown-less bow
  attack" (locks the REFUTED verdict below)

**Sites:** `src/Data/ModCache.lua` (delete the stale
`{{}," to Repeat your most recent  after Evading "}` stub row so the live parser
runs), `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (specialModList rule near the recast handlers:
affix → `RepeatCount` BASE 1 with `KeywordFlag.Bow` + `Condition:UsingEvade`). No
ConfigOptions change — reuses the EXISTING `conditionUsingEvade` toggle ("Are you
Using Evade?", default OFF).

Hydra Arc (uniques_1_4.json uniqueID 441) has the verbatim mod
"100% chance to Repeat your most recent Bow Attack after Evading". Before this the
line baked to an empty ModCache row (silent no-op), so the repeat reached no
computed entity. The handler routes it to the existing RepeatCount/output.Repeats
mechanism (CalcOffence `output.Repeats = 1 + Sum("BASE", skillCfg, "RepeatCount")`),
scoped to the Bow keyword and gated on the existing `Condition:UsingEvade` ("after
Evading" is evade-uptime dependent; the evade toggle defaults OFF).

**REFUTED for the DPS-reach campaign (blast 0), VERIFIED — do NOT re-open as an
under-count.** Even with the evade condition ON, `output.Repeats` does NOT raise
sustained Full DPS for the bow attacks Hydra Arc applies to. `TotalDPS =
AverageDamage × dpsMultiplier × Speed`; `output.Repeats` enters TotalDPS ONLY via
the cooldown Speed-cap (`if output.Cooldown then output.Speed = min(Speed,
1/Cooldown × Repeats)`) and via the FINAL repeatMode `dpsMultiplier /= Repeats`
(a decrease). EVERY Last Epoch bow attack has `cooldown=None` (skills.json), so the
cap never fires and `output.Repeats` only moves the burst-DISPLAY fields
(`AverageBurstHits`/`AverageBurstDamage`), which do NOT feed TotalDPS/FullDPS (see
`flame-reave-return-wave-hits`). Probe (worktree): RepeatCount BASE 1 → Repeats
1→2 but TotalDPS 1000→1000 unchanged on Cinder Strike / Detonating Arrow /
Multishot. This is the same deeper-gap situation as `razorfall-umbral-blades-per-dex`
(the intended lever is DPS-inert without a further engine change). This rule removes
the silent residue, corrects the burst display, and installs the native mechanism;
sustained Full-DPS reach requires a future free-extra-attack-on-evade proc model

Warlock 05.2 Profane Orb, node-gated pr5fm-28), `src/Data/skills.json`
(Warlock 05.2 Profane Orb base).

**Invariant:** LEB modelled only the Profane Veil AURA ("Second Area", Necrotic 10 /
eff 0.5 / isHit 0, the parent `Warlock 05 Profane Veil`). The pr5fm-28 "Profane Orbs"
node ("6 Mana Consumption per second", " Profane Orb each second") makes the veil cast
a homing Profane Orb once per second; its explosion is a SEPARATE isHit component and
is 91% of the build's Profane Veil damage in-game. It was entirely UNMODELED (no
data.skills entry) → node28 builds under-read Profane Veil by ~10x. BASE datamined
WITHOUT fabrication (`profane_veil_prefab_damage.json` "Profane Orb Explosion"
DamageEnemyOnHit → Necrotic 40 (DAMAGE_TYPE_NAMES index 4) / addedDamageScaling 2.0 /
crit 5% / x2.0 / isHit 1 / damageTags 256 Spell / no penetration / no intrinsic
conversion). NODE-gated (requiresNode pr5fm-28) so non-Profane-Orbs Profane Veil builds
stay byte-identical. UNLIKE `avalanche-fissure-grant` this grant does NOT set
`noParentTreeBaseConversion`: the innate Necrotic converts WITH the parent tree
(pr5fm-21 "Lake of Blood" Necrotic → Physical) via the source="SkillId:Warlock 05
Profane Veil" channel — the control capture shows the orb as Physical.
**SCOPE:** per-HIT only (inherits parent includeInFullDPS, like DivineFlare/FlameWave/
ShatterTotem). The 1/sec cast CADENCE and node29 "Hex Flurry" (pr5fm-29: "+1% Orb
Frequency per 1% Cast Speed", "+15% Orb Damage per Curse") are a rate + curse-count
STATE fold DEFERRED as config-gated (the control isolates the base per-hit at curse=0;
node29 scaling cannot be separated from the frequency confound without curve-fitting —
forbidden). A node29 build FullDPS reflects the base orb per-hit (an undercount, same
per-hit-first posture as Abomination Double Strike's deferred cadence).

**Snapshot coverage:** NODE-gated grant → only corpus builds allocating pr5fm-28 gain

### `shatter-totem-count-fold`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestShatterTotemUpheavalChild_spec.lua`
- "the ShatterTotem grant declares the datamined fold-count model"
  (`shatterFoldCountBase = 2`, `shatterFoldCountNodes.th39-2 = 1`,
  `shatterFoldCountNegNodes.th39-3 = 1`).
- "fold = concurrent totem count = 6 for the grounding build" (base 2 + th39-2 x4).
- "th39-3 subtracts one totem" (→ 5); "fold falls back to base" (→ 2 with no nodes);
  "floored at 1" (unspecced / pathological → x1).
- CalcSetup + calcFullDPS guard-marker + wiring assertions.

**Sites:** `src/Data/SubSkillGrants.lua` (Upheaval → ShatterTotem fold fields),
`src/Modules/CalcSetup.lua` (derives `shatterTotemFoldCount`, carries onto the group),
`src/Modules/Calcs.lua` `calcFullDPS` (multiplies the sub-skill's slot by the fold).

**Invariant:** each Upheaval hit shatters ALL concurrent Thorn Totems, so the Shatter
Totem sub-skill's FullDPS contribution folds **× N**, where **N = the concurrent Thorn
Totem count**, DERIVED (not hardcoded to the capture's 6):
`N = shatterFoldCountBase(2) + Σ(alloc × perPoint of th39-2 "+1 Maximum Thorn Totems")
 − Σ(alloc × perPoint of th39-3 "-1 Maximum Thorn Totems")`, floored at 1. base 2 = the
datamined Summon Thorn Totem base Maximum Thorn Totems (in-game 6 with th39-2 at 4/4 →
6−4 = 2; th39-2 maxPoints 4). The count nodes live in the **th39 (Summon Thorn Totem)
tree**; `env.allocNodes` is keyed by node.id across ALL allocated trees, so the uph41-
gated grant resolves the th39 totem-count nodes cross-tree. **SCOPED** to the grant's own
socket group (`group.shatterTotemFoldCount`): `calcFullDPS` multiplies ONLY that sub-
skill's slot (rides the pack `count` like the mirage / auto-summon fold); nil → ×1 for
every other skill and every non-shatter build. Mirrors `upheaval-totem-grant` /
`totem-active-count-from-limit` (count from a data-declared limit, not a literal).

### `grant-base-conversion-scope`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestAvalancheFissureGrant_spec.lua`
- "CalcOffence strips groupSource from the conversion cfg only for flagged grants"
  (`noParentTreeBaseConversion` gate, `convCfg.groupSource = nil`, default
  `local convCfg = skillCfg` byte-identical)

**Sites:** `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (conversion-table build: `convCfg` with
groupSource stripped for `grantedEffect.noParentTreeBaseConversion` skills),
`src/Data/skills.json` (`AvalancheFissure.noParentTreeBaseConversion`).

**Invariant:** A node-granted sub-skill with its OWN intrinsic base (Avalanche's Fissure,
source="SkillId:Avalanche") must not have that base converted by the PARENT tree's
base-conversion nodes the game scopes to the parent's own ability (av75ch-20 Frost
" Physical -> Cold Damage", tooltip "Avalanche's base"). Those reach the grant ONLY via
the `cfg.groupSource == "SkillId:<parent>"` channel (ModStore L798); they convert the
parent's base, not the grant's. The fix builds the conversion table with a conversion-only
cfg whose groupSource is stripped, dropping the parent-tree (SkillId-tagged)
base-conversions while KEEPING global (untagged) gear/passive conversions that the game DOES
route onto the grant (in-game Fissure: ~70% cold + invariant ~26% physical that local Frost
would otherwise zero). Increases/added still inherit via the full skillCfg used elsewhere.
GATED on the skill flag so for every other skill `convCfg == skillCfg` and the conversion
table is byte-identical (corpus-inert). NOTE: opt-OUT per grant, not a default change —
Frost and Ice Branch (sf5rd-34, which NAMES its grants) both parse to the same generic
" Physical -> Cold Damage" with no SkillName tag, so the grant-vs-parent scope lives only in
the tooltip; only AvalancheFissure carries the flag, leaving SprigganForm's intended grant
conversion untouched.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `pure-dot-skill-modflag-dot`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConsecratedGroundGrant_spec.lua`
- "CalcActiveSkill adds ModFlag.Dot for dot && !hit && !ailment"

**Sites:** `src/Modules/CalcActiveSkill.lua` (skillModFlags build, after the Area block).

A PURE damage-over-time skill (`skillFlags.dot`, but it does NOT hit and is NOT an
ailment) deals all of its damage as a degen, so its damage cfg must carry `ModFlag.Dot`
for "increased/more Damage over Time" mods (parsed as `{ "Damage", flags = ModFlag.Dot }`)
to apply — `calcDamage()` sums INC/MORE with this single cfg (there is no separate
dotCfg). The fix is MONOTONIC: adding the flag can only ADD matches for Dot-flagged
mods (exclusively DoT-scaling), and only when the build carries such mods. Gated to
`not hit` (a hit+dot skill keeps its hit damage clean — the merged calcDamage cannot
split hit vs dot scaling) and `not ailment` (ailments compute on the
`data.damagingAilment` path with their own AilmentDamage scaling — untouched). Affects
the 13 pure-DoT skills (Maelstrom, Fire Aura, Disintegrate, Drain Life, Tornado,
Infernal Shade, Wandering Spirits, Black Hole, Arcane Ascendance, Ghostflame, Cremate,
Hail of Arrows, Consecrated Ground); zero snapshot change on the current corpus (no
test build with these skills carries a "damage over time" mod). Without it, Consecrated
Ground silently dropped the Anointed node "+100% Damage Over Time" (pa67ju-3) and every
other DoT scalar, undercounting by the build's whole DoT multiplier stack.

### `type-damage-over-time-dot-only`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConsecratedGroundGrant_spec.lua`
- "'increased fire damage over time' parses to FireDamage with ModFlag.Dot and NOT
  ModFlag.Fire"
- "generic 'increased damage over time' stays Dot-only (unchanged)"

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (the `DamageTypes` loop, "X damage over time" entry).

"X Damage over Time" (e.g. Sunwreath / Invoker's Scorching Grasp "increased Fire Damage
over Time") is scoped to its type by the `"<Type>Damage"` NAME and to DoTs by
`ModFlag.Dot` — exactly like the generic "damage over time" (`{ "Damage", flags =
ModFlag.Dot }`). The old parse ALSO added `ModFlag[damageType]` (e.g. `ModFlag.Fire = 8`),
which required the damage cfg to carry the type's ModFlag; but no skill cfg ever sets a
damage-type ModFlag (CalcActiveSkill only sets Hit/Attack/Cast/Spell/Melee/Projectile/
Area/Dot), so these mods matched NOTHING for any skill and silently dropped (every
fire-DoT build lost its "Fire Damage over Time" affixes). Dot-only keeps hits excluded
(no Dot) and other-type DoTs excluded (the FireDamage name is only summed for
fire-dealing). Monotonic on the corpus (no affected build carries such a mod).

### `elemental-dot-flag-parse`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestElementalDamageOverTimeParse_spec.lua`
- "'X% increased Elemental Damage Over Time' → Fire/Cold/Lightning INC + ModFlag.Dot,
  no residue"
- "Dot-only gating: scales a fire DoT cfg but NOT a fire hit cfg (and not void)"
- "longest-match: the shorter non-DoT 'Elemental Damage' still parses WITHOUT a Dot flag"
- "generic 'increased Damage Over Time' remains type-agnostic Dot (unchanged sibling)"

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (the `modNameList["elemental damage over time"]`
entry added right after the per-type `DamageTypes` loop).

The LE affix "X% increased Elemental Damage Over Time" (e.g. Nameless_King's
"(140-170)% increased Elemental Damage Over Time") is the ELEMENTAL AGGREGATE of the
per-type "<Type> Damage over Time" entries (`type-damage-over-time-dot-only`, above).
Before the fix ModParser had no "elemental damage over time" key, so the string matched
only the shorter `["elemental damage"]` (non-DoT elemental split) and left residue
"over time" → the INC parsed with `flags = 0` (no `ModFlag.Dot`). It therefore scaled
elemental HITS (or, on tree/affix mods where the residue triggers the PassiveTree
non-empty-extra gate, was dropped) instead of the fire/cold/lightning DoT. Empirically
this read Fire Aura's fire+cold DoT ticks ~33% low while its flat light/void non-DoT
portions matched exact (state-matched Nameless_King derivation, 2026-07-07). The fix
splits to `{"FireDamage","ColdDamage","LightningDamage", flags = ModFlag.Dot}`, mirroring
the per-type form: Dot-only keeps hits excluded and each `<Type>Damage` name is only
summed for a skill that deals that type. Longest-match already prefers this key over the
shorter "elemental damage" (same mechanism by which "fire damage over time" beats "fire
damage"). Blast: corpus builds carrying the affix are re-snapshotted; the change moves
the elemental-DoT INC off hits (if it was wrongly applying) and onto the DoT.

### `flame-reave-rhythm-consume`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestFlameReaveRhythmConsume_spec.lua`
- "parse: '...when consuming Rhythm of Fire' → Damage MORE 130 + Condition:ConsumingRhythmOfFire, no residue"
- "raw stat still drops (residue) — this is what the rewrite fixes"
- "LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE['fr11mv-3'] rewrites the consume Damage line residue-free"
- "tree node fr11mv-3: ProcessStats emits Damage MORE 130 scoped to FlameReave + consume Condition"
- "modDB gating: consume off → x1.00; on → x2.30"
- "config toggle 'conditionConsumingRhythmOfFire' exists (default OFF, ifCond-hidden)"

**Sites:** `src/Data/Global.lua` (`LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE["fr11mv-3"]`), `src/Modules/ModParser.lua`
(`modTagList["when consuming rhythm of fire"] = Condition:ConsumingRhythmOfFire`),
`src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` (`conditionConsumingRhythmOfFire` toggle).

Flame Reave "Rhythm of Fire" (fr11mv-3): using Flame Reave grants 4 stacks (cap 12); at 12
the next use CONSUMES all for +130% Damage (MORE, multiplicative, Flame-Reave-scoped). The
raw "+130% Damage when consuming 12 stacks" parses to Damage MORE 130 + residue "when
consuming 12 stacks" → PassiveTree L648 non-empty-extra gate drops the whole MORE. The
rewrite swaps the residue to "when consuming Rhythm of Fire" so the MORE survives with a
Condition tag, gated by the ConfigOptions toggle (default OFF ⇒ corpus-neutral: the 3 corpus
Flame Reave builds carrying fr11mv-3 are unchanged until the toggle is set). Node-scoped
(fr11mv-3.skillId == "FlameReave"). Consume band measured x2.50 vs normal (4guanghuan capture
20260707_140512_03); the game +130% MORE = x2.30 (the small gap is 9-hit sample noise). This
is Flame Reave's OWN Rhythm, distinct from the Bladedancer Dancing-Strikes "Rhythm" and the
Rogue Flow "Rhythm".

### `flame-reave-return-wave-hits`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestFlameReaveReturnWaveHits_spec.lua`
- "raw node stats parse to no hit-count mod (justifies the CalcPerform inject)"
- "no LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE for fr11mv-18 / fr11mv-16 (injected, not parsed)"
- "CalcPerform: Flame Caller fr11mv-18 → AdditionalSameTargetHits BASE 0.5 (return hit at 50% dmg)"
- "CalcPerform: Reflash fr11mv-16 → FlameReaveReflashActive flag, SkillId:FlameReave"
- "CalcOffence: return-waves scale dpsMultiplier; Reflash cast-rate-averaged min(1, 1/(3*Speed))"
- "Reflash cast-rate-average formula: min(1, 1/(3*castRate)) — 2 hits x 0.5 penalty, cap 1"
- "dpsMultiplier composition: base(full) + FlameCaller(0.5) + Reflash"

**Sites:** `src/Modules/CalcPerform.lua` (node-allocation flags, SkillId:FlameReave-scoped, after
the Sentinel-61 grant), `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (folds the return-hit equivalents into
`skillData.dpsMultiplier` right after the dpsMultiplier line).

Flame Reave return-waves are same-cast hits on the SAME target that ALWAYS deal **50% less
damage** (the returning-hit penalty — in-game tooltips on both Flame Caller and Reflash). So
they scale sustained single-target DPS as damage-EQUIVALENTS folded into `dpsMultiplier` (like
ProjectileCount), NOT AverageBurstHits (a burst-DISPLAY field that does not feed TotalDPS).
- **Flame Caller** (fr11mv-18, " Returns To You"): +1 UNCONDITIONAL return hit x 0.5 = +0.5
  equivalent. Default-ON when allocated.
- **Reflash** (fr11mv-16, " Expands and Returns Again" + "3 Cooldown (seconds)"): the wave
  expands+returns a SECOND time for +2 hits at 0.5 each, but on its OWN 3s cooldown (fires
  >=once/3s independent of cast rate) → +2 x 0.5 = +1.0 equivalent per firing, cast-rate-
  averaged to +min(1, 1/(3*castRate)) equivalents/cast.
Both raw stats parse to 0 hit-count mods, so the effect is injected in CalcPerform (Sentinel-61
precedent) rather than via parse — the natural phrase "Additional Same Target Hits" collides
with ModParser's "additional"/"hits" tokens. Capture (4guanghuan 20260707_140512_03): raw
hits/cast ~2.5 (250ms cast-grouping) = main + Flame Caller (1) + Reflash (2, cooldown-limited).
Blast: the 3 corpus Flame Reave builds (<private build>, <private build>, <private build>) that allocate fr11mv-18/16
gain the return-wave multiplier (re-snapshotted). ABSOLUTE magnitude is confounded (LEB models
a faster cast rate than the capture, default buff-state off) — the RATIOS are the validated part.

`{Condition}` gate (the aura then applies unconditionally, over-crediting ranged
builds whose in-game crit is two-valued = intermittent); (3) adding sp38-14 "Aura
of Retribution" (+2% Base Crit/pt) to the registry WITHOUT separate crit
validation — it has partial Storm-Bolt modeling and would double-count (documented
follow-up, deliberately excluded).

### `resource-gain-mode-chance-averaging`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestResourceGainModeChance_spec.lua`
- "'ward when hit': Min=0 / Average=amount*chance/100 / Max=amount"
- "'ward on melee hit': same mode gating into WardOnHit"
- ">100% chance: Average scales past amount, Max = amount*ceil(chance/100)"
- "'ward on kill' routes to WardOnKill (not WardOnHit), mode-gated"
- "emits gated WardOnHit mods, NOT the old silently-dropped ChanceToGainWardWhenHit"
- "config + ModParser source wiring present"

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (`chanceGainResource(out)` helper near
`nsAny` + the four `chance to gain (.+) when hit / when you are hit / on hit /
on kill` catch-alls routed through it → WardOnHit / WardOnKill; plus the
specific `(%d+) ward on melee hit` pattern) + `src/Data/ModCache.lua` (5 stale
baked entries un-baked so they live-re-parse). `resourceGainMode` config in
`ConfigOptions.lua` is unchanged (already sets Condition:AverageResourceGain /
MaxResourceGain).

**Why:** config-tab pipeline audit, Class B-2. Three coupled problems: (1) the
chance-based ward affixes ("X% Chance to Gain Y Ward when/on Hit") parsed to
`ChanceToGainWardWhenHit`+`WardGainedWhenHit` (melee) or were nsAny-dropped
("when hit"), which NOTHING consumed — silent drop; (2) the `resourceGainMode`
Min/Average/Max dropdown's conditions were read nowhere; (3) its
`ifCond="AverageResourceGain"` visibility gate never passed (config hidden).
Adopting PoB's emit-two-gated-mods pattern (PoB clone ModParser ~4489) fixes all
three at once: emit the gain into the consumed/displayed output (WardOnHit /
WardOnKill) twice, gated by Condition:AverageResourceGain (amount*chance/100) and
Condition:MaxResourceGain (amount*ceil(chance/100); ceil makes a >100% chance =
multiple certain procs), Min = neither = 0. The Average tag being emitted also
auto-fixes the visibility gate. **DISPLAY-ONLY / zero DPS-EHP impact**:
`output.WardOnHit`/`WardOnKill` are Calcs-panel display values, not consumed by
EHP or DPS. The mechanism is generic (not PoE content); only the LE affix
strings + ward/mana resources are used (no-PoE-in-LEB). The defensive "ward when
hit" folds into the same per-hit-event WardOnHit display as "on hit"/"on melee
hit" (the planner shows flat per-event ward, not trigger-rate-weighted). The
>100% Max ceil interpretation is principled but in-game-unconfirmed (matters
only for `on kill`, which is the only family with >100% chances). NOTE: the
no-amount "Chance to Gain Ward on Hit" form and the "While Channelling" /
"Shocked Enemy" conditional variants are intentionally NOT routed (fall through
to nsAny / their existing handling).

### `dot-resist-pen-mitigation`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestDotResistPenMitigation_spec.lua`
- A damaging ailment scales by `(1 - (enemyResist - penetration)/100)` for its associated damage type (Bleed=Physical, Ignite=Fire, Poison=Poison, Frostbite=Cold, Electrify=Lightning, …)
- Penetration amplifies past 100% (resist term capped at 75, penetration term uncapped) — matching the game's `(1 - resist + pen)`
- Resist term capped at `data.misc.EnemyMaxResist` (75)
- Armour has NO effect on DoT (even a Physical/Bleed ailment uses Physical RESISTANCE, never the enemy's armour-reduction)
- Unconditional (no config gate), reuses the hit loop's resist/pen helpers; mitigation = 1 when not `env.mode_effective`

**Sites:** `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` — `calcAilmentMitigation(damageType, cfg)` helper (mirrors the hit loop's `effMult` resist/pen factor via `calcResistForType` + `<type>Penetration`/`Penetration` sum, honouring `Ignore<Type>Resistance` / `CannotElePenIgnore` / `HitsInvertEleResChance`) applied in the damaging-ailment loop at both the dual-type per-component site (`baseDmg * incDamage * mitigation`) and the single-type site (`baseDmg * incDamage * moreDamage * mitigation`, using `ailmentData.associatedType`); writes `output.<Ailment>Mitigation`.

### `ailment-scoped-penetration`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestAilmentScopedPenetration_spec.lua` — tests:
- `AilmentBleedPenetration amplifies the Bleed DoT against a 0-resist enemy`
- `AilmentBleedPenetration nets against Physical resistance like normal pen`
- `AilmentBleedPenetration does NOT reach the HIT loop's penetration sum`
- `AilmentBleedPenetration does NOT change a Poison ailment`
- `AilmentPoisonPenetration amplifies only the Poison DoT`
- `AilmentPoisonPenetration does NOT change a Bleed ailment`
- `Salt the Wound (Bleed)/(Poison) parses to a CritMultToAilmentPen LIST mod`
- `Salt the Wound: NOT baked as LEB_NotSupported in ModCache (live-parses)`
- `Salt the Wound (Bleed): 45% of added crit mult 40 -> +18 AilmentBleedPenetration on the Bleed DoT`
- `Salt the Wound (Poison): 45% of added crit mult 40 -> +18 AilmentPoisonPenetration only on Poison`
- `Salt the Wound (Bleed) does NOT inject Poison penetration (ailment-scoped)`
- `no conversion / no ailment-pen mod -> Bleed DoT is identical to baseline`
- `an added crit multiplier WITHOUT the conversion does not move any ailment pen`

**Channel:** a BASE mod named `Ailment<Name>Penetration` (e.g. `AilmentBleedPenetration`, `AilmentPoisonPenetration`) adds penetration that applies ONLY to that ailment's DoT tick, on top of the generic `<type>`/global penetration. It is summed solely inside `calcAilmentMitigation(damageType, cfg, ailmentName)` (gated on the `ailmentName` param the ailment DPS loop passes) — so it can NEVER reach the hit loop (hits never call `calcAilmentMitigation`) nor another ailment (the param differs). General over any single-word ailment.

**Consumer (Salt the Wound, uniques_1_4 #187):** the unique carries two ailment-scoped conversions — `"(40-50)% of added Critical Strike Multiplier Converted to Physical Penetration with Bleed"` and `"… to Poison Penetration with Poison"`. `ModParser.lua` (un-baked from `ModCache.lua`) emits a `CritMultToAilmentPen` LIST mod `{ ailment, pct }`; `CalcOffence.lua` reads the ADDED crit multiplier (`playerExtra` = `BASE CritMultiplier`, the gear/passive bonus above the 100 skill base) and injects `pct% × addedCritMult` as an `Ailment<Name>Penetration` BASE mod (e.g. pct 45 × added 40 → 18). The pen damage type is intrinsic to the ailment, so the `<Type>` word is matched but not captured.

**Sites:** `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` — `calcAilmentMitigation` gained an `ailmentName` 3rd param (both ailment-loop call sites pass it) and sums `Ailment<Name>Penetration` into `pen`; new consumer loop after the `AilmentChanceConversion` stage emits the scoped pen mod from `CritMultToAilmentPen`. `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` — `specialModList["^([%d%.]+)%% of added critical strike multiplier converted to %a+ penetration with (%a+)$"]` (2-capture handler signature `(num, _, ailment)`, dispatch `specialMod(tonumber(cap[1]), unpack(cap))`). `src/Data/ModCache.lua` — the two `LEB_NotSupported` rows removed so the build live-parses.

**Why:** Salt the Wound's two conversions were recognition-only (`LEB_NotSupported`) — the added crit multiplier never reached the ailment DoT. Confirmed against in-game `pen_poison = 0.43`. The channel is a strict no-op without a conversion unique (the consumer loop runs zero times → `output.<Ailment>DPS` byte-identical), and is ailment-scoped so it cannot leak to hits or to other ailments. Builds on `dot-resist-pen-mitigation` (the resist−pen DoT engine). Establishing decision: Decision Log 2026-06-09.

### `ailment-pen-family-fixup`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestAilmentPenFamilyFixup_spec.lua` — tests:
- `ModParser carries the family-fixup inline guard marker`
- `'+10% Physical Penetration with Bleed' parses to ONE AilmentBleedPhysicalPenetration BASE mod, SkillName tag removed`
- `baked row '...' is rewritten` × 4 (exact ModCache strings, both `With`/`with` casings, one Ignite, one Frostbite — pre-checked against `modLib.parseModCache` to prove baked-row coverage)
- `a multi-tag family row keeps its other tags (PerStat survives the rewrite)`
- `skill scope '... with Puncture' / '... with Shadow Daggers' stays a SkillName-tagged PhysicalPenetration`
- `'+30% Cold Penetration With Staff' (Condition-tagged, no SkillName) is untouched`
- `spaced-name map: ailment-only display names map to their stripped key; real-skill collisions do not` (the 7-name map locked verbatim; `Bone Curse`/`Spirit Plague` locked nil)
- `baked row '+10% Void Penetration with Time Rot' (spaced display name) is rewritten to AilmentTimeRotVoidPenetration with residue cleared`
- `collision exception: 'with Bone Curse' / 'with Spirit Plague' stays a SkillName-tagged PhysicalPenetration (real Acolyte skill)` (synthesized lines — no baked family row exists for either, ModCache census 2026-06-11)
- `end-to-end: the spaced family line amplifies a TimeRot DoT on a normal skill (×1.10 at 0 resist)`
- `pseudo-skill channel: AilmentTimeRotVoidPenetration amplifies the Time Rot pseudo-skill's own DoT (spaced granted-effect name)`
- `AilmentBleedPhysicalPenetration amplifies the Bleed DoT against a 0-resist enemy`
- `AilmentBleedPhysicalPenetration does NOT reach the HIT loop's penetration sum`
- `AilmentBleedPhysicalPenetration does NOT change a Poison ailment`
- `parsing the same family line repeatedly returns one stable rewritten mod (no double rewrite)`
- `AilmentBleedPoisonPenetration (wrong type for Bleed) does not move Bleed's Physical mitigation`
- `tree-gate delivery: the tree_0.json node stat '+15% Physical Penetration with Bleed' parses with cleared residue (extra nil) so the PassiveTree/PassiveSpec gates pass`
- `a non-family line keeps its '  with  ' residue (tree gate behaviour preserved for others)`
- `pseudo-skill channel: AilmentIgniteFirePenetration amplifies the Ignite pseudo-skill's own DoT (×1.10 at 0 resist)` + typeless-key (`AilmentIgnitePenetration`) and wrong-ailment-key (`AilmentBleedPhysicalPenetration` on Ignite) controls

**Diagnosis (pre-fix delivery, per channel):** "+X% `<Type>` Penetration with `<Ailment>`" (gear affixes, passives, idols, tree nodes) parses/bakes as a `<Type>Penetration` BASE mod tagged `{type="SkillName", skillName="<Ailment>"}` (165 ModCache rows; with-targets include Bleed 23, Ignite 16, Frostbite 11, Electrify 6, Plague 3, Poison 2, Doom 2, Torment 1 — but ALSO real skills: Puncture 9, Staff 1, Shadow Daggers, Lethal Mirage). An earlier "whole family was inert" diagnosis was FALSE: LEB imports each damaging ailment as a separate ACTIVE skill whose granted-effect name == the ailment name (`skills.json` `Ailment_*`; `CalcActiveSkill.lua` `skillCfg.skillName = grantedEffect.name`; `ModStore.lua` case-insensitive SkillName matching), so that pseudo-skill's cfg DOES match the tag. Precisely:
- **(a) Physical rows** ("+15% Physical Penetration with Bleed"): inert on the hit loop everywhere (the hit loop's Physical branch uses the armour-reduction path and never sums pen — and stays that way, see pseudo-skill site below); live ONLY via the imported pseudo-skill's NESTED-ailment path (`calcAilmentMitigation`'s `<Type>Penetration` sum with `cfg.skillName=="Bleed"` during the Bleed pseudo-skill's run) — item sources only, per (c).
- **(b) non-Physical rows** ("+10% Fire Penetration with Ignite"): LIVE on the imported pseudo-skill channel for ITEM sources (`Item.lua` `isConnectorOnlyExtra` lets the `"  with  "` residue through): `cfg.skillName=="Ignite"` matched the tag at the hit loop's pen sum (the pseudo-skill's own DoT damage) AND inside `calcAilmentMitigation` (its nested ailments).
- **(c) tree/passive sources of ALL types**: dropped wholesale at the tree extra gates (`PassiveTree.lua:556` / `PassiveSpec.lua:1024` drop mods whose `extra` is non-empty) — they never reached modDB; first activated by the connector-residue clearing below.
- **(d)** the <private build> in-game 134.88-pt bleed-pen residual is NOT this family (that build carries zero family lines; the residual tracks a dynamic in-game added crit multiplier — quantized at 9.6 pts = 48% × 20 crit-mult — a separate axis).

**Chokepoint:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` — `fixupAilmentScopedPen(modList)` applied once per cache entry inside the returned closure, the single exit EVERY parse result flows through (ModCache-baked rows are injected directly into the same `cache` table via `Main.lua` `LoadModule("Data/ModCache", modLib.parseModCache)`, bypassing `parseSharedExpanded` — only the closure is common). A mod whose name matches `^(%a+)Penetration$` (non-empty type prefix; bare `Penetration` cannot match, `Ailment...`-prefixed names are skipped) and that carries a `SkillName` tag whose `skillName` is a `data.damagingAilment` key directly OR a spaced display name resolving through `data.damagingAilmentSpacedName` (see "Allowlist gate" below) is rewritten to `name = "Ailment"..<AilmentKey>..<Type>.."Penetration"` (always the internal, space-stripped key) with that one tag removed (all other tags preserved, array compacted). `data` is resolved lazily at call time (ModParser loads before Modules/Data); the per-entry dedupe flag (`entry.ailmentPenFixed`) is only set once the allowlist was actually available, and lives on the entry wrapper — `Main.lua` `SaveModCache` serializes only `entry[1]`/`entry[2]`, so the flag cannot leak into a regenerated `Data/ModCache.lua`, and saving rewritten mods is stable (no SkillName tag remains → structural no-op on reload).

**Tree-gate residue clearing (channel (c)):** at the same chokepoint, when the fixup actually rewrote ≥1 mod AND `entry[2]` (the line's leftover residue) is exactly the bare connector — strictly `type(entry[2])=="string" and entry[2]:lower():gsub("%s+","") == "with"` — clear `entry[2]` to nil so the `PassiveTree.lua:556` / `PassiveSpec.lua:1024` gates accept the mods. This intentionally ACTIVATES tree/passive family sources for the first time (the purpose of the fix). Narrow by construction: no rewrite → no clearing; any other residue is untouched (real skill scopes' `"  with  "` stays because those mods are never rewritten; genuinely unparsed text stays), so the tree gates keep dropping incomplete parses.

**Pseudo-skill site (channel (b) preservation):** `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` hit-loop pen sum (non-Physical branch) — when the active skill is a damaging-ailment pseudo-skill (granted-effect name is a `data.damagingAilment` key directly, or resolves through the spaced-name map below; verified the only granted effects whose names equal/strip to allowlist keys are the `Ailment_*` pseudo-skills themselves plus the two real-skill collisions the map excludes), the Sum is extended with `"Ailment"..asKey.."Penetration", "Ailment"..asKey..damageType.."Penetration"` (`asKey` = the resolved internal key, e.g. `TimeRot` for granted-effect name `"Time Rot"`), restoring the pen the SkillName tag used to deliver to the pseudo-skill's own DoT damage — routing unification, not a behaviour change. The pseudo-skill's NESTED ailments get the rewritten keys inside `calcAilmentMitigation` (the same value the old SkillName match produced there), mirroring dev's shape where the tagged mod matched BOTH sites; each damage pool is penetrated exactly once — no double-count. The Physical branch (armour path) never summed pen on dev — Physical family rows were inert on the pseudo-skill's own hit/DoT damage and STAY inert there (intentionally not extended).

**Allowlist gate:** `data.damagingAilment` membership separates ailment scopes from real skill scopes ("with Puncture", "with Shadow Daggers", "with Staff", "with Frost Claw" stay untouched). SPACED display names that don't equal the internal key (`"Time Rot"` vs `TimeRot`) normalize through `data.damagingAilmentSpacedName` (`src/Modules/Data.lua`, built after `data.skills` loads): a spaced `data.skills` display name maps to its space-stripped form IFF that form is a `data.damagingAilment` key AND no player skill owns the display name — `data.skills[id].treeId` is set only on player-usable skills, the same data-driven signal as the `skillidbylower-prefer-player` guard. The rewrite emits the STRIPPED key (`"+10% Void Penetration with Time Rot"` → `AilmentTimeRotVoidPenetration`) so `calcAilmentMitigation`'s keys (the ailment loop iterates `data.damagingAilment` keys) match. Census 2026-06-11: 9 spaced display names strip to ailment keys — 7 map (`Time Rot`, `Spreading Flames`, `Abyssal Decay`, `Acid Skin`, `Future Strike`, `Serpent Venom`, `Snake Infection`); 2 are genuine collisions with REAL Acolyte player skills and are excluded (**the documented exception**): `"Bone Curse"` (skill id `BoneCurse`, also ailment keys `BoneCurse`/`NecroticBoneCurse`) and `"Spirit Plague"` (skill id `SpiritPlague`, also ailment key `SpiritPlague`) — `"with Bone Curse"` on a pen mod legitimately means the SKILL scope and stays SkillName-tagged. Residual non-rewrites (intentional): the bare-name row `"+40% Spreading Flames Penetration"` (mod name is bare `Penetration` + `{SkillName="Spreading Flames"}`, no `<Type>` prefix) stays outside the typed-prefix gate — its `extra` is already `nil` so it keeps flowing on the pseudo-skill SkillName channel as before; and `"Abyssal Decay"` is shared by the `AbyssalDecay` AND `AbyssalDecayStacking` ailment keys (two `Ailment_*` entries with one display name) — the map resolves it to the stripped display form `AbyssalDecay` (no ModCache row exists for either).

**Type-qualified key:** the rewrite emits `Ailment<Name><Type>Penetration` (NOT the typeless `Ailment<Name>Penetration` Salt the Wound channel) so dual-type ailments stay exact: `calcAilmentMitigation(damageType, cfg, ailmentName)` in `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` sums `"Ailment"..ailmentName.."Penetration", "Ailment"..ailmentName..damageType.."Penetration"` — called once per damage type, each type receives only its own pen.

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (`fixupAilmentScopedPen` + closure application incl. connector-residue clearing before `unpack(copyTable(entry))`) + `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (`calcAilmentMitigation` Sum extended with the type-qualified key; hit-loop pen sum extended for damaging-ailment pseudo-skills — "pseudo-skill site") + `src/Modules/Data.lua` (`data.damagingAilmentSpacedName`, the spaced display-name → key map both consumers share).

**Why:** the family is large (tree nodes, affixes, idols across 8 ailments) and was mis-delivered per channel as diagnosed above. Rewriting at the parse chokepoint fixes baked AND live parses in one place, is idempotent, and reuses the proven ailment-scoped channel (`ailment-scoped-penetration` guard) instead of adding a second consumer loop; the pseudo-skill site keeps the previously-live item channel whole. Establishing decision: Decision Log 2026-06-10.

### `mana-missing-not-full-mechanics`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConfigManaMechanics_spec.lua`
- "ModParser: 'while not full mana' -> Condition:NotFullMana tag"
- "ModParser: 'per N% missing mana' -> Multiplier:MissingManaPercent tag with div=N"
- "ModParser: 'per N missing mana' (absolute) -> Multiplier:MissingMana tag with div=N"
- "behaviour: 'while not full mana' gates on Condition:NotFullMana"
- "behaviour: 'per N% missing mana' scales by Multiplier:MissingManaPercent/N"
- "behaviour: 'per N missing mana' scales by Multiplier:MissingMana/N"
- "config: playerMissingManaPercent exists ... old full/low checks gone"
- "calc: CalcPerform derives Multiplier:MissingMana from the config %"
- Also `spec/System/TestConfigHighlightPhase5PatternsAudit_spec.lua` (b2) updated.

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` (`playerMissingManaPercent` count
replaces removed `conditionFullMana`/`conditionLowMana`) +
`src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (modTagList: `per N missing mana` →
Multiplier:MissingMana, `per N% missing mana` → Multiplier:MissingManaPercent,
`while not full mana`/`not full mana` → Condition:NotFullMana) +
`src/Modules/CalcPerform.lua` (derives `Multiplier:MissingMana` =
`Mana × MissingManaPercent/100`).

**Why:** config-tab pipeline audit (2026-06-02) found `conditionFullMana` /
`conditionLowMana` set `Condition:FullMana` / `Condition:LowMana` that NOTHING
consumed, and ModParser recognised none of LE's actual mana-scaling phrasings —
so a whole family of LE affixes ("+1 Spell Damage per 5 Missing Mana", "1%
Increased Cast Speed per 2% Missing Mana", "+10% Damage While Not Full Mana",
"+1% Leech While Not Full Mana") was silently dropped. LE has NO "full mana" /
"low mana" threshold bonus — only **missing mana** (continuous) and **not full
mana** (binary) — so the full/low checks were the wrong abstraction and are
replaced by a single "Your Missing Mana %" count (mirrors
`playerMissingHealthPercent`). The static planner models current mana as FULL by
default (see `current-mana-damage-scaling` guard), so all three stay inert
(value/condition 0/false) until the user sets the config. `MissingManaPercent`
is config-driven; `MissingMana` (absolute) is derived in CalcPerform from max
mana so absolute "per N missing mana" scales. Kept node-agnostic / build-
agnostic: no effect on any build that has neither the config set nor a
missing-mana mod.

### `no-vestigial-enemy-damage-roll-range`

- "ConfigOptions.lua still loads and neighbouring Enemy Stats configs are intact"

/ `enemyCritChance` / `enemyCritDamage`, which ARE read by CalcDefence and were

### `no-vestigial-liferegen-burst-config`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConfigNoVestigialBurstRegen_spec.lua`
- "ConfigOptions.lua no longer defines the lifeRegenMode config"

### `config-highlight-autoshow`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConfigHighlightAutoShow_spec.lua`
- "carries the autoshow guard marker"
- "defines isHighlighted(varData) mirroring all three orange detections"
- "control.shown ORs `not highlighted` into the gate alongside isShowAllConfig"
- "isHighlighted is defined before control.shown uses it"
- "detectGrantedBuffs / detectMatchingPattern exist"

**Site:** `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (`isHighlighted(varData)` helper before the
control-build loop + `control.shown` ORs `not highlighted` into its gate).

**Why:** orange/highlighted (build-relevant) config options were only fully
visible after pressing "Show All Configurations" — a highlighted config whose
`ifCond`/`ifMult`/... gate failed stayed hidden, so the user had to toggle Show
All to find every orange option (user-requested 2026-06-09). `isHighlighted`
mirrors the three orange-label detections the `labelControl.label` closures use
(`detectGrantedBuffs()[suggestBuff]` / `detectMatchingPattern(suggestPattern)` /
`conditionsUsed`+`enemyConditionsUsed`+`multipliersUsed` count for
`suggestCond`/`suggestEnemyCond`/`suggestMult`) and is OR'd into `control.shown`
alongside `isShowAllConfig`, so ONLY highlighted configs bypass their gate;
non-highlighted gated configs stay hidden until Show All. **Display-only — no
calc/DPS/EHP impact.** NOTE: `isHighlighted`'s modDB-signal branch deliberately
omits the combined `if suggestCond or suggestEnemyCond or suggestMult` guard
(the `tally` returns 0 for nil keys) so it does not duplicate the exact anchor
string `config-highlight-moddb`'s `TestConfigHighlightModDBSignal` greps for.

### `recast-parse`

(2026-06-01) Corpus-wide parse gap found from the melee-weapon-base-damage
SS-tree-node investigation. LE skill specialization-tree recast nodes expose
their recast purely as English `stats` strings — Shatter Strike "Whiteout"
(`1 Recasts`), Iceblink (`+6% Chance for Two Recasts with Two Handed Weapon`),
Chaos Bolts (`10% Chance to recast`). ModParser had **no** recast rule, so each
form fell through the generic chain to an empty mod list and got baked into
`ModCache.lua` as `{{}, "...residue..."}`. The recast therefore never reached
the existing RepeatCount mechanism (`CalcOffence.lua:783`
`output.Repeats = 1 + Sum("BASE", skillCfg, "RepeatCount")`), so `output.Repeats`
stayed `1`.

Fix: `specialModList` handlers route the clean "repeat the whole cast" forms to
a `RepeatCount` BASE mod (`src/Modules/ModParser.lua`):
- `^(%d+) recasts?$` → RepeatCount N (PassiveTree per-point scaling multiplies
  the leading number, so `1 Recasts`→`2 Recasts` at 2 points).
- `^%+?(%d+)%% chance for (%a+) recasts? with (%a+) handed weapon$` →
  RepeatCount = N% × count, gated on `UsingOneHandedWeapon`/`UsingTwoHandedWeapon`.
- `^%+?(%d+)%% chance for (%a+) recasts?$` → RepeatCount = N% × count.
- `^%+?(%d+)%% chance to recast$` → RepeatCount = N%.
Tree-node mods are SkillId-scoped by `PassiveTree.lua` (it appends a `{SkillId}`
tag), so the repeat applies only to the owning skill. The three cached forms in
`ModCache.lua` were patched in lock-step (the parser is the source of truth;
ModCache short-circuits it on hit).

Semantics: RepeatCount is a **cast-rate / hit-rate** effect (`output.Repeats`),
NOT a per-hit magnitude multiplier — per-hit damage is unchanged.

<!-- validation detail omitted: line 3851 -->

**Scope boundary:** divergent-semantics recast strings are deliberately NOT
routed (different mechanic, would need per-skill modelling): on-kill auto-recast
(Rip Blood ` Automatically Recasts On Kill`), spread-on-recast combo (Spirit
Plague ` Spread On Recast`), per-resource recast chance (Divine Flare
`Recast Chance per Symbol Consumed`), skill-named `<Skill> Recast Chance`
expire/cast re-triggers (Black Hole, Thorn Shield).

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestRecastParseGap_spec.lua` (parseMod direct on cached +
uncached forms; scope-boundary no-RepeatCount guards; end-to-end RepeatCount →
output.Repeats=2 and weapon-condition gating).

### `config-visibility-gating`

E batch 1 (2026-06-01). The Config tab showed every "while you have <buff>"
/ "per <stack>" state config on every build (no `ifX` visibility predicate),
cluttering the tab with class-irrelevant options. This gates a verified-safe
batch with `ifCond`/`ifMult` = the SAME Condition/Multiplier their `apply`
sets, so each shows only when the build has a modifier referencing that
state (`mainEnv.conditionsUsed[key]` / `multipliersUsed[key]` non-empty).
(The class-FORM configs — Werebear/Spriggan/Swarmblade/Reaper — were already
gated; this batch adds the buff/stack ones.)

Gated this batch (10): conditionTransformed→Transformed, conditionHaveWard→
HaveWard, conditionHaveLightningAegis→HaveLightningAegis,
conditionOnConsecratedGround→OnConsecratedGround, conditionHaveCompanion→
HaveCompanion, multiplierCompanion→Companion (ifMult), conditionFrenzy→
Frenzy, conditionHaste→Haste, conditionConcentration→Concentration,
multiplierArcaneShieldStack→ArcaneShieldStack (ifMult).

**Correct-by-construction**: the config is shown iff a parsed mod references
the state, which is exactly when toggling it matters; if no such mod exists
the toggle is inert, so hiding is right. An enabled (non-default) config
still shows (the shown-closure keeps value-set configs visible) and "Show
All Configurations" reveals everything — nothing becomes unreachable.

**THE TRAP (locked by the spec):** a gate key the mod parser never emits
would make the config PERMANENTLY hidden (`conditionsUsed[key]` always
empty). The spec asserts every gate key appears as `var = "<key>"` in
ModParser. This is why these are deliberately NOT gated: `conditionHaveFlameWard`
/ `conditionHaveEterrasBlessing` and the four `*Overload` configs set a
Condition only their own apply produces (mods use the generic
`HaveAilmentOverload` / `Multiplier:ActiveOverload`, never the per-ailment
Condition — verified `var = "HaveFlameWard"` etc. give 0 hits in ModParser);
and base-calc configs (Full/Low Life, Full/Low Mana, High Health) affect
EHP/resource even without a conditional mod, so gating would over-hide.
Remaining gateless build-specific configs are gated incrementally as each
key is verified.

E batch 2 (2026-07-06). Extends the same mechanism to mastery-stack and
enemy-ailment state configs, adding the enemy side (`ifEnemyCond`/
`ifEnemyMult` keyed to `enemyConditionsUsed`/`enemyMultipliersUsed`).

Gated this batch (7): multiplierDuskShroudStacks→DuskShroudStacks (ifMult),
multiplierActiveSymbols→ActiveSymbol (ifMult), conditionEnemyChilled→Chilled
(ifEnemyCond), conditionEnemyShocked→Shocked (ifEnemyCond),
multiplierEnemyBleedStacks→BleedStack (ifEnemyMult), multiplierEnemyIgniteStacks
→IgniteStack (ifEnemyMult), multiplierEnemyShockStacks→ShockStack (ifEnemyMult).
Each key was grep-proven to be emitted by ModParser (`per stack of dusk shroud`,
`per symbol`/`from symbols of hope`, `against/to/from chilled|shocked enemies`,
`per bleed|ignite|shock stack`).

SKIPPED this batch (4, documented in the spec): multiplierVoidEssenceStacks,
multiplierContemptStacks, multiplierMoltenInfusionStacks,
multiplierStormInfusionStacks. These apply their per-stack effect as DIRECT
stat mods (Armour/Damage MORE, flat added damage, resists) with **no**
Multiplier/Condition tag var — there is no per-stack key any parsed mod
references, so there is nothing to gate on; inventing one would be the
permanent-hide trap. Maelstrom / Runes (Gon/Heo/Rah) / Firebrand / Ambition /
Dread Shade etc. were already gated by prior per-stack work.

Change is **calc-neutral** — visibility only (`ifX` predicates), no `apply`
math touched; corpus output is byte-identical.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConfigVisibilityGating_spec.lua` (6 assertions:
guard marker; each gated config declares the expected ifCond/ifMult/
ifEnemyCond/ifEnemyMult; gate key matches the apply's Condition/Multiplier;
anti-unreachable — every key ModParser-emitted; unreachable-risk configs
(FlameWard / EterrasBlessing / *Overload) stay gateless; batch-2 stat-only
stack configs stay gateless).
**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `config-highlight-moddb-signal`

D (2026-05-30) of the Config-highlight family. Adds a **modDB-driven**
highlight signal alongside the text-based `suggestBuff` / `suggestPattern`.
A config may declare `suggestCond` / `suggestEnemyCond` / `suggestMult` —
the parsed-modDB relevance key(s). The orange highlight fires (persistent,
Phase 7 style) when the build's modifiers MECHANICALLY reference that
condition / multiplier, read from `mainEnv.conditionsUsed` /
`enemyConditionsUsed` / `multipliersUsed` (the same precise signal PoB uses
for config visibility, built in `Calcs.lua`). This complements the text
signals (union: text OR modDB) and avoids substring false positives.

Why this matters: the text signals (suggestBuff/suggestPattern) scan raw
build text and can false-positive on flavour wording or miss conditions
whose mods don't literally contain the buff word. The modDB signal is exact
— a mod was actually parsed that scales with the condition.

Privacy: the tooltip reports only the COUNT of contributing modifiers
(`"Your build has N modifier(s) that scale with this state."`), NOT
`mod.source` (a raw internal string LEB only surfaces under `devModeAlt`).
So this path cannot leak internal info (cf. `config-tooltip-no-internal-info`).

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| modDB highlight block | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (after the suggestPattern block) | `if varData.suggestCond or suggestEnemyCond or suggestMult` → `countModDBUses()` tallies `#conditionsUsed[k]` / `#enemyConditionsUsed[k]` / `#multipliersUsed[k]`; label orange when count > 0; tooltip reports the count + CTA-when-off. |
| initial keys | `src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` | `conditionCursed` → `suggestCond="Cursed"`; `conditionEnemyCursed` → `suggestEnemyCond="Cursed"`; `conditionHaste` → `suggestCond="Haste"`; `conditionFrenzy` → `suggestCond="Frenzy"`. |

Anti-fabrication: a declared key must be a real mod-tag var (the namespace
ModParser emits) or `conditionsUsed[key]` is always empty and the highlight
never fires. The spec verifies the initial keys (Cursed / Haste / Frenzy)
appear as `var = "<key>"` in ModParser. Add more `suggestCond`/`suggestMult`
keys incrementally during in-game verification (like the Phase 5 patterns).

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConfigHighlightModDBSignal_spec.lua` (7 assertions:
guard marker; block reads the three modDB tables via `countModDBUses`;
tooltip is count-based with no `mod.source`/`formatMod`; label uses a bare
`countModDBUses() > 0` check; initial configs declare the verified keys;
anti-fabrication key check vs ModParser; live `mainEnv` shape behavioral).
**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `config-tooltip-no-internal-info`

2026-05-30 (user-reported). Config `tooltip` strings are user-facing and must
not leak internal developer info. The Eterra's Blessing config tooltip showed
`e.g. eb5656-2 'Safeguard'` (an internal tree-node id) and
`See REGRESSION_GUARDS.md 'eterras-blessing-buff-gating'` (a dev-doc
reference); the Dread Shade tooltip leaked `DreadShadeMutator.DelayedCastOnMinion`
(an internal code symbol) + another REGRESSION_GUARDS.md reference; the
curse-count tooltip leaked `Condition:Cursed` (raw mod-tag syntax). All were
rewritten in plain in-game language while keeping real node/skill display
names (`'Safeguard'`, `Martyrdom`).

Site: `src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` (inline marker above `local options`).
The fix is "scrub + don't reintroduce" — the spec scans every `tooltip = "..."`
string and fails on any of: a REGRESSION_GUARDS reference, an internal code
symbol (`Mutator` / `DelayedCast`), raw mod-tag syntax (`Condition:X` /
`Multiplier:X`), or an internal tree/node id (`%a%a[%l%d]*%-%d`, e.g.
`eb5656-2` / `ch0fs-20`; roll ranges like `(15-40)` and hyphenated words like
`Off-hand` / `4-second` are excluded by the pattern). It also asserts the
cleaned tooltips keep their real in-game example names.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConfigTooltipNoInternalInfo_spec.lua` (3 assertions).
**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `main-skill-dropdown-hide-ailments`

2026-05-30 (user-reported). The "Main Skill" selector dropdown listed
auto-granted ailment / debuff sub-skills (`Bleed (from Puncture)`,
`Shred Armour (from Puncture)`, `Critical Vulnerability (from X)`,
`Blind / Chill / Slow / Frailty (from X)`, ...) — clutter that isn't a
castable main skill.

These are trigger-granted socket groups created in CalcSetup
(`group.triggeredOnHit` set, label `"<skill> (from <source>)"`). They are
distinguished from real damage triggers by `data.skills[id].baseFlags.ailment`.
`buildMode:RefreshSkillSelectControls` (`src/Modules/Build.lua`) now skips a
socket group from the dropdown list when it is BOTH trigger-granted
(`triggeredOnHit`) AND an ailment — so manually-equipped skills (no
triggeredOnHit) and triggered *damage* skills (no ailment flag) are never
hidden. Hidden groups still contribute to Full DPS; only the selector row is
suppressed.

Coupled change: because filtering shrinks the dropdown list, `CalcsTab`'s
"Active Skill" onChange was switched from the positional
`tableKeys(socketGroupList)[index]` to the selected list item's `value.val`
(the socketGroupList key set by `RefreshSkillSelectControls`), so the
index→skill_number mapping stays correct regardless of filtering. (The
main-view sidebar selector in Build.lua already used `value.val`.)

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestMainSkillDropdownHideAilments_spec.lua` (4 assertions:
game-data anchor that the reported skills carry `baseFlags.ailment`; filter
logic gates on `triggeredOnHit` + `baseFlags.ailment`; CalcsTab uses
`value.val`; behavioral — an injected trigger-granted ailment group is
excluded from the rebuilt dropdown list).
**Establishing commit:** <see git log>


### `affix-kind-roundtrip`

Sealed / corrupted / primordial affixes are routed into separate display
buckets via an `affix.kind` field. The tag must survive
`Import → BuildRaw → ParseRaw → Craft`. If any leg drops the tag, sealed
Legendary Affixes (purple in LETools) re-appear above unique inherent mods
instead of below them.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| import (UNIQUE/LEGENDARY branch)   | `src/Classes/ImportTab.lua` (~line 1310) | Forwards `affix.kind` from `ConvertLEToolsItem.pushAffix` into `item.prefixes/suffixes` entry |
| import (Magic/Rare/Exalted branch) | `src/Classes/ImportTab.lua` (~line 1380) | Same, in the non-unique branch |
| serialize (BuildRaw)               | `src/Classes/Item.lua` (~line 990)       | Emits `Prefix: {kind:sealed}{range:...}<id>` ahead of the range tag |
| deserialize (ParseRaw)             | `src/Classes/Item.lua` (~line 444)       | Strips `{kind:...}` before `{range:...}` and forwards onto entry.kind |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestItemParse_spec.lua`
- "Affix kind tag round-trips through BuildRaw/ParseRaw"
