### `skill-base-damage-conversion`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestSkillBaseDamageConversion_spec.lua`
- "live-parse '<n>% of <Skill> Base Damage converted to <Type>' emits skill-scoped conversion (nil extra)"
- "non-skill source falls back to recognition-only (LEB_NotSupported)"
- "Vial of Volatile Ice cached string resolves to functional Acid Flask->Cold conversion"
- "conversion is scoped: a different skill does not see Acid Flask's conversion"
- "Liath's: '50% of Fireball Base Damage converted to Lightning' live-parses to Fireball-scoped 50% conversion"
- "Liath's: NOT baked as LEB_NotSupported in ModCache (live-parses)"
- "Liath's: the 50% Fireball->Lightning conversion is skill-scoped (no global leak)"
- "Yulia: '100% of Maelstrom base damage converted to Necrotic' live-parses to Maelstrom-scoped conversion"
- "Yulia: NOT baked as LEB_NotSupported in ModCache (guards against a future empty re-bake)"
- "Yulia: the Maelstrom->Necrotic conversion is skill-scoped (no global leak)"

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (`skillBaseDamageConversionHandler`, the
handler bound to `^%+?([%d%.]+)%% of (.+) base damage converted to (.+)$` —
previously `nsAny`) + `src/Data/ModCache.lua` (removed the stale `notSupported`
rows for `"100% of Acid Flask Base Damage converted to Cold"` (Vial of Volatile
Ice #331) and `"50% of Fireball Base Damage Converted to Lightning"` (Liath's
Machinations #276) so both live-parse).

**Why:** the phrasing `X% of <Skill> Base Damage converted to <Type>` is the
prose twin of `skill-name-arrow-conversion`'s `<Skill> -> <Type>` arrow form —
both must emit a SKILL-SCOPED `<srcType>DamageConvertTo<dst>` BASE % for every
non-`dst` damage type, feeding the SAME CalcOffence `conversionTable` consumer
(globalConv path, `mult = 1 - converted` removes the source — no double-count).
Before this guard the handler was `nsAny`, so the conversion was recognised but
dropped (`LEB_NotSupported`). Ground truth: Vial of Volatile Ice
(uniques_1_4.json #331) "100% of Acid Flask Base Damage converted to Cold" — the
in-game tooltip (2026-05-30 user SS) and datamine `tooltipDescriptions` both
carry it; Acid Flask's base (physical/poison) hit must become Cold. A non-skill
source (global "base damage", no skill name) still returns `nsAny` — unchanged
for every other build. **Scope note:** the parser fix is general (Fury
Leap/Meteor/Mana Strike/Shield Throw/Volcanic Orb/Wandering Spirits/Shurikens/
Fireball/Maelstrom/Hungering Souls all use this form), but their ModCache rows
stay baked as `notSupported` until removed/regenerated; only Acid Flask's and
Fireball's (Liath's Machinations) rows were removed here. **Liath's is a PARTIAL
(50%) conversion**: the `50` value flows verbatim into `conversionTable`, setting
`mult = 1 - 0.5`, so half of Fireball's Fire base stays Fire and half becomes
Lightning (probe: baseline Fireball FireHitAvg 25 / LightningHitAvg 0; with the
conversion + a discriminating +100% inc Lightning, FireHitAvg 12.5 /
LightningHitAvg 25; a sibling fire skill (Meteor) stays 100% Fire — no leak). No
corpus build equips any of these affixes (grep of `spec/TestBuilds` for `base
damage converted to` = 0 hits; no save equips Liath's Machinations or Vial), so
zero snapshot impact. The companion chance→chance conversion engine (Apex of Thought
glyph-gated ailment-chance→resist-shred-chance, and Vial's own
"Poison Chance from all sources is converted to Frostbite Chance for Acid Flask")
is now landed under `chance-chance-conversion` (see below).

**Establishing observation:** `modLib.parseMod("77% of Acid Flask Base Damage
converted to Fire")` (non-cached, live parser) 1 mod `LEB_NotSupported` → 6
SkillName-scoped `*DamageConvertToFire` BASE 77; cached unique string resolves to
6 `*DamageConvertToCold` BASE 100 scoped to Acid Flask.

**Yulia's Path follow-up (2026-07-14, no code change):** a suspected model gap on
Yulia's Path (Heoborean Boots, uniques.json #218) "100% of Maelstrom base damage
converted to Necrotic" was investigated and found ALREADY MODELED — the exact
string is *absent* from `ModCache.lua` (grep-confirmed), so parseMod's cache-miss
path live-parses it through `skillBaseDamageConversionHandler` to 6 Maelstrom-scoped
`*DamageConvertToNecrotic` BASE 100 (`ColdDamageConvertToNecrotic` is the one that
fires — Maelstrom base is Cold, `skills.json spell_base_cold_damage 8`). No
ModParser/ModCache edit was made; the three `Yulia:` spec cases above were added
purely to lock this state against a future ModCache regen silently re-baking the
string as an empty `notSupported` row. No corpus build uses Maelstrom as a
Yulia-scaled damage skill (<private build> equips Yulia but runs Maelstrom as a buff,
`includeInFullDPS="false"`), so regen is NOT required and snapshot impact is zero.

### `stormhide-empowered-swipe`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestStormhideEmpoweredSwipe_spec.lua`
- "conversion parses to Swipe-scoped + EmpoweredSwipe-gated base->Lightning (nil extra)"
- "added damage parses to Swipe-scoped + EmpoweredSwipe-gated Melee LightningDamage (nil extra)"
- "generic skill conversion (Acid Flask) stays UNGATED (no Condition tag)"
- "no stale Stormhide ModCache rows short-circuit the parser"
- "Condition gates the conversion: OFF -> filtered (no-op), ON -> active"
- "conversion is Swipe-scoped: another skill never sees it even with the condition on"
- "defines conditionEmpoweredSwipe bound to Condition:EmpoweredSwipe, Combat-scoped"
- "conditionEmpoweredSwipe is default OFF (no default attribute key set)"
- "carries the inline regression-guard markers (parse + config sites)"

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (`empoweredSwipeConversionHandler` bound to
`^%+?([%d%.]+)%% of (.+) base damage converted to (.+) %(empowered swipe%)$`, plus
the `+N melee lightning damage with swipe %(empowered swipe%)` handler — both
inline-tagged `@leb-regression-guard:stormhide-empowered-swipe (parse site)`) +
`src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` (`conditionEmpoweredSwipe` check toggle, after
`conditionStoppedMoving`, inline-tagged `... (config site)`) +
`src/Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json` (#202 Stormhide Paws — the two empowered-Swipe
mod strings restructured to the parseable `(Empowered Swipe)`-suffixed forms) +
`src/Data/ModCache.lua` (the two stale rows for the old `(3 second cooldown)`
strings removed so the new strings live-parse).

**Why:** Stormhide Paws (uniques_1_4.json #202) carries an INTERMITTENT
empowered-Swipe effect. In-game tooltip == datamine `tooltipDescriptions` (single
combined stat, 2026-06-01): "Every 3 seconds your next Swipe has 100% of its base
damage converted to Lightning and deals +(30-45) Melee Lightning Damage". The
effect only fires on the empowered (every-3s) Swipe cast, NOT on every Swipe, so
it MUST be gated behind `conditionEmpoweredSwipe` (Condition:EmpoweredSwipe,
default OFF) — otherwise the conversion + bonus over-count on every Swipe and
inflate the baseline. Before this guard: the conversion string parsed to
`LEB_NotSupported` (its "base damage" had no skill-name token for the generic
handler) and the added-damage parsed Swipe-scoped but UNGATED and with dirty
`extra` residue. The dedicated handlers reuse the SAME CalcOffence consumer
(conversionTable / globalConv, `mult = 1 - converted`, no double-count) plus a
`Condition:EmpoweredSwipe` tag. The generic always-on
`skillBaseDamageConversionHandler` (Acid Flask / Shuriken) is UNTOUCHED — only the
`(empowered swipe)`-suffixed form gets the gate. No corpus build equips Stormhide
Paws (0 hits), so zero snapshot impact.

**Establishing observation (synthetic minimal Swipe build,
`spec/tools/probe_stormhide_dps.lua`):** Stormhide config OFF → FullDPS 4.2768,
Swipe-cfg Phys→Light 0, addedLight 0 (== no-Stormhide baseline, byte-identical);
config ON → FullDPS 85.536, Phys→Light 100, addedLight 38. Conversion-only ON
keeps FullDPS 4.2768 (reallocates element, this minimal build has ~0 Swipe base);
added-only ON drives the jump to 85.536. No-Stormhide OFF == No-Stormhide ON
(the config flag with nothing to gate is a no-op).

### `icicle-cold-to-lightning-conversion-toggle`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestIcicleColdToLightning_spec.lua`
- "defines conditionIcicleConvertedToLightning bound to Condition:IcicleConvertedToLightning, Combat-scoped"
- "conditionIcicleConvertedToLightning is default OFF (no default-state attribute)"
- "carries the inline regression-guard markers (config + conversion site)"
- "tooltip is user-facing only (leaks no internal code symbol)"
- "suggestBuff pairs with a buffDetectPatterns row so the highlight is not dead"
- "conversion mod gates correctly: OFF -> 0, ON -> 100, Icicle-scoped (no leak)"
- "(i) default OFF: Icicle hit is Cold, Lightning portion is 0"
- "(ii) toggle ON: base Cold becomes 0, base Lightning = former Cold (hit re-tagged Lightning)"

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` — the `conditionIcicleConvertedToLightning`
check toggle (after `conditionEmpoweredSwipe`), inline-tagged
`@leb-regression-guard:icicle-cold-to-lightning-conversion-toggle (config + conversion site)`
on the comment block and `... (conversion site)` on the `ColdDamageConvertToLightning`
emit. The toggle's `apply()` (run by ConfigTab ONLY for a checked box) emits both the
`Condition:IcicleConvertedToLightning` FLAG (Combat-scoped) and an Icicle-scoped +
Condition-gated `ColdDamageConvertToLightning` BASE 100 consumed by the existing
CalcOffence `conversionTable` channel (globalConv, `mult = 1 - converted`). Plus
`src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` — a `{ name = "HeorotUniqueBowIcicle", pat = "icicle" }` row
in `buffDetectPatterns` (inline-tagged `... (highlight row)`) so the `suggestBuff` highlight
is not structurally dead: Reign of Winter's "...Chance to cast Icicle on Bow Hit" affix
fires it via the Pass-3 equipped-item scan (mirrors the HolyAura `suggestBuff` pairing).
The tooltip is plain user-facing language (no `Mutator`datamining symbols, per
`config-tooltip-no-internal-info`). No skills.json / ModParser / ModCache change — the
conversion is mutator-intrinsic, not a unique stat string.

**Why:** Icicle (skills.json `HeorotUniqueBowIcicle`, granted by the unique "Reign of
Winter" #159 "(23-28)% Chance to cast Icicle on Bow Hit") is pure Cold by default
(`spell_base_cold_damage:100`, no lightning base, no skill tree). `IcicleMutator.Mutate`
(datamined game source, `datamined game source`) performs a 100%
Cold→Lightning BASE-damage conversion —
`DamageStatsHolder.convertBaseDamage(holder, from=2 COLD, to=3 LIGHTNING, proportion=DAT_183d71c08, 0)`
— then re-tags the hit Lightning (field `0xd1 := 3`). DamageType enum 2=COLD / 3=LIGHTNING
is confirmed in `src/Data game_enums.json`. The proportion `DAT_183d71c08` is the GENERIC
1.0f shared across the binary (the universal "+1" base in `Ability.c`; the same const drives
the `(field + DAT_183d71c08) * x` increase→multiplier lines at `datamined game source`, and
is independently asserted = 1.0 in `ChaosBoltsDamage.fixspec`) — so the rate is 100%, NOT an
Icicle-specific magnitude (no fabricated number). The in-mutator conversion is gated on a bool
spec field (`param_1+0x118`, read at `getTags():23` + `Mutate():157`); Icicle has NO skill tree
so no game-data node/affix can write it — the conversion is normally inert, which is why this is
a DEFAULT-OFF toggle (corpus byte-identical; matches current dev's pure-Cold Icicle) rather than
always-on. Mirrors `conditionHolyAuraDamageAura` (a config-gated intrinsic absent from
skills.json/tree).

**Establishing observation (`SelSkill(1, "HeorotUniqueBowIcicle")` on a bare build):**
toggle OFF → `ColdHitAverage` > 0, `LightningHitAverage` == 0 (pure Cold baseline); toggle ON →
`ColdHitAverage` == 0, `LightningHitAverage` == the former `ColdHitAverage` (100% Cold→Lightning,
no type-specific scaling on a bare build). modDB-level: `ColdDamageConvertToLightning` BASE 100
tagged `SkillName=Icicle` + `Condition:IcicleConvertedToLightning` sums to 0 with the condition
off, 100 with it on, and 0 for a non-Icicle skill (Meteor) even with the condition on.

### `grounding-totem-condition`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestGroundingTotemCondition_spec.lua`
- "parses '+15% Hit Damage While Totem Active' to a MORE Hit Damage mod tagged HaveTotem (nil extra)"
- "Condition gates the MORE: no totem -> 0 (no contribution), totem active -> 15"
- "the unconditional '+15% Hit Damage' still parses ungated (no Condition tag)"
- "the ModCache row carries the HaveTotem tag and no leftover residue"
- "game-file: av75ch-12 Grounding still carries the audited stat (1.4 tree)"
- "carries the inline regression-guard marker in ModParser.lua"

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (`modTagList["while totem active"] =
{ tag = { type = "Condition", var = "HaveTotem" } }`, inline-tagged
`@leb-regression-guard:grounding-totem-condition`) + `src/Data/ModCache.lua`
(the baked `"+15% Hit Damage While Totem Active"` row rewritten from a dropped
mod + `"   While Totem Active "` residue to a `Condition:HaveTotem`-tagged MORE
15 with `nil` residue — byte-identical to a `SaveModCache` regen of the same
line).

**Why:** The Avalanche specialization node av75ch-12 "Grounding" carries the
stat `"+15% Hit Damage While Totem Active"` (maxPoints 3 → +45% at 3/3). Its
in-game description is "Avalanche hits deal more damage (multiplicative with
other modifiers) while you have at least one active totem" → MORE, NOT
increased. (The datamine field `AvalancheSnowballMutator.increasedDamageWithATotem`
is only the engine variable name; the SuXes 2026-05-29 per-hit ladder measured a
clean totem factor of ×1.4521 ≈ 3pt×15% MORE, which an `increased` could never
net — it would be diluted by the build's increased pool.) The `"+15% Hit Damage"`
half already parses to `{Damage, MORE, 15, ModFlag.Hit}` (every `"+N% Hit Damage"`
node bakes this), but before this guard the trailing `" While Totem Active"`
survived as parser residue, so the ModCache row carried a non-empty `extra` and
`PassiveTree.lua:ProcessStats` (`if mod.list and (not mod.extra or extra=="")`)
silently DROPPED the whole MORE mod. SuXes (lv92 Shaman, Avalanche + totem)
thereby lost the entire Grounding ×1.45. The fix adds the standard `modTagList`
"while X" → Condition suffix entry, routing through the pre-existing
`Condition:HaveTotem` (config `conditionHaveTotem` / `CalcPerform.lua` auto-set
for totem mains) so the bonus only applies while a totem is active (OFF → no
contribution, matching the conditional in-game). Only the Grounding node uses
this exact string (tree_0.json 1_2/1_3/1_4; no affix/unique), so the general
suffix entry has a Grounding-only reach.

**Establishing observation (SuXes Avalanche −53% root-cause,
`LEB-0.13.2/Avalanche −53% root-cause (SuXes).md`):** the old "−53% base
undermodel" was a misdiagnosis (state-matched LEB cold = in-game +0.008%
out-of-form / +0.94% in-form). Grounding was one of the residual real gaps —
with a totem active the in-game per-hit carries the ×1.4521 factor LEB was
missing because the mod was dropped. With the fix LEB's Avalanche `MORE Damage`
gains the gated ×1.45 (1.40 HW × 1.30 SS × 1.45 Grounding) when
`conditionHaveTotem` is on, and stays at the matched baseline when off. Scope:
bug A of four separately-tracked Avalanche gaps (B large-boulder ×2, C adaptive
flat pre-conversion typing, D boulder no-crit are NOT addressed here).

### `avalanche-large-boulder-double-damage`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestAvalancheLargeBoulder_spec.lua`
- "parses '5% Large Boulder Chance' to a BASE DoubleDamageChance 5 mod (nil extra)"
- "does NOT turn '50% Large Boulder Chance To Leave Frozen Ground' into DoubleDamageChance"
- "does NOT turn '50% Upheaval Chance From Large Boulder' into DoubleDamageChance"
- "DoubleDamageChance is hit-only; 4 points (20) -> x1.20 EV on hits, 0 on ailments"
- "the ModCache row carries DoubleDamageChance BASE 5 and no leftover residue"
- "game-file: av75ch-15 Intensity still carries the audited stat (1.4 tree)"
- "carries the inline regression-guard marker in ModParser.lua"

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (anchored `specialModList` entry
`["^([%d%.]+)%% large boulder chance$"] = function(num) return { mod("DoubleDamageChance",
"BASE", num, "", ModFlag.Hit) } end`, inline-tagged
`@leb-regression-guard:avalanche-large-boulder-double-damage`) + `src/Data/ModCache.lua`
(the baked `"5% Large Boulder Chance"` row rewritten from a no-op
`{{}," Large Boulder Chance "}` to a hit-flagged `DoubleDamageChance` BASE 5 with `nil`
residue — byte-identical to a `SaveModCache` regen of the line).

**Why:** The Avalanche specialization node av75ch-15 "Intensity" carries the stat
`"5% Large Boulder Chance"` (maxPoints 4 → 20% at 4/4; datamine property 5076, 5%/pt).
In-game a fraction of Avalanche boulders spawn as "large boulders" that deal
`AvalancheSnowballMutator.BIG_BOULDER_MORE_DAMAGE = 1` (datamined game source) → +1.0 MORE =
exactly ×2.0 = DOUBLE damage. The SuXes 2026-05-29 per-hit ladder isolated the large
cluster at ×2.0000 exact, observed at ~18% (the 20% node within finite-sample error).
A p-chance to deal double damage is precisely LEB's existing `DoubleDamageChance`
mechanic — `CalcOffence` computes `ScaledDamageEffect *= (1 + DoubleDamageChance/100)`,
the expected-value MORE `(1 + p×(2−1))` the small:large boulder mix produces (20% →
×1.20). Before this guard the stat was a ModCache no-op (`{{}," Large Boulder Chance "}`),
so the entire large-boulder contribution was dropped — the residual of the SuXes
Avalanche gap once bug A (Grounding) was fixed.

**ModFlag.Hit (hit-only):** `BIG_BOULDER_MORE_DAMAGE` multiplies the boulder HIT only.
LE ailments are stack-based with fixed per-stack damage and do NOT scale with the
applying hit's size, so a large boulder must NOT double the Frostbite/Chill/Shock it
inflicts. A flagless `DoubleDamageChance` WOULD: it propagates to Avalanche's triggered
ailments via the SkillId `groupSource` channel and `CalcOffence` applies
`ScaledDamageEffect` to the ailment DoT — a PoE-ism (PoE ailments scale with the hit;
LE's do not). The `ModFlag.Hit` confines the ×1.20 to the boulder hit. Verified on
BOwJRDdE lv74 Shaman (the only corpus build allocating av75ch-15, at 4/4): with the
flag, ONLY `slot5_Avalanche` hit metrics move ×1.20 (AverageHit 935.31→1122.38,
ColdHit 287.40→344.88, PhysHit 491.90→590.28, TotalDPS 1388.94→1666.73), while the
`slot21_Frostbite_from_Avalanche` DoT DPS stays byte-unchanged (411.64); without the
flag the Frostbite DoT was incorrectly ×1.20'd too.

**Anchoring (no sibling collision):** the `^…$` anchor confines the rule to the exact
Intensity stat. The sibling Avalanche tree stats `"50% Large Boulder Chance To Leave
Frozen Ground"` (a chill-ground effect, NOT damage) and `"50% Upheaval Chance From
Large Boulder"` have trailing text that fails the `$`, so they stay unmodelled no-ops.
`"Large Boulder Chance"` exists only on the Avalanche tree (tree_0.json 1_2/1_3/1_4;
no affix/unique/idol/set), and skill-tree node mods are SkillId-scoped by
`PassiveTree.lua` (ModStore SkillId gate), so the `DoubleDamageChance` reaches Avalanche
(and its own triggered children) only — no leak to other skills.

**Scope:** bug B of four separately-tracked Avalanche gaps (A Grounding totem MORE
landed dev `<see git log>`; C adaptive flat pre-conversion typing; D boulder no-crit are
NOT addressed here). Establishing analysis: `LEB-0.13.2/Avalanche −53% root-cause
(SuXes).md` §B + wiki `concepts/avalanche-boulder-mechanics`.

### `chance-chance-conversion`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestChanceChanceConversion_spec.lua`
- "Vial: parses to a SkillName-gated Poison->Frostbite AilmentChanceConversion"
- "Apex: combined string parses to THREE glyph-gated conversions"
- "Apex combined string is NOT baked as LEB_NotSupported in ModCache (live-parses)"
- "Apex: glyph condition gates the conversion list (OFF -> none, ON -> 3)"
- "Vial: SkillName tag returns the conversion ONLY for an Acid Flask cfg"
- "Liath's: parses to a SkillName-gated Ignite->Shock AilmentChanceConversion"
- "Liath's: NOT baked as LEB_NotSupported in ModCache (live-parses)"
- "Liath's: SkillName tag returns the conversion ONLY for a Fireball cfg"
- "Apex end-to-end: glyph ON moves each ailment chance into its res-shred chance"
- "Apex end-to-end: a pre-existing res-shred chance is ADDED to (re-capped at 100)"
- "Ignite Overload reads post-conversion ignite chance, byte-identical without conversion"
- "Ignite Overload sees ZERO when Apex converts the ignite chance away"
- "Carrion: all six strings parse to an UNTAGGED <X>Chance->BleedChance conversion"
- "Carrion: NOT baked as LEB_NotSupported in ModCache (all six live-parse)"
- "Carrion: the untagged conversion applies to EVERY skill cfg (global scope)"
- "Carrion end-to-end: ALL SIX ailment chances move into Bleed chance on any skill"
- "Carrion: a single source converts in isolation, leaving the other ailments untouched"
- "Maehlin's: parses to an UNTAGGED Bleed->Ignite AilmentChanceConversion (global)"
- "Maehlin's: NOT baked as LEB_NotSupported in ModCache (live-parses)"
- "Maehlin's: the untagged conversion applies to EVERY skill cfg (global scope)"
- "Maehlin's end-to-end: Bleed chance moves into Ignite chance on any skill"
- "Maehlin's end-to-end: a pre-existing Ignite chance is ADDED to (re-capped at 100)"
- "Troaka's: parses to TWO SkillName=Puncture Bleed/Poison->Frostbite conversions"
- "Troaka's: NOT baked as LEB_NotSupported in ModCache (live-parses)"
- "Troaka's: SkillName tag returns BOTH conversions ONLY for a Puncture cfg"
- "Troaka's end-to-end: both Bleed and Poison chance accumulate into Frostbite for Puncture"
- "Troaka's end-to-end: a DIFFERENT skill is untouched (skill-scope is exact)"

**Sites:**
- `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` — three handlers emitting `AilmentChanceConversion`
  LIST mods `{ source, dest }`: the Vial handler bound to
  `^poison chance from all sources is converted to frostbite chance for acid flask$`
  (previously `nsAny` recognition-only) with a `SkillName=Acid Flask` tag; the
  Apex handler bound to the combined string
  `^100%% of ignite shock and chill chance converted to fire lightning and cold resistance shred chance while standing on your glyph of dominion$`
  emitting three conversions each with a `Condition:StandingOnGlyphOfDominion` tag; and
  the Liath's Machinations handler bound to
  `^100%% of ignite chance converted to shock chance for fireball$`
  with a `SkillName=Fireball` tag (IgniteChance -> ShockChance, unconditional); and the
  Carrion of Creation handler bound to `^100%% of (.+) chance converted to bleed chance$`,
  which maps the captured ailment name to its source-chance stat
  ({Ignite,Frostbite,Shock,Time Rot,Damned,Poison}Chance) and emits ONE
  **untagged** `{ source = <X>Chance, dest = BleedChance }` conversion -- the absence of a
  tag is what gives it GLOBAL (all-skill) scope (see Why). The Apex/Liath/Carrion strings
  all start with `100%`, so they also match the generic
  `^%+?([%d%.]+)%% of (.+) converted to (.+)$` handler; the full-literal anchored handlers
  win in `scan` because at the same start/end offset the longest pattern string is
  selected (the Vial string has no leading number, so the generic never matches it). The
  Carrion handler returns `nsAny` for any ailment name it does not recognise (or for
  "bleed" itself), so it never fabricates a conversion for a stat LEB does not track.
  Two more handlers added in the same class: the Maehlin's Hubris handler bound to
  `^100%% of bleed chance converted to ignite chance$` emitting ONE **untagged**
  `{ source = BleedChance, dest = IgniteChance }` conversion (GLOBAL, same untagged class
  as Carrion); and the Troaka's Teeth handler bound to
  `^100%% of bleed and poison chance converted to frostbite chance with puncture$`
  emitting TWO `SkillName=Puncture`-tagged conversions
  `{ Bleed->Frostbite }` and `{ Poison->Frostbite }` (two sources collapsing into one dest,
  scoped to Puncture; falls back to `nsAny` if `canonicalSkillName("Puncture")` is nil).
  Both strings start with `100%` so the full-literal anchored handlers again out-score the
  generic `% of X converted to Y` in `scan`. Neither was ever baked in ModCache (no rows to
  remove) — both previously fell through the generic handler to `nsAny` recognition-only.
- `src/Data/ModCache.lua` — removed the Apex combined-string row, the Liath's
  `100% of Ignite Chance Converted to Shock Chance for Fireball` row, AND the six Carrion
  `100% of {Ignite|Frostbite|Shock|Time Rot|Damned|Poison} Chance Converted to Bleed Chance`
  rows, all baked as `LEB_NotSupported notSupported=true` (so the build live-parses through
  the handlers). The Vial string was already absent from ModCache.
- `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` — consumer stage after the ailment-chance BASE sums
  (`output.<X>Chance`) and before the ailment-DPS loop: for each
  `modDB:List(skillCfg, "AilmentChanceConversion")` entry, move the full (0-100
  capped) `output[source]` into `output[dest]` (re-cap at 100) and zero `output[source]`.
  Plus two raw-reader redirects: Ignite Overload (`output.IgniteChance` instead of
  `modDB:Sum`) and Fissure of Wrath (keeps the uncapped `skillModList:Sum` but zeroes
  it when an `AilmentChanceConversion` has converted that stat away).

**Why:** in-game ground truth (tooltips verbatim) —
- Apex of Thought (Mage Helmet, uniques_1_4 #316): "While standing on your Glyph of
  Dominion, 100% of your Ignite Chance is converted to Fire Resistance Shred Chance,
  100% of your Chill Chance is converted to Cold Resistance Shred Chance, and 100% of
  your Shock Chance is converted to Lightning Resistance Shred Chance." The datamine
  packs the three into one combined mod string; the mapping is by ailment, NOT by the
  positional order in the packed string (Ignite→Fire, Shock→Lightning, Chill→Cold).
- Vial of Volatile Ice (Off-Hand Catalyst, uniques_1_4 #331): "Poison Chance from all
  sources is converted to Frostbite Chance for Acid Flask" — 100%, skill-scoped to Acid
  Flask, unconditional.
- Liath's Machinations (Amulet, uniques_1_4 #276): "100% of Ignite Chance Converted to
  Shock Chance for Fireball" — 100%, skill-scoped to Fireball, unconditional. The amulet
  also converts 50% of Fireball base damage to Lightning, so a shocking (not igniting)
  Fireball is consistent in-game. Shock is a debuff chance, not a DoT; the engine moves
  the chance value into `output.ShockChance` with no DoT pipeline involved.
- Carrion of Creation (primordial, uniques_1_4 #431): "100% of Ignite, Frostbite, Shock,
  Time Rot, Damned, and Poison Chance Converted to Bleed Chance" (one verbatim string per
  ailment in the data) — 100% each, **GLOBAL** (no glyph gate, no `for <skill>` scope; every
  skill). Bleed is a damaging ailment (`data.damagingAilment.Bleed`, Physical), so a
  converted Bleed chance drives the real ailment-DPS loop.
- Maehlin's Hubris (Mage Helmet, uniques_1_4 #83): "100% of Bleed Chance Converted to
  Ignite Chance" — 100%, **GLOBAL** (no glyph gate, no `for/with <skill>` scope; every
  skill). Datamine encode (uniques_v3.json uniqueID 83, first mod): value 1.0, canRoll
  false (fixed, rollId null in LEB JSON), property 100, specialTag 2, no skill clause.
  Same untagged-global class as Carrion. Ignite is a damaging ailment (Fire), so a converted
  Bleed chance now drives an Ignite DoT instead.
- Troaka's Teeth (Bow, uniques_1_4 #146): "100% of Bleed and Poison Chance converted to
  Frostbite Chance with Puncture" — 100% each, **skill-scoped to Puncture**, unconditional,
  TWO sources (Bleed Chance AND Poison Chance) collapsing into ONE dest (Frostbite Chance).
  Datamine encode (uniques_v3.json uniqueID 146, fifth mod): value 1.0, canRoll false
  (fixed, rollId null in LEB JSON), property 58 (the chance->chance property shared with
  Liath's #276), specialTag 2, "with Puncture" scope. The two conversions accumulate into
  `output.FrostbiteChance` (each move re-capped at 100), so a Puncture that bleeds+poisons
  instead frostbites; any other skill is untouched (SkillName tag filters them out).

A faithful chance→chance conversion = (1) remove 100% of the source chance so its
ailment no longer applies + (2) add the same amount to the dest chance. Because the
amount is dynamic, this cannot be a static mod; it is applied at the consumer over the
already-computed `output.<X>Chance`. **Scope is expressed entirely by the mod's tag (or
absence of one)**, and `modDB:List(skillCfg, ...)` resolves it automatically: a
`Condition` tag gates on config (glyph OFF → empty list, Apex), a `SkillName` tag gates on
the active skill (wrong skill → empty list, Vial/Liath), and **NO tag means GLOBAL** —
`ModStoreClass:ListInternal` inserts a tagless LIST mod via the `elseif mod.value` branch
(`mod[1] == nil`, so no `EvalMod`/tag check), returning it for EVERY cfg including unrelated
skills and `nil`. Carrion relies on this native behaviour for its all-skill scope; **no
engine change was needed to support global conversions** (verified: a tagless
`AilmentChanceConversion` is returned with count 1 for Fireball, Acid Flask, and nil cfg).
The two pre-existing raw readers of `<X>Chance` (Ignite Overload, Fissure of Wrath) are
redirected to the post-conversion value so a converted-away ailment chance no longer scales
them.

**Regression safety (byte-identical for every other build):** when no conversion unique
is equipped, `modDB:List(skillCfg, "AilmentChanceConversion")` is empty, so the consumer
loop runs zero times and `output.<X>Chance` stays exactly the prior `modDB:Sum` value.
The Ignite Overload redirect therefore reads the identical value (proven: ignite 80 →
overload more 4 = floor(80/20), unchanged). The Fissure redirect keeps reading the same
`skillModList:Sum` and only subtracts a conversion that is absent in non-Apex builds (and
Apex (Mage) / Fissure (Acolyte) cannot co-occur). No corpus build equips Apex, Vial,
Liath's Machinations, Carrion of Creation, or Maehlin's Hubris (grep of `spec/TestBuilds`
for these strings = 0 hits; the only behavioural change is for builds equipping one of these
uniques), so zero snapshot impact. Maehlin's/Carrion's global (untagged) conversions are
likewise inert without the unique: with none equipped the `AilmentChanceConversion` list is
empty for every cfg, so the consumer loop is a no-op and `output.<X>Chance` is the unchanged
`modDB:Sum`.

Troaka's Teeth IS equipped by 7 corpus builds (YsSupportCentre Paladin, DevouringBombah VK,
YsFkTrumpTariffs_S2 Warlock, LichDeezNutz Lich, YsGhostflameReaper Lich, YsFADeadeye Marksman,
BowChick Marksman). Pristine-vs-implemented computed `FullDPS` (loaded from XML on parent
<see git log> vs this branch) is **byte-identical for all 7** (e.g. BowChick 7828.9009336675 →
7828.9009336675, Δ 0.00%). The conversion DOES fire on the per-skill output where Puncture is
the active skill (BowChick mainOutput: BleedChance 71→0, FrostbiteChance 67→100; BleedDPS
721.56→nil, FrostbiteDPS 1074.23→1603.33) — but `FullDPS` is unchanged because (a) Puncture's
`output.TotalDPS` is HIT DPS only (`AverageDamage * dpsMultiplier`, no ailment fold), and (b)
the corpus builds carry each damaging ailment as a SEPARATELY-IMPORTED active skill (the
`Bleed` SkillDPS entry, trigger=Puncture, 263.22 — its own activeSkillList entry, computed
from its own skill data, NOT from Puncture's converted chance). So the ailment chance
conversion correctly re-routes the per-skill ailment-chance summary, but the FullDPS roll-up
folds hit DPS + independent imported ailment sub-skills, which this conversion does not
retarget. That FullDPS-fold boundary is pre-existing and identical across the chance-conversion
class (it would apply equally to Carrion/Liath/Vial); this change does not alter it. **Net: a
snapshot regen of these 7 builds would be byte-identical for FullDPS** (per-skill ailment-chance
display fields could shift on a Puncture-active view, but those are not the snapshotted
FullDPS); regen is deferred to orchestrator review either way.

**Establishing observation:** headless live-parse + pipeline — glyph OFF: Ignite=100
Shock=60 Chill=40, all Res-Shred=0; glyph ON: Ignite=0 Shock=0 Chill=0, FireResShred=100
LightningResShred=60 ColdResShred=40. Vial `AilmentChanceConversion` list count: Acid
Flask cfg = 1, Fireball cfg = 0, no-cfg = 0. Carrion (global): on a Fireball build,
NO-CONV Ignite=80 Frostbite=70 Shock=60 TimeRot=50 Damned=40 Poison=30 Bleed=0; with the
six conversions CONV all six sources = 0, Bleed=100 (sum 330 re-capped at 100). Untagged
`AilmentChanceConversion` list count = 1 for Fireball, Acid Flask, AND nil cfg (global
scope confirmed natively, no engine change).
Maehlin's Hubris (global Bleed->Ignite): on a Fireball build, NO-CONV Bleed=80 Ignite=0;
CONV Bleed=0 Ignite=80. Untagged list count = 1 for Fireball, Puncture, AND nil cfg.
Troaka's Teeth (Puncture-scoped Bleed+Poison->Frostbite): on a Puncture build, NO-CONV

Frostbite=0 (skill-scope exact). List count for the two Puncture mods = 2 for Puncture cfg,

### `tree-node-grants-skill`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestTreeNodeGrantsSkill_spec.lua`
- "LE_TREE_NODE_GRANTS_SKILL maps fw3d-12 to FireAura"
- "CalcSetup injects node-granted skills with includeInFullDPS gated by the buff"
- "ShutFackUp injects Fire Aura into FullDPS only when Flame Ward is active"

**Sites:** `src/Data/Global.lua` (`LE_TREE_NODE_GRANTS_SKILL` registry,
`fw3d-12 → "FireAura"`) + `src/Modules/CalcSetup.lua` (injection loop after the
socket-group active-skill loop: synthesizes a no-support active skill + synthetic
`includeInFullDPS` socket group, gated by `env.allocNodes[nodeId]` and the tree's
`LE_WHILE_ACTIVE_BUFF_BY_TREE_ID` `Condition:Have<X>` flag).

**Why:** the ④ sub-point of the Fire Aura DPS gap. A skill-tree node can GRANT a
continuous DoT/aura skill that is absent from the loadout (fw3d-12 "Fire Aura"
grants the Fire Aura DoT while Flame Ward is active). LEB has no native pipeline
for node-granted active skills — item/ailment grants flow through
`env.grantedSkills`, but tree nodes produce only stat mods — so the granted
aura's damage was missing from Full DPS entirely (Full DPS=0 for Fire Aura).
The injected skill's skillModList receives the ①'
(`tree-conversion-target-skill`) Fire→Cold conversion and the ②
(`skill-scoped-damage-idol-tag`) SkillName="Fire Aura" idol/passive INC mods.
Modeled at 100% uptime (continuous aura). Gating on the buff condition is
essential: Fire Aura must not appear when Flame Ward is inactive (LE's Buffs
panel defaults it OFF), and the loop is a no-op for every build that has not
allocated fw3d-12 — so no other build's Full DPS changes.

**Establishing observation:** ShutFackUp lv85 Spellblade with
`conditionHaveFlameWard` on — Fire Aura appears in activeSkillList
(`includeInFullDPS=true`, source `TreeNodeGrant:fw3d-12`), its skillModList sums
`FireDamageConvertToCold` BASE 100 (Fire Aura cfg) and `Damage` INC 199, and it
contributes to FullDPS (was absent before). With Flame Ward off (default), the
build has no Fire Aura skill. NOTE: the absolute DoT/s (~310 in LEB vs ~794
in-game) still has a scaling gap — multiple Fire Aura stacks, spell-damage
scaling, and the ③ Static-charge lightning component — tracked as a separate
DoT-precision follow-up; the injection mechanism itself is what this guard locks.

### `tree-node-defensive-hit-damage`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestFlameWardBarrierDefensive_spec.lua`
- "registry: LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE rewrites fw3d-18 'Less Hit Damage' -> '...taken'"
- "parse contract: the rewrite flips Damage(Hit) [offensive] -> DamageTaken(Hit) [defensive]"
- "game-file: fw3d-18 'Barrier' is the defensive node the registry targets"
- "scope guard: mush9-6 'Point Blank' (OFFENSIVE 'less hit damage') must NOT be registered"
- "source: PassiveTree applies the rewrite before rank scaling; Global holds the registry"

**Sites:** `src/Data/Global.lua` (`LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE` registry,
`fw3d-18` → `{pat="[Ll]ess [Hh]it [Dd]amage$", repl="less hit damage taken"}`) +
`src/Classes/PassiveTree.lua` (`ProcessStats`: applies the node-scoped rewrite at
the TOP of the `node.stats` loop, BEFORE the rank-scaling block, so the leading
per-point value still multiplies).

**Why:** a few LE tree nodes carry the stat string "X% Less Hit Damage" whose
in-game meaning is DEFENSIVE (the player TAKES less damage from hits), but the
bare string is byte-identical in form to the ~90 OFFENSIVE "hit damage" nodes
("<skill> hits deal less/more damage"). ModParser reads the bare string as
`% less` + `ModFlag.Hit` + name `"Damage"` → an offensive `-X% hit damage DEALT`
(`Damage` MORE `-40` flags=Hit). The disambiguator lives ONLY in the node
description, so the fix re-expresses the stat as "less hit damage taken" →
`DamageTaken` MORE `-40` flags=Hit (a mitigation mod). The rewrite changes ONLY
the mod NAME (`Damage`→`DamageTaken`); type/value/flag are identical — that name
swap is what moves the value off the DPS path and onto EHP. Must stay
node-scoped: `mush9-6` "Point Blank" also has the words "less hit damage" but is
OFFENSIVE ("Multishot deals less hit damage as it travels"), so a blanket string
rule is wrong — the spec asserts mush9-6 is not registered. The `$`-anchored
pattern tolerates LE re-tuning the per-point value; the game-file assertion pins
the live tree-data wiring so a stat-string rename surfaces as a failure rather
than a silent revert.

**Establishing observation:** fw3d-18 "Barrier" (Flame Ward tree, maxPoints 5,
per-point "8% Less Hit Damage", description "You take less damage from hits while
Flame Ward is active") is gated behind `LE_WHILE_ACTIVE_BUFF_BY_TREE_ID` "fw3d"
→ `Condition:HaveFlameWard`. On saved build "ShutFackUp lv85 Spellblade" (Shatter
Strike, allocates fw3d-18 at rank 5) toggling `conditionHaveFlameWard`:
- BEFORE fix: FullDPS 16853 → 10534 (×0.604 = 1 − 8%×5; deterministic &
  reversible — OFF#1=OFF#2=OFF#3=OFF#5 exactly, only ON differs).
- AFTER fix: FullDPS 16853 → 17351 (the −40% DPS penalty is gone; Barrier's
  mitigation now lands on EHP, and the fw3d-12 Fire Aura grant adds a little DoT).

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestSkillScopedDamageIdol_spec.lua`

- "the tagged INC applies only under a Fire Aura cfg (no leak)"
- "ModParser registers the skill-scoped damage idol pattern"

**Why:** the ② sub-point of the Fire Aura DPS gap. A "(N)% increased <Skill>
Damage" idol affix (ShutFackUp's "(30-100)% Increased Fire Aura Damage" prefix)
must parse to a single `Damage INC` mod tagged `SkillName="<Skill>"`, so the
increase lands ONLY on that skill's cfg and never leaks globally or onto other

tagged, and reaches `env.modDB` scoped. It produces no Fire Aura DPS today only
because Fire Aura is a triggered skill absent from `activeSkillList` (the
separate ④ trigger-injection gap), not because the tag is missing.

Aura Damage" sums to **71** under a `{skillName="Fire Aura"}` cfg (19 global + 52
scoped) vs **19** under `{skillName="Shatter Strike"}` and **19** under nil cfg.

### `null-portent-less-damage-taken-per-resist-overcap`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestNullPortentOvercapDamageTaken_spec.lua`

Null Portent (unique body armour) mitigates damage based on how far each
resistance sits above its normal cap. The affix is authored as TWO separate
mod lines that together form one mechanic:
- `1% less Damage Taken per 2% Resistance above the normal cap` (rate: N% per M%)
- `20% Maximum Less Damage Taken per 2% Resistance above the normal cap` (cap: 20%)

**Spec:** in-game tooltip — 85% fire res → fire cap 75% exceeded by 10% →
`10 / 2 = 5%` less **fire** damage taken (multiplicative, **per-type**), capped
at 20% less. Needs 40% over-cap in a type to hit the 20% cap.

**Bug (pre-fix):** both lines short-circuited on stale `Data/ModCache.lua` rows
that baked a bare `DamageTaken MORE -1` / `DamageTaken BASE 20` with dropped
`" per 2% Resistance above the normal cap "` residue — so the over-cap scaling
was never modelled (Symbols-of-Hope-style residue trap). The over-cap-resistance
mitigation was silently absent.

**Fix (3 sites):**
| Site | File | Role |
|------|------|------|
| parse (rate) | `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` specialModList | `1% less Damage Taken per 2% Resistance above the normal cap` → BASE `LessDamageTakenPerResOverCapNum` + `LessDamageTakenPerResOverCapDiv` (no residue) |
| parse (cap) | `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` specialModList | `20% Maximum Less Damage Taken per 2% Resistance above the normal cap` → BASE `LessDamageTakenPerResOverCapMax` (no residue) |
| inject | `src/Modules/CalcDefence.lua` (after resist loop) | For each of the 7 damage types: `<Type>DamageTaken MORE = -min(Max, floor(<Type>ResistOverCap / Div) * Num)`, consumed by `calcs.buildDefenceEstimations` |
| purge | `src/Data/ModCache.lua` | Both stale residue rows deleted so the lines re-parse live |

Cannot use a PerStat tag: it can't express the Maximum cap alongside the
per-type `<Type>ResistOverCap`, and the rate/cap arrive on separate lines.
Floors at integer steps to match the "per M% resistance" injection family
(`urzils-pride-mana-regen-per-uncapped-lightning-res`,
`boneclamor-barbute-ward-per-uncapped-necrotic-res`,
`frostbite-shackles-wr-per-uncapped-cold-res`). DamageTaken is defensive and
never feeds the offensive snapshot — corpus DPS is neutral (byte-identical).

**Do not touch:** the 20% Maximum cap, the /2 divisor, the per-type gate
(each resistance reduces only its own damage type), or the floor.

### `properties-loader-init`

`src/Data/Properties/Loader.lua` exposes the LE `PropertyList`
ScriptableObject (extracted from `resources.assets` via
TypeTreeGeneratorAPI) to runtime Lua, so `itemLib.applyRangeStrict`
callers can pick the correct rounding (Hundredth / Integer / Tenth /
Thousandth) per stat without re-encoding the heuristic.

The contract is initialization ordering: `Properties.load(ver)` must
be called before any access to `Properties.byName` / `Properties.bySP`.
The loader caches per-version — repeat `load()` with the same version
is a no-op; with a different version it overwrites both maps. Tests
that exercise the rounding path must call `load()` in `before_each`
(or once in `setup`) or they will silently read empty tables and fall

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| loader  | `src/Data/Properties/Loader.lua` (~line 21, marker on `Properties.load`) | Caches parsed JSON per version into `byName` / `bySP`; safe to call repeatedly with the same version |
| consumer | `src/Modules/ItemTools.lua` `applyRangeStrict` | Reads `Properties.byName[propName].roundingForAdded` to pick the rounding mode for vshDm |

### `ailment-dps-steady-state-formula`

LEB models damaging ailments as steady-state DPS rather than per-tick
simulation. Three interlocking invariants must hold together; breaking any
one of them silently shifts every ailment DPS by a `durationMult` factor.

Verbatim source quote (`datamined game source §3`,
referring to `Ailment.baseDamage` at offset `+0x88`):

> "Damage represents the total damage dealt over the duration"

<!-- validation detail omitted: line 10244 -->

> "longer duration also means more total damage (i.e. the per-second damage

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| ailment DPS | `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (~line 1795) | Computes per-stack damage, per-stack DPS, steady-state stacks, and clamped total DPS |
| cap constant | `src/Modules/Data.lua` (~line 105) | `DotDpsCap = (2^31 - 1) / 60` (game's int32 damage tick over 1 minute) |

### `ailment-overstacking-uncapped`

**Invariant:** The damaging-ailment steady-state loop derives its application
rate from the **uncapped summed** ailment chance, so chance above 100% produces
guaranteed overstacking. `output.<X>Chance` stays capped at 100 (Ignite/Bleed
Overload and the UI read it); only the application rate re-sums the uncapped value.

Game ground truth (datamining, build 1.4.7c). `AilmentApplication__Apply`
(`datamined game source`) converts a
hit's summed chance `C` (fraction, 1.0 = 100%) into stacks-this-hit with a
floor+remainder loop, then one leftover-fraction roll:

> `for (fVar6 = *(chance); 1.0 < fVar6; fVar6 -= 1.0) { iVar5++; }`
> `if (EpochExtensions__roll(fVar6,0)) iVar5++;`

So **expected stacks per hit = C** (no `min(chance,100)` cap). All "chance to
apply <this ailment>" sources are summed before the roll
(`AilmentApplication__addChance:1454`), and application is per hit-event
(`ChanceToApplyAilmentsOnHit` subscribes to the HitDetector new/again hit events).

The bug: CalcOffence caps every `output.<X>Chance` at `m_min(sum,100)` (line
~2479); the application rate previously used that capped value, discarding all
overstacking (a 282%-Bleed build applied at 100% → ~2.82× under on stack count).

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| appRate | `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (damaging-ailment loop, ~line 2688) | `overstackChance = modDB:Sum("BASE", skillCfg, ailmentName.."Chance")` (clamped ≥ the finalized capped chance); `applicationsPerSec = hitRate * (overstackChance/100)` |
| capped display | `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (~line 2479) | `output.<X>Chance = m_min(sum,100)` — unchanged; every consumer (Overload, UI) still sees the capped value |

**Corpus blast:** builds whose summed chance for a damaging ailment exceeds 100%
gain proportionally more ailment stacks/DPS. Builds with chance ≤ 100 are
byte-identical (the fix is a strict no-op there). `maxStacks` clamp unchanged
(steady state sits at the cap; eviction is oldest/weakest per datamining).

**Not modeled here (deferred):** `hitsPerSecond` still uses cast/attack rate and
does not count multi-hit-per-cast (projectiles/bounces/orbit-ticks). LEB has no
clean hit-COUNT lever separated from `skillData.dpsMultiplier` (which conflates
hit count with damage-equivalents), so multi-hit application-rate is a separate,
larger feature — see the Bleed-Hammerdin note in `project_ballista_rate_dex_guile`
sibling memory / `project_meta43_residual_triage`.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestAilmentOverstackingUncapped_spec.lua`
- "CalcOffence.lua carries the inline regression-guard marker"
- "the application rate uses the UNCAPPED summed chance, not output.<X>Chance"
- "steady-state stacks are LINEAR in the uncapped chance ABOVE 100% (overstacking)"
- "below 100% the stack count is byte-identical (strict no-op for chance <= 100)"
- "the displayed/Overload output.BleedChance stays capped at 100 even at 250%"

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

"+34# Armor Shred Chance for Shadow Attack, Doubled with Bow" keeps
its base Condition{ShadowAttack} gate (entry [1]) and adds the
Bow-mult Condition tag (entry [2]={mult=2,...,var="UsingBow"}); the
residue collapses from `"#  , Doubled  "` to `"#  "`.

### condition-shadow-attack-consumer

**Invariant:** `CalcOffence.offence` assigns
`skillCfg.skillCond["ShadowAttack"]` to `true` whenever the active
skill's `activeEffect.grantedEffect.name` is one of an allowlist of
player-castable Shadow Attack skills, and `false` otherwise. The
allowlist is `{"Shadow Cascade", "Shadow Daggers", "Shadow Rend"}`,
sourced from datamined `ability_keyed_array.json` and
`localized_master.json` in the datamined game source workspace. Skills that
the ShadowClone minion uses (Shurikens, Arrowstorm) are deliberately
NOT included because their player-cast form is not a Shadow Attack
from the player's perspective; the minion's casts go through
`env.minion` scope and bypass this skillCfg. Without this wiring,
every affix carrying `tag={type="Condition", var="ShadowAttack"}`
(emitted by `modTagList["for shadow attack"]` and by the F4 trailing
clause `", doubled for shadow attack"`) silently full-gates to zero
on the player.

**Files:**
- `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (per-skill init, after `SkillIsFocused`)
- `spec/System/TestConditionShadowAttackConsumer_spec.lua`

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### health-regen-applies-to-ward-plus-prefix

**Invariant:** Both anchored parser handlers MUST start with
`^%+?(%d+)` so the affix form (with a leading `+`) and the
Runemaster Sanguine Runestones form (without `+`) both resolve to
`LifeRegenAppliesToWard` BASE. Without the `%+?` the `+`-prefixed
input falls through to the generic `+N% health regen` handler,
silently emits `LifeRegen` INC (wrong stat) and strands `also
applies to Ward` in the parser residue, so the
`LifeRegenAppliesToWard` BASE that `CalcDefence.lua:641, :796`
consumes never fires. The ModCache entries for the 5 known affix
tiers must carry the `LifeRegenAppliesToWard BASE` shape with
`nil` residue.

### cooldown-recovered-on-hit-consumer

**Invariant:** The two unique-mod families "+N% of Lethal Mirage's
remaining cooldown recovered on Melee Hit (up to M times)"
(Black Blade of Chaos Mod[4]) and "+N% chance to recover 8% of
Aerial Assault's remaining cooldown on Throwing Hit (up to M
times)" (Razorfall Mod[4]) MUST emit a paired BASE mod set:
`CooldownRecoveryOnHit` (percent recovered per qualifying hit;
for Razorfall = chance * 8 / 100 effective average) and
`CooldownRecoveryOnHitMaxPerCast` (the per-cast cap, resets when
the named skill is used -- see game `CharacterMutator`
`SinceLast<Skill>Use` counters in `datamined game source` L96712-96719). Both
mods carry a `SkillName=<skill>` tag so they only resolve when
that ability is the active skill (Option A: SkillName reused as
"affects-this-cooldown" target, paralleling F11
`MirageCount`/F10 `ChanceToApplyShadowDaggerOnHit` patterns).
CalcOffence MUST aggregate via `skillModList:Sum("BASE", skillCfg,
...)` into `output.CooldownRecoveryOnHit` and
`output.CooldownRecoveryOnHitMaxPerCast`, and CalcSections MUST
have two `haveOutput=...` rows surfacing them. Without this
wiring the values were parsed-but-unconsumed (silent failure
mirroring F1/F10/F11). Per-cast accumulator semantics are
visible-only at v1 -- combat-loop attribution is deferred.

Additionally, the ModParser dispatcher calls handlers as
`specialMod(tonumber(cap[1]), unpack(cap))`, so any N-capture
handler MUST take `(numericFirst, rawFirst, ...rawN)`. Both
anchored handlers here have two captures (pct/chance + cap) and
therefore use `(_, pctStr, capStr)` / `(_, chanceStr, capStr)`
signatures -- a 2-arg `(pct, cap)` form silently aliases `cap`
to the first raw capture (the pct/chance string) and drops the
`(up to N times)` value, emitting `CooldownRecoveryOnHitMaxPerCast`
equal to the pct value. The runtime-dispatch block in
`TestCooldownRecoveredOnHitConsumer_spec.lua` calls
`modLib.parseMod` directly on rolled-text inputs to lock this
convention.

**Files:**
- `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (two anchored handlers after `mirages-created-by-lethal-mirage`)
- `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (after F10 ChanceToApplyShadowDaggerOnHit)
- `src/Modules/CalcSections.lua` (after Shadow Dagger Apply Chance row)
- `src/Data/ModCache.lua` (Lethal Mirage 15%/12-times anchor + Aerial Assault 17%/3-times anchor)
- `spec/System/TestCooldownRecoveredOnHitConsumer_spec.lua`

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### mod6-v2-combat-loop

**Invariant:** The v1 pair (`CooldownRecoveryOnHit`,
`CooldownRecoveryOnHitMaxPerCast`) emitted by the
`cooldown-recovered-on-hit-consumer` parser anchors (Lethal Mirage
15%/12-times from Black Blade of Chaos; Aerial Assault 1.36%/3-times
chance-folded from Razorfall) MUST fold into an effective skill
cooldown using the closed-form equilibrium

    effectiveCD = baseCD * (1 - pct/100)^cap

published as `output.EffectiveCooldownFromOnHit` AND back-propagated
into `output.Cooldown` so the downstream Speed clamp
(`output.Speed = min(Speed, 1/output.Cooldown * Repeats)`) picks up
the recovery. Removing the fold-in regresses Lethal Mirage / Aerial
Assault DPS to the v1 surface-only state where the chase mod
appears in stat rows but has no impact on cast/hit frequency.

**Game-file authority (datamined game source re-extraction):**
- L96712 `chanceToRecover8pOfRemainingAerialAssaultCooldownOnThrowingHit` (float, chance)
- L96714 `maxTimesToRecover12pOfRemainingAerialAssaultCooldownOnThrowingHit = 3` (const cap)
- L96716 `lethalMirageRemainingCooldownRecoveredOnMeleeHitUpTo12TimesPerUse` (float, pct)
- L96718 `lethalMirageMeleeHitCooldownRecoveryEventsSinceLastUse` (int counter; resets per cast)
- The per-skill `SinceLast<Skill>Use` counters are int event tallies, not float timers --
  the closed form approximates the per-cast reset semantics without a time-axis simulation.

**LEB strategy:** LEB is a PoB-flow static DPS engine with no
combat-loop / time-axis simulation. We approximate the steady-state
fixed point of the recovery loop assuming the cap is reached every
cast -- this is the affix's design intent (otherwise the cap would
be uninteresting) and a defensible best-case upper bound. The
closed form is the analytic limit of a per-tick simulation as the
hit rate goes to infinity.

**Why not Option B (per-tick simulation):** would require a new
combat-loop module, time-axis events, and convergence detection --
~10x the LoC of the closed form, for a 2-skill affix family.
Deferred indefinitely; if a future affix needs sub-equilibrium
behaviour, revisit.

**Files:**
- `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (effective-cooldown site, immediately after `output.Cooldown = cooldown` at L1223)
- `src/Modules/CalcSections.lua` (section site, "Effective Cooldown (CD-on-Hit)" row, after Max CD-Recovery Hits)
- `spec/System/TestCooldownRecoveryOnHitV2_spec.lua`

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### silent-failure-affix-sweep

**Invariant:** The Phase 1 enumeration baseline of "silent failure"
ModCache rows MUST remain frozen until a category-specific Phase 3 PR
deliberately moves it. A "silent failure" row is one of the form
`c["<affix-string>"]={{},"<non-empty residue>"}` in
`src/Data/ModCache.lua` -- ModParser returned an empty modList yet
emitted residue text, so the affix was swallowed without surfacing
into calculations and without raising an error.

**Baseline (current -- 2026-06-13 landing-order tail refresh):**
- total ModCache rows           : 16,537
- parsed (non-empty modList)    : 13,438  (81.25%)
- neutralized (empty residue)   :  1,074
- silent failure (residue text) :  2,025
- combined recognition rate     : 87.75%  (parsed + neutralized / total)
- refined category split (dm-aware):
    a1-pure-flavor   :   0   (bucket emptied by Phase 3a bulk neutralization)
    a2-numeric-real  : 627   (real numeric mods masquerading as flavor; DO NOT neutralize)
    b-dm-numeric     : 127   (dm-confirmed real LE-1.4 numeric, parser regex missing)
    b-parser-gap     : 457   (residue suggests numeric mod, no dm match)
    c-dm-infra       : 220   (dm-confirmed real LE-1.4 trigger/event, infra missing)
    c-infra-gap      : 594   (residue suggests trigger/event, no dm match)
- datamining cross-reference (ModItem_1_4.json + 3 siblings):
    moditem lines scanned    : 9,516
    moditem unique norms     : 974
    silent_failure matched   : 347 / 2,025 (17.1%)
    dm_gap (never reached LEB): 289  (affixes LEB has never attempted to parse)

**2026-06-12 discovery-debt refresh:** the committed snapshot had drifted
stale -- prior un-bakes shrank the live silent set but the tool was never
re-run (the debt was flagged in the `deaths-door-lowlife-critmult` / #13
commit `<see git log>`, which bumped the metadata counts but not the body).
Re-running `enumerate_silent_failures.py` against current dev ModCache
dropped **44 rows from the silent set and added 0** vs the committed JSON.
Every removal attributes to a landed fix (no unexplained newly-silent
affix => no regression):
- trigger-subskill rollout un-baked the "chance to cast <skill>" procs:
  Fire Aura `<see git log>`, Maelstrom-timer `<see git log>`, Divine Bolt
  `<see git log>`, Zap `<see git log>`, Storm Bolt `<see git log>`, Wind Tempest
  `<see git log>`.
- StarSea idol-3 fix `<see git log>` un-baked Pierce-with-Fireball,
  Pierce->Critical Multiplier, and the "different shape" idol line.
- Apocrypha `<see git log>` and Chthonic Fissure of Wrath `<see git log>`
  un-baked the "X -> Y" conversion-arrow rows.
- recast-parse `<see git log>` un-baked the Recast rows.
Of the 44, 39 are now absent from ModCache and 5 re-parse to a non-empty
modList; none remains silent. ModCache itself is UNCHANGED by this refresh
-- it is a snapshot-only update of the tracking registry.

**2026-06-13 landing-order tail refresh:** the 2026-06-12 refresh landed
(`<see git log>`) BEFORE two ModCache-affecting merges -- Avalanche
large-boulder `<see git log>` and minion ActorStats `<see git log>` -- so the
registry missed their un-bakes and went stale again by 1 row (the count
spec stays green regardless because it only compares JSON metadata to its
own baselines, never re-walks ModCache). Re-running the tool against
current dev (`<see git log>`) moved **exactly 1 row out of the silent set and
added 0** => no regression:
- `"5% Large Boulder Chance"` (ModCache row 14870) was un-baked by
  Avalanche-B `<see git log>` into `DoubleDamageChance BASE 5 [Hit]`, so it
  moved silent -> parsed (b-parser-gap 458 -> 457).
- minion ActorStats `<see git log>` wrote `minions.json` + a SkillId-scoped
  Berserk ModParser entry -- no ModCache silent-failure row changed (0).
- adaptive-typing C `<see git log>` touched only CalcOffence -- 0.
Snapshot-only: total/neutralized and all dm baselines hold; parsed
13,437 -> 13,438, silent 2,026 -> 2,025. ModCache UNCHANGED by this refresh.

**Why a guard:** ModParser regex regressions historically grow the
silent-failure pool silently (no error, no test failure, no LETools
diff on builds that don't carry the affix). Locking the baseline
turns any silent regrowth into a deliberate `busted` failure that
forces investigation. Conversely, when Phase 3 PRs wire / neutralise
real affixes, the count shrinks and the spec must be updated in the
same commit -- this becomes the audit trail for the sweep.

**Workflow when the count changes:**
1. Run `python spec/tools/enumerate_silent_failures.py`.
2. Inspect the diff on `spec/Data/silent-failure-affixes.json`.
3. Update the `EXPECTED_*` constants in
   `spec/System/TestSilentFailureSweep_spec.lua` and the baseline
   numbers in this section in the SAME commit as the parser change.
4. If the change is a regression, revert -- do NOT slap the baseline.

**Phase plan:** see `TODO.md` "Category B silent-failure affix sweep".

- Phase 2 (commit `<see git log>`) -- ModItem cross-reference; dm-aware refined
  classifier; safe-to-neutralize bucket (a1-pure-flavor) isolated from
  a2-numeric-real masquerade.
- Phase 3a (commit `<see git log>` lineage) -- bulk neutralize 715
  a1-pure-flavor rows via `--emit-neutralization` mode; recognition
  83.34% -> 87.61%.
- 2026-06-12 refresh -- re-run the tool to clear accumulated discovery
  debt (44 stale silent rows un-baked by later landed fixes); snapshot
  + spec + this baseline updated together. No ModCache / engine change.
- 2026-06-13 tail refresh -- re-run after Avalanche-B (`<see git log>`) +
  minion-actorstats (`<see git log>`) landed post-refresh; 1 row un-baked
  ("5% Large Boulder Chance"), 0 added. Snapshot-only.
- Phase 3b -- spawn-task per b-dm-numeric / c-dm-infra family (347 dm-matched).
- Phase 3c -- parser-gap / infra-gap unmatched require build-source
  research before action.

### unique-hideintooltip-letools-artifact

**ID:** `unique-hideintooltip-letools-artifact`
**Files:**
- `src/Data/Uniques/uniques.json` / `uniques_1_2.json` / `uniques_1_3.json` / `uniques_1_4.json`

**Invariant:** When a game-side unique mod has `hideInTooltip=true`
AND `descriptors.json` has no entry for its
`"<property>,<tags>,<specialTag>,<extraTag>"` key, the LEB string
for that mod is a LETools fallback-formatter artifact (typically
prefixed with `+N` where N is the raw `value` field). Two sub-cases,
both locked here:

1. **Pure descriptive flag** (no `tooltipDescriptions` text either):
   the LEB entry MUST be deleted from `mods`+`rollIds`. Anchor case:
   Black Blade of Chaos (`uniqueID=339`) Mod[0]
   `"+1 Lethal Mirage is a quick attack with no invulnerability"`
   was purged across all 4 unique JSON variants. ModCache lost the
   matching `c["+1 Lethal Mirage is a quick attack with no
   invulnerability"]={{},""}` no-op key as well.

2. **Game tooltipDescription covers it** (game renders authored
   text via `tooltipDescriptions` despite `hideInTooltip=true`):
   the LEB string MUST drop the `+N ` LETools prefix to mirror the
   game text verbatim, and ModCache MUST NOT carry a parser entry
   for either form (the `+N`-prefixed key in particular must not
   exist, because LETools' fallback `+1` value is meaningless and
   any parser that ingests it produces a wrong stat). Anchor cases:
   The Claw (`uniqueID=58`) Mod[2] and The Fang (`uniqueID=60`)
   Mod[3], both `(property=58, tags=8, specialTag=3, extraTag=0)`
   `hideInTooltip=true`, both string-equal to game
   `tooltipDescriptions[0]`:
   `"You can Summon Wolves up to your Maximum Number of Companions"`.
   The previous LEB form `"+1 You can Summon Wolves..."` had a
   ModCache entry incorrectly mapping it to
   `MaxCompanions BASE +1` -- contradicting the in-game altText
   `"Does not increase your maximum number of companions."`. That
   entry was purged and the `+1 ` prefix stripped from all 4
   unique JSON variants.

### proc-rate-limit-metadata-v1

**Invariant:** The static localization suffix
`(up to N times per M seconds)` on chance-to-proc affixes is
surfaced as passive `RateLimit` metadata, NOT as an equilibrium
effective-procs/sec stat. LEB follows the game files: the game
exposes no planner-visible rate-capped chance stat -- the cap is
enforced at runtime only via `ProcTimeTracker`. LEB therefore
stores `(limit, interval)` as metadata and displays it
informationally, without fabricating a derived stat the game
itself does not surface.

**Files:**
- `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (Burning Dagger full-line anchor:
  emits `RateLimit{limit=4, interval=1, var="BurningDaggerOnMeleeFire"}`

  entries carry the RateLimit metadata tag)

  guard locks against accidental handler addition AND against

  are `value = m_min(value, tag.limit)`)

  tag.interval into `output.BurningDaggerChanceOnMeleeFire_RateLimit`
  and `_RateInterval` scalars)
- `src/Modules/CalcSections.lua` (informational `Burning Dagger

**Migration recipe for the next LE patch (1.5+)**, replaying the 1.4
playbook so the next person doesn't trip the same false positives:

1. Run the within-version spec: `bash scripts/regen-shards.sh` then
   `docker compose run --rm busted-tests busted --filter=TestUniqueDataIntegrity`.
   Catches DUP_LINE.
2. Run the Python audit (or copy `.tmp/audit_uniques_1_4_regression.py`
   to `.tmp/audit_uniques_1_5_regression.py` and rebind `P14`/`P13`).
   Triage real DUP_LINE / RANGE_COLLAPSE / ROLLID_LEN immediately.
3. ROW_DROP needs base-implicit subtraction. The 1.4 migration moved
   boots/quiver/sword implicits out of each unique into `bases_1_4.json`,
   so naive cross-version diff flagged 9 false positives (Eterra's Path,
   Suloron's Step, Transient Rest, Raindance, Snowdrift, Foot of the
   Mountain, Stealth, Clotho's Needle, Army of Skin). Use
   `.tmp/verify_base_implicit_migration.py` (or its 1_5 equivalent) to
   subtract base implicits — anything still flagged after subtraction is
   a real ROW_DROP. The verification script matches by
   `(baseTypeID, subTypeID)` and compares range-stripped shapes.
4. Use in-game tooltip screenshots from the user as the final ground
   truth for any unique that still looks suspicious after step 3.

### `import-abilitybar-unspecialized-skills`

A Last Epoch save stores the equipped skills in `abilityBar` (a flat list of
skill treeIDs, one per bar slot) and the specialization slots in
`savedSkillTrees` (treeID + allocated tree nodes). These two lists are NOT the
same set: a skill can be on the bar without being specialized (the player has
equipped it but spent no specialization slot on it), and a skill can be
specialized without being on the bar (kept its tree but is currently swapped
out). In-game only barred skills are castable; an un-specialized barred skill
casts as its BASE skill (empty tree).

`ImportTabClass:ReadJsonSaveData` originally built the imported skill set from
`savedSkillTrees` ALONE, so every bar-only (un-specialized) skill was dropped
from the LEB build entirely. This is low-level-save specific: by endgame every
barred skill is usually specialized, so the two lists coincide and nothing is
lost. At low level they diverge.

The fix adds an `abilityBar` pass after the `savedSkillTrees` loop: each barred
treeID NOT already imported becomes a base-skill socket group (a `treeID-0#1`
root hash, no allocated tree nodes — mirroring the root hash specialized skills
already get). A per-import `importedTreeIDs` set records every treeID added by
the `savedSkillTrees` loop so a skill present in BOTH lists is imported exactly
once (no double-count). The treeID→name lookup that both loops share was lifted
into a local `resolveSkillName` helper.

### `import-rarity-flag-bits`

The offline-save binary item record stores rarity as a single byte whose
low nibble is the base "visual rarity" (`7`=Unique, `8`=Set, `9`=Legendary;
cf. `Item.uniqueRarity`/`setItemRarity`/`legendaryRarity` in the game's
datamined game source dump) with two INDEPENDENT high flag bits layered on top:

- bit6 (`0x40`) = Weaver's Will   → `0x49` = 73 on a legendary
- bit7 (`0x80`) = exalted / fused → `0x89` = 137 on a legendary (a Legendary-
  Potential unique forged with exalted affixes); the same bit on a non-unique
  is the Exalted flag, `0x82` = 130 = `Item.visualRarityForExaltedItems`.

Both flags can co-exist on a legendary, so they must be decoded
independently and routing must use the BASE rarity (low nibble). The old
decode did `isWeaversWill = rarity >= 64` then subtracted only `0x40`, so a
bit7 legendary (`0x89` = 137) collapsed to 73, fell outside the `[7,9]`
unique range, and was routed to the NON-unique affix path: the legendary was
shown as an Exalted item with an affix-generated name, its unique mods were
never loaded, and the unique's roll bytes were misread as bogus affixes
(`[IMPORT-DROP]` ids in no affix table, impossible "tier 12/13").

### `import-nonunique-affix-count`

The offline-save binary item parser's **non-unique** (`effectiveRarity < 5` —
Normal/Magic/Rare/Exalted **and all idols**) affix loop reads exactly the number
of slots the save declares: `count = band(d[BASE + 8], 0x3f)` (game `id[11]`),
never a fixed window. The count is authoritative in both directions because the
game's serialiser writes it as the affix List's `Count` and then emits exactly
that many 3-byte triples from `id[12]`; the deserialiser reads back with the same
bound (`i < count`, 3-byte stride) in a single loop with no second pass. Every
affix an item owns — normal, sealed, primordial, corrupted, **Weaver's-Will
woven** — lives in that one List, so an affix beyond the count cannot exist, and a
byte past the count is the next serialised field (Omen / Woven / altar payload),
not an affix. `count == 0` legitimately means "no affixes" (1134 of 2746 measured
items); the game guards it identically (`if (count != 0)`). **Do not reintroduce a
fixed slot window and do not clamp the count.** Distinct byte and distinct site
from the legendary count (`d[BASE+17] & 7`, `import-fused-affix-overrun`) — the
two paths never intersect; do not conflate them.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| affix-loop bound | `src/Classes/ImportTab.lua` `ReadJsonSaveData` (`rarity < 5` branch) | `for i = 0, serialisedAffixCount - 1` — reads exactly the declared count, was `for i = 0, 6` |
| kind tagging | same loop | positional tagging no longer needs its own `i < serialisedAffixCount` test; the loop bound enforces it |
| slot-7 overflow probe | same branch | **removed** — no window left to overflow; it would now manufacture false `[IMPORT-DROP]` reports from payload bytes |
| sibling spec fixtures | `spec/System/TestImportAffixIdCeilingPhantom_spec.lua`, `TestImportIdolAffixNamespacePhantom_spec.lua`, `TestImportWWIdolAffixOverimport_spec.lua` | their synthetic records set `d[12] = #affixRecords` instead of a hardcoded `0`; an item that declares 0 affixes but carries affix bytes is not a realizable save, and the bounded loop reads none of it |

**Files:** `src/Classes/ImportTab.lua`
**Invariant:** a non-unique item imports exactly `d[BASE+8] & 0x3f` affixes — no
slot at or past the declared count is ever decoded, and no declared slot is skipped.
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestImportNonUniqueAffixCount_spec.lua`
- "must not import trailing payload that decodes to resolvable affixes (count=2)"
- "count=0 must import no affixes even when trailing bytes resolve"
- "count must be masked out of the packed flag byte (0x80|2 -> 2 affixes)"
- "count must be masked out of the packed flag byte (0x40|1 -> 1 affix)"
- "count=6 must import all 6 declared affixes"

### `import-affix-id-ceiling-phantom`

Sibling to `import-fused-affix-overrun`. The offline-save binary item parser
(`ImportTabClass:ReadJsonSaveData`, non-unique affix-loop path) reads a fixed
7 affix slots per item (`dataId = BASE + 10 + i*3`) and filters each decode
against `data.itemMods.Item[modId]`. **Omen Idols / Woven idols / Prophesied
Altars serialize extra "omen" bytes AFTER their real affixes**, and the
fixed-slot loop reads those trailing bytes as bogus 3-byte affix triples. They
decode to affixIds far beyond the game's real affix registry (1.4.7 tops out at
affixId **1112**) with impossible tiers (>7), are correctly rejected — but were
counted as *silently dropped affixes*, inflating the user-facing "N affix(es)
dropped" message and (worse) **repeatedly misleading DPS-gap investigations into
hunting non-existent >1112 idol/altar affixes**.

Root-caused on the Maxroll Hammerdin (`Xiemiel_blank`): the ~−11% Hammer Throw
physical per-hit under-read was hypothesised across sessions to come from 6
"silently dropped" idol/altar affixes (`1822_1`/`1835_12` on a Large Iron Omen
Idol, `3224_7`/`2343_5` on a Heretical Rahyeh Idol, `3238_1` on a Prophesied
Altar — all affixId > 1112). Datamine of the current 1.4.7 assets proved the
game's ENTIRE affix registry (`AffixList` singleAffixes 578 + multiAffixes 534,
`filteredSingle/MultiAffixes` **empty**, all idol affixes 105-1112) maxes at
affixId 1112; LEB's own `ModItem`/`ModIdol` data maxes at 1112 too. So **no
affix can decode above the ceiling** — anything larger is a mis-decode of
non-affix bytes. The drop-idols' *real* affixes (verified via
`ProbeHammerAddedSources`: 1043 Slow-Immunity, 199 Throwing-Crit-Multi, 212
Armor-Shred, 892 Crit, 226 Aspect-of-Shark, 1054 Stun-Avoidance) grant **no
flat added damage**, so the phantom drops carry **zero** damage — the phys
under-read is a *separate* small systematic throwing-added residual (present on
`SUNDAY_blank`, which has zero dropped affixes), not a >1112 coverage gap. This
generalises to earlier "datamine-blocked >1112 affix" claims (Firebrand `2891`,
Golem `2690`/`3341`/`3641`): those are the same phantom over-read, not missing
data.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| ceiling derivation | `src/Classes/ImportTab.lua` `ReadJsonSaveData` (before the `savedItems` loop, ~line 1780) | `maxKnownAffixId` = max numeric prefix over `data.itemMods.Item` keys (≈1112). Derived from data, not hard-coded, so it self-updates if the mod tables gain higher ids. |
| classification | `src/Classes/ImportTab.lua` affix-loop else-branch (~line 1990) | `affixId > maxKnownAffixId` → `[IMPORT-OVERREAD]` (logged, **not** counted in `_droppedAffixes`); `affixId <= ceiling` and missing → `[IMPORT-DROP]` (still counted, a genuine possible data gap). Imported affixes are untouched — this only reclassifies rejected decodes. |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestImportAffixIdCeilingPhantom_spec.lua`
- "derives a registry ceiling matching the datamined 1.4.7 max (1112)"
- "does NOT count an above-ceiling decode as a dropped affix (phantom over-read)"
- "STILL counts an at-or-below-ceiling missing affix as a dropped affix"
- "imports a real below-ceiling affix normally (the loop is genuinely exercised)"
- "mixes valid + phantom on one item: valid imports, phantom not counted"

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `import-save-affix-kind`

Offline-save import never populated `affix.kind`, so every save-imported affix arrived as
`kind = nil` and LEB could not tell a sealed / primordial / corrupted affix from a normal
one. (The LETools path was unaffected — it sets `kind` from which JSON field the affix
arrived in.) The save DOES carry the information; it is just not in the 3-byte affix triple,
which is why the old decoder could not see it. The sealed state is packed into the
affix-count byte, and which affix is which is POSITIONAL, not per-affix data.

Not merely cosmetic: with `kind` nil a sealed/primordial/corrupted affix wrongly contributed
to the affix-derived req.level, which can push an item past the CalcSetup LevelReq filter and
silently drop it from the build.

**Sites:**

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `src/Classes/ImportTab.lua` | reads the count byte at `BASE+8`; tags kind positionally |
| `spec/System/TestImportSaveAffixKind_spec.lua` | 10 cases; 6 fail on the pre-fix decoder |

### `import-idol-affix-namespace-phantom`

Companion to `import-affix-id-ceiling-phantom` for the **SUB-ceiling** case. The
ceiling guard only rejects decodes `> 1112`. But an idol's trailing Woven/Omen
payload can also decode to an affixId that lands `<= 1112` yet is **not an idol
affix** — it is an EQUIPMENT affix id bleeding onto the idol. Root-caused on the
Golem `ACG-3_blank` Minor Weaver Idols: decoded affixId **597** ("Mage Level of
Shatter Strike", tier 9) and **545** ("Primalist Level of Summon Frenzy Totem",
tier 12) — class-specific *+Level of Skill* EQUIPMENT (`multiAffixes`) ids that
cannot roll on an idol. At those impossible tiers they miss `data.itemMods.Item`,
fell to the else-branch, and were counted as genuine `[IMPORT-DROP]` — inflating
the "N affix(es) dropped" message exactly like the >1112 phantoms (this was the
false basis of the "Golem 5%-vs-10% minion-crit = dropped affix" claim, now
refuted).

The distinguishing signal: a real idol affix id is a member of the **idol-affix
namespace**. The pool is built once from LEB's OWN idol mod data (the per-idol-base
tables under `data.itemMods` — `Small/Minor/…/Huge Idol` — which all point at
`ModIdol_<ver>.flat`), so it self-updates with the mod tables and is not
hard-coded. **Datamine cross-check** (`datamined game source`):
LEB's grid-idol id-set (469 ids) equals the datamine `single_idol_affixes` +
`multi_idol_affixes` pool (489 ids) **exactly, minus the 20 "Idol Altar …" affixes
1088-1109** (`canRollOn` baseType 41), which live in LEB's separate `Idol Altar`
table and roll only on the Idol Altar (container 123), never on a grid idol
(container 29). Hence the check is applied to **grid idols only (`containerID ==
29`)**: equipment legitimately carries 545/597, and altars legitimately carry
1088-1109, so gating on container 29 false-rejects neither.

Verified through the real Lua import path (`ReadJsonSaveData` on the actual
`.epoch` saves): ACG-3 Golem `_droppedAffixes` **2 → 0** (the two 545/597 payload
mis-reads reclassified) with the change vs. only the ceiling guard; Hammerdin
`SUNDAY_blank` unchanged at 0 and `Xiemiel_blank` unchanged at 1 (its genuine
in-pool altar affix `1031_2` drop correctly preserved). Logging/diagnostic-only —
imported items, DPS and snapshots are unchanged (the IMPORT-OK branch is untouched;
only the rejected-decode reclassification differs), so **no snapshot regen**.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| idol pool derivation | `src/Classes/ImportTab.lua` `ReadJsonSaveData` (beside the ceiling derivation, ~line 1807) | `idolAffixPool` = set of numeric prefixes over the `data.itemMods[<idol base>]` tables. Data-derived (self-updating), `pairs()` walks only the raw idol keys (not the `__index=ModItem` fallback). |
| classification | `src/Classes/ImportTab.lua` affix-loop, new `elseif` after the `> ceiling` branch (~line 2020) | `itemData.containerID == 29` (grid idol) **and** `not idolAffixPool[affixId]` → `[IMPORT-OVERREAD]` (logged, **not** counted). Equipment (container ≠ 29) and in-pool idol affixes at impossible tiers still `[IMPORT-DROP]`. |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestImportIdolAffixNamespacePhantom_spec.lua`
- "builds a non-empty idol-affix pool that is a strict subset of the registry"
- "(a) imports a real in-pool idol affix normally (0 dropped)"
- "(a) STILL counts a genuine in-pool idol affix missing at its decoded tier as a drop"
- "(c) reclassifies a sub-ceiling non-idol-namespace decode on an IDOL as over-read (not counted)"
- "(b) an EQUIPMENT affix (eqId at a real tier) imports normally on an equipment item"
- "(b) the idol namespace gate does NOT apply to equipment: eqId missing at its tier still DROPs"
- "(d) preserves the >ceiling phantom behavior on an idol (over-read, not counted)"
- "mixes a real in-pool affix + a payload mis-read on one idol: real imports, phantom not counted"
