### `total-dot-dps-row`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestTotalDotDPSRow_spec.lua`
- guard marker in Calcs.lua + Build.lua
- Calcs.lua computes `output.MainSkillDotDPS = mainAilmentTotal + skill-DoT`
- must NOT use PoB "Best"/max ailment semantics (LE ailments stack)
- Build.lua "Total DoT DPS" row backed by `MainSkillDotDPS`
- condFunc hides redundant single-source cases
- placed above "Total DPS inc. Ailments"

**Sites:** `src/Modules/Calcs.lua` (`calcs.buildOutput`, after `MainSkillWithAilmentsDPS`)
+ `src/Modules/Build.lua` (`self.displayStats`, after the per-ailment rows).

**Why:** user-requested PoB-parity "Total DoT DPS" upper-panel row (2026-06-09).
**LE-correctness is the point:** PoB shows "Best Ignite/Bleed DPS" (the single
strongest source) because PoE ailments are NON-stacking; **LE ailments STACK**, so
the LE-correct aggregation is a **TOTAL (sum)**, which LEB already computes per-
ailment via `calcs.aggregateMainSkillAilment` (with per-ailment `maxStacks` clamp,
`CalcOffence.lua:2149-2159`). `output.MainSkillDotDPS` = sum of the main skill's
damaging-ailment DPS + the skill's own DoT when it is itself a DoT skill
(`skillFlags.dot` → `output.TotalDPS` IS the DoT). **"DoT" is LE-native vocabulary**
(`AT_DoT` / StatsPanel "Damage Over Time"), not a PoE-only term — see wiki
`concepts/le-dot-vs-ailment-and-stacking`. The row is **display-only** (new output
key, snapshot-safe like the sibling `MainSkill<Ailment>DPS` keys — no DPS/EHP
impact). The condFunc hides it when it would merely duplicate the Hit DPS (pure DoT
skill, no ailments) or a single ailment row (shown only when 2+ DoT sources).
**Regression to prevent:** copying PoB's "Best"/max semantic (would undercount LE
stacking ailments), or mislabeling a hit skill's pure-hit DPS as DoT.

### `main-skill-ailment-upper-panel`

Generalizes the original Ignite-only upper panel (`main-skill-ignite-upper-panel`)
to EVERY damaging ailment in `data.damagingAilment`. LEB imports each damaging
ailment as a SEPARATE active skill (entry name == the ailment name e.g.
`Ignite`/`Bleed`/`Poison`/`Damned`, `trigger` = parent skill name). Verified on a
Warlock Soul Feast build: `output.SkillDPS` carried `Damned 1099.96`, `Ignite
360.22`, `Poison 42.39` (all `trigger="Soul Feast"`) while only Ignite had been
surfaced before — Damned (the biggest contributor) and Poison were invisible in
the upper panel.

The pure helper `calcs.aggregateMainSkillAilment(output, skillDPSList,
mainSkillName, ailmentName)` reconstructs one named ailment's main-skill total.
**Critical no-double-count rule:** when separate-skill entries match
(`name == ailmentName and trigger == mainSkillName`) their `dps*count` sum IS the
canonical full contribution (it equals `FullDPS - TotalDPS` across all ailments),
so the helper uses ONLY that sum. `output[ailmentName.."DPS"]` is the parent hit's
own partial value already folded inside that entry — adding it double-counts
(Warlock proof: `output.DamnedDPS` 467 was already inside the 1100 Damned entry,
and the buggy seed-then-add produced 1567, pushing the panel total above FullDPS).
The helper falls back to `output[ailmentName.."DPS"]` ONLY when no separate entry
matches (ailment carried directly on the parent's output). `aggregateMainSkillIgnite`
is now a thin wrapper calling this with `"Ignite"`.

`calcs.buildOutput` loops over `data.damagingAilment`, publishes
`MainSkill<Ailment>DPS` for each present ailment, and a single roll-up
`MainSkillWithAilmentsDPS = TotalDPS + Σ(all main-skill ailments)` (verified to
equal FullDPS for the single-skill Warlock). `MainSkillWithIgniteDPS` is still
published for backward compatibility but no longer has its own display row (it
would duplicate "Total DPS inc. Ailments" when Ignite is the only ailment).

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| pure helper | `src/Modules/Calcs.lua` `calcs.aggregateMainSkillAilment` (before `calcs.calcFullDPS`) | per-ailment aggregator; entries-only when matched, else `output[..DPS]` fallback |
| publish | `src/Modules/Calcs.lua` `calcs.buildOutput` (after `output.FullDPS`) | loops `data.damagingAilment`, sets `MainSkill<Ailment>DPS` + `MainSkillWithAilmentsDPS` |
| display rows | `src/Modules/Build.lua` `self.displayStats` (after 2nd "Hit DPS", before CombinedDPS) | 8 conditional per-ailment rows (`data.ailmentTypeList` order) + "Total DPS inc. Ailments" |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestFullDPSFoldAilments_spec.lua`
- describe "aggregateMainSkillAilment (generic per-ailment)" (4 cases incl. no-double-count + fallback)
- describe "aggregateMainSkillIgnite" (4 cases, wrapper)

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `main-skill-ignite-upper-panel`

LEB imports each damaging ailment as a SEPARATE active skill (skillId
`Ailment_Ignite`, entry name `Ignite`, trigger = parent skill name). The main
hit skill therefore carries `notAilment` and computes no own ignite DPS
(`output.IgniteDPS` is nil/0 for e.g. Judgement). To show PoB-equivalent
"Ignite DPS" rows in the upper stat panel, the main skill's ignite is
reconstructed by `calcs.aggregateMainSkillIgnite`, now a thin wrapper over the
generalized `calcs.aggregateMainSkillAilment` (see `main-skill-ailment-upper-panel`
for the no-double-count rule). Two derived outputs are published:

- `MainSkillIgniteDPS`        = aggregated ignite for the main skill
- `MainSkillWithIgniteDPS`    = `TotalDPS + MainSkillIgniteDPS` (still published
  for compatibility; the displayed roll-up is now `MainSkillWithAilmentsDPS`)

The aggregator is a PURE function (no env mutation) so it is unit-testable with
synthetic inputs and cannot perturb any saved snapshot key.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| publish | `src/Modules/Calcs.lua` `calcs.buildOutput` (after `output.FullDPS`) | sets `MainSkillIgniteDPS` / `MainSkillWithIgniteDPS` |
| pure helper | `src/Modules/Calcs.lua` `calcs.aggregateMainSkillIgnite` (before `calcs.calcFullDPS`) | wrapper -> `aggregateMainSkillAilment(.., "Ignite")` |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestFullDPSFoldAilments_spec.lua`
- describe "aggregateMainSkillIgnite" (4 cases)

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `fulldps-fold-ailments-into-parent`

Because ailments import as separate active skills, the default Full DPS
breakdown shows one row per ailment ("Ignite (Judgement)", "Electrify
(Judgement)", …). The desired PoB-parity display folds every damaging-ailment
row whose `trigger` matches a parent entry's `name` back into that parent's
single displayed line (one "Judgement" line = hit + all its ailments).

The fold is done on a FRESH copied list built by `calcs.foldAilmentsIntoParents`
— `actor.output.SkillDPS` itself is left UNMUTATED. This is the load-bearing
invariant: `output.SkillDPS` is a saved snapshot key compared by deep-equal in
`TestBuilds_spec.lua`, so mutating it in-place would break every ailment build's
snapshot. Fold math preserves the grand total and the parent's `count`
(`parent.dps += ailment.dps * ailment.count / parent.count`). An ailment row
whose trigger matches no parent is kept as its own row (orphan fallback); a
skill literally named like an ailment but with empty trigger is treated as a
real parent, not folded.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| pure helper | `src/Modules/Calcs.lua` `calcs.foldAilmentsIntoParents` (before `calcs.calcFullDPS`) | returns folded copy; never mutates input |
| render | `src/Modules/Build.lua` `buildMode:AddDisplayStatList` (`statData.stat == "SkillDPS"` block, ~L1758) | calls `self.calcsTab.calcs.foldAilmentsIntoParents(actor.output.SkillDPS, data.damagingAilment)` then sorts/renders |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestFullDPSFoldAilments_spec.lua`
- describe "foldAilmentsIntoParents" (5 cases incl. input-not-mutated, orphan, no-trigger)

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `minion-ailment-upper-panel`

Minion DPS-layer counterpart to `main-skill-ailment-upper-panel`. **Key structural
difference, verified empirically (Beastmaster Summon Scorpion build):** minion
ailments are computed DIRECTLY onto the minion's OWN `output[ailmentName.."DPS"]`
(same `CalcOffence` loop, `output[ailmentName.."DPS"] = totalDPS`, gated `chance>0`)
— there is **NO** `minion.output.SkillDPS` separate-skill list, unlike the player.
The scorpion dump showed `minion.output.BleedDPS = 315.36` directly on the minion
output and an empty SkillDPS list. So minions do NOT have the player's
separate-skill gap; each minion ailment row simply reads the minion's own
`<Ailment>DPS`.

The pre-existing minion panel only carried Bleed/Ignite/Poison rows. This guard
adds the remaining five (Frostbite/Electrify/Damned/TimeRot/Doom) so the minion
panel surfaces every damaging ailment its CalcOffence loop can populate. Each new
row is gated on `v > 0`, so a minion that applies none of them is unaffected and
no TestBuilds snapshot changes.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| display rows | `src/Modules/Build.lua` `self.minionDisplayStats` (after "Total DPS inc. Poison", before "Decay DPS") | 5 conditional rows reading minion `output.<Ailment>DPS` for Frostbite/Electrify/Damned/TimeRot/Doom |
| compute (shared) | `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (`output[ailmentName.."DPS"]` loop over `data.damagingAilment`) | env-agnostic; populates the minion output keys the rows read |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestMinionAilmentRows_spec.lua`
- "minionDisplayStats has a DPS row for every damaging ailment" (all 8)
- "each ailment DPS row is gated so non-applying minions are unaffected"

### `le-defensive-sidebar-panel`

Defence-layer counterpart to the DPS-layer ailment guards. `CalcDefence` already
COMPUTES a set of LE-specific defence stats onto the player `output`, but the
sidebar (`self.displayStats`) historically never displayed them, leaving the
defence layer incomplete relative to the in-game character sheet (the sole
authority for derived stats). This guard locks the sidebar to surface them:

| Stat (output key) | Row label | Compute site (`CalcDefence.lua`) |
|---|---|---|
| `Endurance` | Endurance | `output.Endurance = m_min(endTotal, EnduranceCap)` |
| `EnduranceThreshold` | Endurance Threshold | `output.EnduranceThreshold = m_floor(etBase*etInc+0.5)` |
| `BlockEffectiveness` | Block Effectiveness | `output.BlockEffectiveness = round(blockEffectivenessRating)` |
| `GlancingBlowChance` | Glancing Blow Chance | `output.GlancingBlowChance = m_min(... ,100)` |
| `CritAvoidance` | Critical Strike Avoidance | `output.CritAvoidance = m_min(Sum BASE CritAvoidance,100)` |
| `StunAvoidance` | Stun Avoidance | `output.StunAvoidance = m_max(round(flatStunAvoidance),0)` |
| `HealingEffectiveness` | Increased Healing Effectiveness | `output.HealingEffectiveness = Sum INC HealingEffectiveness` |

Every row is gated on `v > 0` (and `EnduranceThreshold` additionally on
`Endurance > 0`, since the threshold is meaningless without endurance), so builds
with none of a given stat are unaffected. These are **presentation-only rows that
add no new output keys**, so TestBuilds snapshots are untouched (verified: the
defensive stats already existed in `output`; only their display was missing).

**`HealingEffectiveness` semantics — verified:** the in-game character sheet
labels this stat **"Increased Healing Effectiveness"** and shows the INC portion
(MyLittleStJames lv79 = 189%), which is exactly what
`modDB:Sum("INC", nil, "HealingEffectiveness")` yields. So the row is surfaced
with the label "Increased Healing Effectiveness" (NOT "Healing Effectiveness"),
matching the authority. An earlier draft excluded it pending this verification.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| display rows | `src/Modules/Build.lua` `self.displayStats` (Armor/block section) | 6 conditional rows reading the player `output` defence keys above |
| compute (existing) | `src/Modules/CalcDefence.lua` | populates the keys; unchanged by this guard |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestDefensiveSidebarPanel_spec.lua`
- "displayStats has a row for every LE-specific defence stat" (all 6)
- "each defence row is gated so builds without the stat are unaffected"
- "EnduranceThreshold row hides when Endurance is 0"
- "surfaces HealingEffectiveness as 'Increased Healing Effectiveness'"

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `s4-converted-attr-single-row`

Season 4 (1.4) converts a base attribute into a paired converted attribute
(Str→Brutality, Dex→Guile, Int→Madness, Att→Apathy, Vit→Rampancy). The sidebar
must show each converted attribute on EXACTLY ONE row, in the slot of the base
attribute it replaced. A bug had the converted attributes inserted twice: once
by the `s4AttrPair` loop (correct, in-slot) and again by a second block that
re-listed all five at the end of the attribute section — producing a duplicate
row (reported as "Madness shown twice"). The fix removes the redundant second
block; the pair loop is now the sole insertion site.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| sole insertion | `src/Modules/Build.lua` `self.displayStats` s4AttrPair loop | inserts each converted attribute once, after its base attribute row |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestS4AttrDisplayRows_spec.lua`
- exactly one displayStats row per converted attribute
- each converted attribute directly follows its base attribute

### `s4-converted-attr-source-breakdown`

When you hover a Season-4 converted attribute (Brutality/Guile/Madness/Apathy/
Rampancy) in the Calcs tab, you must be able to see WHERE its value comes from —
the same Base / Quest / item / `Set: ...` / passive-node source list the base
attribute would show — not a collapsed opaque "100% of Str converted" line with
no provenance. That per-source list is shown in the **standard per-source TABLE**
(Value / Notes / Source / Source Name) every other attribute uses — see the sister
guard `s4-converted-attr-table-from-source`, which wires the table to the source
attribute. THIS guard covers the short **textual summary** rendered above that
table by `CalcPerform`: a `<converted> (converted from <Src>)` line, a
`+ <N> (direct grants of <Dst>)` line when the destination is also granted
directly, and a `= <total>` line when more than one component contributes —
mirroring how `breakdown.simple` sits above a normal attribute's source table.
(The summary is intentionally short: the per-source detail — item names, passive
node DISPLAY names like `Might`, equipment slots — lives in the table, resolved by
`AddModSection`, so it is never duplicated as text and never shows a raw node id.)

This is a **UI/breakdown-only** change: it reads `output`/`modDB` but writes
nothing to `output`, so it is **corpus-neutral** (snapshots compare `output`, not
breakdown text — the `#builds` suite is unaffected).

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| summary text | `src/Modules/CalcPerform.lua` (converted-attribute breakdown loop, just after `RawVit` is set) | emits the short `breakdown[conv.dst]` summary: converted-from + direct-grant + total |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestS4ConvertedAttrBreakdown_spec.lua`
- the summary states the value is `converted from <Src>`
- a direct destination grant adds a `direct grants of <Dst>` line and a `= <total>` that equals `output`

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `s4-converted-attr-table-from-source`

A Season-4 converted attribute (Brutality/Guile/Madness/Apathy/Rampancy) takes its
value from the SOURCE attribute it replaced (Str/Dex/Int/Att/Vit) and has (almost)
no mods registered under its OWN name. So its Calcs-tab per-source **TABLE** must
be driven by the SOURCE attribute's `modName`, NOT its own — otherwise the table
is empty and the user sees no provenance (the original bug: hovering Brutality
showed only a collapsed text line / an empty table).

`CalcSections` builds each converted attribute row with `{ modName = <base attr> }`
(e.g. `Str` for the Brutality row, NOT `Brutality`). `AddModSection` then tabulates
the source attribute's mods and resolves each source the standard way — item names
(with rarity colour), passive-node **display names** via `build.spec.nodes[id].dn`
(so `Sentinel-31` renders as `Might`, never the raw id), and equipment slots
("Amulet", "Passive Tree", "Quest", "Base"). The result is the exact same
Value / Notes / Source / Source Name table every other attribute shows.

Because S4 attribute conversion is innately 100% in 1.4, the base attribute row is
hidden (its `output` is 0 via `haveOutput`) and the converted row carries the
table — so showing the source attribute's mods under the converted name is correct,
not a duplicate.

This is **UI/section-wiring only** — no `output` change, corpus-neutral.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| section wiring | `src/Modules/CalcSections.lua` (Attributes section, S4 `s4Pair` converted row) | `{ modName = stat }` (source attr) instead of `{ modName = conv.stat }` so the table tabulates+resolves the source attribute's per-source mods |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestS4ConvertedAttrBreakdown_spec.lua`
- all five converted rows tabulate their SOURCE attribute (`Brutality`→`Str`, `Guile`→`Dex`, `Madness`→`Int`, `Apathy`→`Att`, `Rampancy`→`Vit`)
- driving the real row through `CalcBreakdownControl:SetBreakdownData` renders a TABLE whose tree row resolves to the node display name `Might` under `Passive Tree`, and never the raw id `Sentinel-31`

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `area-level-multiplier-decoupled-from-mitigation`

The single "Enemy / Area Level" config field feeds TWO calc consumers whose
correct DEFAULTS differ, so they are decoupled:

1. **Armor / Block / Dodge mitigation** reads `env.config.enemyLevel`
   (`CalcDefence.lua`). Its default is the **character level** (via
   `ConfigTab:UpdateLevel`), which matches the in-game character sheet —
   validated against ShutFackUp lv85 and MyLittleStJames lv79. This must NOT
   regress to a flat 100.
2. **"depending on Area Level" affixes** (e.g. Cursed Veteran's Boots, affixId
   758) read `Multiplier:AreaLevel` (`ModParser.lua`). Their default is the
   endgame **area level 100** (Empowered Monolith, `Data/Bosses.lua`),
   independent of character level — a lv70 character still runs empowered
   monoliths at area level 100.

An EXPLICIT value typed into the field (`input.enemyLevel > 0`) overrides BOTH;
only the *defaults* are decoupled. The 758 affix DATA is already correct — this
guards the config wiring, not a data value.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| area-level mod | `src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` `enemyLevel` apply fn | `Multiplier:AreaLevel` defaults to 100, explicit `input.enemyLevel` overrides |
| mitigation default | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` `UpdateLevel` | `enemyLevel` mitigation default = character level (unchanged, preserved) |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestAffixRangeFixes_spec.lua`
- with no explicit value (charLevel 70): `mainEnv.config.enemyLevel == 70` while `player.modDB:GetMultiplier("AreaLevel") == 100`
- with explicit value 85: BOTH become 85

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `melee-skill-hit-flag`

LE weapon-delivery skills (melee/bow/throwing) always land a damaging hit, so
`skillFlags.hit` must be true for them. That flag gates the ENTIRE hit-damage
crit pass in CalcOffence (`if skillModList:Flag(cfg, "NeverCrit") or not
skillFlags.hit then output.CritChance = 0; output.CritMultiplier = 0`), so a
missing hit flag silently zeroes a skill's crit chance AND crit multi.

`skills.json` sets `baseFlags.hit` for ~135 skills, but a handful of genuine
attacks (ShatterStrike, CinderStrike, DarkQuiver) omit it, and the PoB-era
`skillTypes` fallback NEVER fires for LE pure-melee skills: `SkillType.Attack =
Melee|Throwing|Bow` and the `band(tags,type)==type` test in DataProcess requires
ALL three bits (a Melee-only skill, bit 512, fails), `SkillType.Damage` is
undefined (nil) in the LE enum, and `SkillType.Projectile = Unsupported`. So a
Melee-only skill was left with `hit=nil`. Observed: in-game ShutFackUp Shatter
Strike shows 35% crit / 227% crit multi; LEB computed CritChance=0 /
CritMultiplier=0 before this fix (TotalDPS 9759→14186 after).

The `not skillFlags.ailment` clause excludes pure ailment-delivery skills
(`Ailment_Laceration` carries a melee flag but only applies a DoT — it does not
directly hit).

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| hit derivation | `src/Modules/CalcActiveSkill.lua` (~line 103) | `skillFlags.hit = skillFlags.hit or ((skillFlags.melee or skillFlags.bow or skillFlags.throwing) and not skillFlags.ailment) or <PoB-era skillTypes fallback>` |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestMeleeSkillHitFlag_spec.lua`
- keeps the `@leb-regression-guard:melee-skill-hit-flag` marker
- locks the `(melee or bow or throwing) and not ailment` delivery clause
- locks that the PoB-era `skillTypes[SkillType.Attack]` fallback remains
- data-locks that ShatterStrike/CinderStrike/DarkQuiver are melee+attack in skills.json
- functional: `data.skills.ShatterStrike` is melee/attack with `baseFlags.hit` unset

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `inherent-base-crit-chance`

LE gives every hit an inherent 5% base critical strike chance
(`datamined game source` `Stats.baseCritChance = 0.05`). In LEB this rides on
each skill via `skills.json` `critChance:5` → CalcActiveSkill copies it into
`activeSkill.skillData.CritChance` → CalcOffence reads it as `baseCrit`
(`source = skillData`) in `output.CritChance = (baseCrit + base) * (1 + inc/100) * more`.

**Root cause:** of the 346 skill entries with stats, only **137** declare
`critChance:5`; **~206** OMIT the field entirely (e.g. Shatter Strike, Wandering
Spirits). For those, `skillData.CritChance` was `nil` → `baseCrit = 0`, silently
dropping the inherent 5%. (3 declare a higher value — Disintegrate/Ghostflame=50,
Shadow Cascade=10 — and 0 declare an explicit zero.)

That made a missing-field melee skill's crit match the GENERIC character-sheet
value only by coincidence. Ground truth: in-game ShutFackUp lv85 Spellblade
Damage tab shows generic Critical Strike Chance 35% but **Melee** 59%; Shatter
Strike is melee, so its true crit is 59%. LEB computed 34.65% before this fix.

**The fix** defaults the nil case per-skill in CalcActiveSkill:
`activeSkill.skillData.CritChance = stats.critChance or data.misc.BaseCritChance`.
- melee Shatter Strike: `(5 inherent + 5 sword-melee + 2 Phantom) * (1+3.95) = 12*4.95 = 59.4` → 59 in-game
- generic/spell: `(5 inherent + 2 Phantom) * (1+3.95) = 7*4.95 = 34.65` → 35 in-game

**NOT a global modDB BASE seed.** An earlier attempt seeded
`modDB:NewMod("CritChance","BASE",data.misc.BaseCritChance,"Base")` in CalcSetup,
which DOUBLE-COUNTED the 137 skills already declaring `critChance:5` (5+5=10%) and
broke `TestSkills` (Lunge/Rive). Using `or` (Lua truthiness keeps `0`) at the
per-skill default touches ONLY the nil case, never the declared-5 skills and never
an explicit `critChance:0`.

`baseCritMulti = 2` (same dump) is already modelled (CritMultiplier 2.27 baseline 2.0).

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| constant | `src/Modules/Data.lua` `data.misc.BaseCritChance` | `= 5` (LE `Stats.baseCritChance` 0.05 → percent) |
| default | `src/Modules/CalcActiveSkill.lua` (in `buildActiveSkillModList`, ~line 1092) | `activeSkill.skillData.CritChance = stats.critChance or data.misc.BaseCritChance` |
| sink | `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (~line 2125/2147) | `baseCrit = critOverride or source.CritChance or 0`; `output.CritChance = (baseCrit + base) * (1 + inc/100) * more` |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestInherentBaseCritChance_spec.lua`
- keeps the `@leb-regression-guard:inherent-base-crit-chance` marker (in CalcActiveSkill)
- asserts `data.misc.BaseCritChance == 5`

### `trigger-chance-to-cast-on-hit-bridge`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestTriggerChanceToCastOnHit_spec.lua`
- "'8% Chance to cast Axe Throw on hit' emits functional ChanceToTriggerOnHit_AxeThrow"
- "the triggered-skill id is the data.skills KEY, not the spaced name"
- "the emitted trigger mod is global (no SkillName scope) so any source skill sums it"
- "no stale 'Chance To Cast Axe Throw On Hit' row short-circuits the parser"
- "ModParser builds skillIdByLower and bridges on-hit to ChanceToTriggerOnHit_"
- "CalcSetup consumes ChanceToTriggerOnHit_<skillId> into grantedTriggeredSkills"

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (the `skillIdByLower` map built alongside
`skillNameByLower`, and the `onHitTriggerBridge` handler registered for
`"X% chance to cast <skill> on hit"`) + `src/Data/ModCache.lua` (the stale
`8% Chance To Cast Axe Throw On Hit` row pruned so it re-parses live). Consumer is
the PRE-EXISTING `src/Modules/CalcSetup.lua` `grantedTriggeredSkills` loop +
`src/Modules/CalcTriggers.lua`.

**Why:** the first general slice of the trigger-skill DPS pipeline (S2). LEB could
not contribute passive/affix-triggered skills to Full DPS. ModParser recognised
`"X% chance to cast <skill> on hit"` only as `ChanceToCast_<SkillNoSpaces>`
(SkillName + Condition tags, `notSupported=true`) — a mod NOTHING consumed — while
LEB's existing trigger framework consumes a DIFFERENT, never-emitted mod
`ChanceToTriggerOnHit_<skillId>` (the data.skills KEY). The bridge emits that
functional, GLOBAL mod (no SkillName scope, so each source skill's `skillModList`
sums it); `CalcTriggers` then derives the trigger rate from the source skill's
hit rate × this chance — uptime is build-derived, not fabricated.

**Scope / faithfulness:** only the bare `on hit$` form is bridged. Rate-capped
variants (`... up to N times per M seconds`, cooldowns) and tag-stripped forms
(`on melee hit`) are intentionally NOT bridged here — their rate cannot be derived
without fabrication. Builds without such an affix are unaffected (no
`ChanceToTriggerOnHit_` mod → the existing consumer loop is a no-op). End-to-end
Full-DPS verification against a build that actually fires an on-hit trigger (e.g.
a Static Orb build) is the S4 rollout step; this guard locks the recognition→
consumption bridge and its no-op safety. See the LEB-0.13.2 trigger design note.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestTriggerRateCap_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (capped variants of the bridged conditions —
on hit / on melee hit — emit the base functional mod PLUS a global
`TriggerRateCapPerSecond_<skillId>` = limit/interval) + `src/Modules/CalcSetup.lua`
(the `grantedTriggeredSkills` entry attaches `triggerRateCapPerSecond` via
`env.modDB:Sum(... TriggerRateCapPerSecond_<id>)`, carried onto the group →
srcInstance) + `src/Modules/CalcTriggers.lua` (gated block:
`output.TriggerRateCap = m_min(output.TriggerRateCap, srcInst.triggerRateCapPerSecond)`)
+ `src/Data/ModCache.lua` (stale `Smite on Melee hit (up to 3 times per second)` row pruned).

**Why & game backing:** LE rate-limits triggered casts with a **ProcTimeTracker**
(`datamined game source` L239352, TypeDefIndex 6250: `int limit` / `float interval` /
`recentProcTimes[]` / `CanProc()` / `TryProc()`) — at most `limit` procs per
`interval` seconds, so the effective cap = **limit/interval**. Affix text maps:
"(up to N times per second)"→N, "(up to N times per M seconds)"→N/M,
"(K second cooldown)" = PTT(1,K)→1/K. datamined game source also shows explicit cooldown consts
(`chanceToCastVolcanicOrbOnFirebrandHitCooldown = 3` L41653) — same max-rate. LEB's
default handler previously only narrowed `TriggerRateCap` via `maxStacks`, so an
affix-specified cap was silently ignored; this adds the missing cap (PoB applies
1/cooldown analogously). Gated on `srcInstance.triggerRateCapPerSecond` so no
existing trigger is affected.

**Scope:** only the capped on-hit / on-melee-hit forms with clean skill names
(e.g. Smite); decorated forms with positional/element qualifiers (`stationary fire
Tornado at a nearby enemy ...`) are not matched (no functional pattern registered).
No corpus build carries a clean capped trigger → zero ripple. Cap forms on on-crit
/ when-hit await those base conditions. End-to-end Full-DPS verification awaits a

### `skillidbylower-prefer-player`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestSkillIdByLowerPreferPlayer_spec.lua`
- "treeId distinguishes the player id from its homonyms (data invariant)"
- "the real affix bridges to ChanceToTriggerCapped_LightningBlast (player id), NOT StormCrowLightningBlast"
- "'Lightning Blast on hit' -> player LightningBlast (not StormCrowLightningBlast)"
- "'Surge on hit' -> player Surge (not 'RogueFalcon Diving Attack')"
- "'Bone Curse on hit' -> player BoneCurse (not Ailment_BoneCurse)"
- "'Spirit Plague on hit' -> player SpiritPlague (not Ailment_SpiritPlague)"
- "repeated parsing resolves the same player id every time"

**Site:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (the `skillNameByLower` / `skillIdByLower`
construction `do` block, ~L1215). Inline marker `@leb-regression-guard:skillidbylower-prefer-player`.

**Why:** `data.skills` contains duplicate skill NAMES — a player skill plus
minion/enemy/ailment homonyms (verified groups: Lightning Blast = `LightningBlast` vs
`StormCrowLightningBlast`; Surge = `Surge` vs `RogueFalcon Diving Attack`; Bone Curse,
Spirit Plague, Arcane Ascendance each vs an `Ailment_*` variant; plus name-only groups
Maul / Melee Attack / Aspect of the Shark / Abyssal Decay / Runebolt with no distinct
player winner). The old `for skillId, skill in pairs(data.skills)` build collapsed each
name to ONE id whose identity depended on `pairs()` iteration order — NON-DETERMINISTIC
across processes. Every trigger bridge resolving a skill by name (`skillIdByLower[lower]`
— the on-hit/on-melee-hit/on-spell-cast bridges, the cooldown `globalCapped` bridge, and
the qualified on-crit rate-cap bridge) could therefore inject the MINION's skill into
Full DPS instead of the player's. The real affix "Lightning Blast on Crit with Frost
Claw" bridging to minion `StormCrowLightningBlast` is a concrete in-game-accuracy bug.

**Fix / heuristic:** iterate `data.skills` keys in SORTED order and, on a name collision,
prefer the id whose skill owns a player skill tree (`data.skills[id].treeId`). `treeId` is
a data-driven signal — set ONLY for player-usable skills; every minion/enemy/ailment
homonym enumerated in `src/Data/skills.json` has `treeId == nil` (NOT a name-prefix
denylist). Higher rank wins; on equal rank the sorted-first id wins, which is identical
across processes. The only multi-`treeId` collision ("Runebolt" = three same-`treeId`
color variants) has no distinct player winner, so the sorted tie-break is correct.

"Fire Damage" with a "Burst" residue, now skill-scopes via the
`skill-scoped-damage-idol-tag` mechanism).

**Why:** S1 of the trigger-skill DPS pipeline. These four triggered sub-skills
were absent from `skills.json`, so the game could not contribute them to Full

runtime/mutator-internal — `EnchantWeaponMutator.zap/fireBurst` resolved by

mirrors the game files: its Lightning Blast = `21 Lightning / eff 1.0 / tags 258
/ Int 4% / mana 3` is byte-identical to LEB's verified entry. Each same-named
variant (there are 3 distinct "Fire Burst" abilities) was disambiguated against
the in-game corpus tooltips by added-damage effectiveness:

| key | LETools internal (index) | base | eff | tags | corpus eff |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| FireBurst | enchantWeaponFireExplosion (803) | 40 Fire | 2.0 | 264 | 200% ✓ |
| Zap | lightningTendril (301) | 50 Lightning | 2.5 | 258 | 250% ✓ |
| IceSpike | icicle (519) | 60 Cold | 3.0 | 260 | 300% ✓ |
| ManaArc | mageLightning (512) | 20 Lightning | 1.5 | 258 | (819 dps) |
| DivineBolt | divineBolt (213) | 20 Fire | 1.0 | 264 | (Attunement-scaled) |
| WindTempest | physTempest (767) | 7.5 Physical | 0.375 | 4353 | (skill-tree on-hit trigger) |

WindTempest is a SKILL-TREE node trigger ("chance to cast Wind Tempest on hit").
Skill-tree / passive-tree node mod text flows through the SAME `modLib.parseMod`
(`PassiveTree.lua` parses each node mod line, then `node.modList:AddMod`), so the
on-hit bridge is source-agnostic: allocated-node "chance to cast X on hit"
triggers (Axe Throw, Storm Bolt, Wind Tempest) emit the functional trigger mod
exactly like affixes. Tree triggers with other conditions (on melee / when hit /
when you / per second / towards) are NOT bridged (engine work, pending TestBuilds).

DivineBolt is a trigger-affix skill the user did NOT capture in-game; verified on
the LETools `/skills/divine_bolt` page (20 Fire, eff 100%, "Per point of
Attunement: 4% increased Damage", tags 264). A full enumeration of every
trigger-cast skill referenced by LEB affixes/idols/uniques (diffed against
`data.skills`) found that beyond the 5 added here, the remaining missing ones are
NOT simple direct-damage skills: Poison Nova / Avalanche Boulder (no
`baseDamageStats` — ailment/sub-projectile), Freezing Concoction (zero damage),
Healing Nova (heal), and Summon Forged Weapon / Bee / Storm Totem (minions —
separate pipeline). They are intentionally not added as hit skills.

In-game-cross-validated (corpus = in-game ground truth, LETools = agreeing
cross-check), not LETools-alone. "Mana Storm" is not a standalone ability (no
datamined game source class) — intentionally absent. With these present, `skillIdByLower`
resolves them and the on-hit bridge emits functional triggers.

can change Full DPS of builds that own such an idol/affix. System suite is green
(1089) but the cross-build numeric ripple must be confirmed against the
TestBuilds corpus (absent in worktrees). The re-tagging is a correctness
improvement (scopes the bonus to the right skill instead of leaking globally).

### `deterministic-skill-stat-merge-order`

`calcs.mergeSkillInstanceMods` must iterate a granted effect's `stats` table in a
STABLE (sorted-key) order, never raw `pairs()` order.

Several stat keys map to the SAME `skillData` key: e.g. `None_base_fire_damage`,
`spell_base_fire_damage`, `melee_base_fire_damage` and `throwing_base_fire_damage`
all map to `SkillData "FireDamage"` (`SkillStatMap.lua`). `CalcActiveSkill` then
populates `skillData` with a **last-wins** assignment
(`skillData[value.key] = value.value`). Lua randomises string-key hash order per
process, so raw `pairs()` made the winning value nondeterministic across runs.

<private build> lv81 Runemaster's Flame Rush declares BOTH `None_base_fire_damage = 20`
and `spell_base_fire_damage = 40`. Run-to-run the base fire damage flipped 20↔40
(`FireDamageBase` 128↔148), cascading into `FullDPS` / `Lightning*Average` /
`StunChance` / EHP families and producing the flaky `TestBuilds_spec` snapshot
mismatches (symptom: ~15 FullDPS-family keys wobbling 1/2/15/39 failures across
suite runs). Sorting the keys makes the delivery-tagged `spell_*` value
deterministically win over the generic `None_*` value, matching the in-game spell
base damage (40 → `FireDamageBase` = 40 + 54×2 = 148).

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| stat merge | `src/Modules/CalcActiveSkill.lua` (~line 60, `mergeSkillInstanceMods`) | Collects `stats` keys, `table.sort`, then iterates — deterministic insertion order for the level mods, so the downstream last-wins `skillData` extraction is deterministic |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestSkillStatMergeDeterminism_spec.lua`
- "colliding base-damage stat keys resolve deterministically to the delivery-tagged value"

**Delivery-tag collision audit (2026-05-27).** The sorted-key + last-wins rule
decides the winner by ASCII order of the FULL stat key. For base-damage tags the
first char ranks `None`(N=78) < `bow`(b=98) < `melee`(m=109) < `spell`(s=115) <
`throwing`(t=116), so the alphabetical-LAST (winning) tag has priority
**throwing > spell > melee > bow > None**. That ordering is alphabetical, NOT
semantic — it is only LE-faithful if, for every skill, its highest-ranked
*present* base-damage tag is also the tag matching its delivery type.

A full sweep of `src/Data/skills.json` was run (every skill's `stats`; there are
no per-level `stats` blocks, and `dot_base_*_damage` keys have NO `SkillStatMap`
entry so they never collide). The complete base-damage→`SkillData` map is
`SkillStatMap.lua` lines 63–80. Result:

> **Exactly ONE collision skill exists: `Runemaster 06 Flame Rush`**
> (`None_base_fire_damage=20` + `spell_base_fire_damage=40` → `SkillData FireDamage`).
> Its delivery is `spell`; alphabetical-last winner is `spell`=40. **MATCH** — the
> in-game spell base (40 → `FireDamageBase` 148) is reproduced. **0 mismatches.**

So alphabetical-last is coincidentally LE-faithful for all current collisions and
the sorted-key fix is kept as-is (no delivery-priority logic needed yet).

**Latent risk for future data:** the rule would be WRONG for a not-yet-existing
skill that declares two same-type base-damage tags where the delivery tag is NOT
the highest-ranked present one — e.g. a **melee** skill with both
`melee_base_*` and `spell_*` (alpha-last picks `spell`, should be `melee`), or a
**bow** skill with `bow_*` + `spell_*`. If `skills.json` ever gains such a skill,
replace the alphabetical sort with explicit delivery-tag priority (pick the tag
matching the skill's `baseFlags` delivery). Re-run the audit when adding skills.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `build-output-wipes-global-cache`

`CalcsTab:BuildOutput()` must wipe `GlobalCache` at its start so each build's
output is independent of whatever build was calculated before it.

`GlobalCache.cachedData` is keyed by `cacheSkillUUID` (`Common.lua`), which is
build-AGNOSTIC — `"<skillName>_<slot>_<groupIdx>"` for a socket-group skill, or
just the skill name otherwise. No build identity is encoded. The interactive app
keeps this safe by wiping the cache on every rebuild (`Build.lua` `buildFlag`
path). The snapshot harness (`TestBuilds_spec.lua`) and snapshot generator
(`GenerateBuilds14.lua` socket-group cycling) call `BuildOutput` directly,
bypassing that wipe, so stale ailment / sub-skill entries from a PREVIOUS build
leaked in.

<private build> lv100 Bladedancer's Frailty enemy-damage debuff read another build's
cached `MaxStacks` (the Frailty stack-count `Multiplier` feeding the enemy "less
Damage" debuff), so its incoming-hit model (`*EnemyDamageMult`) shifted and
`TotalEHP` dropped 18053 → 15852 depending on suite load order — an
order-dependent flake across ~45 EHP / damage-taken keys. Confirmed by bisect:
predecessors `<private build> lv100 Bladedancer` and `BurningMyWood lv83 Beastmaster`
both reproduced the drop; after the wipe, 0 contaminating predecessors remain.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| build output | `src/Classes/CalcsTab.lua` (~line 437, `BuildOutput`) | `wipeGlobalCache()` before the MAIN/CALCS passes; cache is then repopulated and shared WITHIN this BuildOutput as intended |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestBuildOutputCacheIsolation_spec.lua`
- "BuildOutput wipes stale cross-build GlobalCache entries before computing"

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `doubled-if-X-tree-notscaling`

Generic doubling mechanism for tree-node `notScalingStats` lines of the form
` Doubled if <X>`. A 2026-05-28 audit of all 1.4 trees turned up exactly three
nodes that use this pattern:

| Node | Stats (scaled) | notScalingStats | X | Description (game) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ch0fs-20` Death from Below | `+5% Damage` (×pts) | ` Doubled if Cursed` | Cursed | "This effect is doubled if you are cursed." |
| `ch0fs-14` Eradication | `+8% Damage to Rares and Bosses` (×pts) | ` Doubled if Cursed` | Cursed | "This effect is doubled if the enemy or you are cursed." |
| `srtor-11` Taste for Flesh | `+6% Attack And Cast Speed` (×pts) | ` Doubled if Killed Recently` | Killed Recently | (Doubled if killed recently.) |

The literal " Doubled if X" strings stay baked as empty no-op lists in
`src/Data/ModCache.lua` (`{{}, "Doubled if X "}`). The semantics is owned by
`PassiveTree.lua:ProcessStats`: after the per-line `parseMod` pass it scans
`node.sd` for the doubling pattern, maps `X` to a player Condition var, and
attaches `{type="Condition", var=<var>, mult=2}` as a tag on every scaling mod
the node emits. `ModStore.lua:607-621` (guard `condition-tag-mult`) then
delivers `value` when the matching `condition<X>` config toggle in
`ConfigOptions.lua` is OFF and `value * 2` when ON — exact in-game "doubled"
semantics without zeroing out the base contribution.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| scan | `src/Classes/PassiveTree.lua` (in `ProcessStats`, just before the AddMod loop) | Walks `node.sd`, matches `Doubled if X`, builds `doublingTag` |
| apply | `src/Classes/PassiveTree.lua` (inside the AddMod inner loop) | If `doublingTag` is set, appends a fresh copy of the tag table to each scaling mod before `node.modList:AddMod` |
| evaluate | `src/Classes/ModStore.lua:607-621` (`condition-tag-mult` guard) | Treats the tag's `mult` as a multiplier on `value` instead of a full gate |

Mapping rules implemented (extensible — the scan logs nothing unrecognised, the
mod simply stays at base):

| notScalingStats text | Resulting tag | Triggered by config |
|---|---|---|
| ` Doubled if Cursed` | `{type="Condition", var="Cursed", mult=2}` | `conditionCursed` (Are you Cursed?) |
| ` Doubled if Killed Recently` | `{type="Condition", var="KilledRecently", mult=2}` | `conditionKilledRecently` (Have you Killed Recently?) |

Intentional limitations (documented in the inline comment block in
`PassiveTree.lua` and recapped here so a future regression isn't mistaken for
a bug in this handler):

* **`ch0fs-14` Eradication contributes nothing until rare/boss conditional
  damage is implemented system-wide.** Its scaling stat `+8% Damage to Rares
  and Bosses` parses with a non-empty `extra = "  to Rares and Bosses "` which
  fails the `mod.extra == ""` gate in the `AddMod` loop. The doubling tag is
  attached if the parse ever lands, but until then the mod is dropped before
  it reaches `node.modList`.
* **`ch0fs-14`'s `description` reads "doubled if the enemy or you are cursed"
  (OR semantics), but its `notScalingStats` line is plain ` Doubled if Cursed`
  — same as `ch0fs-20` (player-only)** — so the generic handler maps both
  uniformly to player `Condition:Cursed`. The "or enemy" half is not encoded
  in the notScalingStats string and is therefore out of this handler's
  textual scope.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestDoubledIfXTreeNotScaling_spec.lua`
- "PassiveTree.lua holds the doublingTag scan and the per-mod append"
- "ModCache keeps the literal ' Doubled if X' strings as empty no-ops"
- "ModStore Condition-tag with mult=2 returns base when unset and 2*base when set (contract)"
- "ModStore.lua holds the condition-tag-mult contract this spec depends on"
- "game-file: the three known tree nodes carry the expected stats and 'Doubled if X' notScalingStats"

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `config-highlight-suggest-pattern`

**Why a separate mechanism, not just more `suggestBuff` entries:** `suggestBuff`
maps each entry to a single buff name in `buffDetectPatterns` and excludes any
stat that mentions "while you have" / "if you have" (intentional — it detects
buff *grants*, not *consumption*). The configs we want to highlight here
(`conditionCursed`, `conditionEnemyCursed`, `conditionKilledRecently`,
`multiplierCurseOnSelf`, `multiplierEnemyCurseStacks`) are about the
player/enemy *being in* a condition, so the consumption phrasing (" Doubled if
Cursed", "while cursed", "against cursed enemies") IS the relevance signal —
the suggestBuff filter would suppress it. `suggestPattern` runs without that
filter on a separately-cached, lower-cased corpus of every allocated node's
`node.sd` line and does a plain (non-regex) substring match per pattern.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| corpus walk + matcher | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (`getAllocNodeTextCorpusLowered`, `detectMatchingPattern`, just after `detectGrantedBuffs`) | One-pass lowered text gather across `build.spec.allocNodes`; plain substring match per config's pattern list (OR semantics) |
| render hook | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (parallel `if varData.suggestPattern then` block right after the `suggestBuff` block) | Paints the label `^xFFAA00` and adds a tooltip line when matched-and-inactive; never mutates `self.input` |
| pattern declarations | `src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` | `suggestPattern = { ... }` on the five immediately-targeted entries (see below) |

Initial set of pattern declarations (2026-05-28):

| Entry | Pattern list (excerpt) | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| `conditionCursed` | `doubled if cursed`, `while you are cursed`, `while cursed` | ch0fs-20 Death from Below (` Doubled if Cursed` notScalingStats), other self-curse interactions |
| `multiplierCurseOnSelf` | `curse on you`, `curses on you`, `curses affecting you`, `per curse on you`, `bone curse self` | per-curse-on-self stacking |
| `conditionEnemyCursed` | `doubled if cursed`, `against cursed enemies`, `to cursed enemies`, `curse on hit`, `chance to curse` | ch0fs-14 Eradication (OR-semantics: same notScalingStats string as ch0fs-20, so both player and enemy curse configs flag), curse-application skills, "against Cursed enemies" item affixes |
| `multiplierEnemyCurseStacks` | `per curse stack`, `per curse on enemy`, `per curse on the enemy`, `for each curse` | per-curse stacking modifiers |
| `conditionKilledRecently` | `doubled if killed recently`, `killed recently`, `if you have killed` | srtor-11 Taste for Flesh (` Doubled If Killed Recently`), other "killed recently" passives |

Adding more highlights is an **append-only data change** — drop a
`suggestPattern = { ... }` field onto any other `ConfigOptions` entry and the
existing render hook picks it up. No framework change required.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConfigHighlightSuggestPattern_spec.lua`
- "ConfigTab.lua holds the corpus walker, the plain-substring matcher and the inline guard"
- "the render block highlights with the same orange ^xFFAA00 as suggestBuff"
- "the suggestPattern render block is read-only (never assigns to self.input[varData.var])"
- "five immediately-targeted ConfigOptions entries declare suggestPattern with the audited phrases"
- "game-file: 1.4 trees still carry the audited 'Doubled if X' notScalingStats this feature depends on"
- "Phase 1.5: buffDetectPatterns contains rows for every suggestBuff value declared in ConfigOptions"
- "Phase 1.5: each new pattern actually matches grant phrasing in 1.4 tree json (not just consumption)"

Phase 5 fills the *data* gap — 11 ConfigOptions entries that should highlight

### `calcdefence-enemylevel-nil-on-cross-class-import`

`CalcDefence` (`armourReductionF` / `blockMitigationF` / `dodgeChanceF` / EHP
breakdown) reads `env.config.enemyLevel`. Before this guard, the `env.config`
builder in `CalcSetup.lua` had **no** fallback for that key — it only carried
whatever lived in `build.configTab.input.enemyLevel` ∪
`build.configTab.placeholder.enemyLevel`. The companion field `env.enemyLevel`,
populated on the very next line, **did** have one (`build.configTab.enemyLevel
or m_min(data.misc.MaxEnemyLevel, 100)`). That asymmetry is the root cause: the
calc code that actually reads the level had a fragile source while the parallel
field next to it had a robust one.

In normal builds the input/placeholder pair always carries `enemyLevel`
(`defaultPlaceholderState = 100` seeded by `NewConfigSet`, then overwritten to
the character level by `ConfigTab:UpdateLevel` via `SetPlaceholder`-with-notify
in the `enemyLevel` apply). Cross-class XML import + `Save As` reproducibly
leaves both sources without the `enemyLevel` key at the moment triggered-skill
caching (`CalcSetup.lua:~2222` → `calcs.buildActiveSkill` → recursive
`initEnv("CACHE")`) rebuilds `env.config`, so the CACHE-mode defence pass on the
next `OnFrame` after Save As crashes at `CalcDefence.lua:39` ("attempt to
perform arithmetic on local 'enemyLevel' (a nil value)").

**Reproduction (in-app, user-reported 2026-05-28):**
1. Load `ShutFackUp lv85 Spellblade.xml` (Mage / Spellblade)
2. Touch the Config tab; Save
3. Import tab → `DownloadFullImport` of `YsGhostSurfing lv88 Warlock` (cross-class)
4. Repeat the import once more
5. Save As → `YsGhostSurfing lv88 Warlock.xml`
6. Next `OnFrame` → crash at `CalcDefence.lua:39`

The saved XML still records `<Placeholder name="enemyLevel" number="88"/>`, so
the write itself sees a populated placeholder; the nil arises only inside the
CACHE-mode re-read that the triggered-skill caching pass forces.

**Fix:** in `CalcSetup.lua`, after the `build.configTab.input` /
`build.configTab.placeholder` merge into `env.config`, default
`env.config.enemyLevel` along the same chain `env.enemyLevel` already uses
(`build.configTab.enemyLevel or m_min(data.misc.MaxEnemyLevel, 100)`). The
three damage-mitigation `F` functions in `CalcDefence.lua` additionally apply
`enemyLevel = enemyLevel or 100` as defense-in-depth so a future regression in
the env builder cannot crash the calc — they are entry points to the formula
and the natural last line of protection.

An EXPLICIT user-typed `input.enemyLevel > 0` still overrides the fallback (the
`if not env.config.enemyLevel or env.config.enemyLevel == 0 then` gate fires
only when the merge produced nil/0); the boss/monolith simulation override path
is unchanged.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| primary fallback   | `src/Modules/CalcSetup.lua` (just below the env.config merge) | Defaults `env.config.enemyLevel` to `build.configTab.enemyLevel` then `MaxEnemyLevel` cap when the input/placeholder merge left it nil/0 |
| defense-in-depth (armour)  | `src/Modules/CalcDefence.lua` `armourReductionF` | `enemyLevel = enemyLevel or 100` after the `armour == 0` early-return |
| defense-in-depth (block)   | `src/Modules/CalcDefence.lua` `blockMitigationF` | Same pattern, immediately above `local L = enemyLevel + 5` |
| defense-in-depth (dodge)   | `src/Modules/CalcDefence.lua` `dodgeChanceF`    | Same pattern, immediately above `local L = enemyLevel + 5` |

**Companion guard:** `area-level-multiplier-decoupled-from-mitigation` —
documents the same `env.config.enemyLevel` field's role in mitigation calcs and
guards the character-level default of `ConfigTab:UpdateLevel`. The two guards
share the field but protect different invariants: the area-level guard locks
*what value* gets routed where; this guard locks *robustness against missing
value*.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestCalcDefenceEnemyLevelDefault_spec.lua`
- source: marker present in the doc-comment above `armourReductionF`
- source: `CalcSetup.lua` carries `if not env.config.enemyLevel or env.config.enemyLevel == 0 then` followed by the configTab.enemyLevel → MaxEnemyLevel fallback chain
- source: the mirror line `env.enemyLevel = build.configTab.enemyLevel or m_min(data.misc.MaxEnemyLevel, 100)` is still present (locks the symmetry argument)
- source: each of `armourReductionF` / `blockMitigationF` / `dodgeChanceF` declares `enemyLevel = enemyLevel or 100`
- behavioural: each `F` function returns a finite cap-respecting number when called with nil enemyLevel
- behavioural: `BuildOutput` survives a configTab where both `input.enemyLevel` and `placeholder.enemyLevel` are missing (the cross-class-import surrogate state); `mainEnv.config.enemyLevel` lands in [1, 100]
- behavioural: an explicit user-supplied `input.enemyLevel = 85` round-trips unchanged (the fallback only fires on nil/0)

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `config-highlight-skill-loadout-scan`

Phase 1.6 (2026-05-29) of the Config-highlight family. Extends
`detectGrantedBuffs` in `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` to walk the active skill
bar (`build.skillsTab.socketGroupList`) alongside the original passive-tree
pass, reading `activeEffect.grantedEffect.name` per skill and matching the
lower-cased name against the same `buffDetectPatterns` table.

Motivation: Phase 1.5 (`<see git log>` / merge `<see git log>`) added a
`"profane veil"` row to `buffDetectPatterns` for symmetry with the 9
`suggestBuff` declarations in `ConfigOptions.lua`, but Profane Veil has zero
non-consumption hits in any 1.4 passive tree json — it is a Warlock active
skill, not a passive-tree-granted buff. Phase 1.5 registered the row dormant
on purpose with this Phase 1.6 pass as the intended waker.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| pass 1 (passive tree, pre-existing) | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (in `detectGrantedBuffs`, first for-loop over `build.spec.allocNodes`) | Walks node `sd`/`stats`, applies `while/if you have` filter, matches against `buffDetectPatterns` |
| pass 2 (skill loadout, new) | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (in `detectGrantedBuffs`, second block guarded by `if self.build.skillsTab and self.build.skillsTab.socketGroupList then`) | Walks each socket group's `displaySkillList`, reads `activeEffect.grantedEffect.name`, matches against the **same** `buffDetectPatterns` table. Does **NOT** apply the `while/if you have` filter (skill names are not consumption phrasing) |
| shared state | `detected` set | Both passes write to the same `detected` set; a buff matched by either path is recorded exactly once |

Key invariants the spec locks (`spec/System/TestConfigHighlightSkillLoadoutScan_spec.lua`):

1. ConfigTab.lua holds the skill-loadout scan path and the inline guard marker
2. `buffDetectPatterns` is iterated by **exactly 2 passes** (passive tree + skill loadout)
3. The skill-loadout block does **NOT** contain the `while/if you have` exclusion strings
4. Phase 1.5's ProfaneVeil row is preserved in `buffDetectPatterns` AND the corresponding `suggestBuff = "ProfaneVeil"` is preserved in ConfigOptions (the canonical case this pass wakes up)
5. The passive-tree pass STILL applies the `while/if you have` filter (Phase 1 invariant preserved, no regression)
6. `skills.json` still exposes a skill with display name "Profane Veil" — if a future patch renames it, this assertion forces revisit of the buffDetectPatterns pat

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConfigHighlightSkillLoadoutScan_spec.lua` (6 assertions, all pass)

**Effect on existing 8 entries:** Haste / Frenzy / Concentration / LightningAegis / ArcaneShield / FlameWard / EterrasBlessing / DreadShade — these already fire via Pass 1 from passive tree. Pass 2 may redundantly catch a few of them (e.g. a build with Flame Ward in skill bar), but `detected` set semantics ensure no double-write or behaviour change.

### `config-highlight-item-modlist-scan`

Phase 2 (2026-05-29) of the Config-highlight family. Extends BOTH detection
mechanisms (`suggestBuff` via `detectGrantedBuffs` and `suggestPattern` via
`getAllocNodeTextCorpusLowered`) to also walk equipped items' explicit affix
text. Item-relevance signals that previously fell through the gap — e.g.
"+12% Damage Against Cursed Enemies" / "Damage Per Curse Stack" affixes,
"while you have Haste" item mods — now fire the highlight.

Motivation: prior to Phase 2 the corpus was passive-tree-only (Phase 1) plus
skill-loadout names (Phase 1.6). Builds whose curse-relevance / buff-
relevance signal lives on an item affix were not flagged. Phase 2 closes
that gap with the same equipped-only iteration pattern used by `CalcSetup`
(`orderedSlots[*].selItemId → items[id]`), so inventory items the build is
not actually wearing are correctly excluded.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| pass 3 (items, `suggestBuff` side) | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (in `detectGrantedBuffs`, after the Phase 1.6 skill-loadout block) | Walks each equipped item's `explicitModLines[*].line`, lower-cased, matches against the **same** `buffDetectPatterns`. Does **NOT** apply the `while/if you have` filter (item consumption phrasing IS a relevance signal) |
| corpus source B (items, `suggestPattern` side) | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (in `getAllocNodeTextCorpusLowered`, after the existing passive-tree gather) | Appends each equipped item's `explicitModLines[*].line` to the same `self.allocNodeTextCorpus` list `detectMatchingPattern` consumes — no per-call cost beyond the one-time gather |
| slot iteration | both sites use `for _, slot in pairs(self.build.itemsTab.orderedSlots) do; local item = slot.selItemId and self.build.itemsTab.items[slot.selItemId]` | Equipped-only contract — walking `itemsTab.items` directly would over-include inventory |

Key invariants the spec locks (`spec/System/TestConfigHighlightItemModListScan_spec.lua`):

1. ConfigTab.lua holds the `suggestBuff` item-scan path with the inline guard and references `itemsTab` / `orderedSlots` / `explicitModLines`
2. `buffDetectPatterns` is iterated by **exactly 3 passes** now (was 2 in Phase 1.6)
3. The item-scan block does **NOT** contain the `while/if you have` exclusion strings
4. `getAllocNodeTextCorpusLowered` now walks both `allocNodes` (Source A) AND `orderedSlots → items → explicitModLines` (Source B), AND keeps the Phase 1 cache key `self.allocNodeTextCorpus` so the one-corpus-per-session contract holds
5. Passive-tree pass STILL applies the `while/if you have` filter (Phase 1 invariant preserved, no regression)
6. Both Phase 2 paths iterate `orderedSlots` (equipped-only) — verified by `for _, slot in pairs(self.build.itemsTab.orderedSlots)` appearing **exactly 2 times** in source

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConfigHighlightItemModListScan_spec.lua` (6 assertions, all pass)

**Effect on existing entries:** All Phase 1 / 1.5 / 1.6 detection paths continue to fire identically; Phase 2 strictly widens the corpus. Builds that previously had no signal (no relevant passive, no relevant skill on bar) but DO have item affixes mentioning curse / buff / killed-recently phrasing will newly trigger the orange highlight on the matching config row. `detected` set semantics + plain-substring `find` mean redundant detection across Pass 1/2/3 is harmless.

### `config-highlight-source-attribution`

Phase 3 (2026-05-29) of the Config-highlight family. Enriches every
detection-positive entry across all 3 sources (passive tree / skill loadout /
equipped items) with the SOURCE that produced the match — a human-readable
label naming the specific node / skill / item — plus the actual line text
that hit. Both tooltip render hooks (`suggestBuff` and `suggestPattern`)
append a `\nSource: <kind> 'X' - '<line>'` trailer so the user can see
exactly which build element triggered the highlight. The separator is an
ASCII hyphen `-` (not em-dash) because the LEB tooltip font does not have
a glyph for U+2014 — using an em-dash makes the tooltip render the literal
fallback text `[U+2014]` to the user, which is uglier than a plain `-`.

Motivation: prior to Phase 3, the tooltip text was generic ("Your build
mentions 'doubled if cursed'. Consider enabling this option…"), leaving the
user to hunt for the actual signal source. Phase 3 surfaces it inline.

API shape changes (backward-compatible because **Lua tables are truthy** —
all downstream `if detectFoo() and ... then` checks continue to work):

| Symbol | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `detectGrantedBuffs()[buffName]` | `true` | `{ source, line }` |
| `detectMatchingPattern(pattern)` | `bool` | `nil` or `{ source, line }` |
| `getAllocNodeTextCorpusLowered()` entries | `"lowered string"` | `{ text, line, source }` |

Uniform source-label convention (all 5 detection sites):

Labels use only the in-game **display name** — no internal node ids (e.g.
`ch0fs-20`) are surfaced to the user. The internal-id review finding was
caught and removed before the Phase 3 commit landed.

| Source | Label format | Pass / Site |
|---|---|---|
| passive node | `passive node 'Death from Below'` | Pass 1 of `detectGrantedBuffs` + Source A of corpus |
| equipped skill | `skill 'Profane Veil'` | Pass 2 of `detectGrantedBuffs` |
| equipped item | `item 'Boneclamor Barbute'` | Pass 3 of `detectGrantedBuffs` + Source B of corpus |

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Pass 1 attribution | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (inside the `allocNodes` for-loop) | Writes `{ source = "passive node 'X'", line = statText }` instead of `true` on first match (uses `node.name` / `node.dn` only — no `tostring(node.id)`) |
| Pass 2 attribution | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (inside the `displaySkillList` for-loop) | Writes `{ source = "skill 'X'", line = skillName }` |
| Pass 3 attribution | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (inside the `explicitModLines` for-loop) | Writes `{ source = "item 'X'", line = modLine.line }` (uses `item.title or item.name or item.baseName or "?"`) |
| Corpus entries | `getAllocNodeTextCorpusLowered` | Each entry is now `{ text = <lowered>, line = <original>, source = <label> }` |
| Matcher | `detectMatchingPattern` | Returns `nil` on miss, `{ source = entry.source, line = entry.line }` on hit |
| suggestBuff tooltip hook | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (render block ~L883) | Reads `attrib.source` / `attrib.line`, appends `"\n^xFFAA00Source: <source> - '<line>'"` trailer (ASCII hyphen — see font-glyph note below) |
| suggestPattern tooltip hook | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (render block ~L915) | Same trailer pattern |

Key invariants the spec locks (`spec/System/TestConfigHighlightSourceAttribution_spec.lua`, 8 assertions):

1. Phase 3 inline guard marker present in detectGrantedBuffs
2. Pass 1 records `source = "passive node '...'"`(no internal id), plus `line = statText` (original non-lowered)
3. Pass 2 records `source = "skill '...'"`, plus `line = skillName`
4. Pass 3 records `source = "item '...'"`, plus `line = modLine.line`
5. `detectMatchingPattern` returns `nil` on miss and `{ source = entry.source, line = ... }` on hit — no bare `return true` remains
6. Corpus entries carry `text` (lowered) + `line` (original) + `source` (label), AND the Phase 1 cache key `self.allocNodeTextCorpus` is preserved
7. Both tooltip closures (suggestBuff + suggestPattern) emit a `"Source: "` trailer — minimum 2 occurrences in source, both reading `attrib.source`
8. Label render hooks still use the plain truthy check (`if detectFoo() and not active() then`) so the backward-compatible truthy invariant holds

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConfigHighlightSourceAttribution_spec.lua` (8 assertions, all pass)

**Effect on existing Phase 1 / 1.5 / 1.6 / 2 entries:** Detection results are identical (same hits / misses); only the shape of the truthy hit is enriched. The Phase 1 spec line `line:find(lp, 1, true)` literal-string check was relaxed to `:find(lp, 1, true)` (the LHS variable name is no longer `line` — it's now `entry.text` — but the plain-substring contract `find(needle, 1, true)` is unchanged).

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `config-highlight-skill-subtree-scan`

Phase 4 (2026-05-29) of the Config-highlight family. Refines Pass 1's source
attribution so skill-subtree-allocated nodes are correctly labelled. Background:
`self.build.spec.allocNodes` is a single unified table containing BOTH player
passive tree nodes (UpperCamelCase / hex ids) AND skill subtree nodes
(lowercase treeId-prefixed ids such as `ch0fs-20` for Chthonic Fissure). Pass 1
already iterated these transparently through Phases 1 / 1.5 / 3, but mislabelled
every subtree hit as `"passive node 'X'"` — surfacing the wrong attribution
in the tooltip trailer Phase 3 introduced. Phase 4 fixes the label.

Approach: build a `treeId → skill name` lookup from
`skillsTab.socketGroupList[*].grantedEffect.{treeId,name}` lazily and cache it
on `self.treeIdToSkillName`. A shared `getNodeSourceLabel(nodeId, node)` helper
checks whether the node id is `treeId .. "-"`-prefixed for any registered
skill; if so it returns `"skill subtree '<skill>' node '<name>'"`, otherwise
it falls back to the legacy `"passive node '<name>'"` label. Both Pass 1 and
Source A of the corpus builder route through the helper.

No data change — `ConfigOptions.lua` is untouched. Only `Classes/ConfigTab.lua`.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `getTreeIdToSkillName` | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` | Builds `{ treeId = skillName, ... }` lookup from socketGroupList, cached on `self.treeIdToSkillName` |
| `getNodeSourceLabel(nodeId, node)` | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` | Returns `"skill subtree '<skill>' node '<name>'"` for treeId-prefixed ids; `"passive node '<name>'"` otherwise |
| Pass 1 iteration | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (inside `detectGrantedBuffs`) | Now `for nodeId, node in pairs(...)`, source via `getNodeSourceLabel(nodeId, node)` |
| Source A iteration | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (inside `getAllocNodeTextCorpusLowered`) | Now `for nodeId, node in pairs(...)`, source via `getNodeSourceLabel(nodeId, node)` |
| Cache invalidation | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` (`ConfigTabClass:BuildModList`) | `self.treeIdToSkillName = nil` paired with the pre-existing `self.detectedBuffs = nil` reset |

Key invariants the spec locks (`spec/System/TestConfigHighlightSkillSubtreeScan_spec.lua`):

1. Phase 4 inline guard marker present in ConfigTab.lua
2. `getTreeIdToSkillName` reads `socketGroupList[*].grantedEffect.{treeId, name}` and caches on `self.treeIdToSkillName`
3. `getNodeSourceLabel` emits `"skill subtree '..."` for treeId-prefixed ids and `"passive node '..."` otherwise; prefix-match uses `treeId .. "-"` (not bare treeId) to prevent false positives; NO `tostring(node.id)` / `tostring(nodeId)` leaks user-visible internal ids
4. Pass 1 uses `for nodeId, node in pairs(...)` and computes source via `getNodeSourceLabel(nodeId, node)` (no direct `"passive node '" .. label` write left in Pass 1)
5. Source A uses `for nodeId, node in pairs(...)` and computes source via `getNodeSourceLabel(nodeId, node)`
6. `BuildModList` clears both `self.detectedBuffs` and `self.treeIdToSkillName` so a skill loadout change invalidates the lookup

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConfigHighlightSkillSubtreeScan_spec.lua` (6 assertions, all pass)

**Effect on existing Phase 1 / 1.5 / 1.6 / 2 / 3 entries:** Player passive tree hits keep the identical `"passive node 'X'"` label. Only skill-subtree hits change — from the previously-misleading `"passive node 'X'"` to the accurate `"skill subtree '<skill>' node 'X'"`. The Phase 3 specs (`TestConfigHighlightSourceAttribution_spec.lua`) and earlier Phase 1.6 / 2 specs that grepped for the old `for _, node in pairs(self.build.spec.allocNodes)` iteration form were updated to the new `for nodeId, node` form in this same change.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `config-highlight-multi-source`

Phase 4 multi-source extension (2026-05-29). The single-source first-match-wins
shape established in Phase 3 hid additional contributors. A single buff
can be evidenced by MULTIPLE build elements — two skill subtree nodes both
mentioning "you have haste", a passive node + an item affix both granting
Frenzy, etc. The multi-source extension changes the attribution shape to
collect ALL hits while preserving the Phase 3 `attrib.source` / `attrib.line`
canonical-first mirrors for full backward compatibility.

Motivation (user-reported): "複数のスキルノードが you have haste を持っていたら、
すべてのソースの情報が出るであってますか？" — the user expected to see every
contributing node / item in the tooltip; the Phase 3 single-source design
silently hid the rest.

API shape (backward-compatible — `attrib.source` / `attrib.line` keep their
Phase 3 meaning as the canonical first hit):

```lua
detected[buffName] = {
    source  = <first hit's source>,    -- mirror of sources[1].source
    line    = <first hit's line>,      -- mirror of sources[1].line
    sources = {                        -- ALL hits, append order
        { source = "passive node 'A'",            line = "..." },
        { source = "skill subtree 'X' node 'Y'",  line = "..." },
        ...
    },
}
```

`detectMatchingPattern` returns the same shape on hit (`nil` on miss).

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `addBuffSource(detected, buffName, source, line)` | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` | Single write site for Pass 1 / 2 / 3. Initialises `detected[buffName] = { source, line, sources = {} }` on first call, always appends `{source, line}` to `sources`. |
| Pass 1 / 2 / 3 in `detectGrantedBuffs` | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` | Drop the Phase 3 `if not detected[buff.name] and ...` first-match-wins guard. Call `addBuffSource` instead. |
| `detectMatchingPattern` | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` | Accumulate into `result.sources` rather than returning on first hit. Init `result = { source = entry.source, line = entry.line, sources = {} }` to lock canonical-first mirrors. Final `return result` (nil on miss). |
| `suggestBuff` tooltip closure | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` | Branch on `#attrib.sources >= 2` → emit `"\n^xFFAA00Sources:"` header + one indented `"\n^xFFAA00  - <source>: '<line>'"` line per entry. Else fall back to Phase 3 single-line `"\n^xFFAA00Source: <source> - '<line>'"` form. |
| `suggestPattern` tooltip closure | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` | Same multi-source vs single-source branching. |

Key invariants the spec locks (`spec/System/TestConfigHighlightMultiSource_spec.lua`, 10 assertions):

1. Phase 4 multi-source inline guard marker present in ConfigTab.lua
2. `addBuffSource(detected, buffName, source, line)` helper exists; init shape carries `source` / `line` (canonical-first mirrors) + empty `sources = {}`; every call appends via `t_insert(entry.sources, ...)`
3. Pass 1 calls `addBuffSource` and DROPS the `if not detected[buff.name]` first-match guard
4. Pass 2 (skill loadout) calls `addBuffSource` and DROPS the first-match guard
5. Pass 3 (items) calls `addBuffSource` and DROPS the first-match guard
6. `detectMatchingPattern` accumulates `result.sources` and final `return result` (no in-loop early return); init mirrors `entry.source` / `entry.line`
7. Both tooltip closures branch on `#attrib.sources >= 2` and emit a `"Sources:"` header + `for _, s in ipairs(attrib.sources)` iteration
8. Single-source fallback (Phase 3 single-line `"Source: " .. attrib.source` form) is preserved in the `elseif` arm for `#sources == 1` and legacy callers
9. Multi-source trailer uses ASCII hyphen/colon separators (NOT em-dash — LEB tooltip font U+2014 trap from Phase 3 review still applies)
10. Phase 3 single-source `" - '" .. attrib.line .. "'"` render form is intact in the single-source fallback branch

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestConfigHighlightMultiSource_spec.lua` (10 assertions, all pass)

**Effect on existing entries:** When only ONE source contributes (the common case), tooltip rendering is identical to Phase 3 — `"Source: passive node 'X' - '...'"`. When TWO OR MORE sources contribute, the tooltip now reads e.g.:

```
^xFFAA00Sources:
^xFFAA00  - skill subtree 'Chthonic Fissure' node 'Pyrocladic': '20% more damage while you have Haste'
^xFFAA00  - passive node 'Death from Below': 'Cast Flame Ward When Stunned'
^xFFAA00  - item 'Boneclamor Barbute': '+(15-40)% Chance to Gain Haste when Hit'
```

The Phase 3 spec (`TestConfigHighlightSourceAttribution_spec.lua`) was updated in this same change: assertions tied to the literal `line = X` write form were repointed at the `addBuffSource(..., line)` call shape, and the `detectMatchingPattern` in-loop `return` assertion was repointed at the `return result` final-line form.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `config-highlight-item-slot-kind`

Phase 6 (2026-05-29). The equipped-item source label in the highlight
tooltip was a generic `"item 'X'"` for **every** slot. Users asked for the
specific slot kind so the tooltip names what it actually is — `ring`,
`helmet`, `boots`, `idol`, `idol altar`, `blessing (timeline)`, etc.

A shared `getItemSourceKind(item, slotName)` helper derives the kind from
**`item.type`** (the authoritative item classification — see ItemsTab
`SORT_TYPE_TO_CATEGORY`), NOT the slot name, because the type is robust
across slot numbering (`Ring 1` / `Ring 2` → `ring`) and already
distinguishes idol sizes / altar / blessing:

| `item.type` | kind returned |
|---|---|
| `"Idol Altar"` | `idol altar` |
| `"Blessing"` | `blessing (<timeline>)` — timeline from `slotName` (blessing slots are keyed by timeline name) |
| ends with `Idol` (e.g. `"Ornate Idol"`) | `idol` (every idol footprint collapses to one kind) |
| anything else | `item.type:lower()` → `ring` / `helmet` / `boots` / `gloves` / `body armor` / `amulet` / `belt` / `relic` / `bow` / `wand` / `sceptre` / `dagger` / ... |
| `nil` / `""` | `item` (graceful fallback — preserves the old label) |

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `getItemSourceKind(item, slotName)` | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` | Single helper; both equipped-item label sites call it. |
| Pass 3 of `detectGrantedBuffs` | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` | `sourceLabel = getItemSourceKind(item, slot.slotName) .. " '" .. itemName .. "'"`, passed to `addBuffSource`. |
| Source B of `getAllocNodeTextCorpusLowered` | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` | Same `sourceLabel` derivation for the suggestPattern corpus. |

Invariants locked (`spec/System/TestConfigHighlightItemSlotKind_spec.lua`):
guard markers present; helper maps Idol Altar / Blessing(+timeline) /
`...Idol`→idol / generic-lower / nil→item; both Pass 3 and Source B call
`getItemSourceKind(item, slot.slotName)`; no hardcoded `"item '" .. itemName`
remains.

**Effect on existing entries:** a build whose Frenzy comes from a ring
affix now reads `ring 'Red Ring of Atlaria'` instead of `item 'Red Ring
of Atlaria'`. The Phase 3 / Phase 4 specs that asserted the literal
`"item '"` label were repointed at the `getItemSourceKind` call shape.
