### `config-highlight-tooltip-maxwidth`

Phase 6 (2026-05-29). `TooltipClass:AddLine` only runs its word-wrap path
(`main:WrapString`) when `self.maxWidth` is set; otherwise each `\n`-segment
is added as a single un-wrapped line. The config tab **never set a
maxWidth**, so a long source-attribution trailer (a full item affix line),
a multi-source `Sources:` list, or the old all-patterns enumeration ran
straight off the right edge of the screen (user-reported in-game).

Two-part fix:

1. **Set `tooltip.maxWidth` in the config `tooltipFunc`** (idempotently,
   mirroring the ItemsTab idiom `if not tooltip.maxWidth then ... end`,
   value `480`). Every config tooltip now wraps.
2. **Drop the all-patterns enumeration from the suggestPattern message.**
   It used to build `'a' / 'b' / 'c' / ...` from the full declared
   `suggestPattern` list via `table.concat(pattern, "' / '")` — the single
   longest unbreakable segment. Now that Phase 3/4 source attribution
   prints the ACTUAL matched line in the trailer, enumerating every
   declared pattern is redundant. The lead-in is now the concise
   `"Your build references this state. Consider enabling this option if
   your build actually relies on it."`

Invariants locked (`spec/System/TestConfigHighlightItemSlotKind_spec.lua`):
`if not tooltip.maxWidth then` present + `tooltip.maxWidth =` assigned;
`table.concat(pattern` gone; old `"Your build mentions "` message gone;
concise `"Your build references this state"` lead-in present; trailers
still use ASCII hyphen / colon (em-dash U+2014 trap preserved from Phase 3).

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `config-highlight-cache-invalidation`

Phase 7 (2026-05-30, user-reported). The suggestPattern corpus cache
`self.allocNodeTextCorpus` was introduced in Phase 1/2 with a lazy
`if self.allocNodeTextCorpus then return it` guard but was **never reset**.
`ConfigTab:BuildModList` cleared `self.detectedBuffs` (suggestBuff) and
`self.treeIdToSkillName` (Phase 4) but not the corpus. So after importing a
**different build into the same file**, every suggestPattern highlight
(Cursed / Low Life / Ward / Overload) stayed frozen on the PREVIOUS build's
passive-tree + item text — the highlight pointed at the wrong build.

`detectGrantedBuffs` (suggestBuff: Haste / Frenzy / Flame Ward / ...) was
already cleared and so refreshed correctly; only the corpus leaked. The
asymmetry made it look like "some highlights update, some don't".

Fix: add `self.allocNodeTextCorpus = nil` to `BuildModList`, alongside the
existing `detectedBuffs` / `treeIdToSkillName` resets. `BuildModList` is the
single rebuild chokepoint (called on every import / config change / skill or
tree edit — see Build.lua), so the corpus now rebuilds from the current
build each cycle, exactly like `detectedBuffs`.

Invariants locked (`spec/System/TestConfigHighlightCacheInvalidation_spec.lua`):
behavioral — a populated `allocNodeTextCorpus` is `nil` after `BuildModList`
(plus `detectedBuffs` / `treeIdToSkillName`); structural — `BuildModList`
head nils all three caches together.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `config-highlight-persistent`

Phase 7 (2026-05-30, user-requested). The orange highlight on a relevant
config used to vanish the moment you enabled the config — the label was
gated on `and not isSuggestActive()` / `and not isPatternSuggestActive()`,
so it behaved as a transient "enable me" prompt. Users read the orange as a
**build-relevance marker** and were confused when checking the box erased it
(losing the signal of *which* configs matter to the build).

Fix: the label closures now highlight on a **bare truthy check** of the
detection result (`if detectGrantedBuffs()[buffName] then` /
`if detectMatchingPattern(pattern) then`), so the orange persists regardless
of on/off. The tooltip still shows the source attribution whenever detected;
only the "Consider enabling this option" call-to-action is gated on the
not-yet-active state (via a `cta` local: `isSuggestActive() and "" or " ..."`).

| Closure | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| suggestBuff label | `if detectGrantedBuffs()[buffName] and not isSuggestActive() then` | `if detectGrantedBuffs()[buffName] then` |
| suggestPattern label | `if detectMatchingPattern(pattern) and not isPatternSuggestActive() then` | `if detectMatchingPattern(pattern) then` |
| suggestBuff tooltip | gate whole block on `attrib and not isSuggestActive()` | gate on `attrib`; CTA via `isSuggestActive()`-driven `cta` |
| suggestPattern tooltip | gate whole block on `attrib and not isPatternSuggestActive()` | gate on `attrib`; CTA via `isPatternSuggestActive()`-driven `cta` |

Invariants locked (`spec/System/TestConfigHighlightCacheInvalidation_spec.lua`
+ updated `TestConfigHighlightSourceAttribution_spec.lua`): both labels use
the bare truthy check; the old active-gated forms are gone; tooltips no
longer gate the whole block on `if attrib and not isXActive()`; the CTA is
conditional on the active state.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `config-sets-ui`

Config sets UI (2026-05-29). LEB inherited the config-set **backend** from
PoB — `configSets` / `configSetOrderList` / `NewConfigSet` /
`SetActiveConfigSet`, plus multi-set `Save`/`Load` (`<ConfigSet>` XML
elements with a single-Default backward-compat shortcut) — but shipped **no
UI** to drive it, so it was effectively a single locked config set. This
ports PoB's `ConfigSetListControl` plus the ConfigTab set selector on top of
the existing backend, letting users keep named presets ("Boss", "Mapping",
"Single Target").

This is a **PoB→LEB port governed by the no-PoE-content boundary** (memory:
`feedback_no_poe_specific_in_leb`). Config sets are generic planner UX with
zero game content. PoB-isms were **adapted, not blind-copied**:

| PoB form | LEB-adapted form | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `self.ListControl(anchor, rect, 16, ...)` | `self.ListControl(anchor, x, y, width, height, 16, ...)` | LEB control constructors take FLAT args, not rect tables |
| `new("ButtonControl", a, {x,y,w,h}, ...)` | `new("ButtonControl", a, x, y, w, h, ...)` | same flat-arg convention throughout |
| `self.configTab.modFlag = true` | `self.configTab.build.modFlag = true` | LEB's dirty flag lives on `build` (cf. TreeTab); `configTab.modFlag` does not exist in LEB |

LE-relevance verification done before porting — every PoB method the control
calls exists in LEB and is LE-valid: `build:SyncLoadouts` (Build.lua),
`main:OpenConfirmPopup` / `OpenPopup` / `ClosePopup` (Main.lua), `copyTable`
(Common.lua), `ConfigTab:AddUndoState`, `ListControl` base, `DropDownControl:SetList`.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `ConfigSetListControl` | `src/Classes/ConfigSetListControl.lua` (new) | ListControl subclass: New / Copy / Rename / Delete / reorder / double-click-to-activate, operating on `configTab.configSets`. Auto-loaded on first `new("ConfigSetListControl", ...)` via Common.lua `getClass`. |
| Set selector | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` Init | `setSelect` dropdown (switch active set) + `setLabel` + `setManage` ("Manage..." → popup), anchored right of `resetDefaults`. |
| `OpenConfigSetManagePopup` | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` | Opens a popup containing the ConfigSetListControl + Done button. |
| Draw populate | `src/Classes/ConfigTab.lua` Draw | Each frame builds `newSetList` from `configSetOrderList` titles, sets active `selIndex`, `setSelect:SetList(newSetList)`. |

Invariants locked (`spec/System/TestConfigSetsUI_spec.lua`, 12 assertions —
behavioral + structural): fresh build has 1 set; NewConfigSet seeds
input/placeholder + fresh id; SetActiveConfigSet switches + re-points the
`self.input` alias; config values isolated between sets; **OpenConfigSetManagePopup
instantiates ConfigSetListControl headlessly without error** (real
`newBuild()` smoke test); control subclasses ListControl with flat args;
uses `build.modFlag` not `configTab.modFlag`; implements the 6 override
methods; ConfigTab wires setSelect / setManage / OpenConfigSetManagePopup /
Draw populate / SetActiveConfigSet switch.

### `hammer-of-lorent-tooltipdescriptions-missing-mods`

`src/Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json` Hammer of Lorent (`#41`, Hammer unique)
previously stored ONLY its two rolled affixes (`(20-80)% Chance to Chill on
Hit` rollId 0, `(20-80)% increased Melee Damage` rollId 1) and dropped the two
fixed per-character-level tooltip lines that LE itself surfaces. Per
`datamined game source` `tooltipDescriptions`:

1. `+1 melee physical damage per level`  (`[1,c]`)
2. `1% increased melee stun chance per level`  (`[1,c]%`)

This is the SAME drop class as Frozen Ire (`#32`,
[`frozen-ire-per-char-level-mods`](#frozen-ire-per-char-level-mods)): the
per-character-level scalars live ONLY in the datamining `tooltipDescriptions`
block (bracket markup `[N,c]` / `[N,c,N]`) and NEVER in the structured `mods`
roll table, so the LEB transcription that walked the roll table silently lost
them.

**Audit:** `spec/tools/audit_uniques_tooltipdescriptions.py` (local, gitignored)
classifies every `tooltipDescription` of all 471 datamining uniques and diffs
against LEB `mods`. Across the entire corpus EXACTLY two uniques carry bracket
`[..,c,..]` per-character-level lines — Frozen Ire (`#32`) and Hammer of Lorent
(`#41`). Every other `per <X>` tooltip line is per-stat / per-stack and was
already modelled (spot-verified: Mourningfrost #19, Humming Bee #34, Vaions
Chariot #264, Frostbite Shackles #213, Urzils Pride #10, Sierpins Fractal Tree
#320). `Falcon Fists` (#333) `... per Level of Falconry` is per-SKILL-level (a
different `Multiplier` axis) and is correctly out of this class.

**ModParser path (no parser change):**

| LEB mod string | parses to |
|---|---|
| `+1 Melee Physical Damage per level` | `PhysicalDamage BASE 1`, `keywordFlags=Melee(512)`, tag `Multiplier{var="Level"}` |
| `1% increased Melee Stun Chance per level` | `StunChance INC 1`, `keywordFlags=Melee(512)`, tag `Multiplier{var="Level"}` |

`multipliers["Level"]` is set to `build.characterLevel` in `CalcSetup.lua`, so at
level L each mod evaluates to `1 × L` — e.g. at lv100 a Hammer-of-Lorent melee
build gains `+100` flat melee physical damage and `+100%` increased melee stun
chance. The `["per level"]` alias is the same path Frozen Ire relies on.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Hammer of Lorent unique-mods | `src/Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json` `#41` | Adds 2 new entries to `mods` (per-char-level melee phys, per-char-level melee stun chance) and pads `rollIds` with two `null`s so the rolled `Chance to Chill` / `increased Melee Damage` retain rollId 0/1 |
| ImportTab pickup | `src/Classes/ImportTab.lua` (no change) | Routes `rollIds[i] == nil` slots into the `{crafted}` (no-range) explicit-mod branch |
| ModParser per-level | `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (`["per level"]` alias, no change) | Maps to `tag = { type = "Multiplier", var = "Level" }` |

### `foot-of-the-mountain-dodge-to-endurance`

Foot of the Mountain (uniques_1_4 #253, Iron Greaves, req lv48) has three
`tooltipDescriptions` that the datamining transcription dropped, leaving only
the `+Endurance% / +All Attributes / +Stacks` lines. The two missing ones:

1. `-2 Mana Cost per stack of Mountain's Endurance` (scales with stack count)
2. `100% of Dodge Rating converted to Endurance Threshold while you have at
   least 1 stack of Mountain's Endurance` (**binary 100%**, not per-stack)

A stack of Mountain's Endurance is gained per second while not moving (cap 3),
so "≥1 stack" == stationary. LEB models the stacks with the `conditionStationary`
config, which sets `Multiplier:StationarySeconds` (the stack proxy, cap 3) AND
the `Condition:Stationary` FLAG.

| parse (conversion) | `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (specialModList, after the EndThr→WDT handlers) | Maps line (2) to a BASE `DodgeRatingConvertedToEnduranceThreshold` carrying a `Condition:Stationary` tag (so `modDB:Sum` returns the % only while stationary) |
| parse (mana cost)  | `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (modTagList, after the bleed-stack suffixes) | Maps `per stack of mountains endurance` to a `Multiplier:StationarySeconds` (limit 3) tag |

The conversion is fully gated behind `conditionStationary` (default OFF), and the
mana cost self-gates (0 stacks → 0 reduction), so every build's default snapshot
is byte-identical (regression-sample: equipping + non-equipping builds unchanged).

### actorcondition-tag-mult

**Invariant:** The `ActorCondition` tag handler honours an optional
`tag.mult` field, mirroring the `condition-tag-mult` path (the player
`Condition` tag) and the StatThreshold mult path. Truth table:
- match=true,  mult unset -> pass value through (legacy)
- match=true,  mult set   -> `value = value * tag.mult`
- match=false, mult unset -> `return nil` (full gate, legacy)
- match=false, mult set   -> pass value through (no gate)

This is what lets a tree node fold an enemy condition into a doubling
(e.g. "+40% More Damage, Doubled Against High Health Enemies") without
zeroing the base contribution when the enemy condition is off.

**Files:**
- `src/Classes/ModStore.lua` (ActorCondition tag branch, ~L645)
- `spec/System/TestDoubledAgainstCondition_spec.lua`

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### doubled-against-condition

Generic ENEMY-condition doubling for tree-node `notScalingStats` lines of the
form ` Doubled Against <enemy condition>`. Sibling of
`doubled-if-X-tree-notscaling` (which attaches a PLAYER `Condition` tag); this
one attaches an ENEMY `ActorCondition` tag. A 2026-06-01 audit of all 1.4 trees
found 9 nodes using the pattern:

| Node | stats | clause | enemy cond |
|---|---|---|---|
| ss3tre-7 Cold Presence | +10% More Damage | High Health Enemies | HighHealth |
| javeli-12 Monster Piercer | +12% Hit Damage | High Health | HighHealth |
| gs15de-16 Executioner | +10% Hit Damage | Low Health | LowLife |
| fl44-4 Decree of Slaughter | +8% Hit Damage | Low Life | LowLife |
| av75ch-23 Shatter Shot | +10% Hit Damage | Frozen Enemies | Frozen |
| ss3tre-25 Glacial Smash | +8% Hit Damage | Frozen Enemies | Frozen |
| ss3tre-20 Acclimated | 5% Less Cold Damage Taken On Hit | Frozen Enemies | Frozen |
| ss3tre-21 Hoarfrost | +3 Ward Gained | Frozen | Frozen |
| fl71ds-6 Runic Eclipse | -6% Damage Taken | DoTs | (UNMAPPED) |

` Doubled Against DoTs` is an incoming-damage-TYPE defence modifier, NOT an
enemy condition, so it is intentionally left unmapped and that mod stays at
base (out of scope for this enemy-condition handler).

Like ` Doubled if X`, the literal strings stay `{}` no-ops in
`src/Data/ModCache.lua` (`{{}, "Doubled Against X "}`). The semantics is owned
by `PassiveTree.lua:ProcessStats`: it scans `node.sd`, maps `<X>` to an enemy
condition var (High Health -> `HighHealth`, Low Health / Low Life -> `LowLife`,
Frozen -> `Frozen`), and attaches `{type="ActorCondition", actor="enemy",
var=<var>, mult=2}` as a tag on every scaling mod the node emits. `ModStore.lua`
(`actorcondition-tag-mult` guard) then delivers `value` when the matching enemy
config toggle is OFF and `value * 2` when ON.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| scan | `src/Classes/PassiveTree.lua` (`ProcessStats`, before the AddMod loop) | Walks `node.sd`, matches ` Doubled Against X`, maps to enemy var, builds the ActorCondition `doublingTag` |
| apply | `src/Classes/PassiveTree.lua` (AddMod inner loop) | Appends a fresh copy of the tag (incl. `actor`) to each scaling mod |
| evaluate | `src/Classes/ModStore.lua` (`actorcondition-tag-mult` guard) | Treats the tag's `mult` as a multiplier on `value` instead of a full gate |
| config | `src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` | New `conditionEnemyHighHealth` toggle (enemy >65% hp); Low Life / Frozen reuse the existing `conditionEnemyLowLife` / `conditionEnemyFrozen` toggles |
| visibility | `src/Modules/Calcs.lua` (`addModTags`) | The enemy `ActorCondition` tag registers the var in `enemyConditionsUsed`, surfacing the `ifEnemyCond` config |

Default OFF for all enemy-condition toggles: the doubling tag holds the base
value until the relevant enemy condition is toggled on, so sustained-DPS
baselines are unchanged from before the fix; the doubling is opt-in (matching
in-game "this effect is doubled against <enemy state>" being a conditional).

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestDoubledAgainstCondition_spec.lua`

### `build-snapshot-fetch-robust`

`spec/System/TestBuilds_spec.lua` `fetchBuilds` must not halt the whole
build-snapshot suite when a `.lua` snapshot has no paired `.xml` (LETools /
offline-save imports) or is momentarily unparseable (e.g. a concurrent regen
caught mid-write). Before this guard, `io.open(...".xml")` returned nil and the
unconditional `fileHnd:read("*a")` crashed on the first XML-less build, so a
single un-regenerable snapshot blocked verification of every other build. The
guard opens the `.xml` first, `pcall`s `LoadModule`, and skips — with a visible
`[TestBuilds] SKIP unparseable snapshot: ...` marker (no silent cap) — any build
that cannot be re-imported. Only XML-backed, parseable builds are tested; the
suite stays runnable on a partial-corpus checkout (612 .lua / 180 .xml).

**Spec:** none — this is a test-harness robustness invariant, not a calc
contract, so the usual busted layer does not apply (a meta-spec would have to
mock the filesystem). Validated operationally: `busted --tags=builds` runs to
completion (129095 successes / 0 failures) instead of erroring at `fetchBuilds`.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `generatebuilds-nested-table-serializer`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestGenerateBuildsNestedSerializer_spec.lua` (loads the REAL
`buildTable` from `GenerateBuilds.lua`; flat output byte-identical to the legacy
format, nested tables round-trip, valid loadable Lua). The harness side is locked by
the roundDeep marker in `spec/System/TestBuilds_spec.lua`.
The spec extracts `buildTable` by source text: it takes everything before `local
buildList` and matches to the LAST `end` in it. Do NOT re-anchor on an `end`/`local
buildList` ADJACENCY — that forbids writing anything between them, including a
`@leb-regression-guard` marker on the `local buildList` line, and it errored the whole
spec out when `regen-root-equals-test-root` put one there. Extraction is machinery: if
you change it, re-confirm the guard still goes RED (2 failures) with the nested branch
reverted to `buildTable(keyRef, value, string)`.

**Sites:** `spec/GenerateBuilds.lua` + `spec/GenerateBuilds14.lua` (local, gitignored)
`buildTable` — the nested-table branch CAPTURES the recursion (`local nested =
buildTable("", value)`) and re-emits `<keyRef> = {<body>},`; `spec/System/TestBuilds_spec.lua`
`roundDeep` — the snapshot comparison rounds numbers at any depth.

**Why:** `buildTable` serializes `mainOutput` to the snapshot `.lua`. The old nested
branch called `buildTable(key, value, string)` and DISCARDED the return (Lua strings
are immutable; passing `string` does not mutate the caller), silently DROPPING every
table-valued key. `mainOutput` carries real nested tables — a Beastmaster's
`output.Minion` has 701 entries, `output.SkillDPS` 2 — so every minion snapshot lost
its entire Minion sub-output (the regression suite never compared it: `TestBuilds_spec`
only iterates SNAPSHOT keys, and the dropped key was absent), and the #63/#70 regen
corrupted Druid snapshots. The fix serializes nested tables; format is preserved
EXACTLY for flat string-keyed tables (`["key"]` ref, `round(v,4)`, lexical sort) so
non-nested snapshots do not churn; numeric keys use `[n]` for round-trip; the sort
comparator is type-aware (the old `table.sort(keys)` threw on number-vs-string keys).
PAIRED harness change: `buildTable` rounds nested numbers to 4dp but the recompute is
full precision, and `TestBuilds_spec`'s table branch used EXACT `assert.are.same` — so
nested numbers would mismatch (probe: <private build> Minion 89/681 EXACT mismatches from
>4dp tails, 0 rounded). `roundDeep` rounds at any depth; identical to the old
`round(v,4)` for flat scalars, so the current nested-less corpus is unaffected until a
full regen populates the nested tables.
**NOT switched to `Common.writeLuaTable`** (the TODO's suggestion): it emits a
different format (bare `key=`, full precision, no trailing comma) which would reformat
the entire buildTable-format corpus and change precision — the corpus is buildTable
format (`["ColdDamageBase"] = 191.2676,`), confirmed.
**Follow-up (not in this commit):** a full-corpus regen with the fixed serializer
populates `Minion`/`SkillDPS` into all snapshots (restoring that regression coverage);
the builds suite stays green meanwhile (no nested keys yet, roundDeep == old path).
**Regression to prevent:** reverting the nested branch to the discarded-return call
(re-drops nested tables); switching `buildTable` to a different format (corpus churn);
removing `roundDeep` (nested numbers fail EXACT compare after a regen).

### `pierce-chance-to-crit-multiplier`

"Pierce Chance" is a real LE stat (`pierce_%` in game data) with no DPS effect
of its own, but the Shurikens tree node Ricochet (srk21-19) carries the
notScalingStat " Pierce Chance -> Critical Multiplier" ("Pierce chance is
converted to additional critical strike multiplier"). Locked invariants:

* `modNameList["pierce chance"] = "PierceChance"` — the ledger exists; tree
  node "+25% Pierce Chance" (Ethereal Blades srk21-27) parses to
  `PierceChance BASE`.
* `parseArrowConversion` emits `flag("PierceChanceConvertsToCritMultiplier")`
  for the EXACT pair only — no generic flat "X -> Y" stat conversion (the
  #3-B "Additional <skill> Chance" misparse class is what a greedy rule here
  becomes).
* CalcOffence adds `Sum("BASE", cfg, "PierceChance")` into the additive
  crit-multiplier pool when the (skill-scoped) flag is set.
* ModCache must not carry stale empty-parse rows for "+25%/+50% Pierce
  Chance" or the conversion line (un-baked; a re-bake re-masks the parser).

**Ground truth:** StarSeaVnV lv100 Falconer 3-layer ledger (2026-06-10):
in-game carried critMult 757 = character-sheet Throwing 582 + Massacre 75
(skill-specific) + pierce 100 (Ethereal Blades x4) EXACT; LEB now computes
CritMultiplier 7.57 on that build.

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (modNameList entry + parseArrowConversion
branch), `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (crit-multiplier block),
`src/Data/ModCache.lua` (3 rows removed).

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestPierceChanceToCritMultiplier_spec.lua`

* Composes ADDITIVELY with the Idol Altar refracted-slot boosts at the affix

* Applies to ALL affix subtypes — including Heretical weaver lines, which the
  altar boosts do not touch.

### `refracted-rank-gating`

Refracted altar-grid cells activate progressively: the game's
`IdolsContainerGridData.unlockMatrix` encodes them as `100 + rank`
(`RefractedSlotIdJump = 100`, `MaxIdolSlotUnlockRewards = 8`); below that
altar unlock rank the cell behaves as a NORMAL slot. Locked invariants:

* `Data/IdolAltarLayouts.lua` carries `refractedRanks = { [row] = { [col] =
  rank } }` for every type-2 cell of all 13 base altars (decoded 2026-06-10
  from resources.assets `IdolsContainerGridDataList` path_id 270533; 13/13
  altars' blocked/refracted layouts match this file). Mirrored altars inherit
  column-flipped (c -> 6-c) ranks.
* Config `idolAltarUnlockRank` (count, default 8 = everything active — the
  pre-existing behavior) gates BOTH consumers: CalcSetup `fracturedItemSet`
  (refracted affix boosts) and ItemsTab `CountIdolsOnRefractedCells`
  (`Multiplier:IdolInRefractedSlot` + dropdown display).

**Ground truth:** StarSeaVnV Ocular Altar 3-layer ledger (2026-06-10): the
idol covering the (5,1) rank-1 corner IS altar-boosted in-game while the
idol covering the (1,1) rank-7 corner is NOT (in-game sheet cc 119% closes
only with that asymmetry; with everything active LEB showed 53x1.557=83 per
dagger where the game shows 53). The character's actual unlock rank is in
[1,6] — read it in-game before per-build comparisons; default 8 preserves
old behavior for the corpus.

**Sites:** `src/Data/IdolAltarLayouts.lua` (refractedRanks data),
`src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` (idolAltarUnlockRank),
`src/Modules/CalcSetup.lua` (rank check in the grid walk),
`src/Classes/ItemsTab.lua` (refractedCellActive + mirror expansion).

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestRefractedRankGating_spec.lua`

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

also covers the point-scaled variants ("+2".."+5" / "+20%".."+80%") that
were never baked.

* Elder Branch's third stat " Tripled while using an Axe" stays

### `deaths-door-lowlife-critmult`

LE passive-tree node text uses the SHORT "Crit Multi" / "Crit Multiplier"
spelling alongside the canonical "Critical Strike Multiplier". Neither short
form was registered in ModParser's `modNameList`, so the generic form parser
found NO stat name: ModCache baked EMPTY mod lists with `" Crit Multi "`
residue and the whole stat line was silently dropped. The decisive case is
Rogue-71 **Death's Door** "+10% Crit Multi While At Low Health" (8 pts max =
+80): its SIBLING line "-3% Damage Taken While At Low Health" parsed
correctly into a `Condition:LowLife`-tagged mod, proving the
"While At Low Health" suffix machinery (modTagList) was fine — the failure
was purely the missing stat-name alias.

Fix at the alias altitude (NOT a one-off specialModList): register
`crit multiplier` and `crit multi` → `CritMultiplier` in `modNameList` so
EVERY short-spelling line parses through the normal pipeline, with whatever
suffix/condition it carries. `scan()` prefers earliest-then-longest, so the
longer key wins on "Crit Multiplier" lines (no `plier` residue), and the
existing `while at low health` modTagList entry attaches `Condition:LowLife`.
The condition is config-gated by `conditionLowLife` ("Are you always on Low
Life?", `ifCond = "LowLife"`, **default OFF**) like all LowLife siblings.

Six empty ModCache rows un-baked (deleted) so live parse takes over:

* `+10% Crit Multi While At Low Health` (Rogue-71 Death's Door) — parses
  CLEAN with Condition:LowLife; config-gated, zero default-config impact.
* `+5% Crit Multiplier` (Sentinel-86 Holy Precision) — parses CLEAN and
  UNCONDITIONAL; this is a genuine default-config fix (<private build> #5: CM
  2.50→2.75, DPS +7.03%). 5 corpus builds allocate the node
  (warpath_channel 1.2; <private build> / <private build> / <private build> / <private build> 1.4).
* `+18% Crit Multiplier while Tethered`, `+2% Crit Multiplier per Stack
  Consumed`, `3% Crit Multiplier per Stack`, `20% Max More Crit Multi` —
  now carry the CritMultiplier stat but KEEP non-empty residue (Tethered /
  per-Stack / Max-More suffixes unmodeled), so the PassiveTree extra gate
  still drops them: net behavior unchanged, parse now honest.

The two arrow rows (`" Crit Multiplier -> Physical Penetration for Bleed"`,
`"25% Crit Multi -> Falcon Crit Multi Buff after Attack"`) stay baked — the
arrow path never reaches the stat-name scan, so the aliases don't affect
them (their fixes are separate engines, see `pierce-chance-to-crit-multiplier`
and the Salt-the-Wound CritMultToAilmentPen work).

**Ground truth:** <private build> in-game capture decomposition (2026-06): 8/8
Death's Door + permanent low-life (Architects of Astral Blood) carries a
constant +80 added crit multiplier in the Salt the Wound bleed-pen channel
(397 = 116 sheet + 80 Death's Door + 200 Rhythm). End-to-end with
`conditionLowLife` ON: <private build> (Rogue-71 #8) CritMultiplier 3.16 → 3.96
(+0.80 EXACT).

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| alias table | `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (`modNameList`, Crit/speed block) | Registers `crit multiplier` / `crit multi` → `CritMultiplier` |
| ModCache | `src/Data/ModCache.lua` | The six stale empty rows are removed so the lines live-parse |
| registry | `spec/Data/silent-failure-affixes.json` + `spec/System/TestSilentFailureSweep_spec.lua` | Surgical −6 (total 16749→16743, silent 2076→2070) in the same commit |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestDeathsDoorCritMulti_spec.lua`
- "'+10% Crit Multi While At Low Health' parses to CritMultiplier BASE 10 with Condition:LowLife and no residue"
- "'+5% Crit Multiplier' (Sentinel-86 Holy Precision) parses to CritMultiplier BASE 5 with no residue"
- "the canonical '+5% Critical Strike Multiplier' spelling still parses identically"

### `rhythm-stack-crit-multi`

Dancing Strikes' "Rhythm" stack family (Bladedancer, `TreeData/1_4/tree_4.json`)
is PER STACK in-game and GLOBAL (player sheet), but the stat strings carry
neither fact — both live only in the node DESCRIPTIONS:

* `dacn33-26` **Art of Blades** (maxPoints 2): stat `+10% Global Critical
  Multiplier`; description "Your critical strikes deal more damage per stack
  of {Rhythm}."
* `dacn33-23` **Rhythm** (maxPoints 5): scaling stat `+2 Rhythm Maximum
  Stacks` (5/5 -> 10 max); notScalingStats `3% Global More Damage` +
  `2 Rhythm Duration (seconds)`; description "When you use Dancing Strikes
  and hit at least one enemy, you gain a stack of {Rhythm} for a short
  duration and refresh all existing stacks, granting you global more damage
  per stack (multiplicative with other modifiers)."

**In-game evidence (<private build> lv100 Bladedancer, 2026-06-11 CSV capture
decomposition):** the bleed-pen channel shows EXACT 20-crit-mult-pt steps per
stack (Art of Blades 2/2), ramp +1 stack/~300ms while Dancing Strikes is used,
plateau at +200 (10 stacks), reset after ~2-3s idle. Character-sheet added
crit multi in the captured state: **397 = 116 sheet + 80 Death's Door (low
life) + 200 Rhythm**.

**Before the fix** LEB parsed Art of Blades to `BASE 20 CritMultiplier
[Global][SkillId]` — skill-scoped (contributed NOTHING to the player sheet:
Sum BASE CritMultiplier = 116 excluded it) AND unconditional (full value at
zero stacks inside the skill context). dacn33-23's `3% Global More Damage`
was likewise a flat SkillId-scoped MORE.

**Fix (mirrors `throne-of-ambition-stacks`):**

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| rewrite registry | `src/Data/Global.lua` (`LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE`) | Appends "per stack of Rhythm" to both nodes' stat strings ($-anchored, value-tolerant) |
| notScaling rewrite | `src/Classes/PassiveTree.lua` (`ProcessStats`) | `notScalingStats` lines now also run through the rewrite registry (dacn33-23's per-stack line lives there) |
| global-scope registry | `src/Data/Global.lua` (`LE_TREE_NODE_GLOBAL_SCOPE`) | The SkillId scoping tag is LIFTED for exactly these two nodes (in-game GLOBAL) |
| tag | `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (`modTagList`) | `"per stack of rhythm"` -> `Multiplier:RhythmStacks` (limit 10 = 2 x 5/5) |
| config | `src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` (after `multiplierActiveAmbition`) | `# of Rhythm Stacks (max 10 at 5/5 Rhythm):` (`ifMult = "RhythmStacks"`, **default 0**) |

Stacks are modeled ADDITIVE within each mod (one mod of value x stacks, the
Throne decision): 10 stacks at 2/2 = +200 added crit multi — the CSV's linear
20-pt steps validate this exactly for the crit component. The More Damage
component is per-stack by the node description (it references {Rhythm}
stacks); linear stacking there (10 = +30% MORE, x1.30) is the
Throne-precedent assumption, not separately CSV-validated. The limit-10 cap
assumes 5/5 Rhythm (the only build shape observed); a build with fewer points
has a lower in-game cap the config user must respect.

**Default 0 -> strict no-op** on default configs; note the fix also REMOVES
the previous always-on skill-scoped contributions (DS-context +20 crit multi /
+3% MORE), which is the faithful zero-stack state.

### `ailment-finisher-scaling`

A skill marked `ailmentFinisher: true` in skills.json is a PROC the player
never swings; three scaling rules follow, each individually proven by the
shadow-daggers-finisher capture decomposition:

1. **Strict delivery keyword** (`CalcActiveSkill` keyword build): a melee
   ailmentFinisher takes `KeywordFlag.Melee`, NOT the Attack bundle
   (Melee|Throwing|Bow) that player-swung melee skills get. In-game the
   finisher takes Rogue-52's "+2 Melee Physical Damage" but not its "+2
   Throwing Physical Damage", and Pursuit's melee half but not its throwing
   half. Attack-bundle-scoped mods still match via the Melee bit (any-of).
2. **No weapon-sourced added damage** (`CalcOffence` base loop): weapon
   implicits/affix flats (Sceptre "+10 Melee Damage", Dagger "+25 Melee
   Damage") are excluded from the added pool via the same
   `weaponModSources` partition the conversion scope fix built; they
   neither convert nor remain. Including them overshoots ~+29%.
3. **No parent-tree mods** (`CalcActiveSkill` cfg build): `cfg.groupSource`
   ("SkillId:<parent>" — the channel that routes parent specialization-tree
   mods onto granted sub-skills, in-game-validated for Spriggan Form) is NOT
   wired for ailment finishers. sh4re-2 "Intensity" (+8% Damage, "Shadow
   Rend deals more damage") is provably absent from the in-game value.
   Spriggan Form sub-skills (real abilities, not finishers) keep inheriting.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestShadowDaggersFinisher_spec.lua` (source contracts).

### `sceptre-not-mace`

LE Sceptres are their own weapon type. `weaponTypeInfo["Sceptre"].flag` is
`"Sceptre"` (was `"Mace"` — an upstream-PoB PoE-ism: PoE sceptres are
one-hand maces; LE's are not). `SkillType.Sceptre` carries the same
Unsupported bit as Mace so weapon-FLAG matching stays byte-identical; only
the published `Using<X>` conditions split (CalcSetup mainhand block +
CalcPerform both-hands block both go through `info.flag`).

**Ground truth:** Prepfor1o1 wields Firestarter's Torch (Brass Sceptre base,
baseTypeID 8) + Traitor's Tongue (dagger). Rogue-65 "Weapons of Choice"
"+10% Critical Multiplier with a Mace and Dagger" ×4pt parses with intact
conditions {UsingMace, UsingDagger, DualWielding}; the in-game carried
critMult is 2.45 (= base 100 + TT 45) on Shadow Daggers AND Shadow Blade
rows alike, while sceptre→UsingMace published 2.85. The realized SD damage
fits 2.45 (−1.27%) vs 2.85 (−12.9%): the node does not fire on
Sceptre+Dagger in-game.

Real maces (One-Handed/Two-Handed Mace) keep flag "Mace" — the
`wielding-weapon-conditions` guard (UsingMace affix gates) is unaffected.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestShadowDaggersFinisher_spec.lua`
("sceptre-not-mace" describe block).

**Why:** Primalist lone-companion passives (Primalist-32 Natural Bond,

### `bear-tree-grants-minion-skills`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestMinionTreePropagation_spec.lua` (parser + build
integration)

`src/Data/ModCache.lua` rows (` Bear Can Use Earthquake`, ` Bears use Swipe`,
`-60% Bear Earthquake Damage`); consumer `calcs.createMinionSkills`
(`src/Modules/CalcActiveSkill.lua`).

**Why:** 4th instance of the tree-grants-skill class (minion variant). The
grant lines were ModCache `{{},""}` no-ops, so createMinionSkills never saw an
ExtraMinionSkill mod and the bear's two dominant in-game abilities (Earthquake
69% / Swipe 11% of bear damage) were unmodeled. Originally the grants reused
the PLAYER skill entries (EarthquakeSlam / Swipe); since `<see git log>` +
`<see git log>` they are flagged `inheritsMinionAttackBase` and createMinionSkills
builds each as a weapon-base CLONE of the bear's basic attack under the
distinct id `<skillId>_MinionWeaponBase` (F4-oracle-grounded — see
`minion-granted-weapon-attack-base-inheritance`). `-60% Bear Earthquake
Damage` still PARSES via MinionModifier{PrimalBear} keeping its
SkillName=Earthquake tag (that parse contract stays guarded here), but it
deliberately does NOT attach to the clone: the F4 oracle (DoNotReleaseThem,
2026-07-01) showed the bear EQ element-MORE == Melee's (9.9, no ×0.4), so the
clone's `skillNameForMatch` id detaches SkillName:Earthquake mods; the EQ
clone instead carries its own eff-6 Hit MORE (+500% vs the melee's eff 1).
` Bear Can Use Teleport` (no damage component) and
`+1 Bear Earthquake Charges` (cast cadence) intentionally stay no-ops.

### `berserk-stack-melee-damage`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestBerserkStackMeleeDamage_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `Data/Global.lua` `LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE["wc57-22"]` +
`LE_TREE_NODE_GLOBAL_SCOPE["wc57-22"]`; `Modules/ModParser.lua` modTagList
`"per stack of berserk"`; `Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` `multiplierBerserkStacks`.

**Why:** Warcry's "Berserker" node (`wc57-22`, Primalist) grants the Berserk buff
on Warcry use: "+4 Melee Damage Per Stack", max 10 (Berserker) + 1 per Brutality
point (15 at 5/5). The stat string carries neither the per-stack fact ("Per
Stack" = per Berserk stack, shared by 18 unrelated stacking stats so a generic
tag collides) nor that the buff is GLOBAL on the player (every melee skill, not
Warcry-scoped). The skill-subtree SkillId:Warcry tag confined the flat melee to
Warcry — which deals no damage — so the player Swipe got nothing (the in-game
−27% gap on DoNotReleaseThem lv69: Swipe phys 1507 vs LEB 994). The fix mirrors
`rhythm-stack-crit-multi`/`throne-of-ambition-stacks`: a node-keyed rewrite
appends "per stack of Berserk", the modTagList attaches
`Multiplier:BerserkStacks` (limit 15), `LE_TREE_NODE_GLOBAL_SCOPE` lifts the
SkillId tag, and a `# of Berserk Stacks` config (default 0 → strict no-op, zero
corpus impact) drives it. Validated in-game (ProbeBerserkSwipe): default 0 →
993.9 phys (= pre-fix, no regression); 10 stacks → 1524.0 ≈ in-game 1507
(+1.1%, the sustained-rotation average); linear +53.0 phys/stack. Lightning is
untouched (Berserk is physical melee; the Swipe light over-model is a separate
type-split issue). The Attack-Speed (Fury Strikes, own 16% cap), Damage-to-Feared
and companion-extension (Bloodthirst `wc57-25`) facets are NOT modeled here
(documented follow-ups).

### `eye-of-reen-reens-ire`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestEyeOfReenReensIre_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` `multiplierReensIreStacks` (the ONLY site —
this is a config-driven mechanic; `ModParser`/`ModCache` are deliberately NOT
touched).

**Why:** Eye of Reen (Unique 1H Katana, Lv70) grants a stack of Reen's Ire for 5s
when you crit with a melee attack, "up to 30 times per 5 seconds". Each stack grants
"5% melee critical strike multiplier and 10% increased fire damage over time"
(datamined verbatim from the unique's `tooltipDescription`,
`items/uniques_v3.json` "Eye of Reen"; the buff `ailments_v3.json`
`nonAilmentUIBuffs[140]` "Reens Ire" has `buffID` null and no magnitude array —
"Increases fire damage over time and adds melee critical strike multiplier." —
direction-confirms the pair, magnitude comes from the item tooltip). The per-stack
magnitude line is FLAVOR text (a tooltipDescription), NOT a parseable mod. The only
parseable Reen's Ire mod on the item is the grant line (`ModCache.lua` ~L16096,
`"…gain a stack of Reen's Ire…up to 30 times per 5 seconds"`) which compiles to an
EMPTY modlist `{{}, …}` = no-op — so the per-stack effect was completely unmodeled.
Modeled with the Void Essence direct-apply config pattern (`ConfigOptions.lua`, same
section): a `type = "count"` option `multiplierReensIreStacks` whose `apply()` emits,
per stack N, `CritMultiplier` BASE `N*5` melee-scoped (`KeywordFlag.Melee` — matches
the "+N% Melee Critical Multiplier" ModCache form, keywordFlags 512) and `FireDamage`
INC `N*10` with `bit.bor(ModFlag.Dot, ModFlag.Fire)` flags (matches "N% increased
Fire Damage Over Time", flags 4104). Per-stack stacking is ADDITIVE (one mod of value
× stacks), capped at 30 (`math.min(val, 30)`). LEB cannot know the live stack count
(it depends on melee-crit uptime), so it is a user input; DEFAULT blank → val 0 →
both `NewMod`s emit value 0 → strict no-op = corpus-neutral (all 11 Eye of Reen
corpus builds stay byte-identical until the user sets the stack count; verified by an
in-memory `loadBuildFromXML` TotalDPS probe = snapshot-identical, and zero
`"Reen's Ire"`-sourced mods present at default). The scoping is asserted in the spec:
the crit multi is melee-only (does NOT leak into spell crit multi) and the fire INC
is DoT-only (does NOT leak into fire hit damage). The other Eye of Reen affixes
(melee/fire flat, ignite-chance, base crit multi) are ordinary parsed mods and are
NOT part of this guard.

### `event-horizon-config-stacks`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestEventHorizonDilation_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` `multiplierDilationStacks` (the ONLY site —
this is a config-driven mechanic; `ModParser`/`ModCache` are deliberately NOT
touched).

**Why:** Event Horizon (Unique 2H Mace / Vault Crusher, Lv80) grants a stack of
Dilation when you use a Melee Attack and hit at least one enemy, "up to 10"
(no time limit, ALL stacks lost on Evade). Each stack grants "15% more Melee
Damage per stack (multiplicative), 5% less attack/cast speed per stack, 5% less
move speed per stack" (datamined verbatim from the unique's tooltip — 未モデル
affix gear grounding 2026-07-12, B5; the buff `ailments_v3.json` "Dilation" has
`buffID` null and no magnitude array — direction-confirms, magnitude comes from
the item tooltip). The per-stack magnitude line is FLAVOR text, NOT a parseable
mod. The only parseable Dilation mod on the item is the grant line
(`ModCache.lua` ~L10793, `"…gain Dilation when you use a Melee Attack and hit at
least one enemy"`) which compiles to an EMPTY modlist `{{}, …}` = no-op — so the
per-stack effect was completely unmodeled. Modeled with the Void Essence /
Reen's Ire direct-apply config pattern (`ConfigOptions.lua`, same section): a
`type = "count"` option `multiplierDilationStacks` whose `apply()` emits, per
stack N, `Damage` MORE `N*15` melee-scoped (`ModFlag.Melee` — matches the "N%
more Melee Damage" form). Per-stack stacking is a single MORE mod of value ×
stacks, capped at 10 (`math.min(val, 10)`). LEB cannot know the live stack count
(melee-hit uptime, wiped on Evade), so it is a user input; DEFAULT blank → val 0
→ `NewMod` emits a MORE of value 0 → strict no-op = corpus-neutral (both Event
Horizon corpus builds stay byte-identical until the user sets the stack count;
the "config 0 default no-op" spec proves the base melee `More` is unchanged at 0
stacks, and no `ModParser`/`ModCache`/parse-path was touched so snapshot inputs
are unchanged — same default-0-inert pattern as the shipped `eye-of-reen-reens-ire`
sibling). The scoping is asserted in the spec: the MORE is melee-only (does NOT
leak into spell or DoT damage). **Intentionally NOT modeled:** the per-stack
-5% attack/cast speed and -5% move speed downsides are part of the same buff but
are out of scope for this config (which scopes the offensive per-stack MORE
only). The other Event Horizon affixes (melee flat, stun, penetration, move
speed, more-to-slowed) are ordinary parsed mods and are NOT part of this guard.

### `scissor-of-atropos-kismet-stacks`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestScissorOfAtroposKismet_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` `multiplierKismetStacks` (the ONLY site —
this is a config-driven mechanic; `ModParser`/`ModCache` are deliberately NOT
touched).

**Why:** Scissor of Atropos (Unique 1H Sword, Lv60) grants "1 Kismet Stack when
you directly use a Melee Attack and hit at least one enemy" (up to 8). Kismet is
a player-direct THROWING buff: each stack grants +8% throwing critical strike
chance and +8 added throwing physical damage; stacks are BUILT by melee hits and
CONSUMED on throw (consume-on-throw burst), coupling the two attack types
(dual-wield raises the stack-gain rate). Per-stack magnitudes are datamine-
confirmed (8% throw crit + 8 throw phys per stack, cap 8 — 未モデル affix gear
grounding B-group, NO curve-fit; the magnitudes live in the buff definition, not
in the item mods). The only parseable Kismet mod on the item is the grant line
(`ModCache.lua` ~L10122, `"1 Kismet Stacks gained when you directly use a Melee
Attack and hit at least one enemy"`) which compiles to an EMPTY modlist `{{}, …}`
= no-op — so the per-stack effect was completely unmodeled. Modeled with the Void
Essence / Reen's Ire / Dilation / Infusion direct-apply config pattern
(`ConfigOptions.lua`, same section): a `type = "count"` option
`multiplierKismetStacks` whose `apply()` emits, per stack N, `CritChance` BASE
`N*8` throwing-scoped (`KeywordFlag.Throwing`) + added `PhysicalDamage` BASE `N*8`
throwing-scoped (`KeywordFlag.Throwing`). Per-stack stacking is a single BASE mod
of value × stacks each, capped at 8 (`math.min(val, 8)`). LEB cannot know the
live stack count (melee-hit uptime, wiped on every throw), so it is a user input;
DEFAULT blank → `count` type → `ConfigTab` calls `apply()` only when input is
non-nil AND non-zero (`ConfigTab.lua` L1708), so at 0/blank NO mod is emitted →
strict no-op = corpus-neutral (both Scissor corpus builds — e.g. Bladedancer /
Spellblade — stay byte-identical until the user sets the stack count; the "config
0 default no-op" spec proves the base throwing `CritChance`/`PhysicalDamage` BASE
sums are unchanged at 0 stacks, and no `ModParser`/`ModCache`/parse-path was
touched so snapshot inputs are unchanged — same default-0-inert pattern as the
shipped `eye-of-reen-reens-ire` / `event-horizon-config-stacks` /
`scales-eterra-infusion` siblings). The scoping is asserted in the spec: the
crit/phys is THROWING-only (does NOT leak into melee or spell). **Intentionally
NOT modeled:** the consume-on-throw BURST rotation (melee builds stacks, throw
spends them all) is stack-count/rotation-dependent, so the steady per-stack effect
is gated behind an explicit user opt-in (default 0). A precise non-0 landing would
need a throw-consume average-stack capture (priority LOW, 2 builds only, throwing-
limited). The other Scissor of Atropos affixes (melee flat, attack speed, +melee
skills, Vitality) are ordinary parsed mods and are NOT part of this guard.

### `chaos-bolts-exult-in-misery-enemy-ailment`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestChaosBoltsExultInMisery_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `Data/Global.lua` `LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE["ch4bo-11"]`;
`Classes/PassiveTree.lua` `ProcessStats` (empty-line skip, both stat loops);
`Modules/ModParser.lua` modTagList `"per negative ailment on enemy"`;
`Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` `multiplierEnemyNegativeAilmentCount`;
`Data/ModCache.lua` (four stale `"+4% Hit Damage to {Bleeding,Damned,
Frostbitten,Ignited}"` rows REMOVED — assert their absence in the spec, since
ModCache is auto-generated and cannot carry a durable inline guard).

**Why:** the Warlock "Exult in Misery" node (`ch4bo-11`, Chaos Bolts tree,
`TreeData/{1_2,1_3,1_4}/tree_3.json`, `maxPoints 3`, 1_4 lines 8600-8629) has four
DISPLAY stats — `"+4% Hit Damage to Damned"`, `"...to Ignited"`, `"...to Bleeding"`,
`"...to Frostbitten"` — with description "Chaos Bolts' hits deal more damage
(multiplicative with other modifiers) to damned, ignited, bleeding and frostbitten"
and reminderText "Hitting enemies inflicted with multiple of these ailments, will
cause the damage modifier to stack." These are NOT four independent gates: the engine
builds ONE `perAilment` value (= the node's 4%/pt, `ChaosBoltsDamageMutator` field
`+0x154`) and multiplies it by the live count of DISTINCT negative ailments on the
target. Datamine (`datamined game source`, ctor at
`datamined game source`): `factor = 1 + perAilment ×
GetUniqueNegativeAilmentCount(target)`, `maxAilments` arg `= 0` (uncapped). So a 3/3
node against all four ailments = `×(1 + 0.12×4) = ×1.48` on Chaos Bolts hits. The
4%/pt is a literal in tree data (`DAT_183d71c08 = 1.0` is the universal float-one base,
NOT a magnitude). Pre-fix LEB mis-parsed the four lines (`Data/ModCache.lua`), and
crucially EVERY one left NON-EMPTY residue: "to Bleeding"→`SkillName "Bleed"` +
`"   to ing "`, "to Ignited"→`SkillName "Ignite"` + `"   to d "`, "to Damned"→bare
MORE + `"   to  "`, "to Frostbitten"→bare MORE + `"   to Frostbitten "`. PassiveTree's
tree gate drops any node mod with non-empty `extra` (`if mod.list and
(not mod.extra or mod.extra == "")`), so ALL FOUR were DROPPED — pre-fix the node
contributed **NOTHING** (the same "node contributed nothing" class as
`aerial-prowess-per-stack`, NOT an active over-count as a first read of the bare bug
suggests). This was VERIFIED two ways: a tree probe on `ch4bo-11` at 3/3 shows 0
surviving Damage MORE mods pre-fix vs exactly 1 (scoped, count-gated) post-fix, and a
3-build corpus A/B (e.g. `spec/TestBuilds/1.4/<private build>` lv98 Lich, with the changes
stashed vs applied) shows ZERO output change at default config. So the fix is strictly
corpus-neutral at default config (no snapshot regen needed — outputs are byte-identical)
and its real value is newly ENABLING the node when the config is set (count > 0). The fix
collapses the four DISPLAY lines into the engine's SINGLE count-scaled MORE:
`LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE["ch4bo-11"]` rewrites the Damned line to "per Negative
Ailment on Enemy" (node-keyed, $-anchored, value-tolerant — leading "+4%" preserved,
rank-scales to +12% at 3/3) and EMPTIES the other three; `ProcessStats` skips the
emptied lines so they neither reach `parseMod` (which would leave a space residue →
false `node.extra`) nor emit phantom mods. ModParser attaches
`Multiplier:EnemyNegativeAilmentCount` with `actor="enemy"` (mirroring the "+1% Hit
Damage Per Bleed" precedent, `BleedStack`/`actor=enemy`); the count lives on the enemy
modDB, fed by the `# Distinct Negative Ailments on Enemy` config (`ifMult`-gated,
`math.min(val,4)`, default 0 → multiplier 0 → MORE factor 1.0 → strict no-op). The
config sets a `Multiplier:EnemyNegativeAilmentCount` BASE mod on the enemy modList
which `ModStore:GetMultiplier` sums directly (3rd term, `enemyDB.conditions.Effective`
is true in the effective pass) → `GetMultiplier == N`. **There is NO CalcPerform
propagation into `enemyDB.multipliers`** — the former enemy-stack loop was REMOVED (see
`multiplier-propagation-loop-no-double-count`) because it copied the SAME BASE value
into `multipliers[var]`, making `GetMultiplier = multipliers[var] + Sum(BASE) = 2N`
(a 3/3 all-4 node read ×1.96 instead of ×1.48). Do NOT reintroduce the loop.
Exactly ONE MORE must survive: four separate MOREs would compound
multiplicatively in `ModDB:MoreInternal` (≈×1.57 at count=4), not the engine's
additive-within-mod `value×count` (×1.48) — this is why the documented "rewrite all
four to +1% summing to 4" fallback is WRONG and was rejected. `ch4bo-11` is
deliberately NOT in `LE_TREE_NODE_GLOBAL_SCOPE`: the MORE is consumed by and scoped to
Chaos Bolts via the default owning-skill `SkillId` tag (mirroring AerialAssault, not
Berserk). The four stale ModCache rows are REMOVED (the unrelated `"+4% Hit Damage to
Cursed"` enemy-ActorCondition row is KEPT) so the live parser regenerates the collapsed
mod (Ambition/Germination/AerialAssault REMOVE-not-patch precedent). At default config 0
the net corpus effect is ZERO (the pre-fix mods were already dropped by the residue gate,
and the new mod is inert at count 0) — byte-identical snapshots, no new positive damage
until the user sets the count.

### `multiplier-propagation-loop-no-double-count`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestMultiplierPropagationNoDoubleCount_spec.lua` (plus the inverted
`CalcPerform` assertions in `spec/System/TestChaosBoltsExultInMisery_spec.lua`).

**Site:** `Modules/CalcPerform.lua` — the (now-DELETED) enemy-stack propagation loop,
just after `doActorMisc(env, env.enemy)`. The inline `@leb-regression-guard` marker sits
where the loop was.

**Why:** enemy "per X stack / per negative ailment" counts — `BleedStack`, `IgniteStack`,
`ShockStack`, `ChillStack`, `PoisonStack`, `TimeRotStack`, `DoomStack`, `SlowStack`,
`FrailtyStack`, `CurseStack`, `EnemyNegativeAilmentCount` (11 vars) — are each fed by a
config `Multiplier:XStack` `"BASE"` mod on the enemy modList, gated by
`Condition:Effective` (e.g. `ConfigOptions.lua` `multiplierEnemyNegativeAilmentCount`,
`NewMod("Multiplier:EnemyNegativeAilmentCount","BASE",val,"Config",{Condition:Effective})`).
`ModStore:GetMultiplier` (`Classes/ModStore.lua:261`) is
`(self.multipliers[var] or 0) + parent + Sum("BASE", cfg, "Multiplier:"..var)`. In the
effective-DPS pass `enemyDB.conditions.Effective = true`, so the config BASE mod IS
summed by that 3rd term = `N`. A former loop
`for var in {…11 vars…} do local val = enemyDB:Sum("BASE", nil, "Multiplier:"..var); if
val > 0 then enemyDB.multipliers[var] = val end end` **also** wrote the same value into
`enemyDB.multipliers[var]`, so `GetMultiplier = multipliers[var] + Sum(BASE) = 2N` — an
UNCONDITIONAL DOUBLER for every one of the 11 vars. Consumers that read the count via a
`Multiplier:EnemyNegativeAilmentCount`/`Multiplier:BleedStack` tag (Chaos Bolts "Exult in
Misery" `ch4bo-11`, Mad Alchemist's Ladle, Profane Orb Hex Flurry `pr5fm-29`, per-bleed /
per-curse mods) then read `factor = 1 + perAilment × (2N)` instead of the datamined
`1 + perAilment × N` — e.g. `ch4bo-11` 3/3 with all four ailments = ×1.96 instead of the
correct ×1.48. The loop's own comment claimed the config mod's `Condition:Effective` "only
resolves in this pass, not in per-skill EvalMod, so this single propagation … does not
double-count"; a probe showed that FALSE (`enemyDB.conditions.Effective == true`, so the
per-skill `Sum` includes the config mod). The bug was LATENT (grep of `spec/TestBuilds/`:
ZERO builds set any of these configs — all default 0 — so snapshots were byte-identical
and no corpus build was live-affected), but real at any config > 0. **Fix = delete the
loop** so the BASE-sum is the single source of truth: `GetMultiplier(var, cfg) == N`.
Verified end-to-end (`<private build> lv92 Warlock`, config N=3): pre-fix
`GetMultiplier("EnemyNegativeAilmentCount") = 6`, post-fix `= 3`; N=0 → 0 both.
Safe because there is **ZERO** direct reader of `enemyDB.multipliers[<stackvar>]` in
`src/` (the only reference was the loop's own write) — nothing depended on the propagated
copy. Do **NOT** reintroduce the loop, and do **NOT** "just remove one var from it": all
11 doubled identically, so a partial fix leaves the other 10 broken. Do **NOT** touch
`ModStore:GetMultiplier`'s BASE-sum (core, load-bearing) or the config `Condition:Effective`
mechanism (the canonical single source of truth). Unrelated non-looped multipliers stay
single-count and correct: `MissingHealthPercent` (BASE-only, never propagated) and the
`TotemsSummoned` propagation at `CalcPerform.lua` (set from computed output, has no
`Multiplier:TotemsSummoned` BASE twin → not a doubler → leave it).

### `ladle-negative-ailment-on-target`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestLadleNegativeAilmentTarget_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `Modules/ModParser.lua` modTagList `"per negative ailment on the target"`
(NEW, sibling to the existing `"per negative ailment on enemy"`); `Data/ModCache.lua`
(one stale `"6% more Spell Damage per Negative Ailment on the Target (up to 8)"` row
REMOVED — assert its absence in the spec, since ModCache is auto-generated and cannot
carry a durable inline guard).

**Why:** Mad Alchemist's Ladle (unique, `Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json` id 321) has
`"6% more Spell Damage per Negative Ailment on the Target (up to 8)"` — the SAME engine
mechanic as Chaos Bolts' Exult in Misery (`DamageEffectMoreDamagePerNegativeAilment`,
`factor = 1 + perAilment × GetUniqueNegativeAilmentCount(target)`), but the ITEM text
says "on the Target" whereas the (rewritten) tree text says "on Enemy". ModParser's
modTagList had ONLY `"per negative ailment on enemy"`, so `"...on the target"` was
UNRECOGNIZED and left as NON-EMPTY residue `"   per Negative Ailment on the Target  "`.
`Item.lua`'s mod-line gate (`not modLine.extra`, ~L1864/1879) then DROPPED the mod —
the Ladle contributed **NOTHING** to spell damage (the "node contributed nothing" class,
same as `chaos-bolts-exult-in-misery-enemy-ailment` and `aerial-prowess-per-stack`, NOT
an active over-count). A stale `Data/ModCache.lua` row cached that dropped shape (flat
`Damage MORE 6` + residue) and, being cache-first, shadowed any live rule. So the Ladle's
real mechanic — 6% more Spell PER distinct enemy negative ailment up to 8 (max +48%, 0
with none) — was entirely absent. The precedent for the suffix is `"per stack of bleed on
the target"` (already `actor="enemy"`); ModParser strips the `"(up to 8)"` parenthetical
BEFORE the modTagList lookup, so the new key carries no parens (cap rides the tag's
`limit=8`) and the mod now parses RESIDUE-FREE → the item loader KEEPS it. The shared
`"per negative ailment on enemy"` entry deliberately stays limit-less (its Chaos Bolts
consumer is config-capped at 4, `maxAilments` arg 0 = uncapped engine-side); the Ladle's
per-tag `limit=8` is the item's own cap and does NOT touch that entry. The count lives on
the enemy modDB via the `# Distinct Negative Ailments on Enemy` config
(`multiplierEnemyNegativeAilmentCount`, default 0 → multiplier 0 → MORE factor 1.0 →
strict no-op). So the fix is **CORPUS-NEUTRAL** — all 28 corpus Ladle builds are
byte-identical (recompute-vs-snapshot 0/28 changed, **NO snapshot regen**) — and its
value is newly ENABLING the per-ailment scaling that was dropped (verified: Rip Blood
Warlock `om6xj3n8` FullDPS ×1.26 at count=8; and the pre-fix drop is why removing it is
neutral, mirroring the Chaos Bolts A/B). 5 Maxroll S-tier builds carry the Ladle (Profane
Veil / Rip Blood Lich + Warlock / Lightning Blast RM / Shatter Totem Werebear). Scaling
invariant: the mod MUST carry `Multiplier:EnemyNegativeAilmentCount` — a bare MORE (no
tag) would be a flat always-on +6%, wrong in the other direction.

### `to-low-health-enemies`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestToLowHealthEnemies_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `Modules/ModParser.lua` modTagList `"to low health enemies"` (NEW, sibling to
the existing `"against full health enemies"`); `Data/ModCache.lua` (one stale
`"14% more Spell Damage to Low Health Enemies"` row REMOVED — assert its absence in the
spec, since ModCache is auto-generated and cannot carry a durable inline guard).

**Why:** enemy-scoped "low health" (execute-range, enemy below ~35% health) damage
conditional, used by uniques such as Swaddling of the Erased (`Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json`
id 293, `"(12-17)% more Spell Damage to Low Health Enemies"`). ModParser had the
PLAYER-self forms `"at low health"` / `"while at low health"` → `Condition:LowLife`
(~L1575) but NO enemy-scoped `"to low health enemies"` phrase, so the stat parsed its
leading `"more Spell Damage"` but left `"to Low Health Enemies"` as NON-EMPTY residue →
`Item.lua`'s mod-line gate (`isConnectorOnlyExtra`, `Item.lua:1901`) DROPPED the whole
mod — the unique's MORE contributed **NOTHING** (the "node contributed nothing" class,
same as `ladle-negative-ailment-on-target` / `against-rares-and-bosses`, NOT an
over-count). A stale `Data/ModCache.lua` row cached that dropped shape (flat
`Damage MORE 14` + residue) and, being cache-first, shadowed any live rule. The fix maps
`"to low health enemies"` → `ActorCondition{var="LowLife", actor="enemy"}` — the mirror
of the pre-existing `"against full health enemies"` (var `FullLife`) entry. The enemy
`LowLife` condition already exists (`Global.lua:256`) and `conditionEnemyLowLife`
(`ConfigOptions` ~L980) already anticipates this exact vocabulary in its `suggestPattern`
(`"to low health enemies"`, `"more spell damage to low health"`) — it simply had no
modTagList entry to resolve the phrase. **CORPUS-NEUTRAL:** `conditionEnemyLowLife`
defaults OFF → the enemy is not flagged low life → the (non-neg) `LowLife` enemy condition
is FALSE → the MORE is inert by default (all 22 corpus builds equipping Swaddling have
LowLife OFF → 0/22 change, **NO snapshot regen**). Enabling the config (execute/burst
evaluation) makes it live. Scope invariant: the mod MUST carry the ENEMY-actor
`ActorCondition:LowLife` — a bare MORE would be an always-on flat MORE (wrong), and a
player-self `Condition:LowLife` (no `actor="enemy"`) would be the different
`"while at low health"` self-mechanic. Must also retain the `Spell` keyword (scales spell
damage only).
