### `to-moving-enemies`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestToMovingEnemies_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `Modules/ModParser.lua` modTagList `"to moving enemies"` (NEW, the enemy-scoped
sibling of the existing PLAYER-self `"while moving"`); `Data/ModCache.lua` (two stale rows
REMOVED — `"35% more Physical Ailment Damage to Moving Enemies"` [Blood of the Exile resolved
roll] and `"+15% Hit Damage To Moving Enemies"` [affix/tree] — assert their absence in the spec).

**Why:** enemy-motion damage conditional "<stat> to Moving Enemies", used by Blood of the Exile
(`uniques_1_4.json` #306, `"(30-40)% more Physical Ailment Damage to Moving Enemies"`) and the
`"+15% Hit Damage To Moving Enemies"` affix/tree line carried by ~29 corpus builds. ModParser had
only the PLAYER-self `"while moving"` → `Condition:Moving` form (~L918); there was NO enemy-scoped
`"to moving enemies"` phrase, so the stat parsed its leading `"more … Damage"` but left `"to Moving
Enemies"` as NON-EMPTY residue → `Item.lua`'s mod-line gate (`isConnectorOnlyExtra`, `Item.lua:1901`)
DROPPED the whole mod (silent UNDER-count, the "node contributed nothing" class, same as
`to-low-health-enemies` / `ladle-negative-ailment-on-target`, NOT an over-count). Two stale
`Data/ModCache.lua` rows cached that dropped shape (flat MORE + residue) and, being cache-first,
shadowed any live rule. The fix maps `"to moving enemies"` → `ActorCondition{var="Moving",
actor="enemy"}` — the enemy-actor mirror of the player `"while moving"`, matching the exact enemy
`Condition:Moving` flag that `conditionEnemyMoving` raises (`ConfigOptions.lua` ~L960/982; its
tooltip already names "'against moving enemies' modifiers"). **CORPUS-NEUTRAL (deductively proven,
no snapshot regen):** the ONLY code path that sets the enemy `Condition:Moving` flag is the
`conditionEnemyMoving` config's `apply` (`ConfigOptions.lua:982` → `enemyModList` `Condition:Moving`);
that config is ABSENT from EVERY corpus snapshot (`grep conditionEnemyMoving spec/TestBuilds` → 0
hits) → default OFF → the enemy is never flagged moving → the `ActorCondition` is FALSE
(`CalcOffence.lua:2724` `enemyDB:Flag("Condition:Moving")`) → the kept MORE is inert, byte-identical
to the pre-fix dropped state, across all ~29 equipping builds. Enabling the config (e.g. Bleed-on-
moving evaluation) makes it live. Scope invariants: the tag MUST be **enemy**-actor (a bare MORE
would be an always-on flat MORE; a player-self `Condition:Moving` would be the different `"while
moving"` self-mechanic — distinct config `conditionMoving`, `ConfigOptions.lua:86`); the `"+15% Hit
Damage …"` variant must retain its `ModFlag.Hit`.

### `damage-over-time-penetration-parse`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestDamageOverTimePenetrationParse_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `Modules/ModParser.lua` modNameList `"damage over time penetration"` (NEW, the
penetration sibling of `"damage over time"` / `"<type> penetration"`); `Data/ModCache.lua`
(two stale rows REMOVED — `"+23% Damage Over Time Penetration"` and `"+28% Damage Over Time
Penetration"`, both carrying the mangled `Damage MORE (Dot) {SkillName="Net"}` + `"Peration"`
residue shape — assert their absence in the spec).

**Why:** generic DoT penetration, used by Atrophy (`uniques_1_4.json` #116, `"+(20-25)% Damage
Over Time Penetration"`) and Weaver's Gift (#408, `"+(22-33)%"`). modNameList had no key for the
full 4-word phrase, so longest-match fell to the shorter `["damage over time"]` (`{ "Damage",
ModFlag.Dot }`) and consumed `"damage over time"`; the leftover `"Penetration"` was then mangled —
the substring `"net"` matched an ability named **Net** and was eaten as a `{SkillName="Net"}` tag,
leaving residue `"Peration"`. The line thus parsed to a bogus `Damage MORE (Dot) {SkillName=Net}`
with NON-EMPTY residue → `Item.lua`'s mod-line gate (`isConnectorOnlyExtra`, `Item.lua:1901`) /
`PassiveSpec` DROPPED the whole mod — the unique's DoT penetration contributed **NOTHING** (silent
UNDER-count, the "node contributed nothing" class). Two `Data/ModCache.lua` rows cached that mangled
shape and, being cache-first, shadowed any live rule. The fix maps `"damage over time penetration"`
→ `{ "Penetration", flags = ModFlag.Dot }` — the penetration sibling of `["damage over time"]`'s
Dot-flagged Damage. Penetration-family names bake as **BASE** (LE penetration is additive %-shred,
like resistance). `ModFlag.Dot` scopes it to DoT: `CalcOffence` sums generic `"Penetration"` in BOTH
the hit loop (`~L443`) and the ailment/DoT loop (`~L3733/3735`); the Dot flag makes the mod apply to
DoT/ailment damage (cfg carries Dot) and be excluded from hits (cfg lacks Dot) — exactly LE's "Damage
over Time Penetration" semantics. Longest-match already prefers this 4-word key over `"damage over
time"` / `"penetration"` (same precedent as `elemental-dot-flag-parse`). **NOT CORPUS-NEUTRAL (real
DoT-pen):** the 8 corpus builds equipping Atrophy / Weaver's Gift were snapshot-regenerated —
DoT-dealing equippers gain the previously-lost penetration (A/B: `<private build>` DoT Spellblade **+21%
FullDPS**), hit-based equippers are unchanged (the Dot-flagged mod is inert on their hit loop).
Invariants: the mod MUST be `Penetration BASE` (not `Damage MORE`), carry `ModFlag.Dot`, leave NO
residue, and carry NO `{SkillName="Net"}` tag.

### `while-at-full-health`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestWhileAtFullHealth_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `Modules/ModParser.lua` modTagList player forms `"at full health"` / `"while at full
health"` / `"at full life"` / `"while at full life"` / `"on full health"` / `"while on full health"`
(NEW, the player-self FullLife mirror of the LowLife player forms); `Data/ModCache.lua` (four stale
rows REMOVED — `"27% more Physical Damage while at Full Health"` [Xithara], `"+40% Melee Critical
Strike Multiplier while at Full Health"`, `"+40% Throwing Critical Strike Multiplier while at Full
Health"`, `"10% Increased Damage at Full Health"` — assert their absence in the spec).

**Why:** player-self "at Full Health/Life" damage/crit conditional, used by Xithara's Conundrum
(`uniques_1_4.json` #133, `"(25-30)% more Physical Damage while at Full Health"`) and the common
`"+40% <Melee/Throwing> Critical Strike Multiplier while at Full Health"` / `"10% Increased Damage at
Full Health"` affixes (carried by ~23 corpus builds, mostly Marksman/Bladedancer crit). The parser
had the ENEMY form (`"against full health enemies"` → `ActorCondition FullLife`) but NO player-self
`"while at full health"` phrase, so these parsed the leading stat but left `"while at Full Health"` as
NON-EMPTY residue → `Item.lua`'s mod-line gate (`isConnectorOnlyExtra`, `Item.lua:1901`) /
`PassiveSpec` DROPPED the whole mod (silent UNDER-count, the "node contributed nothing" class, same
as `to-low-health-enemies` / `to-moving-enemies`). Maps to the player `Condition{var="FullLife"}` —
the config's own flag. `conditionFullLife` (`ConfigOptions` L92) ALREADY anticipates this exact
vocabulary in its `suggestPattern` (`"while at full health"`, `"while at full life"`, `"while on full
health"`, `"on full health"`); it simply had no modTagList entry to resolve the phrase. **CORPUS-
NEUTRAL (deductively proven, no snapshot regen):** the ONLY setter of the player `Condition:FullLife`
flag is `conditionFullLife`'s `apply` (`ConfigOptions.lua:93` → `modList:NewMod("Condition:FullLife")`);
that config is ABSENT from EVERY corpus snapshot (`grep conditionFullLife spec/TestBuilds` → 0 hits) →
default OFF → the player is never flagged full life → the `Condition` is FALSE → the kept mod is inert,
byte-identical to the pre-fix dropped state across all ~23 equipping builds. (SkillStatMap entries with
`{type="Condition", var="FullLife"}` are consumers that GATE on the flag, not setters.) Enabling the
config (opener/burst evaluation) makes it live. Scope invariants: the tag MUST be the **player**
self-`Condition:FullLife` (`actor=nil`) — an enemy `ActorCondition` would be the different `"against
full health enemies"`; the crit-mult variant must retain its `Melee`/`Throwing` keyword.

### `enemy-full-health-alt-order`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestEnemyFullHealthAltOrder_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `Modules/ModParser.lua` modTagList enemy forms `"to full health enemies"` / `"to full life
enemies"` / `"vs full health enemies"` / `"vs full life enemies"` / `"against enemies at full health"`
/ `"against enemies at full life"` (NEW, word-order aliases of the existing `"against full health
enemies"` key); `Data/ModCache.lua` (four stale rows REMOVED — `"+10% Damage To Full Health Enemies"`,
`"+25% Melee Damage Vs Full Health Enemies"`, `"+30% Hit Damage Against Enemies At Full Health"`,
`"+30% Hit Damage Vs Full Health Enemies"`).

**Also covers** the es6ai-10 (Erasing Strike Ruthless) raw line `"+25% Melee Damage Vs Full Health Enemies"`:
the `"vs full health enemies"` key makes it parse residue-free (Damage MORE + Melee keywordFlag + non-neg
enemy FullLife), which retired its former `LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE["es6ai-10"]` entry as a NO-OP (see
retired `erasing-strike-ruthless-fullhealth` above). The spec asserts the es6ai-10 raw line stays MORE (not
INCREASED) with the Melee keyword — if either the bare-form→`BASE_MORE` behaviour or the `"vs full health
enemies"` key breaks, that case goes red here.

**Why:** the enemy "at full life" damage conditional appears in affix/tree lines in several word orders
(`"<stat> To Full Health Enemies"`, `"<stat> Vs Full Health Enemies"`, `"<stat> Against Enemies At Full
Health"`), but only the single `"against full health enemies"` order was registered in modTagList. So
the alt-order lines parsed the leading stat but left `"To/Vs Full Health Enemies"` / `"Against Enemies
At Full Health"` as NON-EMPTY residue → `Item.lua`'s mod-line gate (`isConnectorOnlyExtra`,
`Item.lua:1901`) DROPPED the whole mod (silent UNDER-count, the "node contributed nothing" class, same
as `against-full-health-enemies` / `to-low-health-enemies` / `to-moving-enemies`). All six new keys map
to the SAME enemy `ActorCondition{actor="enemy", var="FullLife"}` that `conditionEnemyFullLife` raises
(`ConfigOptions` L984; its `suggestPattern` already lists `"to full life enemies"`/`"to full health
enemies"`). **Longest-match invariant:** `"against enemies at full health"` CONTAINS the player-self
`"at full health"` substring (`ModParser` ~L1691); `scan()` is earliest-then-longest, so the longer
enemy key wins and the line stays enemy-scoped — the spec asserts this (the player self-Condition must
NOT attach) and fences the player self-form (`"while at Full Health"`) so it stays player-scoped.
**CORPUS-NEUTRAL (deductively proven, no snapshot regen):** the ONLY setter of the enemy
`Condition:FullLife` flag is `conditionEnemyFullLife`'s `apply` (`ConfigOptions.lua:985`); that config
is ABSENT from EVERY corpus snapshot (`grep conditionEnemyFullLife spec/TestBuilds` → 0 hits; `grep
Condition:FullLife` → 0) → default OFF → the enemy is never flagged full life → the (non-neg) FullLife
condition is FALSE → the kept MORE is inert, byte-identical to the pre-fix dropped state across every
equipping build. Enabling the config (opener/burst evaluation) makes it live. Scope invariants: the tag
MUST be the **enemy** `ActorCondition` (`actor="enemy"`, non-negated) — a negated FullLife would be the
different `"against damaged enemies"`, and a player self-`Condition` would be `"while at full health"`.

### `warpath-warslash-spin-duration-more`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestWarpathSpinDurationMore_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `Modules/ModParser.lua` modNameList `["slash damage"] = "Damage"` (name
site) + modTagList `"per second spinning"` (tag site);
`Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` `multiplierWarpathSpinSeconds`; `Data/ModCache.lua`
(stale `"+15% Slash Damage Per Second Spinning"` row REMOVED; the
`"+15% Area Per Second Spinning"` sibling row LEFT inert).

**Why:** the Warrior "Giant Splitter" node (`va53st-21`, Warpath tree,
`TreeData/1_4/tree_2.json`, maxPoints 5) grants `" Warslash After Warpath"`,
`"+15% Slash Damage Per Second Spinning"`, `"+15% Area Per Second Spinning"` plus
notScalingStats `"5 Maximum Duration Benefit (seconds)"`. Description: "After
spinning for at least 2 seconds you do a Warslash when you stop spinning. This
deals more damage (multiplicative with other modifiers) in a larger area for each
second you spent spinning, up to a maximum duration." So the per-second value is a
MORE that scales with the number of seconds spent spinning, capped at 5s.
datamining formula (`datamined game source`,
`datamined game source`): `MoreStat(min(spinSeconds, 5) × (15% × pointsAllocated))`.
Pre-fix the line baked to a FLAT `Damage` MORE 15 with `" Slash  Per Second
Spinning "` residue (`ModCache.lua`): the `"Slash"` melee-delivery descriptor was
never consumed, and the tree's non-empty-`extra` gate (`PassiveTree.lua:566`) then
DROPPED the node mod — the node contributed NOTHING (the AerialProwess pre-fix
failure mode). UNLIKE `aerial-prowess-per-stack`, the `"per second spinning"`
phrase is UNIQUE to `va53st-21` across every tree version (1_2/1_3/1_4) and appears
nowhere else in `src/Data`/`src/TreeData`, so NO `LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE` is
needed — the tag is routed directly: modNameList `["slash damage"] = "Damage"`
consumes the decorator so the line resolves to a clean generic `Damage` MORE, and
modTagList `"per second spinning"` attaches `Multiplier:WarpathSpinSeconds`
(`limit 5` = the node's "5 Maximum Duration Benefit (seconds)" cap). `va53st-21` is
deliberately NOT in `LE_TREE_NODE_GLOBAL_SCOPE`, so the DEFAULT owning-skill
`SkillId` tag (`node.skillId == "Warpath"`) keeps the MORE on Warpath — modeling the
in-game stored-MORE carried onto the Warslash fired when Warpath ends. A
`Seconds spent Spinning (Warpath, max 5)` config (`ifMult WarpathSpinSeconds`,
default 0 → strict no-op, `math.min(val, 5)` clamp; the planner cannot know runtime
spin time and no corpus build allocates `va53st-21`) drives it; the stale FLAT-baked
ModCache row is REMOVED so the live parser regenerates it WITH the multiplier (the
Ambition/Germination/AerialProwess REMOVE-not-patch precedent). Per-second stacking
is ADDITIVE within the mod (one MORE of value × seconds): at 5 points and 5 seconds
Warpath gains +375% MORE Damage (15% × 5 points × 5 seconds = 4.75×), at 0 seconds
nothing. SCOPE: only the per-second Damage MORE is modeled. The sibling `"+15% Area
Per Second Spinning"` baked row is LEFT inert (this fix does not touch it), and the
Warslash sub-ability is NOT registered as a damage-dealing sub-skill — its base hit
damage is absent from `prefab_damage.json`/`subprefab_damage.json`/
`ability_attribute_scaling.json` (no base/effectiveness), so a separate sub-ability
would need an invented base; documented follow-up, NOT modeled here.

### `dragonfang-stack-fire-damage`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestDragonfangStackFireDamage_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `Data/Global.lua` `LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE["htsk5-15"]`;
`Modules/ModParser.lua` modTagList `"per stack of dragonfang"`;
`Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` `multiplierDragonfangStacks`; `Data/ModCache.lua`
(stale `"+1 Bow/Spell/Throwing Fire Damage Per Stack"` rows REMOVED).

**Why:** the Marksman "Dragonfang" node (`htsk5-15`, Heartseeker tree,
`TreeData/1_4/tree_4.json`) grants "+1 Bow/Spell/Throwing Fire Damage Per Stack"
(stats); a Dragonfang stack is gained per consecutive Recurve (10s, "up to a
maximum of 20"). The per-stack flat-Fire semantics live in the node, and the bare
"Per Stack" phrasing is shared by ~18 unrelated stacking stats (e.g. the unrelated
"+5% Fire Damage Per Stack" MORE on a different `tree_4.json` node, L6862), so the
raw lines cannot be tagged generically — they compiled to stale FLAT `FireDamage`
BASE rows with `"   Per Stack "` residue (`ModCache.lua`), so the per-stack scaling
contributed NOTHING. Datamine proof (`datamining`):
`L580/585/591` `Stats__AddedStat(0, <tag>, field+0x144)` = `+1` Fire per stack,
capped at `0x14 = 20` (`L603/608`). The fix mirrors `aerial-prowess-per-stack`/
`berserk-stack-melee-damage`/`throne-of-ambition-stacks`/
`germination-per-companion-scaling`: `LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE["htsk5-15"]`
rewrites ONLY the trailing "Per Stack" → "per stack of Dragonfang" (node-keyed,
`$`-anchored, value-tolerant; the leading Bow/Spell/Throwing keyword and "Fire
Damage" survive, so the keyword-flagged `FireDamage` BASE 1 parse is preserved),
and the modTagList attaches `Multiplier:DragonfangStacks` (limit 20 = the node's
"up to a maximum of 20"). The flat Fire is granted to and consumed by Heartseeker,
so `htsk5-15` is deliberately NOT in `LE_TREE_NODE_GLOBAL_SCOPE` — the DEFAULT
owning-skill `SkillId` tag (Heartseeker) keeps it on that skill (unlike Berserk,
whose buff is player-global). A `# of Dragonfang Stacks (max 20)` config
(`ifMult DragonfangStacks`, default 0 → strict no-op, zero corpus impact until the
user sets it — the planner cannot know runtime stacks) drives it; the stale
FLAT-baked ModCache rows are REMOVED so the live parser regenerates them WITH the
multiplier (the Ambition/Germination/Aerial-Prowess REMOVE-not-patch precedent).
Per-stack stacking is ADDITIVE within the mod (one BASE mod of value × stacks): at
10 stacks each Heartseeker keyword (Bow/Spell/Throwing) gains +10 flat Fire, capped
at +20 stacks; at 0 stacks nothing.

### `umbral-blades-edge-of-obscurity-per-shroud`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestUmbralBladesEdgeOfObscurity_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `Data/Global.lua` `LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE["ub5d9-7"]`;
`Modules/ModParser.lua` modTagList `"per stack of dusk shroud"`;
`Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` `multiplierDuskShroudStacks` apply (the EXISTING
"Dusk Shroud Stacks" config now ALSO emits `Multiplier:DuskShroudStacks`).

**Why:** the Rogue "Edge of Obscurity" node (`ub5d9-7`, Umbral Blades tree,
`TreeData/1_4/tree_4.json`, maxPoints 3) grants `"+2% Damage per Dusk Shroud, up
to 20"` (stats) — Umbral Blades gains MORE damage (multiplicative) per active Dusk
Shroud, +2% per allocated point (so +6% at 3/3), capped at 20 Dusk Shrouds. The
bare "per Dusk Shroud" phrasing collides with unrelated Dusk-Shroud stats (a
sibling Shadow node `sh4re-8` carries `"+1% Damage per Dusk Shroud"` with NO "up
to 20"), so the raw line cannot be tagged generically — it misparsed via
`ModCache.lua` row 4465 to a `SkillName="Dusk Shroud"` MORE with residue
`" per , up to 20 "`, which (residue) was dropped, so the node contributed NOTHING.
Datamine proof (`datamined game source`): MORE =
`(InsideSmokeBomb?2:1) × nodeFloat(0x108 = 2%) × getStacks(0x52)`, capped at
`DAT_183d71c44 = 20`. The fix mirrors `aerial-prowess-per-stack`/
`berserk-stack-melee-damage`/`germination-per-companion-scaling`:
`LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE["ub5d9-7"]` rewrites the Damage line to end in "per
stack of dusk shroud" ($-anchored, value-tolerant) and DROPS the literal "20"
(folded into the modTagList key as `limit = 20`); the rewrite runs in
`PassiveTree:ProcessStats` at L393-397, BEFORE rank-scaling at L398-421, so "+2%"
scales to "+6%" at 3/3 while the "per stack" tail (no digit after "per") never
trips the "per N divisor" guard. The modTagList attaches
`Multiplier:DuskShroudStacks` (limit 20). UNLIKE Berserk, the MORE is scoped to
Umbral Blades (the tree's own skill), so `ub5d9-7` is deliberately NOT in
`LE_TREE_NODE_GLOBAL_SCOPE` — the DEFAULT owning-skill `SkillId` tag keeps it on
that skill. The EXISTING `multiplierDuskShroudStacks` config (default 0 → strict
no-op) now ALSO emits `Multiplier:DuskShroudStacks` off the SAME stack count, so
one count gates both the defensive Glancing Blow/Evasion and this offensive MORE
(semantically correct: both are "per Dusk Shroud" in-game). The stale `ModCache`
row 4465 is LEFT IN PLACE (the rewrite changes the node string before lookup, so
the row goes dead — the Berserk leave-it precedent; confirmed by the end-to-end
test producing the multiplier mod, not the row's `SkillName` misparse). Per-stack
stacking is ADDITIVE within the mod (one MORE of value × stacks): at 10 stacks /
3/3 Umbral Blades gains +60% MORE Damage, at 0 stacks nothing. The Smoke-Bomb ×2
doubling (notScalingStats `" Doubled Inside Smoke Bomb"`, datamine `(InsideSmoke
Bomb?2:1)`) is a documented follow-up (Mechanic 2), NOT modeled here. Corpus-
neutral (config default 0 → no-op), so no build snapshot regen beyond the spec.

### `spark-charge-detonation`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestSparkChargeData_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `src/Data/skills.json` (`SparkChargeExplosion` entry +
`excludeFromTriggerNameList`), `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (the `<name> chance`
trigger rule skips `excludeFromTriggerNameList`).

**Why:** the Spark Charge a Runemaster applies was modeled only as the stacking
debuff `Ailment_SparkCharge` (duration + stacks, 0 base damage); the actual
damage — the detonation HIT, ~60% of URA_YA_RANGE's in-game hit damage — was
absent from `data.skills` entirely. Game ground truth (datamined game source):
resources.assets ability `SparkChargeExplosion` (extracted/_spark_charge.json +
ability_attribute_scaling.json) = one `DamageEnemyOnHit` Lightning 20, eff 1.0,
isHit=1, crit 0.05/×2.0, tagsBitmap 258 (Lightning+Spell), attributeScalings
["Intelligence"]; the sibling `SparkCharge` asset is a no-hit SPAWNER.

**DATA-ONLY landing (no auto-grant).** This records the per-hit base + the
collision fix, but does NOT grant the detonation into builds. The detonation's
**name** stays "Spark Charge" (so Spark-Charge-scoped DAMAGE mods would reach it),
which collides with the `Ailment_SparkCharge` stack on the greedy ModParser
"`<name> chance`" → `ChanceToTriggerOnHit_<id>` rule (last writer wins). The
`excludeFromTriggerNameList` flag removes `SparkChargeExplosion` from that rule so
"X% Spark Charge Chance On Hit" (which applies a STACK = 0 damage, e.g. tree node
lb23il-25 "Cloud Answer") keeps resolving to `ChanceToTriggerOnHit_Ailment_SparkCharge`
and NOT to the explosion HIT (20 Lightning) — without this flag the new entry
would fabricate damage. With it, every build resolves byte-identically to before
the entry existed (verified: Zapp FullDPS 65,875 unchanged).

**Grant status — SUPERSEDED, now LANDED.** The grant + rate are no longer deferred:
the detonation is granted at a DERIVED rate by `spark-charge-detonation-grant` (below).
The two old blockers both dissolved: (1) the rate is fully derivable from the landed
Lightning Blast chain-rehit model + the parsed SC/Nova chances (it was never actually
RVA-blocked); (2) the "~11.5% Shock amplification" channel is REAL (wiki
`subskill-grant-shock-enemy-amplification`) but it does NOT reach the main skills in
this timer-trigger grant: the detonation does spawn an `Ailment_Shock` applier and raise
the shared enemy ShockStack (URA: 30.9 → 41.2), but the MAIN skills' DPS is read from the
CACHE pass (computed before this non-CACHE grant inserts its applier), so Lightning Blast
/ Spark Nova are byte-identical and the grant adds only the detonation's own hit DPS.
(`output.ShockChance` has no enemy-resistance consumer either way — the −5% Lightning
Res/stack is the `Ailment_Shock` applier's buff modList, not `output.ShockChance`.) This
data-only entry stays as the base-data + name-collision guard.

### `nondamaging-ailment-stack-cap`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestSparkChargeDetonationGrant_spec.lua` (describe "Spark Charge
detonation participates in Shock, capped by maxInstances"). **Site:**
`src/Modules/CalcActiveSkill.lua` — the ailment buff-mod loop (the `GlobalEffect`/`Debuff`
that builds `effectStackVar`). **Supersedes** `spark-charge-detonation-no-shock` (the
detonation-Shock suppression — removed).

**What:** wire each non-damaging ailment debuff's stack count to its game-data cap. LEB
summed every applier's `output.MaxStacks` (`Speed × Duration`) into `Multiplier:<id>Stack`
**uncapped** (CalcPerform "Process ailment debuffs stack count" loop), then applied
`−5% Lightning Res × stackCount` for Shock — with no clamp. The cap data was already
present and unused: `data.skills.Ailment_Shock.stats.maximum_stacks = 10` (==
`data.nonDamagingAilment.Shock.maxStacks`, == game-data `Ailment.maxInstances` for Shock;
Chill=3, Slow=3, Blind=1). The fix sets the Debuff `GlobalEffect`'s `effectStackLimit` from
`stats.maximum_stacks` (scoped to `baseFlags.ailment` skills), which flows to
`buff.stackLimit` (calcs `~L1319`) and clamps `stackCount` via `m_min` (CalcPerform `~L1007`).
**Guard `maximum_stacks > 0`** — 0/nil = "no cap" (like damaging ailments' `maxStacks=nil`),
and 0 is TRUTHY in Lua so a bare `and X or nil` would wire a 0 stackLimit and ZERO the debuff.

### `spark-charge-gear-apply`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestSparkChargeGearApply_spec.lua` (7 cases: on-Hit /
cache-miss on-Hit / on-Melee-Hit / on-Lightning-Melee-Hit parse to SC chance with
the right flags; a known ailment (Bleed) is NOT diverted; an unknown ailment still
→ LEB_NotSupported; no `apply a Spark Charge` ModCache row carries `notSupported`).

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (`isSparkChargeName` / `sparkChargeApplyMod`
inside `ailmentApplyHandler` + `ailmentApplyHandler2`), `src/Data/ModCache.lua`
(17 `+N% Chance to apply a Spark Charge on [Melee/Lightning Melee] Hit` rows
re-baked from LEB_NotSupported to the real mod).

**Why:** the gear/idol affix `+N% Chance to apply a Spark Charge on [Melee/
Lightning Melee] Hit` (URA_YA_RANGE crafted suffix `+(10-12)% Chance to apply a
Spark Charge on Hit`) parsed to `LEB_NotSupported`. "Spark Charge" is absent from
`knownAilmentChances`, and the `SparkChargeExplosion` HIT skill carries
`excludeFromTriggerNameList` (`spark-charge-detonation`), so the generic ailment
chain has no route for it — it fell through to `nsAny`. The handlers now special-
case it and emit `ChanceToTriggerOnHit_Ailment_SparkCharge` BASE — the **same stat**
the Cloud Answer tree node "X% Spark Charge Chance On Hit" already emits — so the
gear is just another source of the SC **application** chance (never a HIT trigger,
so it cannot fabricate `SparkChargeExplosion` damage).

**Flag mapping** (mirrors `modFlagList` "on melee hit"): bare `on Hit` →
`ModFlag.Hit` (8388608); `on Melee Hit` → `ModFlag.Melee|Hit` (8389120); `on
Lightning Melee Hit` → `ModFlag.Melee|Hit` + `KeywordFlag.Lightning` (2). ModCache
rows are patched directly (REGENERATE_MOD_CACHE=1 is blocked by a pre-existing
malformed-pattern bug; same workaround as `lightning-blast-chain-rehit`).

**Inert for DPS (by design).** This only corrects the SC *application* chance; the
detonation damage (`SparkChargeExplosion`) is still deferred (`spark-charge-
detonation`). Verified end-to-end on URA_YA_RANGE: Lightning Blast cfg SC chance
30 → **42** (Cloud Answer node 30 + gear 12; the +12% roll is a ModCache MISS so
the live handler produced it), Spark Nova cfg SC chance **42** too (multi-source),
`Ailment_SparkCharge` deals 0 base damage so FullDPS = 3,773,641 is **unchanged**.
The corrected chance is the honest input the deferred detonation-rate grant needs.

### `modnamelist-deterministic-trigger-resolution`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestRunemasterLightningSubskills_spec.lua`

**Site:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` — the `for skillId, skill in
pairsSortByKey(data.skills)` loop that builds the `"<name> chance"` /
`"chance to <name>"` / `"to <name>"` → `ChanceToTriggerOnHit_<skillId>` entries.

**Why:** when two skills resolve the same name/altName key, the LAST `modNameList`
write wins, so the resolved trigger target depended on Lua's `pairs` hash order —
which shifts whenever any skill is added to / removed from `data.skills`. Adding
`SparkChargeExplosion` (data-only Spark Charge) silently flipped **Bone Curse**
(`BoneCurse` → `Ailment_BoneCurse`) and **Arcane Ascendance** (`ArcaneAscendance`
→ `Ailment_ArcaneAscendance`). Iterating with `pairsSortByKey` makes the winner the
alphabetically-greatest `skillId`, STABLE against future additions. There are FIVE
order-sensitive collision groups; the greatest key wins each:
- **Bone Curse**: `BoneCurse` > `Ailment_BoneCurse`, `Ailment_NecroticBoneCurse`
- **Arcane Ascendance**: `ArcaneAscendance` > `Ailment_ArcaneAscendance`
- **Spirit Plague**: `SpiritPlague` > `Ailment_SpiritPlague`
- **Runebolt**: `Runemaster 05c3 Runebolt Cold` > `05c1 Fire`, `05c2 Lightning`
  (3 element variants; no element-neutral base, so the suffix tiebreak is arbitrary
  but deterministic)
- **"Mark For Death"** (name-vs-altName): `MarkForDeath` > `Ailment_MarkedForDeath`
  (whose altName is "Mark For Death"). The winner FLIPS vs `pairs` here.

ZERO corpus impact, verified by regen of **12 builds** across every affected class
(Acolyte/Necro/Warlock, Mage/Sorcerer/Runemaster, Rogue) — NOT because the names
are unused (affixes DO name these skills: `+N to Bone Curse/Runebolt`,
`Chance to Marked For Death on Hit`), but because every USED form is unaffected:
`+N to <skill>` is consumed by the `+N to skill` handler in `specialModList` BEFORE
this rule; the used trigger form `Marked For Death` (with the -ed) has NO collision
(only `Ailment_MarkedForDeath` carries that exact name); and the lone form whose
winner this flips, `Mark For Death` (no -ed), has zero corpus users. The fix exists
to keep that true against future skill additions. `Spark Charge` stays resolved to
`Ailment_SparkCharge` via `excludeFromTriggerNameList` (only the ailment registers);
a future ailment-application collision that needs the `Ailment_` variant rather than
the greatest key would use that same flag.

DECISIVE invariants (both fabrication-critical):
1. **NO Int scaling.** The "Cold Snap" damage children have `attributeScaling []`;
   the PARENT invocation `Runemaster 21 Expanding Cold Snap` (displayName "Wave of
   Frost", a *different* ability) does carry `[Intelligence]`. We model the child
   (what the log names "Cold Snap"), so Cold Snap is NO-Int — exactly the Lightning
   Explosion distinction. Confirmed by diffing the full Ability typetree of the
   known-good anchors `SmallLightningNova` (Int) vs `LightningExplosion` (no-Int):
   the field is `attributeScaling` (singular; `attribute: 2` = Intelligence), NOT
   the top-level `attributeScalings`/`damageTags` (both null/uniform). The same
   field read `[]` for the two Cold Snap children and `[Intelligence]` for the
   parent + SmallLightningNova.
2. **eff 2.5, not 1.** Unlike the lightning sub-skills (eff 1.0), Cold Snap's
   `addedDamageScaling` is 2.5 → `damageEffectiveness: 2.5`.
3. **skillTypeTags 260 mirrors the Ability-level `tags` field, NOT the per-hit
   `DamageEnemyOnHit.damageTags`** (which is uniformly 256 = Spell for every one of
   these sub-skills). Reproduced 258 (Spell+Lightning) for the already-merged
   `SmallLightningNova`/`LightningExplosion` from that same `tags` field before
   reading 260 (Spell+Cold) for the three Cold Snap assets — so the convention is
   consistent, not fabricated.

No `data.skills` skill is named "Cold Snap" (the only other "Cold Snap" in the repo
is the **Glacier** tree node `gl14-15`, a passive that never enters data.skills),
and no affix references "Cold Snap chance", so adding the key cannot collide. It
registers its own (currently unused) trigger-name entry; `pairsSortByKey` (the
`modnamelist-deterministic-trigger-resolution` guard) keeps every other collision
group's winner byte-stable against the addition.

### `auto-summon-registry`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestAutoSummonFramework_spec.lua`
- data: `data.autoSummons` loaded; every `summonSkill` exists in `data.skills`; bee entries map `BeesPerTenSeconds` / `ElementalBeesPerTenSeconds` → `SummonBee`
- linkage: `SummonBee.minionList` = `["Bee"]` (resolves to the real minions.json prefab; stale `"SummonedBee"` key gone)
- parser: `+N Bees Per 10 Seconds` → `BeesPerTenSeconds` BASE; `+N%` → INC; `Elemental` variant → `ElementalBeesPerTenSeconds`; `+N Melee Damage for your Summoned Bees` → Bee-scoped `MinionModifier`
- ModCache: bee rows rebaked to real mods (no `{{}}` empty-parse, no `" Bees Per 10 Seconds "` residue)
- end-to-end: `BeesPerTenSeconds > 0` injects `SummonBee` as an `includeInFullDPS` granted skill (source `AutoSummon:<stat>`, `noSupports`, `autoSummonCountStat` carried onto the group); no bee stat → no injection
- Phase B (datamine v1): registry rows for **Tyrannosaur** (Tyrant's Skull `+100% Summons Tyrannosaur Minion` → `TyrannosaursSummoned` BASE 1 → `Summon Giant T_Rex Minion` → `PrimalTyrannosaur`, Bite 125 phys), **Tolmat** (`+N Tolmat's Historic Minions` → `TolmatHistoricMinions` BASE N → `Summon Tolmat Minion` → `TolmatMinionDivine`, Melee 16 phys), **Anurok** (`1 Summon Anuroks up to your Companion Limit` → `AnuroksSummoned` BASE 1 → `Summon AncientOasis01 Primordial Minion` → `PrimalAnurok`, Melee 30 phys). Each summon skill's dangling minionList fixed to the real minions.json key; each minion's PRIMARY attack skill encoded in `skills.json` (datamine base damage + `addedDamageScaling`→`damageEffectiveness` + `useDelay`→`castTime`; index-1 of the resolvable kit). The `%` in the Tyrannosaur affix is a magnitude → parse count = 1, not 100. Tolmat count = N (stacks). Anurok = gate `AnuroksSummoned`=1, pack count = `MaxCompanions` (via `packCountStat`; in-game Deluyi capture showed count=1 was ~7.5× low → now ~3.1×, residual = general per-minion-scaling gap), primary = Tongue Slap (04, the dominant in-game attack, not 01 Melee). Secondaries/buffs/beams, Anurok pack-count, bee attack-rate (`castTime` vs `useDelay`) and minion `ActorStats` completeness all deferred to a refinement pass.
- Queen Bee (datamine v1, **set-bonus path**): Apiarist's Set 3-piece bonus `"Summon the Queen Bee"` → `QueenBeeSummoned` BASE 1 → **NEW** summon skill `SummonQueenBee` (`minionList ["QueenBee"]`) → `QueenBee` minion, primary attack **`Queen Bee 01 Scratch`** encoded (60 phys, `damageEffectiveness` 3, `castTime` 0.5). KEY: the granting string is a SET BONUS, not an item affix — `CalcSetup.applySetBonuses` runs each bonus tier through `modLib.parseMod`, so the ModParser rule fires and lands `QueenBeeSummoned` on `itemModDB`→`modDB` (no item-affix/ModCache row needed). Count always 1 (persistent). Quadruple Scratch + on-death Bee Explosion deferred (v1 single primary). In-game cross-check: Fehm's Apiarist build capture shows `SummonedQueenBee` casting Scratch.

**Sites:** `src/Data/AutoSummons.lua` (the `data.autoSummons` registry, `{countStat, summonSkill}` rows — bees + 3 Phase B + Queen Bee), `src/Modules/Data.lua` (loads it next to `subSkillGrants`), `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (bee + Phase B + Queen Bee count `specialModList` handlers + `modNameList` conditional-tail aliases), `src/Data/ModCache.lua` (15 rebaked bee rows + 3 rebaked Phase B count rows; Queen Bee needs none — set-bonus live-parse), `src/Data/skills.json` (3 Phase B + Queen Bee `SummonQueenBee` summon skill + `Queen Bee 01 Scratch` minion-attack skill + 3 minionList dangling fixes), `src/Modules/CalcSetup.lua` (the `grantedAutoSummons` source-independent scan + the `applySetBonuses` set-bonus→`parseMod` path + the `group.autoSummonCountStat` carry).

**Why:** LE auto-summons some minions from gear/affixes/passives rather than slotted skills (Apiarist "Bees" from "+N Bees Per 10 Seconds"). LEB recognized the affix text but baked it to an EMPTY mod, so no minion was modeled. The framework is data-driven: a registry row maps the granting COUNT stat to the existing summon skill, and a source-independent CalcSetup scan (mirroring the timer/capped trigger scans) injects that summon skill as a Full-DPS-only granted skill when the stat is present on the PLAYER modDB. The count stat MUST live on (and be summed from) the player modDB — the minion modDB is built fresh and does not inherit it. **Regression to prevent:** re-baking the bee ModCache rows back to empty (re-masks the parser rules); routing the count through `minionData.limit` (resolves against the minion modList = 0); or making the inject source-dependent (a slotted-skill requirement defeats the "non-skill-bound" contract). Adding a new auto-summon must stay a one-row `data.autoSummons` change with no engine edit.

### `auto-summon-pack-dps`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestAutoSummonFramework_spec.lua` (end-to-end pack tests)
- `BeesPerTenSeconds = 5` → Full DPS `Summon Bee` entry has `count = 5`, single-bee `dps > 0`
- raising the stat 5 → 10 raises the pack count to 10 while the single-bee `dps` is unchanged (the count is the multiplier, not the per-minion value)
- a non-bee build leaves all other minions at `count = 1` (no count multiply leaks)
- **gate≠count (Anurok):** when a registry row carries `packCountStat`, the count resolves THAT stat (e.g. `MaxCompanions`) while `countStat` (the gate, `AnuroksSummoned`=1) still controls injection. Spec: Anurok `+5 Maximum Companions` → count ≥ 5 (tracks MaxCompanions, NOT the gate's 1); the group carries `autoSummonPackCountStat`.

**Site:** `src/Modules/Calcs.lua` (`calcs.calcFullDPS`, minion block): `minionCount = floor(resolved)`, min 1, where `resolved` comes from `resolveStat = group.autoSummonPackCountStat or group.autoSummonCountStat` (see the refinement in `auto-summon-packcount-base-companions` below for HOW it is resolved); used in BOTH the `fullDPS.skills` `count` and the `combinedDPS` minion term; defaults to the existing `activeSkillCount` (= 1) for every non-auto-summon minion. `src/Modules/CalcSetup.lua` carries `autoSummonPackCountStat` from the registry row onto the granted skill + socket group (alongside `autoSummonCountStat`).

**Why:** Full DPS sums each skill's `dps * count`; for minions `calcFullDPS` hardcoded `count = 1` (per-single-minion — no minion sets a count multiplier). A pack of auto-summoned bees deals single-minion DPS × active count. The count comes from the build's count stat resolved against the PLAYER modDB (`usedEnv.modDB`), since the minion modDB does not carry it. The minion's per-hit DPS stays count-independent so the multiplier is applied exactly once, in Full DPS, scoped to auto-summons only. Poison/impale/etc. minion sub-DPS lines keep their existing `activeSkillCount` (Phase A leaves ailment-pack scaling untouched to avoid changing any current minion's numbers). **Regression to prevent:** applying the count to non-auto-summon minions (would multiply every existing minion build), resolving the count against the minion modDB (yields 0 → pack collapses to 1), or folding the count into the per-minion `dps` (double-counts on re-runs).

### `auto-summon-packcount-base-companions`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestAutoSummonFramework_spec.lua`
- end-to-end: `+5 Maximum Companions` + Anurok gate → `output.MaxCompanions == 7` (2 base + 5) AND the Anurok Full-DPS entry `count == 7` (NOT the bonus-only 5)
- source contract: the pack count for a `packCountStat` resolves from `usedEnv.player.output[sg.autoSummonPackCountStat]`, not the raw modDB

**Site:** `src/Modules/Calcs.lua` (`calcs.calcFullDPS`, minion block, pack-count resolution): when `sg.autoSummonPackCountStat` names a value present in `usedEnv.player.output`, resolve the pack count from that COMPUTED player output; otherwise fall back to `calcLib.val(usedEnv.modDB, resolveStat)`.

**Why:** Anurok's `packCountStat = "MaxCompanions"` is a COMPUTED output: `CalcDefence` sets `output.MaxCompanions = 2 + modDB:Sum("BASE", "MaxCompanions")` — the **2 base companions are NOT a modDB BASE mod**. So `calcLib.val(usedEnv.modDB, "MaxCompanions")` returned only the BONUS companions and undercounted the Anurok pack by 2 (worst case count 1 vs 2 → Anurok FullDPS ~2× low; a +5-companion build read 5 instead of 7). Chorus of the Anurok summons "up to your Companion Limit" = the FULL limit (datamined unique text, `Data/AutoSummons.lua`), so the count must be the computed `output.MaxCompanions`. Plain count stats (`BeesPerTenSeconds` / `TyrannosaursSummoned` / `TolmatHistoricMinions`) have no `output` entry → unchanged modDB fallback. **Regression to prevent:** reverting the pack-count resolution to a raw `calcLib.val(modDB, "MaxCompanions")` (re-drops the base companions); or generalising the output read to plain count stats that have no output entry (would resolve nil). CORPUS: affects the 88 Anurok corpus builds' FullDPS (`spec/TestBuilds` is git-untracked → a LOCAL snapshot-regen concern, not a tracked diff).

### `leech-le-instance-model`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestLeechLeInstanceModel_spec.lua`
- source invariants: `Data.lua` defines `LeechDuration = 3` (no `LeechRateBase = 0.02`);
  CalcOffence computes `LifeLeechRate = LifeLeechPerHit * leechHitRate` and
  `LifeLeechDuration = LeechDuration / (1 + IncreasedLeechRate)` with no
  `MaxLifeLeechRate` clamp; CalcDefence no longer computes the `MaxLifeLeechRate` /
  `MaxLifeLeechInstance` pool caps; `breakdown.leech` uses the LE-model signature;
  CalcSections drops the "Life/Mana Leech Cap" rows
- parse contract: `20% of Damage Leeched as Health` → `DamageLifeLeech BASE 20` (SP51);
  `100% Increased Leech Rate` → `LeechRate INC 100` (SP102)
- behavioural (Fireball): leech is non-zero (the PoB port made it identically 0);
  `LifeLeechPerHit ≈ leech% × AverageHit`; window `= 3/(1+ILR)` (3.0 → 1.5 at +100%);
  the sustained rate is INVARIANT under Increased Leech Rate; doubling leech% doubles
  the rate (no cap)

**Site:** `src/Modules/Data.lua` (`LeechDuration = 3`); `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua`
(leech-instance amount, "Calculate leech rates" block); `src/Modules/CalcDefence.lua`
(removed leech-cap block); `src/Modules/CalcBreakdown.lua` (`breakdown.leech`);
`src/Modules/CalcSections.lua` (Leech & Gain on Hit section).

rows back to empty (`{{},""}`) which silently re-shadows the parse; gating the multiplier on a
nil/global cfg (the flags are SkillId-tagged skill-tree stats, invisible to a global query, so

`dpsMultiplier` but not both (they are independent code paths — the direct multiplier never
reaches the ailment rate); or modelling the geometry-dependent orbit re-hits as a fixed
multiplier (curve-fit).

### `ice-spiral-double-chance-ev`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestIceSpiralDoubleChance_spec.lua`
- "parses '25% Chance for Double Ice Spirals' to a BASE DoubleDamageChance 25 mod (nil extra)"
- "the '+100% Ice Spiral Damage when Doubled' ModCache row is an empty no-op (no Damage MORE 100)"
- "the '25% Chance for Double Ice Spirals' ModCache no-op row is removed"
- "1 point (25) -> x1.25 EV on the hit; ailment/DoT context gets 0"
- "4 points (100) -> x2.0 -- the previously-inflated number is only correct at full allocation"
- "CalcOffence folds DoubleDamageChance into ScaledDamageEffect"
- "game-file: frc87w-21 Chaos Whirl still carries the audited stats (1.4 tree)"
- "carries the inline regression-guard markers and the anchored specialModList entry"

**Sites:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (anchored `specialModList` entry
`["^([%d%.]+)%% chance for double ice spirals$"] = function(num) return { mod("DoubleDamageChance",
"BASE", num, "", ModFlag.Hit) } end`, inline-tagged
`@leb-regression-guard:ice-spiral-double-chance-ev`) + `src/Data/ModCache.lua` (two inline-tagged
edit sites: the `"+100% Ice Spiral Damage when Doubled"` row rewritten from an UNCONDITIONAL
`Damage MORE 100` to an empty no-op `{{}," Ice Spiral  when Doubled "}`, and the
`"25% Chance for Double Ice Spirals"` no-op row REMOVED so the line cache-misses to the live
`specialModList` parse — a `SaveModCache` regen re-bakes it as `DoubleDamageChance BASE 25`,
hit-flagged, `nil` residue).

**Why:** The Frost Claw specialization node frc87w-21 "Chaos Whirl" (`maxPoints` 4, tree_1.json
1_2/1_3/1_4) carries the per-point scaling stat `"25% Chance for Double Ice Spirals"` (`stats[]`)
plus the flat descriptor `"+100% Ice Spiral Damage when Doubled"` (`notScalingStats[]`). Node text:
"When you cast Ice Spirals there is a chance that the number of projectiles will be doubled and
they'll all deal double damage." A successful roll makes the cast's spirals deal DOUBLE damage
(+100% = exactly ×2.0); the game's own `IceSpiralMutator.getTempStatsForTooltipDPS` folds
`extra = chance`, i.e. the displayed EV multiplier is `(1 + chance×(2−1))`. A p-chance to deal
double damage is precisely LEB's existing `DoubleDamageChance` mechanic — `CalcOffence` computes
`ScaledDamageEffect *= (1 + DoubleDamageChance/100)` (the same channel `avalanche-large-boulder`
uses; no calc-side change). Before this guard the node pair OVER-counted: the `+100%` descriptor
was a ModCache `Damage MORE 100` applied UNCONDITIONALLY (always ×2.0, never gated on the roll)
while the `25%` chance stat was a ModCache no-op (dropped) — so any 1..4-point allocation inflated
Ice Spiral hits to a flat ×2.0. Per-point scaling now gives `25 × points` → EV `(1 + 0.25×points)`:
1/4 → ×1.25, **4/4 → ×2.0 (= the old number)**, so the over-count existed only for partial
allocations; a 4/4 build is byte-identical.

**ModFlag.Hit (hit-only):** the roll doubles the Ice Spiral / Frost Claw HIT only. LE ailments are
stack-based with fixed per-stack damage and do NOT scale with the applying hit's size, so a doubled
hit must NOT double the Frostbite/Chill it inflicts. A flagless `DoubleDamageChance` would leak into
the ailment DoT (a PoE-ism; PoE ailments scale with the hit, LE's do not). The `ModFlag.Hit` confines
the ×(1+p) to the hit — mirrors `avalanche-large-boulder-double-damage`.

**Anchoring (no collision):** the `^…$` anchor + value-tolerant `([%d%.]+)` confine the rule to the
exact stat. `"Chance for Double Ice Spirals"` exists ONLY on the Frost Claw tree (tree_1.json
frc87w-21; no affix/unique/idol/set), and skill-tree node mods are SkillId-scoped by `PassiveTree.lua`
(ModStore SkillId gate), so the `DoubleDamageChance` reaches Frost Claw only — no leak to other skills.

**Scope:** allocation-gated (only builds that allocate frc87w-21 change) and it REDUCES the previously
inflated number; the default corpus (no allocation) is byte-identical, but Frost Claw builds carrying
frc87w-21 at <4/4 need a snapshot regen before their `builds` suite is green. **Follow-up (separate,
also game-source):** the roll ALSO doubles the projectile/spiral COUNT (`Mutate iVar7=iVar2*2`); the
game tooltip ignores count-doubling (`getTempStatsForTooltipDPS` reads field `0x104` directly), so this
per-hit EV MORE matches the tooltip and is the faithful minimal fix — modeling the EV count increase
(count factor 2, chance 25%) is a tracked follow-up.

### `rive-temporal-warrior-void-conversion`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestRiveVoidConversion_spec.lua`

**Sites:** `Data/Global.lua` `LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE["sndr1-5"]` (rewrite only).
`Modules/ModParser.lua` (`parseArrowConversion`) and `Modules/CalcOffence.lua`
(conversionTable) are the UNCHANGED consumers; `Data/ModCache.lua` is deliberately
LEFT untouched.

**Why:** the Void Knight "Temporal Warrior" node (`sndr1-5`, Rive tree,
`TreeData/1_4/tree_2.json:13213`) converts 100% of Rive's base PHYSICAL damage to
VOID ("Swaps Rive's {Physical} tag for a {Void} tag"). Its stat string is the bare
display form `" Void Conversion"`, which matches NO ModParser pattern, so the node
compiled to an inert empty mod (`ModCache c[" Void Conversion"]={{},""}`) and
contributed NOTHING — Rive stayed 100% Physical in LEB. Datamine proof
(`datamining`): `L472` gates on the
form byte `+0x124` (= node allocated); `L490` =
`DamageStatsHolder__convertAllDamageOfType(holder, 0, 5, 0)` = convert ALL of
Physical(0) → Void(5). No proportion float, no `DAT_` load → the rate is
STRUCTURALLY 100% (no in-game capture needed), and it converts the PHYSICAL type
ONLY. The fix mirrors `aerial-prowess-per-stack` (node-keyed
`LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE`, NOT a new parser): the rewrite re-expresses
`" Void Conversion"` as the damage-type ARROW form `"Physical -> Void"`, which
`parseArrowConversion` already turns into a SINGLE skill-agnostic
`PhysicalDamageConvertToVoid BASE 100` mod (no parser tag);
`PassiveTree:ProcessStats` then appends the node's DEFAULT owning-skill `SkillId`
tag (`Rive1`, from `treeId sndr1`), scoping the conversion to Rive alone — so
`sndr1-5` is deliberately NOT in `LE_TREE_NODE_GLOBAL_SCOPE`. The arrow form is
chosen over `"100% of <X> base damage converted to <Y>"` precisely because the
latter (a) routes to `skillBaseDamageConversionHandler`, which needs
`canonicalSkillName("Physical")` to be a SKILL (it is `nil` → `nsAny` → dead), and
(b) converts EVERY non-dst type, over-converting any non-physical added base on
Rive. The arrow form converts Physical ONLY, matching `convertAllDamageOfType(0,5)`
exactly. `ModCache.lua` is LEFT untouched: the rewrite fires BEFORE `parseMod` (the
parser sees `"Physical -> Void"`, not a cache key), and the bare `" Void Conversion"`
string is SHARED by other-skill nodes (`gs15de-18` Vengeance `tree_2.json:6094`,
`sm87r4-32` Smite `tree_2.json:13121`) that must stay inert — so the row is NOT
unique to `sndr1-5` (the inverse of AerialProwess, whose string was unique and its
stale row removed). ALLOCATION-GATED: output changes only for a build that allocates
`sndr1-5`, so a corpus Rive build taking the node needs a snapshot regen before its
`builds` suite is green; if no corpus build allocates it, snapshot impact is zero.

### `tyrant-skull-per-attribute-minion-scope`

**Problem.** Tyrant's Skull (unique 424) grants its summoned PrimalTyrannosaur a
per-attribute damage block that LEB never encoded: `+2 Tyrannosaur Melee Damage
per Strength`, `1% more Tyrannosaur Health and Damage per 1% Uncapped Endurance`,
`+1% Tyrannosaur Physical Penetration per Intelligence`, `+1% Tyrannosaur
Critical Strike Multiplier per Attunement`, `1% increased Tyrannosaur Attack and
Cast Speed per Dexterity`. The strings matched no parser form and were dropped to
residue (Bite per-hit undercut ~1.573x vs in-game). Adding the strings to
`uniques_1_4.json` alone is a NO-OP — ModParser has no generic form for
named-minion-scoped per-attribute mods.

**Fix.** Five `specialModList` handlers in `ModParser.lua` (mirroring the
`crit-for-totems-per-int-and-multi` idiom) emit `MinionModifier LIST` mods scoped
`minionTypes = {"PrimalTyrannosaur"}`. Per-attribute inner mods carry an explicit
`actor="parent"` PerStat tag so the scaling reads the player's stat (see
`minion-modifier-perstat-parent-actor`); the Endurance term reads the player's
UNCAPPED Endurance (`stat="EnduranceTotal"`). COEFFICIENTS are in-game-confirmed
(item tooltip; pen 0.27 == Int x1%, crit mult 2.79 == base + Att x1%; Endurance
MORE slope matches a belt toggle, in-game x0.9232 vs LEB x0.9226).

### `ballista-attack-speed-minion-scope`

**Problem.** The "(X)% Increased Ballista Attack Speed" affix family (datamine
affix 536 "Rogue's" Max Ballistae+AS `sAEM=0.5`, affix 640 Level of Ballista+AS on
Void Star `sAEM=0.0`; property 58 / summonBallista tag 379) scales the summoned
**RogueBallista** minion's `BallistaBolt` FIRING rate in-game. The default parse
stripped the "ballista" skill-name token and produced a PLAIN player-side
`INC Speed flags=Attack tag=SkillName:"Ballista"`. Two independent faults made it
miss the minion: (a) the `SkillName="Ballista"` tag names the player SUMMON skill
("Ballista"), not the minion firing skill ("Ballista Bolt") the minion Speed query
is scoped to; (b) it was never wrapped as a `MinionModifier`, so no CalcPerform
channel copies it to `env.minion.modDB`. Probe (Rem-MK3, 2026-07-08): a rolled
INC 29 sat on the player and was ABSENT from the minion Speed list -> ballista
firing rate under-modeled (minion Speed 1.4537 -> 1.8078 once routed).

**Fix.** One `specialModList` handler in `ModParser.lua` (mirroring the
`tyrant-skull-per-attribute-minion-scope` idiom) emits a `MinionModifier LIST`
scoped `minionTypes = {"RogueBallista"}` whose inner mod is a plain `INC Speed`
with **flags=0 and NO SkillName tag** — an unscoped INC Speed matches the minion's
"Ballista Bolt" Speed query in `CalcOffence.lua`; a SkillName tag would re-scope it
to the player summon skill and re-break it. Dispatch flows through
`CalcPerform.lua` (see `minion-modifier-multi-type-gate`). NOT gated — this is a
plain magnitude-carrying affix route, no config toggle.

**Residual (separate, NOT this guard).** On attribute-converted builds (Rogue
"100% of Dexterity Converted to Guile") the ballista's per-Dexterity node
(`ba1574-18` "Agile Engineering", +0.2% AS/Dex) reads `output.Dex=0` and is inert,
whereas datamine (`Property_Player_652` AltText) states "Guile counts as Dexterity
for skills and nodes that gain bonuses based on your Dexterity". That
Guile-counts-as-Dex gap is SYSTEMIC (all converted-attribute per-Dex scaling) and
is tracked separately, not fixed here.

Spec: `spec/System/TestBallistaAttackSpeedMinionScope_spec.lua` (source-text lock:
handler registered, RogueBallista-scoped, inner INC Speed carries no SkillName tag).

### `ballista-agile-engineering-attack-speed-inc`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestBallistaAgileEngineeringAS_spec.lua`

**Problem.** Ballista spec node **`ba1574-18` "Agile Engineering"** (maxPoints 1)
carries two stats: `"+1% Placement Speed per Dexterity"` (unmodeled, inert) and
`"+1% Attack Speed per 5 Dexterity"` — the latter scales the summoned
**RogueBallista**'s `BallistaBolt` FIRING rate in-game. Because the attack-speed
line lacks the word "increased", the parser mapped `"+X% Attack Speed"` to Speed
**BASE** (parse probe: `Speed BASE 1 PerStat{Dex,div=5}@parent`). The minion
attack-rate formula (`CalcOffence.lua` ~2143) reads only `Sum("INC",Speed)` +
`More(Speed)` and NEVER `Sum("BASE",Speed)`, so the node's per-Dexterity bonus
was silently dropped from the fire rate. (Guile counts as Dexterity here via the
`s4ConvertedTwin` twin-add, guard `s4-perstat-base-includes-converted-twin`, so
the node is NOT inert on Dex->Guile-converted builds — it just parsed to the wrong
aggregation bucket.)

**Fix.** `LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE["ba1574-18"]` rewrites ONLY the attack-speed
line to the "increased" form → `"X% increased attack speed per 5 dexterity"` →
parses to `Speed INC + PerStat{Dex,div=5}` (parse+save probe verified). The
placement-speed line is left untouched (out of DPS scope). Value-tolerant capture
`^%+([%d%.]+)%% Attack Speed per 5 Dexterity$`.

### `ballista-per-dex-attack-speed-intrinsic` / `ballista-minion-ignores-owner-weapon-attack-rate`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestBallistaPerDexAttackSpeed_spec.lua`
**Sites:** `src/Data/skills.json` (SummonBallista.baseMods, BallistaBolt.castTime +
`minionIgnoresOwnerWeaponAttackRate`), `src/Data/minions.json` (RogueBallista modList),
`src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (minion Speed formula, ~2144).

**Problem.** The Ballista (RogueBallista / BallistaBolt) fire-rate model under-read on
every Dexterity-scaling Falconer build. Root cause: fix#1 (commit `<see git log>`) removed
the intrinsic `"1% increased Minion Attack Speed per player Dexterity"` from
SummonBallista, mistaking it for a duplicate of node `ba1574-18` (a SEPARATE 0.2%/Dex
bonus). That left LEB with NO per-Dexterity fire-rate scaling — the dominant term (the
in-game skill tooltip reads "1% Increased Attack Speed per point of Dexterity"). Three
miscalibrations stacked on top: (a) the RogueBallista actor's innate `Speed INC 20`
was applied as a SEPARATE additive increase, corrupting the per-Dex slope (Dex-0 rate
0.78/s vs observed 0.65/s); (b) `BallistaBolt.castTime` 1.3939 (0.717/s) was too fast
vs datamining 2.3/1.5 = 1.5333 (0.652/s); (c) the minion fire rate was multiplied by the
OWNER's weapon `AttackRate` (`env.player.weaponData1.AttackRate`), but the ballista
fires weapon-independently.

<!-- validation detail omitted: line 18963 -->
<!-- validation detail omitted: line 18964 -->

| char-sheet Dex | in-game rate | model `0.652*(1+0.01*Dex)` |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 75 (config 05) | 1.135/s | 1.141 (+0.6%) |
| 66 (config 03) | 1.078/s | 1.083 (+0.4%) |
| 50 (config 04) | 0.973/s | 0.978 (+0.5%) |

Model-free linear regression: `rate = 0.649 + 0.00648*Dex = 0.649*(1 + 0.01*Dex)` —
intercept 0.649 ≈ datamining base 0.652, slope exactly 1%/Dex. Config 05 has LEB
`output.Dex=0` (Guile conversion) yet the intrinsic resolves to 75 because it reads
`PerStat{Dex}` (twin-add includes converted Guile, guard
`s4-perstat-base-includes-converted-twin`). Config 03 (bow, weaponData1 rate 1.05) and
04 (unarmed, 1.2) fit the SAME base → the owner-weapon multiply is spurious.

**Fix (all ballista-scoped; other minions untouched).** (1) restore the intrinsic
attack-speed baseMod on SummonBallista (mirrors the surviving 4%/Dex damage intrinsic);
(2) remove the RogueBallista innate `Speed INC 20` (the datamined +20% is baked into the
calibrated base 0.652); (3) set `BallistaBolt.castTime` = 1.5333333; (4) add the
`minionIgnoresOwnerWeaponAttackRate` flag on BallistaBolt and gate the CalcOffence
owner-weapon multiply on it. Post-fix probe reproduces all three captures to ≤0.6%.

**Scope / blast.** The 61 Ballista Falconer corpus builds change (Dex intrinsic +,
innate-20 −, weapon-rate −, base −); high-Dex builds get faster (correcting the
under-read). The weapon-rate gate is data-flagged to BallistaBolt only, so no other
minion is affected; the innate-20 removal and castTime are RogueBallista/BallistaBolt
only. Stacks on top of `ballista-agile-engineering-attack-speed-inc` (node 0.2%/Dex).

**Regression to prevent:** re-adding a separate additive `Speed INC` on RogueBallista
(re-corrupts the per-Dex slope); reintroducing the 5%/Dex misparse; reverting castTime
to 1.3939; or removing the weapon-rate gate (re-applies the owner weapon rate to the
turret).

### `conversion-flag-requires-sourced-type`

**Problem.** `CalcOffence.lua`'s `skillHasConversion` flag gates whether the typeless
generic added flat (`"Damage"` BASE — the weapon's `+N Melee Damage`, which is
typeless/generic in LE) is deferred out of the pre-conversion per-type pool and
redistributed across the POST-conversion base (`adaptive-added-post-conversion-typing`).
It was set true if ANY damage type's `conversionTable[t].mult ~= 1` — including a
conversion of a type the skill deals ZERO of. An OFF-TYPE global conversion then
spuriously triggered the deferral, distributing the generic melee (physical weapon
damage) onto the off-type's heavy post-conversion base instead of the skill's own
physical lane.

<!-- validation detail omitted: line 19011 -->
<!-- validation detail omitted: line 19012 -->
<!-- validation detail omitted: line 19013 -->

**Fix.** Gate the setter on `source[t.."Damage"]`: `skillHasConversion` is set true only
when a type the skill actually SOURCES converts. For Warpath the only sourced type is

→ LEB phys 62% matches in-game 63%, void 309.0 ≈ 306.6, per-hit 822.7 vs 832.6 (−1.2%).
Genuine-conversion guard cases are preserved: WardingMySchitzer (Swarmblade phys→cold)
and SuXes (Avalanche phys→cold) SOURCE the converting Physical, so they still set the
flag and defer (their adaptive-added specs stay green).

**⚠ Build-general / regression.** The change affects any build with a global off-type
conversion + a skill that does not source the converting type + generic/weapon added.
A full-corpus snapshot regen (MAIN repo) is required before dev merge — the programmatic
adaptive-added/conversion specs pass, but fixture-backed corpus builds must be re-baked.

## minion-monster-actor-damage-scaling

Repurposed-MONSTER minions (Anurok via Chorus of the Anurok, Tyrannosaur via
Tyrant's Skull, Tolmat historic minions via Tolmat's Incorrect History) are
spawned in-game through `MonsterGenerator.ApplyZoneScalingAndMods` ->
`ActorScaler.scaleToLevel(actor, level)`, which multiplies the actor's damage
stat by `damageScaleTable[charLevel] / damageScaleTable[fromLevel]` (datamining
`by_namespace/_global/ActorScaler.c`, `scaleToLevel` datamined offset; `fromLevel` =
the actor's authored ActorStats level, `toLevel` = zone/player level capped 100).
This is NOT the player-companion scaling path — companions (Wolf/Bear) do not go
through ActorScaler and keep the `+0.8%/level` MinionLevelScaling MORE.

LEB models this by tagging the affected minions in `minions.json` with
`monsterScaling.fromLevel` (datamined per minion) and, in CalcPerform's minion
init, applying a `MonsterActorLevelScaling` MORE =
`data.monsterDamageScaling.getMonsterDamageMorePercent(fromLevel, charLevel)`
**in place of** (not on top of) the companion MORE.

## Layering vs canary strings


Canary strings (`@leb-canary v1 / id:leb-... / do-not-remove`) are file-level
markers that protect against entire modules being deleted or rewritten by a
mass refactor. Regression guards are block-level and protect specific
correctness invariants. Both should be present where they apply; they don't
substitute for each other.


### `devouring-orb-persistent-pulse-hit`

Devouring Orb is a non-DoT damaging area that re-applies its per-pulse **hit**
every `damage_interval` (0.25 s) for as long as the orb persists (`duration`
flag, 10 s), rather than dealing one hit per cast. It is the **unique** skill in
`skills.json` carrying `damage_interval` with `(dot=false, hit=true,
duration=true)` — every other interval skill is `dot`-flagged and already uses
the pulse path. Lacking a `dot` flag, Devouring Orb previously fell through to the
cast-rate else-branch (`TotalDPS = AverageDamage × castRate`, cooldown-limited to
~0.25-0.30/s), so the 0.25 s pulse cadence was read but never applied — the orb's
4 pulses/second of sustained area damage were modeled as ONE hit per cast
(~13× understatement on FullDPS build `<private build>`: 2387 → 31566).

The fix adds a `persistentPulseHit = not dot and hit and duration and
damageInterval` predicate; such skills get `TotalDPS = AverageDamage /
damageInterval` (pulses per second). Because duration (10 s) > cooldown (4 s) the
orb is always alive, so the steady-state rate is the full pulse rate (no extra
cast-rate multiply).

<!-- validation detail omitted: line 19264 -->
<!-- validation detail omitted: line 19265 -->
<!-- validation detail omitted: line 19266 -->
<!-- validation detail omitted: line 19267 -->

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| DPS dispatch | `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (~line 2604, `persistentPulseHit`) | non-dot pulse skills divide TotalDPS by damageInterval instead of multiplying by cast rate |
| breakdown    | `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (~line 2695) | Calcs panel shows "damage per pulse / damage interval" |

**Game source:** `src/Data/skills.json` DevouringOrb baseFlags `{spell,hit,duration}`
(no `dot`), `damage_interval=250`, `base_skill_effect_duration=10000`,
`cooldown=4`; `src/Data/SkillStatMap.lua` divides both by 1000.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestDevouringOrbPersistentPulse_spec.lua`
- "CalcOffence routes non-dot+hit+duration+damageInterval to the pulse path"
- "DevouringOrb skill data still has the persistent-pulse shape (no dot flag)"

**Establishing observation:** `<private build> lv99 Void Knight` Devouring Orb TotalDPS
2387.16 → 31565.74 (= AverageDamage 7891.43 / 0.25). Blast radius = 1 FullDPS
corpus build; the other 19 corpus builds socket Devouring Orb as
`includeInFullDPS="false"` utility (Calcs-panel display only).

### `pure-dot-skill-dot-flag`

Pure-DoT skills carry the DoT bit in `skillTypeTags`
(`skillTypes[SkillType.Dot]==true`) but their `baseFlags` omit `dot`. Because
`skillFlags` is initialised as a literal `copyTable(baseFlags)`,
`skillFlags.dot` stayed `nil` for these skills, so the skill mod-flag set
(`skillModFlags` → `cfg.flags`) never gained `ModFlag.Dot` and every
`ModFlag.Dot`-gated mod ("increased Damage Over Time", parsed as
`Damage + ModFlag.Dot`) was silently filtered out of the skill's damage.

Establishing build: **Profane Veil** (skills.json key
"Warlock 05 Profane Veil", `skillTypeTags` 4384 = DoT 4096 + Spell 256 +
Necrotic 32) on YsGhostSurfing dropped +521% increased-DoT → LEB AverageHit
178.5 vs in-game 400.775 (×2.245 under). After the fix AverageHit = 399.93
(INC Damage 320 → 841), matching in-game within 0.3%.

The `and not skillFlags.hit` gate restricts the derivation to PURE-DoT skills
and EXCLUDES hit+dot skills (DevouringOrb, EntanglingRoots, HungeringSouls,
Chthonic Fissure, Judgement, Skeletal Mages Necrotic Projectile) whose hit
path must not change. The fix newly flags exactly six skills (DoT bit set,
`baseFlags.dot` absent, no hit/projectile): Profane Veil, AbyssalEchoes,
AuraOfDecay, FireTrail, SpiritPlague, Runemaster 01 Frost Wall.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| derive dot flag | `src/Modules/CalcActiveSkill.lua` (~line 105, after `skillFlags.hit`) | `skillFlags.dot = skillFlags.dot or (skillTypes[SkillType.Dot] and not skillFlags.hit) or nil` |
| carry ModFlag.Dot | `src/Modules/CalcActiveSkill.lua` (~line 922, `skillModFlags`) | `bor(skillModFlags, ModFlag.Dot)` when `skillFlags.dot`, so DoT-gated mods match `cfg.flags` |
| duration nil-guard | `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua` (~line 2287) | gate `baseDmg / skillData.duration` so permanent-aura pure-DoT (AuraOfDecay, no duration) does not divide by nil |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestPureDotSkillDotFlag_spec.lua`

**Establishing observation:** Profane Veil (slot 59 capture) AverageHit
178.5 → 399.93, INC Damage 320 → 841, vs in-game 400.775.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

**CORRECTION 2026-06-25: CF routes Torment through the TRIGGER-SKILL path, not the
`data.damagingAilment` path.** `Warlock 04 Chthonic Fissure` carries
`chance_to_cast_Ailment_Torment_on_hit_% = 100`, which `SkillStatMap` maps to
`ChanceToTriggerOnHit_Ailment_Torment` → it triggers the **`Ailment_Torment`**

3s duration). It does **NOT** set a `TormentChance` mod, so
`output.TormentChance = 0` and the `data.damagingAilment.Torment` ailment-DPS
loop (and its `multiplierChthonicTormentStacks` override) is **never reached for
CF** — that override is INERT for Chthonic Fissure (it remains only for any other
skill that might apply Torment through the damagingAilment path; none in the
current corpus). CF is the ONLY skill that triggers `Ailment_Torment`.

**THE FIX — `Ailment_Torment.stats.maximum_stacks = 6` (was 1).** With `maxStacks
= 1` the dominant component was under-counted ~6×. The Spirits emit at a **FIXED
~2/s** (498ms inter-arrival in the capture, ≈0.5s, independent of the build's
226% cast speed) and each applies a 3s Torment → **DPS-equivalent steady-state
stacks = 2/s × 3s = 6** (6 × per-stack 1157/s = 6942/s = in-game active Torment
DPS). LEB triggers `Ailment_Torment` at the CF cast/hit rate (e.g. `om6xj3n8`
uncapped = 4.28/s → 13 stacks), which over-counts because in-game it is the
Spirit emit rate (2/s) that applies Torment; `maximum_stacks = 6` caps to the
Spirit-limited count.

### `chthonic-fissure-fire-dot`

Native (non-Spine) Chthonic Fissure leaves a **FIRE DoT** on the ground. It
is a pure skill-DoT (spell + dot), **NOT a Bleed ailment**. Pre-remodel this fire
over-time component was not modelled at all (the CF entry is hit+duration with no
`dot`/`damage_interval`); only the gen393 hit + Torment ailment were.

Modelled as a separate `skills.json` entry **"Warlock Unique Chthonic Fissure
DoT"** (`spell` + `dot`, `spell_base_fire_damage = 5`, `damageEffectiveness = 0.25`,
`damage_interval = 258`, **NO `treeId`** — ConsecratedGround pattern). As a granted
sub-skill it gets the CF tree via `groupSource` (`"SkillId:Warlock 04 Chthonic
Fissure"`): Blood Gulch (`ch0fs-28`) converts this FIRE base → Physical, Valley of
Defilement (`ch0fs-31`) → Poison (VERIFIED: BgRrekvv Blood-Gulch build → line DoT
`PhysicalDamageBase` 22.25, `FireBase` 0); Torment (Necrotic) is NOT converted.
**treeId was REMOVED** (2026-06-25): carrying `treeId=ch0fs` wrongly enrolled the
persistent line DoT in the FullDPS cast-cycle (×1/N, diluting the build's real CF
skills); without it the DoT contributes at count=1.

**Datamined base (NOT a placeholder):** offline datamine (2026-06-25,
`extract_subprefab_damage.py`, PARENTS += 'Chthonic Fissure') gives prefab
**'Fire Fissure'** (`fs47re`) `RepeatedlyDamageEnemiesWithinRadius` = **Fire 5.0
per tick**, **addedDamageScaling 0.25**. `addedDamageScaling` IS the per-TICK
`damageEffectiveness` for flat added damage. `damage_interval` 258ms = the
Spine-OFF blank-capture tick (the prefab's serialized interval field was not
captured).

**eff CORRECTION 2026-06-25 (`<see git log>`):** a prior commit set eff **1.2** by
conflating the per-second tooltip ('120% per second' ≈ 0.25 × 4.8 ticks/s) with
the per-tick added scaling. Decomposing YsGhostSurfing (Spine-ON, Blood Gulch
fire→phys) proved the error: Spine of Malatros `+(61-72) Spell Damage` (rolled

Blood-Gulch conversion state; LEB applies generic 'increased Damage' 9.59×
conversion-invariant). **In LE, flat added damage scales a DoT only at this
datamined effectiveness (0.25), NOT the hit's effectiveness.**

sub-skill via `src/Data/SubSkillGrants.lua` `["Warlock 04 Chthonic Fissure"]`

### `call-to-arms-increased-not-more`

"Call To Arms" (ah443-10, Holy Aura tree, Paladin) grants the player and allies
physical damage. Node description: **"Holy Aura grants you and your allies
INCREASED physical damage."** The LE→LEB extraction dropped the "increased"
keyword — the node stat is the bare **"+10% Physical Damage"**, which ModParser
parses as a **multiplicative `PhysicalDamage MORE`** (the correct LEB default for
a bare "+N% <Type> Damage" string: of 51 such tree-node stats, 45 have a
"more"/"multiplicative" description and ARE genuinely MORE). ah443-10 is the
exception — its description says "increased", so it must be additive INC.

**Fix:** `LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE["ah443-10"]` (Data/Global.lua) rewrites the
bare stat → "+N% increased Physical Damage", which parses to `PhysicalDamage INC`.
**Node-scoped** — the global bare→MORE default is unchanged, so the 45
genuinely-MORE nodes are untouched. Value-tolerant ($-anchored on "Physical
Damage"; the per-point % still rank-scales).

**Grounding:** the node DESCRIPTION (the in-game text) is authoritative for the
increased-vs-more distinction. Sibling ah443-11 "Strength From Afar"
("+12% Throwing Attack Damage") is ALREADY correct — that phrasing parses to
`Damage INC` by default, so no rewrite needed. (Two other bare-stat nodes were
checked and NOT changed: av75ch-19 "Dead of Winter" — its desc "increased" refers
to FREEZE CHANCE, not the +8% Cold Damage; st38ml-8 "Grounding Conduit" — its
"+15% Lightning Damage" is CONDITIONAL on a Storm Totem having hit a shocked enemy
recently — now handled by the `grounding-conduit-conditional-inc` guard below.)

**Impact:** MORE ×1.5 (at 5/5) → INC +50% (diluted into the additive pool)
REDUCES physical damage for builds with Call To Arms — corrects an over-count.
Affected corpus: <private build> / <private build> / <private build> (lv100/96 Paladin), YsSupportCentre
(lv80 Paladin, bin/), 1.3/throwing.xml. (Also reduces the PALADINF Shield Throw
over-count's Call-To-Arms component — see `project_paladinf_shield_throw_more_overcount`.)

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| data | `src/Data/Global.lua` (`LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE["ah443-10"]`) | Rewrites bare "+N% Physical Damage" → "+N% increased Physical Damage" so Call To Arms parses INC, not MORE |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestCallToArmsIncreasedNotMore_spec.lua`
- "bare '+N% Physical Damage' parses to MORE by default (why the rewrite is needed)"
- "'+N% increased Physical Damage' parses to INC (the rewrite target)"
- "ah443-10 carries a rewrite that turns its bare stat into 'increased'"

### `grounding-conduit-conditional-inc`

"Grounding Conduit" (st38ml-8, Summon Storm Totem tree, Shaman) grants the **player**
lightning damage. Node description: **"You deal INCREASED lightning damage IF a Storm
Totem has hit a shocked enemy recently."** The LE→LEB extraction dropped BOTH the
"increased" keyword AND the condition — the node stat is the bare **"+15% Lightning
Damage"**, which ModParser parses as an **UNCONDITIONAL multiplicative
`LightningDamage MORE`** (the bare "+N% <Type> Damage" default). The node must be
(a) additive **INC**, not MORE, and (b) **conditional** on an active Storm Totem.

**Fix:** `LE_TREE_NODE_STAT_REWRITE["st38ml-8"]` (Data/Global.lua) rewrites the bare
stat → **"+N% increased Lightning Damage while totem active"**. "increased" → INC, and
the " while totem active" suffix routes through the pre-existing ModParser entry
`["while totem active"] → Condition:HaveTotem` (the SAME machinery as the
`grounding-totem-condition` guard for the Avalanche av75ch-12 "Grounding" node).
**Node-scoped**; value-tolerant ($-anchored on "Lightning Damage").

**Grounding:** the node DESCRIPTION is authoritative for both the increased-vs-more
distinction and the totem condition. `Condition:HaveTotem` is auto-set for totem
**mains** (CalcPerform.lua) and otherwise OFF unless the build enables
`conditionHaveTotem` — the standard LEB safe-default-OFF treatment for every
conditional damage bonus. The "hit a shocked enemy recently" sub-clause is
approximated by plain HaveTotem (a Storm Totem build with Static Field shock satisfies
it throughout sustained combat; gated OFF by default regardless).

**Impact:** corpus — only **ChevyVolt** (lv96 Shaman, 1.4/bin) allocates st38ml-8
(#3 = +45%). Its main is GatheringStormMelee (melee, not a totem) and it sets no
`conditionHaveTotem`, so HaveTotem is OFF. **CORPUS OUTPUT-NEUTRAL** — an A/B
(rewrite present vs reverted to parent `<see git log>`) on ChevyVolt gives byte-identical
mainOutput (688 numeric fields; FullDPS = 8133.0187 both ways). The node's lightning
bonus never reached the full output even as the prior unconditional MORE, because a
skill-tree node mod scopes to its own skill (Summon Storm Totem, which is
`includeInFullDPS=false`). So this is a **latent correctness fix** (right type + right
condition), NOT a corpus DPS change — it would manifest for a build where Storm Totem
is the `includeInFullDPS` main (HaveTotem auto-ON), where the bonus would correctly
apply as conditional INC instead of unconditional MORE. Node stats are parsed live
(PassiveTree:ProcessNode), so no ModCache/snapshot regen is needed; the committed
ChevyVolt snapshot still matches. (The node desc reads player-global "You deal…";
whether a skill-tree node should propagate globally to the player is a separate
pre-existing scoping matter, out of scope for this type/condition fix.)

### `tree-also-applies-to-minions`

LE passive-tree nodes use a leading-space **follow-up modifier** on its own stat
line, **" Also Applies To Minions"**, to make the PRECEDING stat lines of the same
node ALSO apply to the player's minions. Canonical node: **Sentinel-37 "Smelter's
Might"** (`tree_2.json`), stats =
`["+7% Bleed Chance", "+7% Ignite Chance", " Also Applies To Minions", " Doubled for you with a 2h weapon"]`
— in-game description: *"You and your minions have a chance to inflict bleeding and
ignite on hit."* `modLib.parseMod` returns `unknown` for the bare follow-up line, so
before this fix the line was dropped and the minion **never received the bonus**. On a
Forge Guard Manifest Armor build that node is the minion's ONLY ailment source.

**Fix:** `PassiveTree.lua:ProcessStats` scans `node.sd` for the normalized phrase
`"also applies to minions"` and, for every real mod parsed on a line BEFORE the
follow-up (back to the previous follow-up boundary or node start), emits an
ADDITIONAL `MinionModifier` LIST copy whose inner mod is the freshly-copied parsed mod
(taken before the player loop appends any SkillId/Condition tags). CalcPerform.lua's
MinionModifier dispatch (guard `minion-modifier-multi-type-gate`) lands the inner mod
on `env.minion.modDB`. The player's own copy is left intact ("Also" = player AND
minion); player-only follow-ups that come AFTER (e.g. " Doubled for you with a 2h
weapon") are NOT inherited by the minion copy. The handler is **generic** — it wraps
whatever mods precede the phrase (Damage, ailment chance, …), not an ailment-specific
list.

**Impact:** **CORPUS OUTPUT-NEUTRAL.** The minion-side `ChanceToTriggerOnHit_Ailment_*`
mods this lands are not yet consumed: LE ailments are modeled as **triggered skills**
(`ChanceToTriggerOnHit_Ailment_Bleed > 0` → a granted `Ailment_Bleed` skill), and the
trigger-grant loop (`CalcSetup.lua`) scans **player socket groups only**, not minion
skills — so minion ailment DPS stays 0 until minion triggered-ailment modeling is added
(a separate, corpus-wide effort). A/B on VoidMaster_blank lv100 Forge Guard (the
most-affected build: Sentinel-37 #5 + Manifest Armor minion) is byte-identical:
player FullDPS = 15728.7418, minion TotalDPS = 426.8715 both ways. This is therefore a
**latent correctness fix** (the minion now correctly carries the propagated chance),
NOT a corpus DPS change → **no snapshot regen needed**. Node stats are parsed live
(`ProcessStats`), so ModCache is unaffected.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| consumer | `src/Classes/PassiveTree.lua` (`ProcessStats`, `minionApplyBoundaries`) | Scans node stat lines for " Also Applies To Minions" and emits a MinionModifier LIST copy of each preceding parsed mod |

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestTreeAlsoAppliesToMinions_spec.lua`
- "Smelter's-Might shape wraps each preceding ailment-chance mod and excludes the trailing 'Doubled' line"
- "the player keeps its own copy of the preceding mod (Also = player AND minion)"
- "the handler is generic, not ailment-specific (a Damage mod is wrapped)"
- "a node without the follow-up emits no MinionModifier (corpus-neutral)"
- "rank scaling carries into the minion copy (alloc=5 -> value*5)"
- "game-file: Sentinel-37 'Smelter's Might' still carries ' Also Applies To Minions'"

### `bare-form-damage-affix-increased`

The ITEM-AFFIX analogue of `call-to-arms-increased-not-more`. Five LE item-affix
families had their **"increased"** keyword dropped in the LE→LEB extraction, so
their templates read as a bare **"+(X)% &lt;Type&gt; Damage"**. ModParser's
`BASE_MORE` rule (the bare "+N% …" form) makes that a **multiplicative damage
MORE** — the correct default for the many skill/tree nodes that render a genuine
bare MORE (e.g. "+200% Vine Melee Damage", "+10% Riposte Fire Damage") — but
WRONG for these affixes, which are additive INCREASED in-game.

**Grounding** (`datamined game source`,
`affixProperties[].modifierType` enum: **0=Flat/Added, 1=Increased, 2=More**;
decoded against known cases — 986 melee modifierType 1 matches its in-game tooltip
"137% increased Melee Damage", and 979/986-mana modifierType 2 match their "more"
text):

| Affix | Name | Type | modifierType | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 959 | Keplahan's Cryolith Reforged | Cold | 1 | → increased |
| 960 | Keplahan's Pyrolith Reforged | Fire | 1 | → increased |
| 961 | Kuzon's Fury Reforged | Fire | 1 | → increased |
| 986 | "Increased Melee Damage and Damage for Melee Attacks per 1 Mana Cost" (Rusted Cleaver "Cleaver Solution" sealed affix) | Melee | 1 | → increased |
| 1090 | Rogue's / Level of Bladestorm | Throwing | 1 | → increased |
| 979 | "Chance to Poison on Hit and **More** Damage against Poisoned Enemies" (Global Conditional) | — | **2** | **LEFT bare (genuine MORE)** |

**Fix:** DATA-side, edited the templates in `Data/ModItem_1_4.json` (Cold ×8,
Fire ×16, Melee ×8, Throwing ×8 = 40) and legacy `Data/ModItem.json` (Melee ×3,
Throwing ×7 = 10) from `"+(X)% <Type> Damage"` → `"(X)% increased <Type> Damage"`.
**Not a parser change** — a broad bare-damage→INC promotion would flip the genuine
bare-MORE skill/tree nodes. The inline marker lives at the `BASE_MORE` rule in
