## skill-mana-cost-data

**What:** `src/Data/skills.json` `stats.cost.Mana` populated for player skills from datamine
`ability_attribute_scaling.json`. Prerequisite for per-mana-cost scaling (Brutality
"0.02% more Melee Damage per 1 Mana Cost, cap 20" = Property_Player_650; and the
"X per 1 Mana Cost" affix family). Before this, only 35/380 skills had a cost, so
`output.ManaCost=0` for most skills (incl. Forge Strike) — the per-mana-cost MORE had
nothing to scale on.

**Method (validated 31/31, 0 mismatch vs the pre-existing 35 curated costs):** join by
`playerAbilityID`; unambiguous id (all datamine prefab records agree) → use it; else pick
the prefab whose name normalises to the skill name (disambiguates the player ability from
enemy/boss variants that ALIAS the same playerAbilityID — e.g. me27 "Meteor"=56 player vs
"BruteHarbinger…Meteor"=60; st4th "SmeltersWrath"=30 player vs "Sentinel Champion…"=35).
Only `manaCost>0`, only where `stats.cost` was ABSENT (curated values never overwritten).
98 skills filled.

**Corpus impact:** DPS-INERT — no Sacrificial Zeal / Archmage build (the only
`output.ManaCost`→damage paths) exists in the 1.4 corpus, so no recorded DPS changes.
Snapshots that record `ManaCost` DO change that field for the filled skills (cosmetic;
mechanical regen, no DPS delta). The Brutality/affix per-mana-cost damage fix lands ON TOP
of this data.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestSkillManaCostData_spec.lua`
- Forge Strike cost = 25, Smelter's Wrath = 30 (player prefab, not enemy 35)
- sample fills (Acid Flask 10 / Manifest Armor 60 / Assemble Abomination 65)
- curated costs NOT overwritten (Meteor stays 56 not 60, Fireball stays 3 not 4)

## per-mana-cost-melee-affix

**What:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (3 special patterns) + `src/Data/ModCache.lua` (5 baked
entries) model the crafted affix family *"X% [Damage / Critical Strike Chance / increased Area]
for Melee ... per 1 Mana Cost"*. Each parses to a mod scoped to the **Melee KEYWORD** carrying a
`PerStat:ManaCost` tag (so it scales by the ACTIVE skill's Mana cost):
- Damage prefix → `Damage MORE value` , `ModFlag.Melee`, `PerStat{ManaCost, div=1, limit=20}` (the "(up to 20)" cap)
- Crit variant → `CritChance BASE value`, `ModFlag.Melee`, `PerStat{ManaCost, div=1}` (no "(up to 20)" text → no cap)
- Area variant → `AreaOfEffect INC value`, `KeywordFlag.Melee`, `PerStat{ManaCost, div=1}`

**Why:** the old ModCache bake scoped Damage/Crit to `SkillName "Melee Attack"` (the BASIC attack
only, so they applied to NOTHING on Warpath / Forge Strike / Rive) AND dropped both the per-mana
scaling and the cap → they contributed ~0. The datamine (`Property_Player_636` "Damage for Melee
Attacks per 1 Mana Cost (up to 20)", AltText "more, Multiplicative with other modifiers") gives
Melee-keyword scope + multiplicative + cap-20. Same scaling as the Brutality attribute intrinsic
([[brutality-per-manacost-melee-more]]).

**Basis (channel skills):** the basis is `output.ManaCost` — for the channeled **Warpath** this is
the ability's NOMINAL `manaCost` field = **1** (datamine `ability_attribute_scaling.json` va53st
`manaCost 1.0`, NOT `channelCost 18`, NOT 0). Confirmed in-engine by `spec/tools/ProbePerManaBasis.lua`
(Warpath `output.ManaCost` 1, Forge Strike 20) and that `PerStat:ManaCost` resolves at damage-sum
time (`spec/tools/ProbePerManaTag.lua`: Warpath ×1, Forge Strike ×20, cap works).

**Prerequisite:** `skill-mana-cost-data` (skills.json `stats.cost.Mana`); without it `output.ManaCost=0`
and the whole family is inert.

**Corpus impact:** MODEST and narrow. On the current corpus every melee `output.ManaCost` ≤ 20, so
the cap is non-binding, and the dominant Warpath builds have basis 1 (≈0.2% MORE). The meaningful
mover is the Damage prefix on a higher-cost melee MAIN skill (e.g. Forge Strike, MC 20 → +4% MORE).
Builds whose main/summed skill is a spell / non-melee, or whose melee skill has MC 0, are unchanged.
Snapshot regen over the affected builds; merge gated (user-approved).

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestPerManaCostMeleeAffix_spec.lua` (9/9) — parse structure (nil residue),
Damage MORE scaling + cap (MC20/MC100 → +4%), channel basis (MC1 → visible, not ×18/×0), MC0 no-op,
Melee-only scope (spell excluded), Crit BASE scaling.

## per-mana-cost-melee-affix-fractional-precision

**What:** `src/Modules/ItemTools.lua` `applyRange` no longer collapses the fractional
*"... for Melee Attacks per 1 Mana Cost"* affix family to an integer percent. The generic
`"% ⇒ integer percent"` step (default rounding ⇒ `precision 100`, then `/100 ⇒ 1`) is now
skipped when the line contains the `per 1 mana cost` token, so the sub-integer roll survives
weapon-slot scaling. Scoped by `isPerManaCostFractional = line:lower():find("per 1 mana cost")`.

**Why:** affix 986 is COMBINED — an integer *"increased Melee Damage"* part (legitimately
`{rounding:Integer}`) AND a FRACTIONAL *"Damage for Melee Attacks per 1 Mana Cost"* MORE sub-line.
LE property_list_1_4.json property 0 "Damage" `roundingForMore = Hundredth` (and the crit sibling
ships an explicit `{rounding:Thousandth}`), so these roll fractions like 0.2%/0.3%. Pre-fix, the
`%`-collapse rounded the scalar-scaled value to an integer: on a weapon slot with
`{scalar:1.829}`, `0.3 × 1.829 = 0.549 → round → 1` (~3-5× too high), while smaller rolls
(`0.2 × scalar < 0.5`) rounded to **0** (silently inert). The bug was PRE-EXISTING but only
EXPOSED once `per-mana-cost-melee-affix` un-inert-ed the family (dev <see git log>); before that the
mod was scoped to SkillName "Melee Attack" and contributed nothing regardless of value.

**Effect:** `0.549 → 0.55` (Hundredth) for Damage; the crit sibling respects its declared
Thousandth (`+(0.2-0.3)% ... range 143 → 0.256`, not the Tenth-collapsed `0.3`). Values on
`scalar 1.0` slots (literal, no scaling) are untouched. The generic non-per-mana percent path
(`(20-30)% increased Melee Damage @ 1.829 → 40%`) still rounds to integer — verified by spec.

**Corpus impact:** all changes are CORRECTIONS of the old 0/1 integer artifacts to true
fractions (Damage 0/1 → 0.37/0.55, crit 0 → 0.2x). Builds whose per-mana affix sits on a
`scalar 1.0` slot, or whose melee mod does not feed the summed skill, are unchanged. Snapshot
regen over the affected builds; merge gated (user-approved).

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestPerManaCostMeleeAffix_spec.lua` — `describe("applyRange keeps the
fractional per-mana value ...")`: Damage @1.829 → +0.55% (not +1%), Damage @1.0 unchanged, crit
range respects Thousandth (→0.256), regression: normal `% increased Melee Damage` stays integer.

## tree-rank-scale-skip-weapon-hand-token

**What:** `src/Classes/PassiveTree.lua` `ProcessStats` → `scaleNumbers` no longer rank-scales
a digit glued to `h`/`H` (the 1h/2h weapon-hand token inside a CONDITION phrase). The
`gsub` is `(%d[%d.]*)(%a?)` and returns the digit run unscaled when the captured suffix is
`h`/`H`; otherwise it scales (×`node.alloc`) and re-appends the suffix.

**Why:** the bare `%d[%d.]*` scaler multiplied EVERY number by the node's allocated points,
including the `2` inside `2h`. Master of Arms (Sentinel-68, tree_2.json, maxPoints 8)
`+2 Strength With 2h Weapon` at 8 pts became `+16 Strength With 16h Weapon`; ModParser has
`with 2h weapon` but not `with 16h weapon`, so the `UsingTwoHandedWeapon` condition was lost
and the entire Str mod dropped. Aurora_LEB Forge Guard: LEB Brutality **98** vs in-game
**116** — the +16 Master of Arms Strength vanished. This was the bulk of the long-chased
"-18 Strength" Forge Strike gap (which was wrongly chased through idol-decode / LP-fused /
set-completion / quest-count before this root). With the fix Brutality 98→**114** (remaining
−2 = the separate .5 attribute-rounding convention: in-game rounds .5 up, LEB/LETools down).

**Scope / corpus impact:** NOT inert. Affects every multi-point (`alloc>1`) tree node whose
stat carries a `1h`/`2h` token — Master of Arms, Battlemaster's Blade `+20% Area With 2h`,
Heorot's Arsenal `+8 Spell Damage With 2h Weapon`, `7% Increased Melee Damage With 2h Weapon`,
weapon-subtype nodes (`with 2h Sword/Axe/Mace`), `with 1h Weapon` nodes, etc. Builds
allocating such a node with >1 point AND the matching weapon equipped now get the correct
(conditional) mod. Full-corpus snapshot regen required before merge (gated, user approval).
Note: `with 1h weapon` is not yet a recognised ModParser condition (separate gap) — this fix
only restores the value/token integrity, not the missing 1h condition pattern.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestTreeRankScaleWeaponHandToken_spec.lua` (4/4)
- `+2 Strength With 2h Weapon` @8pts → Str BASE **16** with `UsingTwoHandedWeapon` (not dropped)
- `+8 Spell Damage With 2h Weapon` @5pts → Damage **40**, condition kept
- ordinary `+2 Strength` @8pts still scales to 16 (no over-guard)
- inline guard marker present in PassiveTree.lua

### `smelters-wrath-max-charge-more`

Smelter's Wrath builds charge while channelling and deals up to **+100% MORE damage
at maximum charge**. LEB modeled **zero** charge, so a max-charge hit was ~×2 under.

**Grounding — INTRINSIC ramp, not a tree node** (datamined game source
`datamined game source`):
`getTempStats` (L284-296) adds `MoreStat(0 /*Damage*/, 0, age / maxDuration)`;
`maxDuration` defaults to **2.0s** in the mutator `.ctor` (L847) and is set from the
channel duration (L511). At full charge (`age == maxDuration`) the value is **1.0 ⇒
+100% more (×2.0)**. Gated only on `maxDuration ~= 0` (always set), so it applies to
**every** Smelter's Wrath build regardless of tree allocation. The similarly named
tree node "Smelter's Wrath More Damage From Charging" (0.5 MORE/pt, max +250%;
`datamined game source`, init 0.0) is a **separate, additive** bonus that only
allocating builds get — NOT this ramp.

**Fix:** `Modules/CalcOffence.lua` — for the Smelter's Wrath skill, add
`Damage MORE = (100/2)% × Multiplier:SmeltersWrathChargeSeconds`, and default /
cap that multiplier at **2.0** (mirrors the `MomentumStacks` auto-default above ⇒
modeled at MAX charge by default). `Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` —
`multiplierSmeltersWrathChargeSeconds` (ifMult `SmeltersWrathChargeSeconds`, capped
`m_min(val,2)`) overrides the charge state (0–2s). Linear ramp: +50%/charge-second.

**Sites:**

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `Modules/CalcOffence.lua` | skill-gated Damage MORE + auto-max-charge default/cap |
| `Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` | `multiplierSmeltersWrathChargeSeconds` config (0–2, capped) |

**Files:** `src/Modules/CalcOffence.lua`, `src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua`
**Invariant:** Smelter's Wrath gets +100% more Damage at max charge by default
(linear +50%/s, capped at the 2.0s `maxDuration`); the config scales it; no leak to
other skills.
**Verification** (state-matched `Aurora_blank` capture 2026-06-29, **0 Smelter's
Wrath tree nodes** — verified in the `.epoch`: `st4th` `nodeIDs []`): per-hit pre-mit
phys 41735 / fire 36087 vs LEB **before** 19162 / 16694 (×2.17 under) → **after**
38457 / 33509 (residual ~**8%**). The ~8% residual (capture ×2.17 vs modeled ×2.0)
is an **ungrounded open item** (candidate: `moreCritAtMaxCharge` / `statsPerSecondCharged`
base entries / beam-vs-End hit routing; needs an uncharged-vs-max A/B capture).
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestSmeltersWrathCharge_spec.lua` (5/5)
**Snapshot coverage:** intrinsic ⇒ all Smelter's Wrath corpus builds shift at max
charge by default; full-corpus snapshot regen required before merge (GATED, user
approval — NOT run here).
**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `smelters-wrath-charge-scaling-nodes`

Smelter's Wrath **skill-tree** nodes that scale with charge time / full charge were
**silently dropped or zeroed**, so a fully-spec'd build was ~×4.5 (phys) / ×6.4 (fire)
**under** at max charge — a large multi-root gap distinct from (and on top of) the
intrinsic `smelters-wrath-max-charge-more` ramp.

Two failure modes:
- **Per-second nodes** parsed to a flat MORE with an **unparsed residue** (`Per Second`),
  which `PassiveTree`/`PassiveSpec` treat as `node.extra` and **drop** (Tempered Blows
  `15% More Damage Per Second`, Whetstone `+2% Melee/Fire Damage per Second`); and the
  bare form (Heavy Strike `+5% Damage Per Second`) routed to
  `Condition:Channelling × Multiplier:ChannellingSeconds` — both **0** because Smelter's
  Wrath is not flagged Channelling and `ChannellingSeconds` was unset.
- **Full-charge nodes** likewise left residue (`At Full Charge`) and dropped (Vulcanic
  Mastery `+50% Damage At Full Charge`, `100% More Crit Chance At Full Charge`).

**Grounding** (datamined game source
`datamined game source`,
`getTempStats`): per-second stats (L256-281) are added as `Stat(stat, age)` — value ×
`age` (seconds charged, **capped at `maxDuration` = 2.0s**, .ctor L847) ⇒ **×2.0 at max
charge**, exactly `Multiplier:SmeltersWrathChargeSeconds`. Full-charge stats (L298-324)
apply in full while `fullyCharged`. The charge **is** the channel in-engine
(`getTempStats` reads the `ExistsWhileChannelling` component and drives `age` from it).

**Fix:**
- `Modules/ModParser.lua` — full-line `specialModList` handlers for the residue forms,
  all MORE (consistent with the existing `channelling-per-second-stacking-buff` bare
  handler and the datamining's `MoreStat`): `more damage per second`,
  `melee damage per second` (KeywordFlag.Melee), `fire damage per second`,
  `damage at full charge`, `more crit chance at full charge`. Per-second → routed to
  `Condition:Channelling × Multiplier:ChannellingSeconds`; full-charge →
  `Condition:FullyCharged`. **Every one of these exact strings exists ONLY in the
  Smelter's Wrath tree** (`src/TreeData/1_4/tree_2.json` st4th-*) ⇒ zero blast radius
  outside Smelter's Wrath.
- `Modules/CalcOffence.lua` — for Smelter's Wrath, publish the charge=channel state
  **scoped to the skill's own modList** (never the global modDB, so Flurry / Volcanic
  Orb keep their Config-tab `ChannellingSeconds`): `Multiplier:ChannellingSeconds` =
  the charge-seconds value (= `age`, default 2.0), `Condition:Channelling`, and
  `Condition:FullyCharged` (when at max charge).
- `Data/ModCache.lua` — 5 stale rows that baked the dropped-residue parse deleted so
  the strings re-parse live: `15% More Damage Per Second`, `+2% Melee Damage per Second`,
  `+2% Fire Damage per Second`, `+50% Damage At Full Charge`,
  `100% More Crit Chance At Full Charge`.

**Sites:**

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `Modules/ModParser.lua` | 5 full-line handlers for the residue forms (Smelter's-only strings) |
| `Modules/CalcOffence.lua` | skill-scoped `Channelling` / `ChannellingSeconds` / `FullyCharged` state |
| `Data/ModCache.lua` | 5 stale dropped-residue rows removed |

## anurok-damage-per-character-level

The Summon Anurok skill ("Summon AncientOasis01 Primordial Minion", name "Summon
Anurok") scales its damage **per CHARACTER LEVEL** — in-game tooltip (authority,
2026-06-30): *"PER CHARACTER LEVEL: 6% (600%) Increased Damage"*. Its per-Strength
grant is **Physical Penetration** (not Damage); per-Att = Crit Chance; per-Dex =
Crit Multiplier (all already present). The Primal Anurok auto-summons to fill
unused companion slots and **does NOT count as a companion**, so the companions'
"4% increased Minion Damage per player Strength" (on Wolf/Bear/Storm Crow's own
summon skills) does NOT apply to it.

**Fix** (`src/Data/skills.json`, Summon Anurok `baseMods`): added
`"6% increased Minion Damage per level"` → MinionModifier wrapping `Damage INC`
with `Multiplier:Level`. The minion's Level multiplier is the character level
(`CalcActiveSkill.lua:1323` `minion.level = env.build.characterLevel`;
`CalcPerform.lua:538` `env.minion.modDB.multipliers["Level"] = env.minion.level`),
so this resolves to 6×characterLevel (600% at lvl100, 504% at lvl84, …) exactly
matching the per-character-level tooltip.

**Why this replaced the GlobalMinionDamageScaling broadcast (<see git log>, REVERTED):**
the −44% under was a MISSING per-character-level damage scaling, NOT a mis-scoped
per-Str. The broadcast gave the Anurok the companions' per-Str, which only
COINCIDENTALLY matched blank Deluyi (4×Str≈600≈per-char-level at lvl100) and
OVER-shot spec'd ToBee by +8.6% (engine MinionStatDumper
`minion_runtime_stats_20260630_141431`: Anurok generic Damage INC **951** = ~351
shared global item/tree INC + **600** per-char-level; Wolf **1139** = 351 + 788
its-own-per-Str — the Anurok gets NO per-Str damage).

**Ground truth (no fabrication):** in-game tooltips (Summon Anurok / Bear / Storm
Crow / Chorus of the Anurok helmet) + engine dumps. Validated both builds (probes
`spec/tools/ProbeToBeeLEBAll.lua` / `ProbeDeluyiAnurok.lua`, gitignored): Anurok
Deluyi PhysHitAvg **14373** vs in-game **14845** (−3.2%), ToBee **10639** vs
**11075** (−3.9%) — now IN-LINE with the companions' shared ~−4% state residual
(monster MORE LEB 6.20 vs engine 6.448), no longer an Anurok-specific gap. Wolf/
Bear/Crow unchanged (the per-level baseMod is scoped to the Anurok's own skill).

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestAnurokDamagePerCharacterLevel_spec.lua` (3/3).
**Snapshot coverage:** changes Anurok damage on all Anurok-summoning corpus builds
(~88) ⇒ full scoped snapshot regen required before merge (GATED, user approval —
NOT run here).
**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

## firebrand-per-stack-added-fire

Firebrand builds a stacking buff: *"Each stack of the Firebrand buff increases the
size of subsequent Firebrand attacks and **adds melee fire damage**."* Each active
stack grants a **flat +5 added melee fire damage**. LEB modeled the Firebrand stack
**only** for a Ward-per-second modifier (`ConfigOptions multiplierFirebrandStack →
WardPerSecond`), **not** for damage, so the per-stack fire was missing.

> ⚠️ **Premise correction — the originating "fire ×62 under" was a probe artifact.**
> `spec/tools/ProbeSkillPreMit.lua` reads raw `skillModList:Sum("BASE","FireDamage")`
> **without making Firebrand the main skill / running the added-damage pipeline**, so
> it read a base of ~3 instead of the real **155.75** (the per-type fire base after the
> global added-melee→fire pool is folded in). Building Firebrand as the main skill, the
> true pre-mit fire was **3854** vs in-game **4653 (−17%)**, NOT ×62. Always state-match
> via a main-skill build (`ProbeFirebrandProper.lua`), not a bare skill-mod sum.

**Grounding — INTRINSIC per-stack added flat, not a tree node** (datamined game source
`datamined game source`):
`ModifyFirebrandStacks` (L2283, L2469) does `uVar16 = DAT_183d720e4 (= 5)` then
`uVar8 = 0x208` (melee-fire damage-type mask; `0x202` under the Lightning Brand
conversion flag) and `Stats__AddedStat(0, uVar8, uVar16, ...)`, attached once per
active stack. **Base max stacks = 4** (`GetMaxStacks` datamined offset: `field(0x134) +
4`; `0x134` = tree-granted extra max stacks = **0** on a blank char). The
added-damage effectiveness (**1.25**) and the player's increased/more melee+fire
then apply, so each stack adds **5 × 1.25 = 6.25** to the per-type fire base. The
per-stack MORE/increased terms in `getTempStats` (mutator offsets 0x150/0x158/0x85c)
are all **tree-driven** (0 on a blank char) — a SEPARATE, larger item.

**Fix:** `Modules/CalcOffence.lua` — for the Firebrand skill, add
`FireDamage BASE = 5 × Multiplier:FirebrandStack` (`ModFlag.Melee`), and default that
multiplier to **4** when the user has not set it (mirrors the `MomentumStacks` /
Smelter's Wrath auto-max default ⇒ modeled at max stacks by default).
`Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` — the existing `multiplierFirebrandStack` (ifMult
`FirebrandStack`) overrides the count; its tooltip now documents the damage role.

**Sites:**

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `Modules/CalcOffence.lua` | skill-gated `FireDamage BASE` per stack + auto-max-stack default |

## upheaval-totem-grant

**What:** Upheaval cast via uph41-30 "Upheaval Totems" is delivered 100% by an Upheaval Totem
minion ("attacks with Upheaval from it RATHER THAN YOURSELF"), not the player. LEB modeled it as
player-cast = 1176 (x3.13 under the capture). Three load-bearing parts close it: a node-gated
summon grant, routing the player's GLOBAL added-flat onto the totem, and suppressing the now-replaced
player-cast hit so Full DPS does not double-count.

**Game source:** `TreeData/.../tree_0.json` uph41-30 (maxPoints 1) "create an Upheaval Totem ...
RATHER THAN YOURSELF ... Limited to 1 ... last 8 seconds"; uph41-10 (Stonethorn Pillars) + uph41-11
(Mountain Fortress) each "+1 Maximum Upheaval Totems". `minions.json` UpheavalTotem skillList=[Upheaval],
DamageTaken -50%. In-game `UpheavalTotemAdapter` copies the player's Upheaval stat fields (incl.
added-flat) onto the totem.

**Sites:**

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `Data/skills.json` | new `SummonUpheavalTotem` (minionList [UpheavalTotem], treeId uph41, 8s duration) |
| `Data/SubSkillGrants.lua` | `Upheaval -> SummonUpheavalTotem` (requiresNode uph41-30, summon, replacesParentHit, summonActiveCountBase 1 + summonActiveCountNodes {uph41-10, uph41-11}) |
| `Data/Global.lua` | `LE_PLAYER_ADDED_FLAT_MINIONS = { UpheavalTotem = { skill = "Upheaval" } }` (opt-in whitelist) |
| `Modules/CalcPerform.lua` | player GLOBAL BASE added-flat <Type>Damage -> minion modDB (whitelist+delivery-flag gated; BASE only; SkillId/SkillName + Tree excluded) |
| `Modules/CalcSetup.lua` | multi-node count consumer (cap = base + allocated +1 nodes); replacesParentHit -> SkillName:Upheaval DisableSkill on the player modDB |

**Invariant:** The totem inherits ONLY the player's GLOBAL BASE added-flat (the in-game adapter
copy) -- never INC/MORE (those already flow via the treeId inheritIds channel + minion-damage gear;
copying them would overshoot). Copy is MINION-modDB-only (zero player ripple), delivery-flag gated
(spell/wrong-weapon flats skipped -- no blanket fold, unlike the abandoned melee fix <see git log>), and
WHITELIST-keyed by minion type (opt-in; no other summon/build is touched). When uph41-30 is allocated
the player-cast Upheaval direct hit is disabled (player-actor only) so it drops out of Full DPS while
the totem still spawns + casts.

### `no-cooldown-flag-zeroes-cooldown`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestNoCooldownFlagZeroesCooldown_spec.lua` (4/4)
- `calcSkillCooldown` (`CalcOffence.lua`) must honour the `NoCooldown` flag and set
  `cooldown = 0`.
- ModParser maps `"no cooldown"` → `flag("NoCooldown")`; ModCache bakes `" No Cooldown"`
  → a `NoCooldown` FLAG mod.
- the bug: "X No Cooldown" spec nodes (Erasing Strike / Shield Throw / Judgement /
  Focus / Forge Strike / Shield Bash / ...) convert a skill's cooldown into a mana
  cost, removing the cooldown so the skill fires at cast/attack speed. LEB parsed
  these into a `NoCooldown` FLAG but `calcSkillCooldown` never read it, keeping the
  base cooldown. Erasing Strike's 5s cooldown made LEB model 0.28 casts/s vs the
  in-game biman11 ~3.6/s (a 12× cadence under-count).
- locks: `if skillModList:Flag(skillCfg, "NoCooldown") then cooldown = 0 end` inside
  `calcSkillCooldown`.

**Grounded 2026-07-02:** biman11 Erasing Strike (No Cooldown node allocated) — Speed
0.28 → 1.68/s, TotalDPS 99,343 → 596,508 (in-game 754,144; −21% vs −87% before);
AverageHit unchanged (cadence-only, per-hit untouched).

**Snapshot coverage:** NOT corpus-neutral — ~73 builds allocate a No Cooldown node
(Forge Strike ×30, Shield Throw ×22, Erasing Strike ×7, Judgement/Shield Bash/Shield
Rush ×4, Focus ×2); those with the No-Cooldown skill as their includeInFullDPS main
recompute HIGHER (were cadence-under-counting). Corpus snapshots are gitignored
(local, per-machine) so this commit carries only src+spec+guard; affected builds'
local snapshots are regenerated as-needed (lazy). Fix is non-breaking (cooldown 0 is
a valid value) and validated on biman11.
**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `elemental-arrows-resource`

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestElementalArrows_spec.lua` (8/8)

Rogue/Marksman **Elemental Arrows** resource (game `Property_Player_109-115`, datamined game source
`localization/properties_localization.json`). Bow attacks CONSUME Elemental Arrows (auto-generated,
max 3); each consumed arrow ADDS fire+lightning (`Property_113`) and increased-elemental
(`Property_115`) to that hit. The tree stats phrase this "... **with Elemental Arrow**" (Rogue-24
"+3 Fire/+3 Lightning per pt", Rogue-35 "125% inc Elemental") and "... **consumed per bow attack**"
(Rogue-32 Elemental Barrage).

The bug: there is no skill named "Elemental Arrow", so the "with Elemental Arrow" lines failed to
parse (no `SkillName` match) and were SILENTLY DROPPED — AmHoA Hail of Arrows lightning read ~4.8×
UNDER in-game (lightning has no conversion confound, so it is the clean proof type).

Fix (`@leb-regression-guard:elemental-arrows-resource`, 3 sites):
- **ModParser modTagList:** `"with elemental arrow"` / `"per elemental arrow[ used]"` →
  `Multiplier:ElementalArrowConsumed` tag (scales the added/increased by the consumed count).
- **ModParser:** `"elemental arrow[s] consumed per bow attack"` → BASE `ElementalArrowExtraConsume`;
  bare-number `"N maximum elemental arrows"` → BASE `ElementalArrowMax` (specialModList).
- **CalcPerform** (`calcs.perform`, after the ailment-stack block): when `ElementalArrowMax>0` OR
  `ElementalArrowExtraConsume>0`, inject `Multiplier:ElementalArrowConsumed = min(1 + extra, cap)`
  (cap = parsed max, else the game-base 3 Rogue-24 grants). Non-EA builds have both stats 0 → untouched.

**⚠ Parse-quirk note (RESOLVED — ModCache shadow, not a live-parse collision):** the v1 "max parses
unreliably" limitation was NOT the "Maximum" form keyword / "Elemental" damage-type collision (the
specialModList bare-number rules parse every variant correctly) — it was **stale pre-fix ModCache
entries shadowing the live rules** (parseMod is cache-first). 7 entries DELETED from
`src/Data/ModCache.lua` (same class as `spellblade-weapon-melee-added-gained-as-spell`):
- empty modlists (line silently dropped): `"3 Maximum Elemental Arrows"`, `"+1 Maximum Elemental
  Arrows"`, `"+1 Elemental Arrow consumed per bow attack"`, `"1 Elemental Arrows Per Second"`
- tag-less stale mods: `"+3 Fire Damage with Elemental Arrow"` / `"+3 Lightning Damage with Elemental
  Arrow"` (missing the `Multiplier:ElementalArrowConsumed` per-arrow tag), `"25% Increased Elemental
  Damage with Elemental Arrow"` (missing the `Condition:HaveElementalArrows` ×1 gate)
Consequence before deletion: any node rank whose exact text matched a cached key lost the mod — a
Rogue-24-only build (no Barrage: max-stat cached-empty + ExtraConsume 0) got `Multiplier = 0` and NO
per-arrow added at all. Now the max-cap parses from the node → detection no longer relies on
Elemental Barrage; the cap=3 fallback in CalcPerform is kept as belt-and-suspenders. Left untouched
(out of scope, defensive/no-op either way): `"15 Ward Gain Per Elemental Arrow"`, `"7% Elemental
Arrow Generation Rate"`, the two flavor lines. Spec locks the cache-first parse path (8/8).

**Calibration — added per-arrow, increased x1:** the per-arrow ADDED (Property_113, "+N Fire/Lightning
Damage with Elemental Arrow") scales x consumed; the increased ("125% increased Elemental Damage with
Elemental Arrow", Rogue-35) is a x1 Condition (`HaveElementalArrows`), NOT per-arrow — matching LEB's
"with arcane shield" = Condition convention. Applying the increased x consumed over-shot AmHoA in-game
lightning ~1.6x.

**Validation:** AmHoA `save_20260703_031914` Hail of Arrows (pre-mit NON-CRIT basis) — Lightning
3105 (4.8x UNDER) → **12983**; in-game non-crit floor 9681 / median 10384 → **~1.25x** (added-x3 +
increased-x1). Fire 18860 → 26447 (still UNDER; fire additionally needs the separate whole-attack
phys→fire conversion — a distinct OPEN work-item). Residual lightning ~1.25x over the median is a
consumed-count uncertainty (steady-state 3 vs generation-limited ~2 is underdetermined from one
capture) — a documented follow-up, not curve-fit further without more captures / generation datamine.

### `aspect-effect-buff-scalar`

**Family:** Beastmaster "(N)% Increased Aspect of the {Lynx,Shark,Viper,Boar} Effect" item affixes.

**Ground truth (verbatim, no fabrication) — `src/Data/ModItem_1_4.json`:**
- `(10-25)% Increased Aspect of the Lynx Effect`
- `(6-20)% Increased Aspect of the Shark Effect`
- `(10-25)% Increased Aspect of the Viper Effect`
- `(5-12)% Increased Aspect of the Boar Effect`

**Silent failure:** ModCache baked all 49 rolled values as `{{}," Effect "}` — an empty modList with
an `" Effect "` residue. Cause: ModParser's `skillNameList` post-scan strips "Aspect of the
Lynx/Shark/Viper/Boar" (a real skill/buff name) from the line, leaving a bare "Effect" that reaches no
`modNameList` key. So a `modNameList["aspect of the lynx effect"]` alias can never match (the phrase is
already dismantled by the time the modName scan runs).

**Fix (`src/Modules/ModParser.lua`, `specialModList`):** four whole-line handlers, scanned FIRST
(`scan(line, specialModList)` at the top of `parseMod`, before the skillName strip):
```
["^%+?([%d%.]+)%%? increased aspect of the lynx effect$"]  -> mod("AspectoftheLynxEffect",  "INC", num)
["^%+?([%d%.]+)%%? increased aspect of the shark effect$"] -> mod("AspectoftheSharkEffect", "INC", num)
["^%+?([%d%.]+)%%? increased aspect of the viper effect$"] -> mod("AspectoftheViperEffect", "INC", num)
["^%+?([%d%.]+)%%? increased aspect of the boar effect$"]  -> mod("AspectoftheBoarEffect",  "INC", num)
```
Stat names are NOT invented: CalcPerform buff scaling reads the per-buff effect scalar as
`skillModList:Sum("INC", skillCfg, buff.name:gsub(" ", "").."Effect")` (`src/Modules/CalcPerform.lua`
~L733 / ~L751), and the four buffs are named "Aspect of the {Lynx,Shark,Viper,Boar}"
(`src/TreeData/1_4/tree_0.json`), so `gsub(" ","").."Effect"` yields exactly
`AspectoftheLynxEffect` / `AspectoftheSharkEffect` / `AspectoftheViperEffect` / `AspectoftheBoarEffect`.
This is the same mechanism as the long-working `"frenzy effect"->"FrenzyEffect"` modName alias.

**ModCache re-bake:** the 49 stale silent-failure rows were DELETED (not re-baked with explicit
values) so they re-parse live via the new handlers — regen-equivalent, self-maintaining (same
convention as `throwing-attack-damage-inc`). The silent-failure sweep JSON + `TestSilentFailureSweep`
baselines were re-run (`enumerate_silent_failures.py`) and updated in the same commit
(total 16452->16403, silent 1994->1945, b-dm-numeric 114->65).

**Residue-drop trap:** handlers emit `nil` extra (residue-free), so
`PassiveTree:ProcessStats` (`if mod.list and not mod.extra`) does not drop them.

**Verification (modDB-level, not just parseMod):** `modLib.parseMod("125% Increased Aspect of the Lynx
Effect")` -> `{name="AspectoftheLynxEffect", type="INC", value=125}`, extra=nil; adding to a fresh
`new("ModDB")` then `db:Sum("INC", nil, "AspectoftheLynxEffect")` returns `125` — i.e. the mod lands
under exactly the stat the engine Sums. Spec `spec/System/TestAspectEffect_spec.lua` (11/11).

**Corpus blast radius (MAIN `spec/TestBuilds/`):** 17 builds carry these affixes and will change on
regen (15 Beastmaster + 2 Shaman): `1.4/<private build>`, `1.4/<private build>`, `1.4/<private build>`, `1.4/<private build>`,
`1.4/BOwJRDdE` (Shaman), `1.4/<private build>`, `1.4/BakEOnPz`, `1.4/<private build>`, `1.4/<private build>`, `1.4/<private build>`,
`1.4/QDxqOprR`, `1.4/<private build>`, `1.4/<private build>`, `1.4/QkYkwRea`, `1.4/bin/BurningMyWood`,
`1.4/bin/ChevyVolt` (Shaman), `1.4/bin/Nokia3310`. (Snapshots not regenerated in this worktree — corpus
is gitignored/absent.)

### `increased-healing-effectiveness-alias`

**Family:** the bare skill-tree node stat "(N)% Increased Healing" (NO "Effectiveness" word).

**Ground truth (verbatim, no fabrication) — `src/TreeData/1_4/tree_0.json` + `tree_2.json` node stats,
each with the node's OWN description proving it is Healing Effectiveness:**
- Blossoming Garden (`Primalist-72`) `10% Increased Healing` — desc "Increases healing effectiveness for you and your minions."
- Blessed Springs (`Primalist-98`) `7% Increased Healing` — desc "Increases cold damage and healing effectiveness ..."
- Improved Blessing (`eb5656-23`) `+20% Increased Healing` — desc "Eterra's Blessing has increased healing effectiveness."
- Violent Squall (`mas54-10`) `+200% Increased Healing` — desc "Maelstrom ... has significantly increased healing effectiveness ..."
- Redemption (`ah443-14`) `+10% Increased Healing` (Paladin tree_2)
- Virtue of Patience (`hh7pa3-28`) `24% Increased Healing` (Paladin tree_2)

These strings also appear as ModCache keys (baked from tree processing across 1_2/1_3/1_4).

**Silent failure:** ModCache baked the 6 rolled values as `{{},"  "}` — an empty modList with a
whitespace-only residue. Cause: the generic "increased X" path strips "increased" and looks up the
remainder "healing" in ModParser's modName map (`src/Modules/ModParser.lua`), which has an entry ONLY
for "healing effectiveness" -> `HealingEffectiveness` (L409). "healing" alone resolves to no modName,
so the node stat dropped silently. (The already-working `"(N)% Increased Healing Effectiveness"` item
affix parses fine precisely because it keeps the "effectiveness" word.)

**Fix (`src/Modules/ModParser.lua`, `specialModList`):** one whole-line handler, scanned FIRST
(`scan(line, specialModList)` at the top of `parseMod`):
```
["^%+?([%d%.]+)%%? increased healing$"] -> mod("HealingEffectiveness", "INC", num)
```
The stat name is NOT invented: it is the same `HealingEffectiveness` the "... Effectiveness" affix already
emits and that `CalcDefence.lua` L1845 consumes
(`output.HealingEffectiveness = modDB:Sum("INC", nil, "HealingEffectiveness")`). Each node's own
description confirms the semantics are identical.

**Scoping (no collision):** the pattern ends in `healing$` directly after the number, so it does NOT match

### `effect-of-buff-on-you-bare-alias`

**Family:** the bare affix "+N% Effect of {Haste,Frenzy} on You" — the SAME stat as the
already-working "increased" form "(N)% increased Effect of {Haste,Frenzy} on You", just
rendered WITHOUT the word "increased" and WITH a "+" prefix.

**Ground truth (verbatim, no fabrication) — `src/Data/ModItem_1_4.json`:**
- `(3-5)% increased Effect of Haste on You` ... `(90-100)% increased Effect of Haste on You` (L75499+)
- `(3-5)% increased Effect of Frenzy on You` ... `(90-100)% increased Effect of Frenzy on You` (L75643+)

The "increased" rendering already parses: ModCache proves
`"14% increased Effect of Haste on You"` -> `HasteEffect INC 14`,
`"14% increased Effect of Frenzy on You"` -> `FrenzyEffect INC 14`. The modName map also
carries the direct aliases `["haste effect"]="HasteEffect"` / `["frenzy effect"]="FrenzyEffect"`
(`src/Modules/ModParser.lua` L210-211).

**Silent failure:** LE ALSO renders these rolls without "increased" and with a "+"
("+11% Effect of Haste on You"). ModCache baked those 24 rows as `{{}," Effect of  on You "}`
— an empty modList with the buff name stripped out of the residue (the skill-name post-scan
consumes "Haste"/"Frenzy"), so the affix was silently swallowed with no modName reaching
calcs. Because `parseMod` short-circuits on an exact `parseModCache[line]` key, the baked empty
row would have BYPASSED any new handler, so these rows were DELETED (not re-baked).

**Fix (`src/Modules/ModParser.lua`, inside the `knownBuffsOnYou` loop, L3364):** a second
whole-line handler per known buff, alongside the pre-existing "increased" one:
```
["^%+?([%d%.]+)%% effect of " .. esc .. " on you$"] -> mod(bVar .. "Effect", "INC", num)
```
The stat name is NOT invented: `bVar` is `buff.name:gsub(" ","")` — the exact transform
`CalcPerform.lua:1216 / :1234` applies when it reads the per-buff effect scalar
(`skillModList:Sum("INC", skillCfg, buff.name:gsub(" ", "").."Effect")`), which scales the
active Haste/Frenzy buff's modList by `(1 + inc/100)`. Only "Haste" and "Frenzy" appear in the
bare ModCache form; both are in `knownBuffsOnYou`, so the handler auto-covers exactly them.

**Scoping (no collision):** the bare pattern matches `"%% effect of <buff> on you$"`, which
cannot match the `"%% increased effect of ..."` string (the word "increased" sits between the
`%%` and `effect`), so the pre-existing "increased" handler is untouched. Not a minion family
(these are on-you buffs) — no overlap with the active minion workstream.

**ModCache re-bake:** the 24 stale bare-form silent-failure rows were DELETED (not re-baked) so
they re-parse live via the new handler. The silent-failure sweep JSON + `TestSilentFailureSweep`
baselines were re-run (`enumerate_silent_failures.py`) and updated in the same commit:
total 16396->16372, silent 1938->1914, c-dm-infra 220->196, silent_failure_matched 285->261,
dm_gap 294->296.

**Residue-drop trap:** the handler emits `nil` extra (residue-free), so
`PassiveTree:ProcessStats` (`if mod.list and not mod.extra`) does not drop it.

**Verification (modDB-level, not just parseMod):** `modLib.parseMod("+14% Effect of Haste on You")`
-> `{name="HasteEffect", type="INC", value=14}`, extra=nil; adding the parsed mods to a fresh
`new("ModDB")` then `db:Sum("INC", nil, "HasteEffect")` returns the value — the mod lands under

`(name,type,value)`. Spec `spec/System/TestEffectOfBuffAlias_spec.lua` (14/14).

### `fangs-berserker-frenzy-effect`

**Family:** two Fangs of the Berserker (unique **446**) buff-effect scalars that carry a
SUFFIX the pre-existing "on you" handlers don't anchor:
- `(12-20)% increased Effect of Frenzy while Dual Wielding`
- `0.5% increased Effect of Frenzy per Strength`

**Ground truth (verbatim, no fabrication):** `src/Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json` unique 446
carries both strings; the datamine (`datamined game source` unique 446) confirms the coefficients —
mod idx 6 `val 0.12 / max 0.20` (dual-wield 12→20%), mod idx 7 `val 0.005 / max 0.01`
(per-Str is a **0.5%→1% rollable**; legacy `uniques{,_1_2,_1_3}.json` render the 1% end). The
number is therefore CAPTURED from the string, never hardcoded.

**Silent failure:** "Frenzy" is stripped by the skill-name post-scan, leaving a bare
`" Effect of "` residue, so ModCache baked `{{}," Effect of   "}` (empty modList) at
`src/Data/ModCache.lua:10026` (per-Str) and `:11708` (dual-wield). Because `parseMod`
short-circuits on an exact `parseModCache[line]` key, the baked empty rows BYPASS any handler,
so both rows were **DELETED** (not re-baked) to re-parse live.

**Fix (`src/Modules/ModParser.lua`, inside the `knownBuffsOnYou` loop, after the "on you"
handlers):** two whole-line handlers per known buff:
```
["^([%+%-]?[%d%.]+)%% increased effect of "..esc.." while dual wielding$"]
    -> mod(bVar.."Effect","INC",num, { type="Condition", var="DualWielding" })
["^([%+%-]?[%d%.]+)%% increased effect of "..esc.." per strength$"]
    -> mod(bVar.."Effect","INC",num, { type="PerStat", stat="Str" })
```
`bVar` is `buff.name:gsub(" ","")` — the exact transform `CalcPerform.lua:1305 / :1323` applies
when it reads the per-buff scalar (`skillModList:Sum("INC", skillCfg, buff.name:gsub(" ","").."Effect")`),
which scales the active Frenzy buff's modList by `(1 + inc/100)`. The `DualWielding` Condition
tag (`modTagList "while dual wielding"`, ModParser.lua:952) and `PerStat:Str` tag
(`Attributes[2]="Str"`, Global.lua:97; precedent `ModCache.lua:10280` "…per player Attunement"
→ FrenzyEffect INC + PerStat) are standard tags carried INLINE on the mod. `createMod` treats a
leading table arg as a tag and leaves `source=nil` (NOT `""`) so a strict `not extra` consumer
keeps the flag.

**Scoping (no collision):** the patterns require `"%% increased effect of <buff> while dual
wielding$"` / `"… per strength$"`, which cannot match the `"… on you$"` handlers (different
suffix). Both strings appear ONLY on unique 446 across the versioned unique files — no affix
(ModItem) and no other buff's ModCache row carries them — so the fix is single-item-source and
cannot leak to off-target builds.

**Residue-drop trap:** the handlers emit `nil` extra (residue-free), so
`PassiveTree:ProcessStats` (`if mod.list and not mod.extra`) does not drop them.

**Verification (modDB-level):** `modLib.parseMod("16% increased Effect of Frenzy while Dual
Wielding")` → `{name="FrenzyEffect", type="INC", value=16, [1]={type="Condition",
var="DualWielding"}}`, extra=nil; `db:Sum` returns 16 only when `conditions.DualWielding` holds,
0 otherwise. `"0.5% … per Strength"` → PerStat:Str, `db:Sum` with `actor.output.Str=100` returns
50. Spec `spec/System/TestFangsBerserkerFrenzyEffect_spec.lua` (11/11). Adjacent
`TestEffectOfBuffAlias` / `TestAspectEffect` / `TestMinionFrenzyBuff` / `TestModParse` all green.

### `exulis-haste-effect-per-rampancy`

**Family:** a buff-effect scalar carrying a SUFFIX the pre-existing "on you" / "per strength" /
"while dual wielding" handlers don't anchor:
- `5% Increased effect of Haste per 10 Rampancy` (Exulis, the Oracle Amulet unique)

**Ground truth (verbatim, no fabrication):** `src/Data/Uniques/uniques_1_4.json:9476` and
`src/Data/Uniques/uniques.json:10662` carry the string verbatim. Both the coefficient (5) and the
divisor (10) are CAPTURED from the string, never hardcoded.

**Non-DPS (parse-completion, not a DPS change):** Haste is movement-only in-game — datamine
ailment id 33 "Increases movement speed", a single buff `property 9 = MovementSpeed`,
`increasedValue 0.30`, `dealsDamage=false`. LEB models it as `MovementSpeed INC 30`
(`ConfigOptions.lua:511`). `HasteEffect` INC therefore scales the Haste buff's movement speed
only (`CalcPerform.lua` `skillModList:Sum("INC", skillCfg, buff.name:gsub(" ","").."Effect")`
→ `(1 + inc/100)` on the buff's modList); it never touches per-hit / FullDPS.

**Silent failure:** "Haste" is stripped by the skill-name post-scan, leaving a bare
`" effect of "` residue, so ModCache baked `{{}," effect of   "}` (empty modList) at
`src/Data/ModCache.lua:14683`. Because `parseMod` short-circuits on an exact
`parseModCache[line]` key, the baked empty row BYPASSES any handler, so the row was **DELETED**
(not re-baked) to re-parse live.

**Fix (whole-line handler, one per known buff, inside the `knownBuffsOnYou` loop):**
```
["^([%+%-]?[%d%.]+)%% increased effect of "..esc.." per (%d+) rampancy$"]
    -> mod(bVar.."Effect","INC",num, { type="PerStat", stat="Rampancy", div=per })
```
`bVar` is `buff.name:gsub(" ","")`. **Capture-index trap:** `parseMod` (ModParser.lua ~L6298)
invokes a matched specialMod as `specialMod(tonumber(cap[1]), unpack(cap))`, i.e. the args are
`(coefficientAsNumber, cap[1], cap[2], …)`. A two-capture pattern's SECOND capture (the divisor)
therefore arrives as the **THIRD** parameter — the signature must be `function(num, _, per)`, NOT
`function(num, per)` (which binds `per` to the re-passed `cap[1]` = the coefficient, silently
producing `div = coefficient`). This mirrors the existing
`chance to gain <Buff> for N seconds when you Echo` handler's `function(num, chance, duration)`.
Rampancy is the Vit-converted Season-4 attribute (`ModParser.lua:1816` registers the stat;
`CalcPerform.lua:344` converts Vit→Rampancy); `ModStore.lua:413/450` resolves `PerStat` and
applies `base/div`. `Rampancy` has no `s4ConvertedTwin` forward entry, so only `output.Rampancy`
contributes.

**Scoping (no collision):** the pattern requires `"… per (%d+) rampancy$"`, which cannot match
the `"… on you$"` / `"… per strength$"` / `"… while dual wielding$"` handlers (different suffix).
The whole-line special consumes the entire line (`#specialLine==0`), taking precedence over the
generic `modTagList["per (%d+) rampancy"]` (ModParser.lua:1821) — necessary because the CORE
`"N% increased effect of haste"` has NO `modNameList` resolver, so the generic tag path alone
would leave the whole line as residue.

**Residue-drop trap:** the handler emits `nil` extra (residue-free), so
`PassiveTree:ProcessStats` (`if mod.list and not mod.extra`) does not drop it.

**Verification (modDB-level):** `modLib.parseMod("5% Increased effect of Haste per 10 Rampancy")`
→ `{name="HasteEffect", type="INC", value=5, [1]={type="PerStat", stat="Rampancy", div=10}}`,
extra=nil; `db:Sum` with `actor.output.Rampancy=100` returns 50 (`5 × 100/10`), 0 at Rampancy=0.
Spec `spec/System/TestExulisHasteEffectRampancy_spec.lua` (7/7).

**Corpus blast radius (MAIN `spec/TestBuilds/`):** 51 build XMLs reference Exulis. Live before/after
probe on `A6PJ1WXG lv98 Marksman` (Exulis equipped in the Amulet slot, Rampancy=38):
`HasteEffect 0 → 19` (= 5 × 38/10, exact); `MovementSpeedMod` unchanged at 1.24 (Haste inactive in
that saved config); FullDPS/TotalDPS **byte-identical** (50162.367927502 = snapshot 50162.3679).
The stat now FLOWS but is DPS-neutral (movement only). Snapshots NOT regenerated in this worktree
(corpus absent/gitignored); a local regen of the 51 Exulis builds only refreshes the non-DPS
`HasteEffect` (and `MovementSpeedMod` where Haste is active) fields — the corpus DPS gate stays
green regardless.

### `effect-of-buff-signed-value`

**Bug (in the sibling `effect-of-buff-on-you-bare-alias` handlers):** both the "increased
Effect of {buff} on You" and the bare "Effect of {buff} on You" patterns anchored the value
with `%+?` (optional PLUS only) and captured `([%d%.]+)` (digits, no sign). A REDUCED roll
renders "-7% Effect of Frenzy on You" (found live in a captured build): the `%+?` anchor failed
to match the "-" entirely (SILENT FAILURE), and even had it matched, the sign sitting OUTSIDE
the capture would have flipped a -7 reduction into a +7 increase.

**Fix (`src/Modules/ModParser.lua`, `knownBuffsOnYou` loop):** both patterns now capture the
optional sign INSIDE the number group — `^([%+%-]?[%d%.]+)%% ...` — and pass `tonumber(num)`, so
"-7% Effect of Frenzy on You" -> `FrenzyEffect INC -7` (a genuine reduction), while positive and
unsigned rolls are unchanged (byte-identical parse for "14% ..." / "+14% ...").

**Verification:** `spec/System/TestEffectOfBuffAlias_spec.lua` test #8 (signed cases:
`-7%`/`-12%` Frenzy -> INC -7/-12; `-5% increased Haste` -> INC -5). No corpus build carries a
negative buff-effect line (grep 0) — corpus-neutral, no regen.

### `trigger-chance-on-throwing-hit-dps`

**Files:** `src/Modules/CalcTriggers.lua` (DPS read, the fix) — with siblings
`src/Modules/CalcSetup.lua` + `src/Modules/ModParser.lua`
(`trigger-chance-to-cast-on-throwing-hit`, source gating + parse bridge).
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestTriggerOnThrowingHitDPS_spec.lua`

**Contract:** the on-throwing-hit trigger DPS path must read its chance at DPS time
under the SAME source-type gate used to CREATE the granted group. The throwing
bridge emits the chance as `ChanceToTriggerOnThrowingHit_<skillId>` (global), and
CalcSetup sums it only for a `SkillType.Throwing` source, then routes it through the
on-hit (`triggeredOnHit`) path. But the `configTable["cast on hit"]` handler in
CalcTriggers computed the trigger chance from ONLY `ChanceToTriggerOnHit_<id>`. So a
throwing-only chance was 0 at DPS time: the group was created (and correctly flagged
`includeInFullDPS`) but its rate collapsed to `trigRate x 0% = 0` and it was dropped
by the `output.TotalDPS > 0` Full-DPS gate. Symptom: "X% chance to cast Smite on hit
with throwing attacks" idols produced NO Smite entry in Full DPS.

**Fix:** in `configTable["cast on hit"]`, after reading `ChanceToTriggerOnHit_<id>`,
add `ChanceToTriggerOnThrowingHit_<id>` when `source.skillTypes[SkillType.Throwing]`.
Gated on the source type so a non-throwing source sums nothing (byte-identical for
every non-throwing-triggered build).

## trigger-chance-to-cast-on-bow-hit / trigger-chance-on-bow-hit-dps

**Files:** `src/Modules/ModParser.lua` (parse bridge), `src/Modules/CalcSetup.lua`
(source gating + group creation), `src/Modules/CalcTriggers.lua` (DPS-time read),
`src/Modules/ConfigOptions.lua` (opt-in toggle), `src/Data/ModCache.lua` (stale rows
deleted).
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestReignOfWinterIcicleProc_spec.lua`

**Bug (silent failure):** the unique bow **Reign of Winter** (`uniques_1_4.json` #159 /
`uniques.json`) affix `"(23-28)% Chance to cast Icicle on Bow Hit"` reached NO computed
entity — `"on bow hit"` matched no `specialModList` rule, so the line baked to an EMPTY
`ModCache.lua` row (`c["26% Chance to cast Icicle on Bow Hit"]={{}," to cast  on   "}`)
and the proc contributed nothing to Full DPS on the 61 builds that equip it. The
triggered skill is `data.skills.HeorotUniqueBowIcicle` (name "Icicle"; spell, hit, cold
base 100). The verbatim source affix string maps 1:1 to the code condition
`^%+?([%d%.]+)%% chance to cast icicle on bow hit$`.

**Fix (config-gated trigger wire, bow sibling of the throwing/melee/spell bridges):**
1. ModParser `onBowHitTriggerBridge` emits a functional, GLOBAL
   `ChanceToTriggerOnBowHit_HeorotUniqueBowIcicle` BASE mod (new scoped family, no
   default consumer). Also handles the `"+X%"` combined-affix form.
2. CalcSetup's `grantedTriggeredSkills` loop sums it ONLY for a `SkillType.Bow` source
   AND when `Condition:ModelReignOfWinterIcicleProc` is set, routing it through the
   `triggeredOnHit` path (group creation).
3. CalcTriggers' `cast on hit` handler reads the SAME stat with the SAME
   Bow + config gate at DPS time (else the created group collapses to
   `trigRate x 0% = 0` and is dropped by the `TotalDPS > 0` gate — the identical
   failure the throwing/melee/spell siblings fixed).
4. ConfigOptions adds the `conditionModelReignOfWinterIcicleProc` `check` toggle,
   default OFF, mirroring `conditionHolyAuraDamageAura`.
5. The 6 stale empty `ModCache.lua` rows for this affix text are DELETED so the affix
   re-parses live through the new rule (parse cache is loaded cache-first in headless).

**Why config-gated (default OFF), NOT auto-folded:** the proc CHANCE is datamined
(23-28%), but its RATE CAP / internal cooldown is NOT. Folding at the full bow-hit rate
x chance would be a fabricated magnitude, so the fold is opt-in. No curve-fit: the
modelled rate uses only the datamined affix chance and the bow skill's build-derived hit
rate. When the user opts in, `ChanceToTriggerOnBowHit_` is consumed and Icicle enters
Full DPS at `bow hit rate x hit chance x affix chance`.

**Corpus impact:** BYTE-IDENTICAL by default. Nothing consumes `ChanceToTriggerOnBowHit_`
unless the toggle is on, so the extra parsed mod is inert and no snapshot changes — NO
regen needed. (Verified: the sum is behind `sourceIsBow and modelBowHitProc`, and the
DPS-time read behind the same gate; deleting the stale empty ModCache rows only swaps a
no-mod parse for an inert-mod parse.)

## flow-conditional-damage

**Bug (silent failure):** the Rogue/Bladedancer "Flow" resource cluster — the
"Rhythm" mastery node plus adjacent tree nodes (Rogue-2 / Rogue-54 / Rogue-57) —
grants damage/crit modifiers conditioned on generating or consuming Flow. Each
line parsed to a valid numeric mod PLUS a non-empty residue ("when generating or
consuming Flow" / "when Consuming Flow"), so `PassiveTree:ProcessStats` dropped
the WHOLE family. On AfiyaLapizDSTake2 the modDB held 0 Flow-tagged mods — the
entire Flow damage package (incl. two "100% More Damage When Consuming Flow"
nodes) was inert.

**Fix:** two `modTagList` entries in `ModParser.lua` strip the phrase and attach a
`Condition` tag (`GeneratingOrConsumingFlow` / `ConsumingFlow`); two `check`
toggles in `ConfigOptions.lua` (default OFF, `ifCond`-gated) drive those
Conditions. The 5 stale silent-failure rows in `ModCache.lua` were deleted so the
new handlers are not bypassed by the parse-cache short-circuit. "when consuming
flow" cannot match "...OR consuming flow", so the two keys never collide.

**Default OFF => corpus-neutral:** 0 of the 1.4 corpus builds carry any
Flow-conditional stat, and the mods are Condition-gated off by default, so no
snapshot changes. No regen required to land.

## trigger-chance-on-spell-cast-dps

**Bug (latent):** spell-cast sibling of `trigger-chance-on-throwing-hit-dps` /
`trigger-chance-on-melee-hit-dps`. "cast <skill> on (spell) cast" emits
`ChanceToTriggerOnSpellCast_<id>` (ModParser `onSpellCastTriggerBridge`) and
CalcSetup already sums it (`sourceIsSpell`) to CREATE the Full-DPS group, but the
`configTable["cast on hit"]` DPS handler in CalcTriggers read only the bare
`ChanceToTriggerOnHit_<id>` -> spell-cast-triggered skills computed triggerChance=0
and the group was dropped by the TotalDPS>0 gate.

**Fix:** in the same handler, after the melee read, add
`ChanceToTriggerOnSpellCast_<id>` when `source.skillTypes[SkillType.Spell]`. Unlike
the hit-based siblings, a SPELL source takes no Melee/Attack hit-chance branch in the
handler, so the returned `useCastRate=true` makes trigRate the source's CAST rate:
`SkillTriggerRate = min(cap, castRate x chance)` -- the "rate = cast_rate x chance"
form the framework already assumes.

## trigger-spell-cast-cooldown-cap

**Bug (latent, completes `trigger-chance-on-spell-cast-dps`):** the on-spell-cast bridge
emitted only the chance, no rate cap. Lagon's Answer (Shaman node `Primalist-69`) casts
Storm Bolt (`PrimalLightning`) with a **1s trigger cooldown carried in its REMINDER TEXT**,
not an inline "(1 second cooldown)" the ModParser capped-variant patterns read from the
line. So `SkillTriggerRate` was `castRate x chance` with no ceiling -> a very fast-casting
Lagon's Answer build would be over-read (proc rate can never exceed 1/s in-game).

**Fix:** `ModParser.onSpellCastTriggerBridge` now carries a datamined reminderText-cooldown
table `onSpellCastReminderTextCooldownCap = { PrimalLightning = 1 }` (skillId -> 1 / cooldown
seconds) and, when the triggered skill is in it, emits
`TriggerRateCapPerSecond_<skillId>` alongside the chance. The rest of the pipeline already
existed: CalcSetup (`trigger-rate-cap-ptt` loop) reads `TriggerRateCapPerSecond_<skillId>`
and attaches it to the injected group's `srcInstance.triggerRateCapPerSecond`; CalcTriggers
min-applies it (`output.TriggerRateCap = m_min(..., srcInst.triggerRateCapPerSecond)`), so
`SkillTriggerRate = min(1/s, castRate x chance)`. The cap is the trigger cooldown (1/s),
independent of the chance roll (both 8% and 40% cap at 1/s).

**Datamine ground truth:** Storm Bolt = `data.skills.PrimalLightning` (no skill-data
cooldown of its own -> the 1s lives on the Lagon's Answer trigger, `tree_0.json` node 69).
Ground-truthed non-binding at the observed cast rate (SuXes_StormBolt2, proc gaps >= 4.7s;
even button-held Avalanche peaks ~1.37 casts/s x 0.40 = 0.55 proc/s < 1/s, so the cap does
not bind for Avalanche -- it protects only a genuinely fast-casting source).

**Corpus-neutral:** the cap only rides on the on-spell-cast bridge, whose sole would-be
carrier (Lagon's Answer) is not held by any corpus build (the "on spell cast" corpus affix
is "Avalanche Boulder drop", a different mod). `min()` only ever lowers a rate, and no build
routes through it -> TotalDPS / FullDPS byte-identical pre/post.

**Guard:** inline `@leb-regression-guard:trigger-spell-cast-cooldown-cap` at the ModParser
emit site (`src/Modules/ModParser.lua`, `onSpellCastTriggerBridge`) + the CalcTriggers CD-cap
comment; spec `TestTriggerOnSpellCastDPS_spec.lua` (cap emitted = 1, chance-independent, guard
marker present, CalcSetup/CalcTriggers wiring present).

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestTriggerOnSpellCastDPS_spec.lua`.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

## minion-multiskill-cadence-fold

**Gap (single-minion multi-skill FullDPS):** a minion that casts several damaging
skills on ONE action economy — Manifest Armor = Melee + Forge Breath + Whirlwind +
Charge — has only its DEFAULT (main) skill summed into the FullDPS headline
(`Calcs.lua` minion FullDPS loop adds `minion.output.TotalDPS`, the main skill only).
Manifest Armor's Melee-only headline is ~21% of the true multi-skill output. You
cannot just SUM each skill's standalone DPS: the minion time-shares one timeline, so
each skill fires a FRACTION of the time. Correct contribution = `Sum_S cadence_S ×
perHit_S`, and that cadence is emergent minion-AI behaviour — it is NOT in the skill
data (the granted skills carry no cooldown / attack-rate stat) and NOT derivable from
cooldowns, so it can only come from a capture.

## tree-tag-swap-determinism

**Bug (cross-process nondeterminism, pre-existing on dev):** repeated identical
headless loads of `spec/TestBuilds/1.4/bin/YsSmiteVK.xml` (loadBuildFromXML +
OnFrame) flipped between byte-identical-to-snapshot (majority) and a uniform
~-9% (×10/11) shift on ~32 hit/DPS keys (FullDPS 1070.36 vs 1016.26,
NonCritAverageHit 306.41 vs 278.56), roughly 1-2 in 6 runs.

**Root cause (two order-dependent sites in `src/Modules/CalcActiveSkill.lua`):**

1. **Producer — `calcs.getTreeTagSwaps`:** the swaps table is keyed by source
   damage-type bit, so two allocated nodes on one tree that both convert FROM
   the same type collide last-writer-wins. YsSmiteVK's Smite tree has exactly
   that collision: `sm87r4-21` " Fire -> Lightning Damage" writes
   `swaps[Fire]=Lightning`, and `sm87r4-32` " Void Conversion" (source-less;
   source inferred from Smite's intrinsic Fire tag) writes `swaps[Fire]=Void`.
   The loop iterated `pairs(env.allocNodes)` — string keys, whose hash order is
   randomised per process — so the winner flapped: when Fire→Void won, Smite
   carried the Void tag and the Void Knight Echo gate
   (`skillTypes[SkillType.Void] and skillFlags.spell`, CalcActiveSkill
   void-knight-echo-more site) granted its 10% Damage MORE; when
   Fire→Lightning won, the Void tag vanished and every hit/ailment key dropped
   by exactly ×1/1.1. **Fix:** collect the prefix-matched node ids, `table.sort`
   them, and process in sorted order — the LEXICALLY-LAST node id
   deterministically wins a same-source collision (`sm87r4-32` > `sm87r4-21` ⇒
   Void wins, matching the snapshot corpus and the build's in-game intent).

2. **Consumer — `calcs.applyTreeTagSwaps`:** the old incremental loop
   (`out[src]=nil; out[dst]=true` per swap) let one swap's destination feed the
   next swap's source test, so a chained swaps table ({A→B, B→C} with A,B both
   present) double-hopped or not depending on `pairs(swaps)` iteration order
   (numeric-bit keys; layout follows insertion order). **Fix:** two-phase apply
   decided entirely against the PRE-swap tag set: build removeMask/addMask
   first, then clear sources, then add destinations (a destination that is also
   a removed source stays present). keywordFlags get the same mask treatment.

**Verified:** before the fix 5/15 identical runs diverged; after, 15/15 runs
byte-identical to the YsSmiteVK snapshot (4dp roundDeep over all mainOutput
keys). Independently re-confirmed with one build per PROCESS (fresh string-hash
seed per run): YsSmiteVK, `QqwprgdN lv100 Necromancer` and `BurningMyWood lv83
Beastmaster` — the three builds observed to flap on dev — each produced a single
distinct output hash across 10 runs, all matching snapshot. No snapshot regen
required. Focused busted subset green (65 assertions over the tag-swap /
conversion / Void-Knight-echo specs, incl. this guard's spec); the full suite was
NOT run for this change.

**Mechanism note:** LuaJIT seeds string hashing per process, so `pairs()` over a
string-keyed table is *usually* stable across runs but occasionally reorders —
measured directly: 1 of 4 fresh processes reordered a 9-key string table. That
matches the observed ~1-2-in-6 flap rate, and is why the bug looked intermittent.
Address-keyed (table-ref) tables reorder on essentially every process.

**Corpus-sweep trap (caused one false diagnosis here):** a sweep comparator that
skips only a *leaf* key named `MinionSkillBreakdown` still recurses into it when
both sides hold a table, counting display-only breakdown TEXT as output diffs.
That makes every minion build look "DIFF vs snapshot" and made two of them look
like numeric flappers. Skip the whole `MinionSkillBreakdown` SUBTREE.

**Regression to prevent:** reverting either site to raw `pairs()` order
(re-introduces run-to-run output flapping that masquerades as stale snapshots
in corpus sweeps); "simplifying" the two-phase apply back to incremental
(chain order-dependence returns); changing the collision winner rule
(lexically-last) without regenerating affected snapshots — YsSmiteVK's Smite
must keep the Void tag.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestTreeTagSwapDeterminism_spec.lua`.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `tree-version-loadable-vs-offered`

Retiring a game version from the UI must not change what LEB can open. Two lists,
never one: `treeVersionList` = versions LEB can LOAD (never shrink),
`offeredTreeVersionList` = versions the UI OFFERS (retire here, and only here).
1.2/1.3 are retired from the UI while their data files stay on disk and loaded.

| Site | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `src/GameVersions.lua` | Declares both lists |
| `src/Modules/Data.lua` (per-version load loop) | Loadable — iterates `treeVersionList` |
| `src/Modules/Main.lua` (`main:LoadTree`) | Loadable — gates lazy tree load on `treeVersionList` |
| `src/Classes/TreeTab.lua` (Version dropdown, `BuildVersionList`) | Offered |
| `src/Classes/TreeTab.lua` (`validateTreeVersion` lower bound) | Offered |

**Files:** `src/GameVersions.lua`, `src/Classes/TreeTab.lua`.

**Invariant:** Every offered version is also loadable. A build saved on a retired
version opens on its OWN tree and data (`build.spec.tree == main.tree[ver]`,
`data.uniques == data.versionData[ver].uniques`), computes, and is offered
conversion via `showConvert` rather than being converted — LEB never re-points a
saved build at another version. Dropping a version from `treeVersionList` kills
`data.versionData[ver]` and `main:LoadTree` (build dies indexing a nil tree);
dropping it from the `treeVersions` table additionally makes `Build.lua` force a
convert-or-cancel modal, so the build can no longer be opened as itself. The
Version dropdown lists the active spec's version even when retired — `SelByValue`
no-ops on a miss and would otherwise display a 1.2 build as "1.4".

**Snapshot coverage:** none — no corpus build uses a retired version (all 644 are
`treeVersion="1_4"`), so the spec drives a synthetic build instead.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestTreeVersionRetire_spec.lua`.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `default-tree-version-named-not-positional`

`defaultTreeVersion` (the version assumed for a `<Spec>` with no `treeVersion`
attribute) is a NAME, declared as a literal. It was `treeVersionList[2]`.

**Files:** `src/GameVersions.lua`.

**Invariant:** `defaultTreeVersion` is a literal version string and its
declaration does not index `treeVersionList`. Positionally, shrinking the list
silently rebinds it to a different version (measured: 3 entries → 2 rebinds it
from "1_3" to "1_4"); it does not go nil, so no runtime check catches it, and
value assertions pass while the list is unshrunk. The spec therefore asserts on
the declaration text as well as the value. `latestTreeVersion` stays positional
(`treeVersionList[#treeVersionList]`) by design: "last == newest" must keep
tracking the end of the list as seasons are added.

**Snapshot coverage:** none — no corpus build takes the attribute-less path.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestTreeVersionRetire_spec.lua`.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `legacy-target-version-live`

`legacyTargetVersion` is the `targetVersion` given to a build whose XML has no
`targetVersion` attribute, and it drives `data.setActiveVersion` — i.e. which
game version's item/unique/base data interprets that build. It was `"1_2"`.

**Files:** `src/GameVersions.lua`, consumed at `src/Modules/Build.lua`
(`self.targetVersion = xml.attrib.targetVersion or legacyTargetVersion`).

**Invariant:** `legacyTargetVersion == liveTargetVersion`, and it names an
offered version. A build of unknown version is interpreted with live data, not
with retired season-2 data that no one chose. Retired-version data remains
loadable for builds that explicitly ask for it by attribute.

**Snapshot coverage:** none, and 0 blast — all 644 corpus builds carry
`targetVersion="1_4"`, so none reach this default.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestTreeVersionRetire_spec.lua`.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `corpus-build-key-is-path-not-basename`

The corpus test keyed its build map by BASENAME while the regen drivers keyed by full
path. `spec/TestBuilds/1.4/` and `1.4/bin/` hold 6 pairs of same-named but genuinely
different builds (distinct md5, e.g. `VoidCleaver lv84 VK.xml`), so each pair collapsed
to one entry: 6 builds were never tested, and which copy survived was decided by
directory-walk order. A build that is never enumerated cannot fail, so the suite stayed
green over the hole. Enumeration now lives once, in `spec/CorpusScope.lua`, and returns
a sorted ARRAY of paths -- an array cannot collide, and sorting makes the order
deterministic (`pairs()` is not).

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| walker | `spec/CorpusScope.lua` `listBuildFiles` | recursive walk -> sorted array of paths |
| identity | `spec/CorpusScope.lua` `buildName` | root-relative name (`1.4/bin/X.lua`), unique |
| consumer | `spec/System/TestBuilds_spec.lua` `fetchBuilds` | keys `buildList` by root-relative path |

**Files:** `spec/CorpusScope.lua`, `spec/System/TestBuilds_spec.lua`
**Invariant:** a build is identified by its PATH. Never key a corpus map by basename, and
never return a name-keyed set from the walker -- both silently drop one of every
colliding pair. Test names carry the root-relative path so the pairs stay distinguishable.
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestCorpusScope_spec.lua`
**Snapshot coverage:** the 6 previously-unenumerated builds are now tested; no snapshot
values change (enumeration only).
**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `regen-root-equals-test-root`

The snapshot-regen driver defaulted to `../spec/TestBuilds/1.4` (639 builds) while the
corpus test walked `../spec/TestBuilds` (644). The 5 builds outside `1.4/` (`1.2/` x3,
`1.3/` x1, `StarSeaVnV_LEB.xml`) were tested but unreachable by any regen -- not a recent
addition, they had never been in scope. Both scopes exit 0, so the gap only ever surfaced
as a stale snapshot nobody could regenerate (measured: `warpath_channel` in `1.2/`). The
root is now one constant in `spec/CorpusScope.lua` that the test and the regen drivers
share.

| Site | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| constant | `spec/CorpusScope.lua` `M.ROOT` | the one corpus root, unpinned to a version |
| default | `spec/CorpusScope.lua` `resolveBuildRoot` | `LEB_ROOT` or `M.ROOT`; only the DEFAULT is locked |
| consumer | `spec/GenerateBuilds.lua` | roots regen at `CorpusScope.ROOT` |
| consumer | `spec/System/TestBuilds_spec.lua` | walks `CorpusScope.ROOT` |

**Files:** `spec/CorpusScope.lua`, `spec/GenerateBuilds.lua`, `spec/System/TestBuilds_spec.lua`
**Invariant:** the DEFAULT regen root and the test root are the same tree. Explicit
`LEB_ROOT` narrowing stays allowed -- that is what targeted regen uses; a narrow DEFAULT
is the bug. Consumers take the root from `CorpusScope.ROOT`, never a literal.
**Spec:** `spec/System/TestCorpusScope_spec.lua`
**Snapshot coverage:** none -- enumeration/scope only, no calc change.
**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `run-specs-no-vacuous-green`

`scripts/run-specs.sh` refuses the two ways this repo hands back a GREEN THAT TESTED
NOTHING. Both were hit for real on 2026-07-17/18 by separate sessions, and both were
already written up in three hand-offs first -- prose did not stop them.

1. Naming a tag-excluded spec (`run-specs.sh ../spec/System/TestBuilds_spec.lua`):
   `.busted` sets `exclude-tags = "builds,allSkills"`, so busted skips every corpus
   test, reports the file's few untagged successes and exits 0 in ~5s.
2. Asking for the builds tag where `spec/TestBuilds/` is absent (every worktree, and
   CI): the corpus is gitignored, main-repo only, so zero builds are enumerated and
   the suite passes vacuously. Tell: ~100s instead of ~900-1100s.

The tag scan is anchored to `describe|it|expose|insulate` TITLES. A bare `#builds`
match flags any file that merely mentions the tag, and a false refusal here trains
people to route around the check -- the same failure mode
`dev-merge-guard-gate-matching` records for `LEB_SKIP_CONVENTION_GATES`.

**Sites:**

| site | role |
|---|---|
| `scripts/run-specs.sh` Trap 3 | refuses a named spec whose tag `.busted` excludes |
| `scripts/run-specs.sh` Trap 4 | refuses `--tags=builds` where `spec/TestBuilds/` is absent |

**Files:**
- `scripts/run-specs.sh`
- `spec/System/TestRunSpecsNoVacuousGreen_spec.lua`

**Invariant:** the runner exits non-zero rather than report success for a run that
exercised none of what was asked for. If `exclude-tags` cannot be parsed out of
`.busted` the script must SAY SO on stderr -- a guard that silently stops guarding is
worse than no guard, so the spec pins the `.busted` form the parser depends on.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestRunSpecsNoVacuousGreen_spec.lua` "refuses a tag-excluded
spec instead of reporting a fast green"

**Snapshot coverage:** none -- test tooling, not calc.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `passive-tree-progress-indicator-layer`

The mastery skill-unlock bar's vertical indicators (the gold progress slider and the
unselected-mastery lock chain) span up from the bar into the passive tree. In-game they
sit BEHIND the tree's connectors and nodes; LEB drew them at the skill-bar main layer
(1), so the gold line covered the nodes. The fix drops just those two draws to the
tree's main layer 0 at sublayer 10 -- below the connectors (sublayer 20) and nodes
(sublayer 25) -- then restores main layer 1 for the skill icons. The progress marker
diamond must still land ON the bar (in front), so the slider's bottom-diamond tex slice
is excluded from the behind-the-tree draw and a separate top-diamond slice is drawn at
layer 1, centered on the bar. Display-only, DPS/calc-inert, snapshot-neutral.

**Sites:**

| site | role |
|---|---|
| `src/Classes/TreeTab.lua` (skill-bar draw) | `SetDrawLayer(0, 10)` before the lock bar + slider, `SetDrawLayer(1)` after; slider drawn with tex `0,0,1,0.94` (no bottom diamond); marker drawn with tex `0,0,1,0.05` at main layer 1 |

**Files:**
- `src/Classes/TreeTab.lua`
- `spec/System/TestPassiveTreeProgressIndicatorLayer_spec.lua`

**Invariant:** the vertical progress indicator draws behind the tree (main layer 0,
sublayer < the connector sublayer 20) and the on-bar progress marker draws in front
(skill-bar main layer 1). Collapsing both onto one layer makes the line cover the nodes
again.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestPassiveTreeProgressIndicatorLayer_spec.lua` "draws the
vertical indicator behind the tree and the marker on the bar"

**Snapshot coverage:** none -- UI draw order only, no calc change.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `progress-bar-fill-tiled-per-point`

The mastery skill-unlock bar's gold fill was one `progress-fill` image stretched from
the bar start to the current progress position. In-game the fill reads as a repeated
frame per point, so the fill is now tiled: one copy of the image per allocated point,
each occupying one point slot (`lineWidth / maxUnlockLevel` wide), drawn from the bar
start. N points spent => N copies, capped at the bar's point length. Display-only,
DPS/calc-inert, snapshot-neutral.

**Sites:**

| site | role |
|---|---|
| `src/Classes/TreeTab.lua` (skill-bar fill) | loop `for i = 0, min(masteryPointsSpent, maxUnlockLevel) - 1` drawing `progress-fill` at `lineLeft + i * pointWidth` |

**Files:**
- `src/Classes/TreeTab.lua`
- `spec/System/TestProgressBarFillTiled_spec.lua`

**Invariant:** the fill is drawn once per allocated point (N points => N `progress-fill`
draws, capped at the bar length), not a single image stretched across the whole fill.
Collapsing it back to one stretched DrawImage loses the per-point frames.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestProgressBarFillTiled_spec.lua` "draws one fill image per
allocated point (5 points => 5 fills, not 1)"

**Snapshot coverage:** none -- UI draw only, no calc change.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `notes-codeblock-verbatim-monospace`

Fenced code blocks in Notes render in the fixed-width CODE_FONT and their body lines
are captured verbatim -- never routed through the inline markdown tokenizer. This is
what lets template ASCII art (the Showcase "LAST EPOCH BUILDING" owl banner) keep its
columns aligned. Display-only, DPS/calc-inert, snapshot-neutral.

**Sites:**

| site | role |
|---|---|
| `src/Modules/MarkdownRender.lua` (parse code branch) | captures fenced-block body lines verbatim into `node.lines` |
| `src/Modules/MarkdownRender.lua` (render code branch) | draws each `codeLine` in `CODE_FONT` ("FIXED") |
| `src/Data/NotesTemplates/Showcase.md` | owl banner fixture the guard fingerprints |

**Files:**
- `src/Modules/MarkdownRender.lua`
- `src/Data/NotesTemplates/Showcase.md`
- `spec/System/TestNotesCodeBlockVerbatim_spec.lua`

**Invariant:** code-block bodies are stored and drawn verbatim in the fixed-width
CODE_FONT, and the Showcase owl banner stays inside a code fence with no ** markers and
a letter row spelling LASTEPOCHBUILDING. Routing code lines through tokenizeInline or a
proportional font, or dropping the banner's fence, breaks every ASCII-art banner.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestNotesCodeBlockVerbatim_spec.lua` "captures body lines
verbatim, keeping ** and leading spaces" / "has no ** markdown markers in the banner"

**Snapshot coverage:** none -- Notes preview render only, no calc change.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `notes-preview-scroll-covers-render`

The Notes preview scrollbar extent is the larger of the cached measure() height and
the height the renderer actually drew last frame (`max(contentH, lastPreviewRenderedH)`),
not the raw measure. measure() is cached and can lag the live render -- an async image
finishing its load grows the drawn content, and measure()/render() also drift a few px
on identical content -- so trusting the shorter measure left the bottom section
(References) unreachable until a reload. Display-only, DPS/calc-inert, snapshot-neutral.

**Sites:**

| site | role |
|---|---|
| `src/Classes/NotesTab.lua` (`DrawPreview`) | sizes the vertical scrollbar with `scrollH = max(contentH, lastPreviewRenderedH)` and stores `lastPreviewRenderedH` from the renderer's return |

**Files:**
- `src/Classes/NotesTab.lua`
- `spec/System/TestNotesPreviewScrollExtent_spec.lua`

**Invariant:** the preview vertical scroll extent covers the full rendered document
height, so trailing content is always reachable even when the cached measure is shorter
than the live render. Reverting to raw `contentH` re-hides trailing content whenever
render > measure. The stale rendered height is reset on content/scale change so a taller
old document cannot over-extend a shorter new one.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestNotesPreviewScrollExtent_spec.lua` "uses the larger of measure
and rendered height for the extent" / "grows with more content (height is cumulative)"

**Snapshot coverage:** none -- Notes preview scroll UI only, no calc change.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `calc-section-output-key-underscore`

CalcSectionControl:FormatStr substitutes `{output:KEY}` / `{N:output:KEY}` placeholders
whose KEY contains underscores or digits (e.g.
`BurningDaggerChanceOnMeleeFire_RateLimit`), not only letters. The key character class
was `[%a%.:]+`, so any underscore/digit key silently failed to match and the raw
`{0:output:...}` text rendered in the Calcs tab. Surfaced by the dev "Show All" toggle
which reveals rows normally hidden at 0. Display-only, DPS/calc-inert.

**Files:**
- `src/Classes/CalcSectionControl.lua`
- `spec/System/TestCalcSectionOutputKeyUnderscore_spec.lua`

**Invariant:** the `{output:...}` and `{N:output:...}` placeholder key class is
`[%w_%.:]+`, so underscore/digit output keys substitute their value; narrowing it back
to letters re-breaks every stat whose output key has an underscore.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestCalcSectionOutputKeyUnderscore_spec.lua` "substitutes output
keys that contain underscores"

**Snapshot coverage:** none -- Calcs tab text render only, no calc change.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>

### `calc-section-last-row-frame-gap`

CalcSectionControl reserves a 2px gap after each expanded subsection's rows so the last
row's label/value does not sit flush against the section's bottom colour frame (or the
next subsection's header border). Every row label fills its row to the bottom edge, so
without the gap the final row's text touched the orange frame line. Display-only,
DPS/calc-inert.

**Sites:**

| site | role |
|---|---|
| `src/Classes/CalcSectionControl.lua` (UpdateSize) | `self.height + 22 + 2` per expanded subsection |
| `src/Classes/CalcSectionControl.lua` (Draw) | `lineY = lineY + 2` after the row loop |

**Files:**
- `src/Classes/CalcSectionControl.lua`
- `spec/System/TestCalcSectionRowLayout_spec.lua`

**Invariant:** an expanded subsection of N single-line rows makes the section height
`2 + 18*N + 22 + 2`; dropping the trailing +2 puts the last row flush against the bottom
frame. UpdateSize and Draw share the same +2 so measured height and drawn content agree.

**Spec:** `spec/System/TestCalcSectionRowLayout_spec.lua` "reserves a 2px bottom gap
after the last row (2 rows)"

**Snapshot coverage:** none -- Calcs tab layout only, no calc change.

**Establishing commit:** <see git log>
